## 9. Tenant Registration, Onboarding and Provisioning

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (registration, legal acceptance, subscription creation, job orchestration) and Tenant (seeded data, onboarding checklist) |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `Tenancy` (registration and provisioning), `Legal` (legal documents and acceptances) |
| **Depends on** | §6, §7, §10, §11, §12, §13, §14, §17 |

### 9.1 Onboarding Lifecycle

Onboarding spans three records, each with its own status. A tenant is **fully active** only when all three agree.

| Record | Statuses | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `tenant_registrations.status` | `pending_verification` → `converted`, or `expired` | §9.3 |
| `tenants.status` | `awaiting_payment` → `provisioning` → `active` (or `provisioning_failed`); later `suspended`, `closed`, `purged` | §6.5 |
| `subscriptions.status` | `incomplete` → `trialing` or `active` → `past_due` → `cancelled` | §14.3 |

```
POST /api/register ─► registration: pending_verification ── not verified within 24 h ─► expired
        │ owner verifies the email
        ▼
registration: converted, and the tenant row is created
        ├─ price is free, or has an eligible trial with no payment method required
        │     └─► subscription trialing or active ─► tenant: provisioning ─► active
        └─ paid price without an eligible trial, or a trial that requires a payment method
              └─► subscription incomplete ─► tenant: awaiting_payment
                    ├─ payment (or authorisation) succeeds ─► provisioning ─► active
                    └─ none within unpaid_registration_expiry_days ─► closed ─► purged
```

**Fully active** means:

- `tenants.status = active`, so provisioning has completed
- the owner's email is verified. This is always true, because verification happens before the tenant exists.
- the subscription is `trialing` or `active`, or `past_due` within the grace period (§6.5)

The architecture deliberately does **not** create a tenant database before the email is verified, or before a required first payment succeeds. Unverified or unpaid sign-ups therefore cost one landlord row, not a database, which protects the database servers from sign-up abuse.

The requested intermediate states "plan selected" and "payment pending" are not separate statuses. The plan price is part of the registration request itself, and "payment pending" is `awaiting_payment`.

### 9.2 Legal Documents and Acceptance

Legal acceptance is recorded server-side, per document version. A checkbox in the frontend is only the input.

```
legal_documents  [DB: landlord]  audited
id
document_type             enum(terms_of_service, privacy_policy, data_processing_agreement, acceptable_use_policy,
                               affiliate_agreement)
                          affiliate_agreement is accepted by affiliates at application (§21A.2), never by tenants
version                   string            e.g. "2026-09-01"
title                     string
body                      text              rich content
status                    enum(draft, published, retired)  default draft
published_at              datetime nullable
effective_at              datetime nullable  defaults to published_at
required_at_registration  bool     default false
requires_reacceptance     bool     default false  existing tenant owners must accept this version (see below)
unique(document_type, version)
```

- A published document is **immutable**: `body`, `version` and `document_type` cannot change. An edit is a new draft with a new version.
- The **current version** of a type is the latest `published` row whose `effective_at` has passed. Publishing a new version automatically sets the previous current version to `retired`.
- Registration is refused with 503 `registration_unavailable` while any type that the platform marks `required_at_registration` has no current version. The platform cannot accidentally launch without published terms.

```
legal_acceptances  [DB: landlord]  immutable (never updated or deleted, except as noted)
id
legal_document_id        fk -> legal_documents
tenant_registration_id   fk -> tenant_registrations  nullable
tenant_id                string   nullable  fk -> tenants.id; set when the registration converts, or for in-app acceptance
affiliate_id             fk -> affiliates  nullable  set for affiliate agreement acceptances (§21A.2)
accepted_by_user_id      int      nullable  tenant users.id; snapshot, no foreign key (§6.4)
accepted_by_name         string
accepted_by_email        string
context                  enum(registration, reacceptance, affiliate_application)
ip_address               string(45) nullable
user_agent               string(512) nullable
accepted_at              datetime
created_at               datetime
index(tenant_id), index(affiliate_id), index(legal_document_id)
```

- **At registration**, the request carries `accepted_legal_document_ids`. It MUST contain exactly the current version of every type with `required_at_registration = true`. A stale version returns 422 `legal_version_outdated` with the current versions in `details`, so the client can show them again. One acceptance row is written per document, with the request IP and user agent.
- **Re-acceptance.** When the current version of a type has `requires_reacceptance = true`, `GET /api/admin/auth/me` returns it in `pending_legal_documents` for users holding the `owner` role, until the owner accepts it through `POST /api/admin/legal-acceptances`. Publishing such a version sends `tenant.legal_reacceptance_required` to every tenant owner. v1 records and surfaces pending acceptance. It does not block API access: whether to block is a contractual decision for the platform, and blocking can be added in the middleware without a schema change.
- **Retention.** Acceptance rows are kept for as long as the landlord keeps the tenant row, including after purge (§6.7), because they are the platform's contract records. Rows of registrations that expire without converting are deleted with the registration (§9.3), because no contract was formed.
- **Storefront customers** accepting a *tenant's* terms at checkout are not recorded in v1 (Appendix C). Tenant policies are published as CMS pages (§24).

The landlord website's legal pages render the current version through a `legal_document` page section (§24.2), so legal text is never duplicated between CMS content and `legal_documents`.

### 9.3 Registration Flow

**Step 1: register.** `POST /api/register` on a landlord domain, with:

- `business_name` (string, required)
- `owner_name` (string, required)
- `email` (required). It must not belong to a tenant that is not `closed` or `purged`, or to a registration that is still `pending_verification`. One email owns at most one live store in v1 (Assumption A-72).
- `password` (required, confirmed, Laravel's default password rules)
- `country_id` (required; a World country)
- `default_currency` (optional; ISO 4217; defaults to the country's currency from World data)
- `plan_price_id` (required; an active price of an active, public plan)
- `accepted_legal_document_ids` (required; §9.2)
- `coupon_code` (optional; a platform subscription coupon, validated by `PlatformCouponService::validateForRegistration()`, [§14.8](#148-platform-subscription-coupons)). An invalid code returns 422 with the coupon rejection `reason`; the client may resubmit without it.
- `referral_token` (optional; the value of the affiliate cookie, [§21A.4](#21a4-attribution)) and `ref` (optional; the referral code from `/register?ref=CODE`). Neither ever fails registration: an invalid or expired value is ignored and logged.

Registration is refused with 503 `registration_unavailable` while `platform_settings.tenant_registration_enabled` is false ([§9.9](#99-onboarding-switches)). `TenantRegistrationService::register()` validates the input and generates a slug. It resolves affiliate attribution with `AffiliateAttributionService::resolveForRegistration()` and stores the result on the registration. It then writes the `tenant_registrations` row and its legal acceptances in one transaction, and sends `tenant.registration_verification` to the email address. The notification carries a 6-digit code and a signed verification link with the same token. The response is HTTP 202 `{registration_id, status: "pending_verification", expires_at}`.

```
tenant_registrations  [DB: landlord]
id
public_id                 uuid     unique   used in URLs and responses; never the numeric id
business_name             string
slug                      string            reserved slug; re-checked for uniqueness at conversion
owner_name                string
email                     string   index
password_hash             encrypted nullable  a bcrypt hash, additionally encrypted at rest; cleared after provisioning
country_id                int
default_currency          char(3)
plan_price_id             fk -> plan_prices
platform_coupon_id        fk -> platform_coupons  nullable  validated at step 1, reserved at step 2 (§14.8)
affiliate_click_id        fk -> affiliate_clicks  nullable  the winning attribution touch (§21A.4)
affiliate_source          string   nullable  link | registration_code | coupon: which touch won (a coupon touch uses platform_coupon_id)
verification_token_hash   char(64)          sha256 of the code; the plaintext is only in the notification
verification_expires_at   datetime          created_at + platform_settings.registration_verification_hours
verification_attempts     int      default 0  5 wrong codes invalidate the token; the user requests a new one
status                    enum(pending_verification, converted, expired)
verified_at               datetime nullable
tenant_id                 string   nullable  fk -> tenants.id; set at conversion
ip_address                string(45) nullable
user_agent                string(512) nullable
index(status, verification_expires_at)
```

The plaintext password is never stored or queued. The hash is held encrypted in `tenant_registrations` only until provisioning creates the owner, and is then set to null.

**Step 2: verify.** `POST /api/register/verify` with `{registration_id, code}` (or the link's token). The code is compared in constant time. On success, `TenantRegistrationService::verify()` does the following in one transaction:

1. sets `status = converted` and `verified_at`
2. creates the `tenants` row (`name`, `owner_name`, `email`, `country_id`, `default_currency`, `slug`) and the default subdomain `domains` row
3. sets `tenant_id` on the registration's legal acceptances
4. when the registration carries an affiliate attribution, creates the tenant's `affiliate_referrals` row through `AffiliateAttributionService::attachToTenant()` ([§21A.4](#21a4-attribution)). This is the moment attribution stops depending on the browser.
5. creates the initial subscription through `SubscriptionService::createInitialSubscription()` (§14.7), which resolves the trial (§11.6) and reserves the platform coupon, if any (§14.8):
   - an eligible trial (resolved trial days > 0) on a price with `trial_requires_payment_method = false`: `trialing`, `trial_ends_at = now() + resolved trial days`, and `tenants.trial_consumed_at = now()`
   - a price with `amount = 0`, or a first-cycle total of 0 after a coupon: `active`
   - otherwise: `incomplete`
6. sets `tenants.status` to `provisioning` when the subscription is `trialing` or `active`, and dispatches `ProvisionTenantDatabase` after commit. Otherwise it sets `awaiting_payment`.

The response is HTTP 200 `{tenant_id, domain, tenant_status, next_action}`, where `next_action` is `none` or `payment`. For `payment`, it also carries `checkout_url`, from `SubscriptionService::subscribeTenantToPlan()`. For a trial that requires a payment method, the checkout authorises the method, and the first charge is dated at trial end (§11.6).

**Step 3: payment** (only when `awaiting_payment`). The owner completes the gateway checkout. A new checkout URL can be requested with `POST /api/register/{registration}/checkout`. The billing webhook (§15.6) reaches `SubscriptionService::handleSuccessfulCharge()`, which activates the subscription (or starts the trial, for an authorisation) and, because the tenant is `awaiting_payment`, sets `tenants.status = provisioning` and dispatches `ProvisionTenantDatabase`.

**Step 4: provisioning** (§9.4). The signup UI polls `GET /api/register/{registration}/status` until the tenant is `active`. The owner then logs in on the tenant domain as a staff user ([§10](#10-authentication-and-identity)).

**Housekeeping** (daily landlord maintenance, §72.2):

- Registrations past `verification_expires_at` become `expired`. Expired and converted registrations are deleted 30 days later, with the unconverted ones' legal acceptances.
- Tenants still `awaiting_payment` after `platform_settings.unpaid_registration_expiry_days` (default 7) are closed with `status_reason = registration_unpaid` and `purge_after = now()`. They have no database, so purge only removes landlord traces that are not financial records (§6.7).

**Abuse controls.** Every registration route uses the `auth-sensitive` limiter. `POST /api/register/resend` is limited to one request per 60 seconds per registration, and a resend issues a fresh code and invalidates the previous one.

### 9.4 Provisioning Job

`ProvisionTenantDatabase` runs on the `landlord-default` queue. Its payload is the tenant ID and the registration ID. It carries no secrets. While `platform_settings.tenant_provisioning_enabled` is false, the job does no work: it dispatches a fresh copy of itself with a 10-minute delay and exits, and the tenant stays `provisioning` ([§9.9](#99-onboarding-switches)). Re-dispatching (rather than `release()`) means holding never consumes the job's single try.

1. Place the tenant on a database server (§6.6), then create the tenant database (stancl `CreateDatabase`).
2. Run all tenant migrations (stancl `MigrateDatabase`).
3. Enter the tenant context and run `TenantDefaultsSyncService::sync()` ([§12.6](#126-permission-and-default-data-sync)), which seeds the defaults in §9.5.
4. Seed the `tenant_settings` values that differ from their documented defaults ([§13.4](#134-tenant-business-settings)): `store_name = tenants.name`, `store_contact_email = tenants.email`, `default_currency = tenants.default_currency` and `timezone` (the country's primary timezone from World data). Every other key uses its documented default and needs no row. Also seed the base `tenant_currencies` row (`is_base = true`, [§48.1](#481-tables)), even when `multi_currency` is not enabled, and the default warehouse ("Main", code `MAIN`, `country_id = tenants.country_id`).
5. Create the owner staff user: name = `owner_name`, email = the registration email, password = the registration's hash, `email_verified_at = tenant_registrations.verified_at`, role `owner` ([§12.3](#123-tenant-roles-and-permissions)). Then set `tenant_registrations.password_hash = null`.
6. Leave the tenant context, and call `ModuleActivationService::syncAutoModules()` ([§11.12](#1112-services)), which enables the plan's `auto` modules and runs their `seedDefaults()`.
7. Set `tenants.status = active` and `provisioned_at = now()`. Fire the `TenantProvisioned` event. Its listener dispatches `SendTenantWelcomeNotification`, which sends `tenant.provisioning_complete`.

**Failure handling.** If any step throws, the job's `failed()` handler sets `tenants.status = provisioning_failed` and records the exception in `failed_jobs`. The subscription is left as it is. A trial's clock is extended by the time spent in `provisioning_failed` when a retry succeeds. Retrying is an operational task (`tenants:retry-provisioning`, §77.6). A retry API is deferred ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)). Every step MUST be idempotent, so a retry is safe. Step 5 checks for an existing owner by email, and the registration's hash is cleared only after the owner exists.

### 9.5 Default Tenant Data

Only data that genuinely belongs to every tenant is seeded at provisioning. Module-specific defaults are seeded by the module's `seedDefaults()` the first time the module is enabled (§11.4). Everything below is inserted by `TenantDefaultsSyncService` (§9.4 step 3), except the warehouse, base currency and settings rows, which §9.4 step 4 inserts once. All of it is additive: a later sync never overwrites a tenant's changes.

| Seeded | Values | Why every tenant needs it | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Canonical permissions | Every permission in `config/permissions/tenant.php` | Roles reference them | §12.4 |
| Roles | `owner`, `admin`, `manager`, `staff`, `accountant`, `sales`, `warehouse`, `hr` | Usable team setup on day one | §12.3 |
| Notification templates and channel rows | Every tenant notification key | Notifications work without setup | §17.4 |
| System account categories and system accounts | Seven categories; the system accounts | Postings reference them by `system_key`, and the accounting and expenses modules can be enabled at any time (Assumption A-42) | §57.2 |
| Unit of measure | "Piece" (`pc`) | Every product needs a unit | §29.1 |
| Customer group | "Standard" (default) | Every customer belongs to a group | §26.3 |
| Warehouse | "Main" (`MAIN`) | Checkout needs a fulfilment warehouse | §32.2 |
| Invoice template | One A4 template, numbering from 1 | Every order can be invoiced | §43.1 |
| Base currency | `tenant_currencies` row for the base currency | Price resolution reads it | §48.1 |
| Storefront content | Draft policy pages (`privacy_policy`, `terms`, `refund_policy`, `shipping_policy`, `cookie_policy`) with empty bodies, a `home` page, and empty `header` and `footer` menus | The storefront can render its structure immediately. The tenant writes its own policies, because the platform must not supply legal text on its behalf. | §24.6 |
| Settings | Only the values in §9.4 step 4. All other keys use documented defaults. | Avoids stale copies of defaults | §13.4, §13.5 |

**Not seeded:**

- **Order, payment and shipment statuses, and payment methods.** These are PHP backed enums in code (§5.5), not rows.
- **Tax rates, shipping zones and payment gateway credentials.** They are specific to each tenant's jurisdiction and contracts, so the onboarding checklist (§9.6) prompts for them.
- **Demo products or customers.**
- **Module defaults for modules that are not enabled.** For example, AI assistant intents are seeded when `ai_assistant` is first enabled.
- **Document layouts** (receipts, packing slips). These are Blade templates in code (§43).

### 9.6 Onboarding Checklist

`OnboardingService::checklist()` (Tenant) computes the owner's setup progress from existing data. There is no checklist table:

| Step | Complete when |
|---|---|
| `store_details` | `store_logo_media_id` and `store_contact_phone` are set |
| `payment_gateway` | At least one active `live` `tenant_payment_settings` row exists and `tenant_settings.payment_mode = live` (§15.4, §15.9) |
| `shipping` | At least one active shipping method exists, or every active product is digital or a service |
| `tax` | At least one active tax rate exists, or `tenant_settings.tax_setup_confirmed` is true (the owner confirms that no tax applies) |
| `first_product` | At least one active product exists |
| `policies` | The `privacy_policy`, `terms` and `refund_policy` pages are published |
| `custom_domain` (optional) | A verified custom domain exists |

`tenant_settings.onboarding_dismissed` hides the checklist in the admin frontend. It changes nothing else.

### 9.7 Services

`TenantRegistrationService` (Landlord):

- `register(array $data, Request $request): TenantRegistration`: step 1 of §9.3
- `resendVerification(TenantRegistration $registration): void`
- `verify(TenantRegistration $registration, string $code): array`: step 2 of §9.3
- `createCheckout(TenantRegistration $registration, string $gateway): array`: step 3 of §9.3
- `expireStaleRegistrations(): void` and `closeUnpaidTenants(): void`: housekeeping, called by daily landlord maintenance
- `provision(Tenant $tenant, TenantRegistration $registration): void`: the steps in §9.4, called by `ProvisionTenantDatabase`

`LegalDocumentService` (Landlord):

- `createDraft(array $data): LegalDocument`, `updateDraft(LegalDocument $document, array $data): LegalDocument`
- `publish(LegalDocument $document): void`: retires the previous current version of the type
- `current(string $type): ?LegalDocument`, `currentRequiredForRegistration(): Collection`
- `recordAcceptances(array $documentIds, array $subject, string $context, Request $request): void`
- `pendingForTenant(Tenant $tenant): Collection`: current versions with `requires_reacceptance` that the tenant's owner has not accepted

`OnboardingService` (Tenant): `checklist(): array`.

### 9.8 Routes

**Landlord public** (group `landlord.public`, every route with the `auth-sensitive` limiter):

| Method | URI | Action (`Landlord\Tenancy\...` unless stated) |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/register` | `RegistrationController@store` |
| POST | `/api/register/verify` | `RegistrationController@verify` |
| POST | `/api/register/resend` | `RegistrationController@resend`: body `registration_id` |
| GET | `/api/register/{registration}/status` | `RegistrationController@status`: registration status, tenant status and domain only. `{registration}` binds `public_id`. |
| POST | `/api/register/{registration}/checkout` | `RegistrationController@checkout`: body `gateway`. Only while the tenant is `awaiting_payment`. |
| GET | `/api/legal-documents/current` | `Landlord\Legal\LegalDocumentController@current`: the current version of every type, with `required_at_registration` |
| GET | `/api/legal-documents/{type}` | `Landlord\Legal\LegalDocumentController@show`: the current version of one type |

**Landlord admin** (group `landlord.admin`):

| Method | URI | Action (`Landlord\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/tenant-registrations` | `Tenancy\Admin\TenantRegistrationController@index`: filters `status`, `email` |
| GET | `/api/admin/legal-documents` | `Legal\Admin\LegalDocumentController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/legal-documents` | `Legal\Admin\LegalDocumentController@store`: creates a draft |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/legal-documents/{document}` | `Legal\Admin\LegalDocumentController@update`: drafts only |
| POST | `/api/admin/legal-documents/{document}/publish` | `Legal\Admin\LegalDocumentController@publish` |
| GET | `/api/admin/legal-documents/{document}/acceptances` | `Legal\Admin\LegalAcceptanceController@index` |

**Tenant** (group `tenant.admin`, always available):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\...`) | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/onboarding` | `Tenancy\Admin\OnboardingController@show` | none (any staff user) |
| POST | `/api/admin/legal-acceptances` | `Legal\Admin\LegalAcceptanceController@store`: body `legal_document_id`; calls `LegalDocumentService` under §6.4 | derived (`legal-acceptances.create`, seeded only to `owner`) |

### 9.9 Onboarding Switches

"Disabling tenant support" is two platform settings, because stopping new sign-ups and stopping the creation of databases are different operational needs. **Neither setting ever disables, suspends or restricts an existing tenant.** Suspending a tenant is a per-tenant action (§6.5, §7.4), and platform-wide downtime is `maintenance_mode` (§18.4).

| Setting ([§13.2](#132-platform-settings)) | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `tenant_registration_enabled` | true | Accept new sign-ups. Switched off to stop marketing-driven growth, during abuse, or before launch. |
| `tenant_provisioning_enabled` | true | Create tenant databases. Switched off during a database-server incident or migration, so new tenants wait instead of failing. |

Behaviour when a setting is **false**:

| Flow | `tenant_registration_enabled = false` | `tenant_provisioning_enabled = false` |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/register` | 503 `registration_unavailable` | Accepted |
| Verifying a registration already `pending_verification` | Allowed: the owner was accepted before the switch. `POST /api/register/resend` also works. | Allowed; the tenant is created and waits in `provisioning` |
| First payment of an `awaiting_payment` tenant | Allowed | Allowed; the tenant moves to `provisioning` and waits |
| `ProvisionTenantDatabase` | Runs | Held (§9.4); resumes when the setting returns to true |
| Existing tenants: login, admin, storefront, checkout, webhooks | Unaffected | Unaffected |
| Staff invitations and staff creation inside a tenant (§25) | Unaffected | Unaffected |
| Subscription renewals, plan changes, billing routes | Unaffected | Unaffected |
| Affiliate clicks | Still recorded; the landing page shows that sign-up is paused | Unaffected |
| `GET /api/platform/config` | Returns `tenant_registration_enabled`, so the landlord website hides the sign-up form | Returns nothing new |

Both changes are audited (`PlatformSetting` is audited, §19.2), and switching either off sends `platform.onboarding_paused` to super-admins, so a forgotten switch is noticed.

# Part 3: Identity and Access

## 10. Authentication and Identity

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (platform users, affiliates) and Tenant (staff, customers, sellers, drivers) |
| **Feature key** | none. Seller authentication requires `marketplace`. Driver authentication is part of core commerce (shipping). Affiliate authentication requires `platform_settings.affiliate_program_enabled` for new applications only (§21A.1). |
| **Code module** | `Auth` |
| **Depends on** | §6, §8 |

### 10.1 Actors

There are exactly six authenticating actor types. Each has its own table, guard, token owner type, login routes and password-reset broker. A token issued to one actor type MUST NOT be accepted on another actor type's routes.

| Actor | Table | Database | Guard | Credentials | Auth route prefix | Roles/permissions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform user | `platform_users` | Landlord | `platform` | email + password | `/api/admin/auth/*` (landlord domain) | spatie, guard `platform` (§12.2) |
| Affiliate | `affiliates` | Landlord | `affiliate` | email + password | `/api/affiliate/auth/*` (landlord domain) | none; access to own records only (§21A) |
| Staff user | `users` | Tenant | `staff` | email + password | `/api/admin/auth/*` (tenant domain) | spatie, guard `staff` (§12.3) |
| Customer | `customers` | Tenant | `customer` | email + password | `/api/auth/*` | none; access to own records only |
| Seller | `sellers` | Tenant | `seller` | email + password | `/api/seller/auth/*` | none; access to own records only |
| Driver | `drivers` | Tenant | `driver` | phone + PIN (OTP for first login and PIN reset) | `/api/driver/auth/*` | none; access to own deliveries only |

The following never authenticate in v1:

- guests, who are identified by `X-Guest-Token` ([§38.2](#382-guest-carts-and-merge))
- HR employees without a linked staff user, and job candidates ([§58](#58-human-resources))
- sales agents ([§52](#52-sales-agents))
- suppliers and billers

There is **no landlord-side identity for tenant owners.** A tenant owner is the first staff user of their tenant ([§9.4](#94-provisioning-job)). They manage billing through tenant-domain routes that call landlord services ([§14.6](#146-routes)).

The same person MAY hold separate accounts in different actor tables (for example a staff user who also shops as a customer). The accounts are independent. Email uniqueness is enforced per table. An affiliate who also owns a tenant has two unrelated accounts, and can never earn commission on their own tenant (§21A.7).

### 10.2 Sanctum Configuration

- Laravel Sanctum **personal access tokens** (stateless bearer tokens) for every actor. The landlord `personal_access_tokens` table serves platform users and affiliates. Each tenant's `personal_access_tokens` table serves that tenant's four actor types. Both are distinguished by `tokenable_type`.
- When a token is issued, it receives exactly one ability equal to the actor type (`platform`, `affiliate`, `staff`, `customer`, `seller` or `driver`).
- The `auth.as:{actor}` middleware ([§71](#71-middleware-reference)) authenticates the bearer token and rejects it with HTTP 401 unless both the token's ability and its `tokenable_type` match `{actor}`.
- The `auth.as.optional:customer` middleware resolves a customer when a valid customer token is present and continues as a guest otherwise. It is used on cart and checkout routes.
- Token lifetime: `config('sanctum.expiration')`, set per environment. Refreshing issues a new token and revokes the current one.

### 10.3 Authentication Services

`AuthService` (Landlord; platform users):

- `login(string $email, string $password): array`: token plus platform user
- `logout(PlatformUser $user): void`: revokes the current token
- `verifyEmail(string $id, string $hash): void`
- `resendVerificationEmail(PlatformUser $user): void`
- `forgotPassword(string $email): void`
- `resetPassword(string $token, string $email, string $newPassword): void`
- `updatePreferences(PlatformUser $user, array $preferences): PlatformUser`: display preferences only (§5.10)

`AffiliateAuthService` (Landlord; affiliates, [§21A](#21a-affiliate-marketing)):

- `apply(array $data, Request $request): Affiliate`: wraps `AffiliateService::apply()`. The affiliate starts `pending` and must verify its email. Refused with 503 `affiliate_program_unavailable` while `affiliate_program_enabled` is false.
- `login(string $email, string $password): array`: token plus affiliate. Allowed for `pending`, `approved` and `suspended` affiliates, so they can see their status and history; `rejected` and `closed` affiliates are refused.
- `logout(Affiliate $affiliate): void`
- `verifyEmail(string $id, string $hash): void`, `resendVerificationEmail(Affiliate $affiliate): void`
- `forgotPassword(string $email): void`, `resetPassword(string $token, string $email, string $newPassword): void`
- `changePassword(Affiliate $affiliate, string $current, string $new): void`

`AuthService` (Tenant; staff users):

- `login(string $email, string $password): array`: token plus user plus effective permissions. Rejects deactivated users.
- `logout(User $user): void`
- `refreshToken(User $user): array`
- `forgotPassword(string $email): void`
- `resetPassword(string $token, string $email, string $newPassword): void`
- `changePassword(User $user, string $current, string $new): void`
- `updatePreferences(User $user, array $preferences): User`: display preferences only (§5.10)

`CustomerAuthService` (Tenant):

- `register(array $data, ?string $guestToken = null): array`: delegates creation to `CustomerService::registerCustomer()`. Merges the guest cart when `$guestToken` is present ([§38.2](#382-guest-carts-and-merge)). Sends `customer.welcome`.
- `login(string $email, string $password, ?string $guestToken = null): array`: token plus customer. Merges the guest cart when `$guestToken` is present.
- `logout(Customer $customer): void`
- `verifyEmail(string $id, string $hash): void`
- `resendVerificationEmail(Customer $customer): void`
- `forgotPassword(string $email): void`: sends `customer.password_reset`
- `resetPassword(string $token, string $email, string $newPassword): void`
- `changePassword(Customer $customer, string $current, string $new): void`

`SellerAuthService` (Tenant; requires `marketplace`):

- `register(array $data): Seller`: wraps `SellerService::registerSeller()` and creates the seller's credentials. The seller starts with `status = pending`.
- `login(string $email, string $password): array`: rejects sellers that are not `approved`
- `logout(Seller $seller): void`
- `forgotPassword(string $email): void`
- `resetPassword(string $token, string $email, string $newPassword): void`
- `changePassword(Seller $seller, string $current, string $new): void`

`DriverAuthService` (Tenant; core commerce):

- `requestOtp(string $phone): void`: sends a one-time code by SMS ([§16.3](#163-sms)) for first login or PIN reset
- `verifyOtpAndSetPin(string $phone, string $otp, string $newPin): Driver`: sets `drivers.pin_hash` and `phone_verified_at`
- `login(string $phone, string $pin): array`: token plus driver. Rejects inactive drivers.
- `logout(Driver $driver): void`

A driver who is also a staff user (`drivers.user_id` set) authenticates separately as a driver for the delivery app, and as staff for admin routes. The two identities are independent.

### 10.4 Password Reset Brokers

| Broker | Table | Database |
|---|---|---|
| `platform_users` | `platform_user_password_reset_tokens` | Landlord |
| `affiliates` | `affiliate_password_reset_tokens` | Landlord |
| `users` | `password_reset_tokens` | Tenant |
| `customers` | `customer_password_reset_tokens` | Tenant |
| `sellers` | `seller_password_reset_tokens` | Tenant |

Each table has the Laravel standard columns `email` (primary key), `token` and `created_at`. Drivers reset their PIN through OTP instead of a broker.

## 11. Modules, Plans, Features and Usage Limits

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (registry, plans, entitlements, overrides, activation records, services). Tenant (enforcement middleware, module self-service, usage view). |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `Plans` (plans, prices, limits, overrides, the module registry, activation and access resolution). One code module owns every rule of this section, so entitlement, activation and state are never split across modules. |
| **Depends on** | §6, §7 |

This section is the single owner of what a module is, which modules exist, how they are sold, how a tenant turns them on and off, and what happens to their data when they stop being available.

### 11.1 Concept Separation

**Plans control commercial access. Modules control technical capability.** A plan never *is* a module. A plan *entitles* a tenant to modules, and the tenant then *activates* the modules it wants.

| Concept | Question it answers | Stored in | Owned by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Module (feature key)** | Which capabilities exist in the product, and what do they depend on? | `config/modules.php`, the code registry ([§11.4](#114-module-registry)) | Engineering. It changes only with a release. |
| **Plan** | Which commercial package is the tenant paying for? | `plans`, `plan_prices` ([§11.6](#116-plans-and-prices)) | Platform (landlord) |
| **Entitlement** | Is the tenant *allowed* to use module X? | `plan_features` (default) and `tenant_features` (override), [§11.7](#117-plan-features-overrides-and-activation) | Platform |
| **Activation** | Has the tenant *turned on* module X? | `tenant_modules` ([§11.7](#117-plan-features-overrides-and-activation)) | Tenant owner, within its entitlements |
| **Module state** | What can happen in module X right now? | Computed from entitlement, activation and requirements ([§11.5](#115-module-lifecycle-and-disabled-behaviour)) | Computed by `FeatureAccessService` |
| **Limit** | How much may the tenant use? | `plan_limits` (default) and `tenant_limit_overrides` (override), [§11.8](#118-limit-registry) | Platform |
| **Tenant override** | Does this tenant have a negotiated or temporary exception? | `tenant_features`, `tenant_limit_overrides` | Platform |
| **Setting** | How does the tenant want an entitled, enabled module to behave? | Settings tiers ([§13](#13-settings)) | Platform or tenant, by tier |
| **Permission** | May this staff user perform this action? | spatie tables in the relevant database ([§12](#12-roles-and-permissions)) | Tenant (staff roles) or platform (platform roles) |

A request to a tenant admin route is checked in this order:

1. tenant status
2. authentication
3. **module state** (`feature:{key}`)
4. module notice
5. **limit** (create actions only)
6. **permission**

See the full stack in [§70.3](#703-route-group-map). A permission can never grant access to a module the tenant cannot use. A setting can never switch on a module the tenant is not entitled to.

### 11.2 What a Module Is

A **module** is a reasonably independent business capability that meets **all** of these criteria:

1. It has its own domain concepts: its own tables, or at least its own records and lifecycle.
2. It has its own services, routes and permission group (the first URI segment after `/api/admin/` in its route tables, [§12.4](#124-permission-naming-and-derivation)).
3. It can be switched off for a tenant without breaking core commerce, because every call into it from elsewhere is an integration hook ([§2](#2-architecture-principles) Principle 7).
4. Its dependencies on other modules are declared in the registry, and are acyclic.
5. It can be commercially gated: selling it separately makes sense to a customer.
6. It can evolve and be released without changing another module's contract.

Something that fails any criterion is **not** a module. It is one of the following:

| Kind | Meaning | Feature key | Can be disabled? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core platform capability** | Infrastructure every tenant needs to operate at all (identity, access, settings, notifications, audit, media, exports, custom fields, content, billing views) | none | No |
| **Core commerce domain** | Commerce every store needs (catalogue, inventory, customers, cart, checkout, orders, payments, tax, shipping, promotions, returns, documents) | none | No. Differentiated only by limits. |
| **Module** | Meets all six criteria | own key | Yes, by the tenant, when entitled |
| **Submodule** | A module whose key requires a parent module. It lives in the parent's section and code module, but is entitled and activated separately, because it is sold or depended on separately. | own key, requires parent | Yes |
| **Vertical module** | A module serving one industry | own key | Yes |
| **Integration** | A module whose purpose is to exchange data with, or deliver through, an external system under the tenant's own account | own key | Yes |
| **Capability** | A plan-gated extension of a core domain or of the platform. It has records and routes, but no independent business domain. It uses the same lifecycle as a module and is activated automatically when entitled. | own key | Yes |
| **Feature inside a module** | Behaviour that belongs to a module and is never sold separately (for example seller payouts inside the marketplace) | none; gated by its module | With its module |
| **Setting** | A configuration choice inside an entitled, enabled module or core domain | none | n/a |
| **Plan limit** | A numeric ceiling on a core domain or module ([§11.8](#118-limit-registry)) | none | n/a |

Reports, notifications, permissions, tax, discounts, customers, SEO and invoices are **not** modules. They are used by nearly every other part of the system, so switching them off would break core commerce.

`config/modules.php` registers **tenant** modules only: the unit of entitlement and activation is a tenant. Landlord platform modules (affiliate marketing) are enabled by platform settings, have no tenant state, and are never entitled, activated or sold.

### 11.4 Module Registry

`config/modules.php` is the authoritative registry, and this table is its specification. Keys are lowercase `snake_case`, and a key is also the module key used by module notices ([§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode)). The registry is code, not data: routes, middleware, jobs and permissions reference these keys, so a key can only be added or removed with a release. Plans, overrides and activation rows reference keys, and are validated against the registry.

Columns:

- **Class**: from §11.2.
- **Requires**: hard dependencies. A module is `enabled` only while every required module is `enabled`.
- **Activation**: `auto` modules become enabled as soon as they are entitled. `manual` modules become `available`, and the tenant owner enables them.
- **Read when inactive**: whether admin `GET` routes stay open in the `disabled` and `locked` states ([§11.5](#115-module-lifecycle-and-disabled-behaviour)).

| Key | Module | Class | Section | Code module | Requires | Activation | Read when inactive |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pos` | Point of sale | Module | §51 | `Pos` | none | manual | yes |
| `purchasing` | Suppliers and purchasing | Module | §49 | `Purchasing` | none | manual | yes |
| `accounting` | Accounting (general ledger) | Module | §57 | `Accounting` | none | manual | yes |
| `expenses` | Expenses, income and billers | Module | §57.4 | `Expenses` | none | auto | yes |

`core` is a reserved key. It is not entitled, activated or sold. It exists only as the module key for module notices on core routes ([§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode)).

**Registry entry shape.** Each entry in `config/modules.php` declares `name`, `class` (the module class above, not a PHP class), `code_module` (the folder under `app/Modules`, [§73.5](#735-module-wiring)), `requires`, `activation`, `read_when_inactive`, `permission_groups` (the URI resource prefixes its permissions derive from, used by `RoleService::listPermissions()`), `custom_field_entities` ([§23](#23-custom-fields)), and optionally `lifecycle`, a class implementing `App\Contracts\ModuleLifecycle`:

- `seedDefaults(): void`: idempotent default data, run in the tenant context the first time the module is enabled, and by the defaults sync for tenants where it is enabled ([§12.6](#126-permission-and-default-data-sync))
- `disableBlockers(): array`: reasons the tenant may not disable the module right now (for example active customer subscriptions). An empty array allows it.
- `onEnabled(): void` and `onDisabled(): void`: optional side effects, for example restarting or stopping an integration sync chain

**Dependency map.** "Requires" is a hard dependency. "Hooks into" is a soft dependency: the call is skipped when the target is not `enabled`. Core commerce is omitted from "Requires", because it is always present.

| Module | Requires | Hooks into (soft) | Called by (soft) | When it is not `enabled`, this stops | This keeps working |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pos` | none | `gift_cards`, `reward_points`, `sales_agents`, `multi_currency`, `accounting` | `restaurant` (hard) | Register sessions, POS quotes and sales, terminal charges. `restaurant` stops too. | POS orders stay in order history, returns and reports |
| `purchasing` | none | `accounting`, `multi_currency`, `approval_workflows` | `expenses` (supplier as payee), `manufacturing` | New suppliers, purchase orders and quotations | Stock already received; supplier records readable |
| `accounting` | none | none | orders, payments, returns, `gift_cards`, `purchasing`, `expenses`, `marketplace`, `pos`, `hr_payroll` | New postings: outbox rows are not written, so the ledger has a gap for the inactive period (§57.1) | Every business flow. Journals and reports stay readable. |
| `expenses` | none | `accounting`, `approval_workflows`, `purchasing` | `ai_assistant` | New expenses and income entries | Existing entries readable. Accounting postings already made stay posted. |
| `hr` | none | `approval_workflows` (leave) | `booking` (staff), dashboard | Employees, attendance, leave. `hr_payroll` and `hr_recruitment` stop too. | Staff users and authentication, which never depend on HR (§58.1) |
| `hr_payroll` | `hr` | `accounting` | none | New payroll runs and salary changes | Finalized runs, payslips and history readable |
| `hr_recruitment` | `hr` | none | none | Public careers routes and new postings | Applications readable |
| `marketplace` | none | `accounting`, `approval_workflows` | catalogue (`seller_id`), promotions (seller-funded), product questions | Seller self-service writes, seller registration, seller products in the storefront and checkout | Seller balances and payouts in wind-down (§11.5) |
| `gift_cards` | none | `accounting` | cart, checkout, POS, refunds | Selling and issuing cards | Redemption of existing cards, and balance checks (a customer liability) |

| `reward_points` | none | none | checkout, POS, customers | Earning, redeeming and expiring points | Balances, which are retained unchanged |
| `sales_quotations` | none | `sales_agents`, `multi_currency` | none | Quotation requests and quotations | Orders already converted from quotations |
| `sales_agents` | none | none | checkout, POS, quotations | Crediting new commissions | Marking earned commissions paid (wind-down) |
| `product_subscriptions` | none | none | payments | New subscriptions | Renewals of existing subscriptions (wind-down) |

| `support` | none | none | none | Conversations and live chat | Conversation history readable |

### 11.5 Module Lifecycle and Disabled Behaviour

**Entitlement** (platform-controlled). A tenant is *entitled* to a module when, after applying overrides that are currently in force (`starts_at` passed, `expires_at` not passed):

- a `tenant_features` row with `effect = grant` exists, **or** the current subscription's plan has a `plan_features` row for the key,
- **and** no `tenant_features` row with `effect = revoke` exists.

A `tenant_features` row with `effect = suspend` makes the module `suspended`, whatever the entitlement.

**Activation** (tenant-controlled). A `tenant_modules` row records the tenant's choice: `enabled` or `disabled`. `auto` modules get an `enabled` row as soon as they are entitled (`ModuleActivationService::syncAutoModules()`, [§11.12](#1112-services)).

**States.** `FeatureAccessService::state()` computes exactly one state per tenant and module:

| State | Condition | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unavailable` | Not entitled, and no `tenant_modules` row | The tenant has never had the module. Nothing to show. |
| `available` | Entitled, no `tenant_modules` row (manual modules only) | The tenant may enable it |
| `enabled` | Entitled, row `enabled`, and every required module `enabled` | Fully usable |
| `disabled` | Entitled, and either the row is `disabled` or a required module is not `enabled` | Turned off by the tenant, or blocked by a requirement. Read-only. |
| `locked` | Not entitled, and a `tenant_modules` row exists | The tenant used it, then lost the entitlement (downgrade, cancellation, an expired or revoked override). Read-only until the entitlement returns. |
| `suspended` | An active `suspend` override | Blocked by the platform (for example abuse or a legal hold). No access, no processing. Data untouched. |

**Transitions.**

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `unavailable` | `available` (manual) or `enabled` (auto) | Entitlement gained: plan change applied, or a grant override takes effect |
| `available` or `disabled` | `enabled` | Tenant owner: `POST /api/admin/modules/{key}/enable`. Rejected with 422 `module_requirements_not_enabled` if a required module is not `enabled`. |
| `enabled` | `disabled` | Tenant owner: `POST /api/admin/modules/{key}/disable`. Rejected with 422 `module_has_dependents` while an enabled module requires it, and with 422 `module_disable_blocked` while `ModuleLifecycle::disableBlockers()` returns reasons. |
| `enabled`, `disabled` or `available` | `locked` (had a row) or `unavailable` (no row) | Entitlement lost |
| `locked` | `enabled` or `disabled` (its previous choice) | Entitlement regained. The activation row was never deleted, so the previous choice returns automatically. |
| any | `suspended` | A platform user adds a `suspend` override |
| `suspended` | the computed state | The `suspend` override is removed or expires |

Core commerce and core platform capabilities have no state. They are always usable, subject to tenant status and subscription access ([§6.5](#65-tenant-status-and-access)).

**What each state allows.** No state ever deletes data.

| Aspect | `enabled` | `disabled` and `locked` | `suspended` | `unavailable` and `available` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admin `GET` routes (`tenant.admin`) | Yes | Yes, when the registry says "read when inactive". Otherwise 403. | 403 `module_suspended` | 403 |
| Admin writes | Yes | 403 `module_disabled` or `module_locked`, except the wind-down operations below | 403 `module_suspended` | 403 |
| Storefront, customer, seller and driver routes | Yes | No, except the wind-down operations below | No | No |
| Integration hooks into the module | Run | No-op | No-op | No-op |
| Queued jobs and daily maintenance tasks of the module | Run | Skipped, except wind-down jobs | Skipped | n/a |
| Permissions | Assignable and effective | Kept on roles. Listed, so roles stay editable. Only the read permissions have an effect. | Kept, no effect | Not listed |
| Custom fields on the module's entities ([§23.4](#234-module-gating)) | Active | Values readable. Definitions cannot be created or changed. | Hidden | Definitions cannot be created |
| Exports of the module's data ([§19.4](#194-asynchronous-exports)) | Yes | Yes, when "read when inactive" | No | n/a |
| Module notices | Apply | Apply | n/a | n/a |

Error codes are defined in [§70.8](#708-errors): 403 `feature_unavailable` (not entitled), `module_disabled` (entitled but `available` or `disabled`), `module_locked` and `module_suspended`. Each carries `details.state` and, for `locked`, `details.entitled_by_plans` (the public plans that include the module), so the frontend can offer an upgrade.

**Wind-down.** When a module stops being `enabled`, obligations already made to third parties (customers, sellers, employees, suppliers) are still honoured, but nothing new is created. The operations below remain allowed in the `disabled` and `locked` states, never in `suspended`. Routes that perform them carry `feature:{key},wind-down` instead of `feature:{key}`. This table is the only list of wind-down operations.

| Module | Wind-down operations (routes and jobs) |
|---|---|
| `gift_cards` | Applying an existing card at checkout and POS (`CartGiftCardController@store` and `@destroy`, and gift-card payment in `SaleController@store`), `GiftCardBalanceController@show`, refunds to a card, and `ExpireGiftCards` |
| `installments` | `InstallmentController@pay`, `ChargeDueInstallments` and `MarkOverdueInstallments` for existing plans |
| `product_subscriptions` | Renewals of existing subscriptions (`ProcessProductSubscriptionRenewals`), and the customer's `pause`, `resume` and `destroy` routes |
| `marketplace` | Seller login and logout, every seller `GET` route, `SellerPayoutController@store` and `@markPaid` for balances already earned, and seller ledger reversals caused by refunds of past orders |
| `pos` | `SessionController@close` for open sessions, and `SaleController@store` for offline sales whose client-recorded sale time precedes the moment the module stopped being enabled (§51.6) |
| `restaurant` | `TableOrderController@settle` and `@void` for open table orders |
| `purchasing` | `PurchaseOrderController@receive` for purchase orders already sent, `SupplierPaymentController@store` against existing purchase orders, and purchase returns of goods already received |
| `hr_payroll` | `PayrollRunController@markPaid` and `PayrollItemController@markPaid` for runs already finalized |
| `sales_agents` | `SalesAgentCommissionController@markPaid` for commissions already earned |
| `booking` | `BookingController@cancel` (admin and customer) and `BookingController@complete` for existing bookings |
| `repair` | `RepairJobController@updateStatus` on existing jobs |
| `manufacturing` | `WorkOrderController@complete` and `@cancel` for work orders already started |
| `approval_workflows` | `ApprovalController@approve` and `@reject` for pending requests |
| `accounting` | `PostAccountingEntry` for outbox rows recorded before the module stopped being enabled |

**Rules that follow from the states:**

- When `marketplace` is not `enabled`, products with a `seller_id` are excluded from the storefront catalogue, carts and checkout, because a sale could not be credited to the seller. They stay in the admin catalogue.
- When `multi_currency` is not `enabled`, the storefront offers the base currency only. `product_prices` and exchange rates are kept.
- When `reward_points` is not `enabled`, points are neither earned, redeemed nor expired. Balances are kept and apply again on re-enable.
- When `accounting` is re-enabled after a gap, events from the gap are not posted retroactively (Assumption A-41). `GET /api/admin/modules` reports the gap (`inactive_periods`, derived from `tenant_modules` timestamps and the audit trail), so the accountant can post adjustments.
- `product_subscriptions` cannot be disabled by the tenant while any customer subscription is `active` or `paused`. The tenant cancels them first, and each customer is notified. On `locked` (entitlement lost), existing subscriptions keep renewing under wind-down, because the tenant has a commitment to its customers.
- `pos` cannot be disabled while a register session is open. `marketplace` cannot be disabled while any seller has an unpaid balance. `hr_payroll` cannot be disabled while a run is `finalized` but unpaid. These are the modules' `disableBlockers()`.

### 11.6 Plans and Prices

A plan is one commercial tier. Its prices, one per currency and billing interval, are child rows. There are never separate plans such as "Basic Monthly" and "Basic Yearly": features and limits belong to the plan and are shared by all of its prices.

```
plans  [DB: landlord]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Basic"
slug                 string            unique; e.g. "basic"
description          text    nullable
tagline              string  nullable  short marketing line for the pricing page
is_active            bool              default true   false = no new subscriptions; existing ones continue
is_public            bool              default true   false = a private plan, assigned only by a platform user
is_recommended       bool              default false  the platform's own editorial choice; at most one active public plan
marketing_badge      string  nullable  free text chosen by the platform, e.g. "Best for growing teams"
sort_order           int               default 0
```

- `is_recommended` and `marketing_badge` are editorial. They are set by a platform user, never computed, and never phrased as a statistic. The API never claims a plan is "most popular" unless a platform user types that badge. `PlanService` enforces at most one recommended active public plan.

```
plan_prices  [DB: landlord]
id
plan_id                        fk -> plans
currency_code                  char(3)
billing_interval               enum(monthly, yearly)
amount                         money             fixed price, deliberately set per currency (no live FX conversion)
trial_days                     int     nullable  null = use the platform default (platform_settings.default_trial_days);
                                                 0 = no trial on this price; > 0 = this price's own trial length
trial_requires_payment_method  bool              default false
is_active                      bool              default true
gateway_references             json    nullable  provider-side plan identifiers created by PaymentGatewayInterface::createPlan(),
                                                 keyed by payment mode then provider (§15.9), e.g.
                                                 {"live": {"paystack": "PLN_x", "stripe": "price_x"}, "test": {"stripe": "price_y"}}
index(plan_id, currency_code, billing_interval, is_active)
```

- **At most one active price** per plan, currency and interval. `PlanService` enforces this.
- **Prices are immutable once used.** `amount`, `currency_code` and `billing_interval` cannot change once any subscription references the row. To change a price, a platform user creates a new price and deactivates the old one. Existing subscriptions keep their price (grandfathering) until a platform user moves them, or until the tenant changes plan. `trial_days`, `trial_requires_payment_method` and `is_active` stay editable.
- **Trials belong to the price**, not to the plan, the registration code or the tenant. Any plan and interval can have any trial length. The platform setting supplies only a default for prices that do not set their own (see trial resolution below). There is exactly one resolved value per subscription, and it is snapshotted.
- **Annual savings are computed, never stored or typed.** For a plan with both intervals active in the same currency, `PlanService::annualSavingsPercent()` returns `floor((monthly × 12 − yearly) ÷ (monthly × 12) × 100)`. The result is rounded **down**, so the displayed saving is never overstated. The public plan API returns it next to the yearly price. A plan with no monthly price in that currency shows no saving.

**Price resolution.** `PlanService::getPriceForTenant()`:

1. Use the active `plan_prices` row matching the requested currency and interval.
2. If none exists, use the active USD row for that interval.
3. If there is no USD row either, the plan is not purchasable in that interval, and the service returns a 422.

**Trial resolution** (decides UD-34). `PlanService::resolveTrialDays(PlanPrice $price): int` is the only place a trial length is computed. Precedence, first match wins:

1. `platform_settings.trials_enabled` is false: **0** for every price. This is the global kill switch, for example during a fraud wave.
2. `plan_prices.trial_days` is not null: that value (0 means this price never has a trial, whatever the platform default says).
3. Otherwise: `platform_settings.default_trial_days` (default 7).

The resolved value is written to `subscriptions.trial_days` and turned into `subscriptions.trial_ends_at` when the subscription is created. **Changing either platform setting or a price's `trial_days` affects only subscriptions created afterwards.** A running trial changes only through `SubscriptionService::extendTrial()` (§14.3), which is audited. Both platform settings and `plan_prices` are audited (§19.2).

**Trial eligibility.** A new subscription starts `trialing` only when all of these hold:

1. the resolved trial days are greater than 0
2. it is the tenant's first subscription
3. no other tenant with the same owner email (compared lower-cased) has `trial_consumed_at` set

When a trial starts, `tenants.trial_consumed_at` is set. A platform user may extend a running trial (§14.6). A plan change during a trial ends the trial and charges the new price, unless the new price also resolves to a trial greater than 0, in which case the trial keeps its original end date. A trial never generates affiliate commission; only the first paid charge after it can (§21A.5).

When `trial_requires_payment_method` is true, registration collects a payment method before provisioning (§9.3): the gateway driver creates the provider subscription with its first charge dated at `trial_ends_at`. When it is false (the seeded default), no payment details are collected, and the owner pays through the billing routes before the trial ends (§14.3).

### 11.7 Plan Features, Overrides and Activation

```
plan_features  [DB: landlord]
id
plan_id              fk -> plans
feature_key          string            a key from §11.4
unique(plan_id, feature_key)
```

```
tenant_features  [DB: landlord]
id
tenant_id            string            fk -> tenants.id
feature_key          string            a key from §11.4
effect               enum(grant, revoke, suspend)
starts_at            datetime nullable  null = in force immediately
expires_at           datetime nullable  null = until removed; a temporary grant or suspension sets it
reason               string   nullable  shown to platform users; also shown to the tenant for suspend
extra_amount         money    nullable  add-on price per billing cycle for a billed grant (§14.5)
extra_currency_code  char(3)  nullable  required when extra_amount is set; must equal the subscription currency
billed               bool              default true; meaningful only when extra_amount is set
overridden_by        fk -> platform_users  nullable
unique(tenant_id, feature_key)
```

- A **grant** entitles the tenant to a module its plan lacks: a negotiated add-on (billed), a goodwill extra (`billed = false`) or a time-boxed trial of a module (`expires_at`).
- A **revoke** removes a module the plan includes, for example by contract.
- A **suspend** blocks the module entirely while keeping its data (§11.5).
- Plan features are **not** copied into `tenant_features`. Entitlement falls back to `plan_features` at read time, so plan edits reach every tenant on the plan.

```
tenant_modules  [DB: landlord]
id
tenant_id            string            fk -> tenants.id
module_key           string            a key from §11.4
status               enum(enabled, disabled)
enabled_at           datetime nullable  last time it became enabled
disabled_at          datetime nullable  last time it became disabled
changed_by_user_id   int      nullable  tenant users.id; snapshot, no foreign key (§6.4)
changed_by_email     string   nullable  snapshot
unique(tenant_id, module_key)
```

- The activation record lives in the landlord database, next to the entitlement it is resolved with, so one cached lookup yields the state. It is written only through `ModuleActivationService` (listed in §6.4).
- A row is never deleted while the tenant exists. Its existence is what distinguishes `locked` (the tenant has data to protect) from `unavailable`.
- Every change is written to the landlord activity log with the acting user snapshot.

### 11.8 Limit Registry

```
plan_limits  [DB: landlord]
id
plan_id              fk -> plans
limit_key            string            a key from the registry below
limit_value          int     nullable  see "Values" below
unique(plan_id, limit_key)
```

```
tenant_limit_overrides  [DB: landlord]
id
tenant_id            string            fk -> tenants.id
limit_key            string
limit_value          int     nullable  replaces the plan value; same value rules
extra_amount         money   nullable  negotiated add-on price per billing cycle (§14.5)
extra_currency_code  char(3) nullable  required when extra_amount is set; must equal the subscription currency
billed               bool              default true; false = goodwill override with no charge
is_active            bool              default true
expires_at           datetime nullable  null = until removed; a temporary raise sets it
reason               string  nullable
overridden_by        fk -> platform_users  nullable
unique(tenant_id, limit_key)
```

**Values.** These meanings are fixed and apply to plans and overrides alike:

| Stored value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `null` | **Unlimited.** Used only where the registry below allows it. |
| `0` | **None allowed.** The action is blocked from the first attempt. |
| a positive integer | **The maximum.** An action is allowed while `current < limit`. |
| no row | **A configuration error.** It is treated as `0` (fail closed) and logged as an error. `PlanService` creates a row for every registry key when a plan is created, and a plan cannot be activated while any row is missing. |

**Registry.** `config/limits.php` holds these keys. Limit kinds: `count` is a live row count (§11.10), `storage` is a sum, and `rate` is a per-minute throttle.

| Limit key | Kind | What is counted | Enforced on | Unlimited allowed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_users` | count | Active staff `users` ("staff accounts") | Staff user create and reactivate | yes |
| `max_products` | count | `products` rows that are not soft-deleted | Product create (admin and seller) | yes |
| `max_warehouses` | count | Active `warehouses` ("locations") | Warehouse create | yes |
| `max_orders_per_month` | count | `orders` created in the current calendar month, in the tenant timezone, excluding test orders (§40.8) | Order create (all order sources) | yes |
| `max_storage_mb` | storage | Sum of `media.size` in the tenant database, in MB | Every media upload | no |
| `max_pos_registers` | count | Active `pos_registers` | POS register create | yes |
| `max_custom_domains` | count | Landlord `domains` rows of the tenant with `type = custom` | Custom domain create (§7.5) | no |
| `max_custom_fields` | count | Active `custom_field_definitions` | Custom field create and reactivate (§23) | no |
| `max_employees` | count | Active `hr_employees` | Employee create and reactivate (§58) | yes |
| `max_sellers` | count | `sellers` with `status = approved` | Seller approval (§50.2) | yes |
| `max_api_requests_per_minute` | rate | Requests per minute across all of the tenant's clients | The `tenant` rate limiter (§70.5) | no |

**Deliberately not limited:**

- **Customers.** Shoppers register themselves. Blocking registration would make a tenant lose sales because it is succeeding. Customer volume is already priced through orders and storage.
- **Product variants.** They are bounded by `max_products`, plus a technical validation cap of 100 variants per product (§28.2).
- **Suppliers, invoices and quotations.** These are low-volume records with no cost driver. Invoices are renderings of orders, which are already limited.

`platform_settings.max_pos_registers_per_warehouse` is a separate operational ceiling, not a billing limit ([§13.2](#132-platform-settings)).

### 11.9 Access Resolution

`FeatureAccessService::state(Tenant $tenant, string $key): ModuleState` applies §11.5 in this order:

1. The key is `core`: `enabled`.
2. An in-force `suspend` override: `suspended`.
3. Compute entitlement from in-force overrides and the current subscription's plan (§11.5). While a plan change is scheduled but not yet applied, the old plan remains in effect (§14.2).
4. Read the `tenant_modules` row.
5. Derive the own state from the §11.5 table.
6. If the own state is `enabled`, check every required module recursively. If any is not `enabled`, the state is `disabled`, with `details.reason = requirement_not_enabled`.

The effective states of every key for a tenant are computed together and cached (§74). The cache entry expires no later than the earliest future `starts_at` or `expires_at` among the tenant's overrides, so time-boxed overrides take effect on time without a scheduled job.

**The `feature:{key}` middleware** ([§71](#71-middleware-reference)):

- `enabled`: passes.
- `disabled` or `locked`: passes `GET` and `HEAD` requests on the `tenant.admin` group when the registry says "read when inactive". Passes routes declared `feature:{key},wind-down`. Otherwise it returns 403 `module_disabled` or `module_locked`.
- `suspended`: 403 `module_suspended` on every route, including wind-down routes.
- `unavailable`: 403 `feature_unavailable`. `available`: 403 `module_disabled`.

**Integration hooks and jobs** call `FeatureAccessService::tenantCanAccess($tenant, $key)`, which is true only in the `enabled` state. A job for a module exits without work unless the module is `enabled`, or the job is listed as a wind-down job in §11.5.

### 11.10 Usage Tracking

- **v1: live counts.** When a limit is checked, the enforcing code counts the actual rows in the tenant database at the moment of the action. No extra table is needed, and the count is always accurate.
- **Deferred: cached counters.** A `tenant_usage` table (landlord: `tenant_id`, `metric_key`, `current_value`) would be introduced only once live counting becomes a measured performance problem ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)).
- The `usage.limit:{key}` middleware obtains the current count through a registered counter per limit key (`UsageCounterRegistry`), then calls `PlanLimitService::isWithinLimit()`. When the limit is reached, it returns HTTP 403 in the standard envelope (§70.8): `{"success": false, "message": "Upgrade your plan...", "data": null, "meta": {"error_code": "limit_reached", "details": {"limit": "<key>", "used": n, "limit_value": m}}, "errors": {}}`.
- When usage reaches 80% of a limit (Assumption A-8), `subscription.plan_limit_approaching` is dispatched, once per limit per billing cycle. When a create is blocked, `subscription.plan_limit_reached` is dispatched.
- `rate` limits are enforced by the rate limiter, not by this middleware. `storage` limits are checked by the upload validation of every media collection.

### 11.11 Plan Changes, Cancellation and Expiry

No commercial event deletes tenant data. Every case below changes only what the tenant may do next.

| Event | Modules | Limits | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Upgrade** (applied at once or at renewal, per `proration_mode`, §14.4) | Newly entitled `auto` modules become `enabled`. `manual` modules become `available`. `locked` modules return to their previous choice. | New values apply when the change applies | Unchanged |
| **Downgrade** (always at the next renewal, §14.4) | Modules the new plan lacks become `locked` (read-only, wind-down) | New values apply at renewal. Usage above a new limit is kept: existing products, users, warehouses, registers, domains, fields, employees and sellers stay active and usable. Only creating or reactivating more is blocked until usage is below the limit. | Unchanged |
| **Cancellation** | Unchanged until `ends_at` | Unchanged until `ends_at` | After `ends_at`, access is `blocked` (§6.5) except billing, exports and authentication. The tenant may be closed and later purged under §6.7, with notice. |
| **Trial or plan expiry without payment** (`past_due` beyond the grace period) | Unchanged | Unchanged | Access is restricted by `platform_settings.past_due_restriction` (§6.5). Nothing is deleted. |
| **Resubscription** | States recompute. Activation rows were kept, so the tenant's previous choices return. | New plan values | Unchanged |
| **Tenant disables a module** | `disabled` (read-only, wind-down) | Unchanged | Kept, and fully restored on re-enable |
| **Override expires** | Recomputed at expiry (§11.9) | The plan value applies again. Usage above it is kept, as for a downgrade. | Unchanged |

**Impact preview.** Before scheduling a downgrade, `SubscriptionService::previewPlanChange()` returns the modules that would become `locked` and every limit the current usage would exceed. `POST /api/admin/billing/subscription/swap-plan` requires `confirm_impact = true` when the preview is not empty, and the tenant owner receives `subscription.plan_downgraded` with the same list.

### 11.12 Services

`ModuleRegistry` (context-free, in `Plans`; reads `config/modules.php`; the only class that reads it):

- `all(): array`, `get(string $key): ModuleDefinition`
- `requires(string $key): array` (transitive) and `dependents(string $key): array` (modules that require it)
- `isWindDownRoute(string $key, string $routeName): bool`
- `customFieldEntities(string $key): array`

`PlanService` (Landlord):

- `createPlan(array $data): Plan`: also creates a `plan_limits` row for every registry key, with the registry default
- `updatePlan(Plan $plan, array $data): Plan`: enforces the single recommended plan
- `deactivatePlan(Plan $plan): void`
- `addPrice(Plan $plan, string $currency, string $interval, float $amount, ?int $trialDays = null, bool $trialRequiresPaymentMethod = false): PlanPrice`: deactivates any other active price for the same currency and interval, calls `createPlan()` on each enabled platform gateway in each mode that has credentials (§15.10), and stores `gateway_references` keyed by mode. A gateway configured later receives its plans lazily on the first checkout that uses it.
- `resolveTrialDays(PlanPrice $price): int`: §11.6 trial resolution
- `updatePrice(PlanPrice $price, array $data): PlanPrice`: `trial_days`, `trial_requires_payment_method` and `is_active` only
- `attachFeatureToPlan(Plan $plan, string $featureKey): void` and `detachFeatureFromPlan(Plan $plan, string $featureKey): void`: validate the key against the registry
- `setPlanLimit(Plan $plan, string $limitKey, ?int $value): PlanLimit`: rejects `null` for a key that does not allow unlimited
- `getPriceForTenant(Plan $plan, Tenant $tenant, string $interval): PlanPrice`: resolution order in §11.6
- `annualSavingsPercent(Plan $plan, string $currency): ?int`: §11.6
- `listPublicPlans(?string $currency = null): Collection`: active public plans with active prices, each price's **resolved** trial days (§11.6), computed savings, features grouped by class, and limits

`FeatureAccessService` (Landlord):

- `state(Tenant $tenant, string $key): ModuleState` and `states(Tenant $tenant): array`: §11.9
- `tenantCanAccess(Tenant $tenant, string $key): bool`: true only when `enabled`
- `canRead(Tenant $tenant, string $key): bool`: `enabled`, or `disabled`/`locked` with "read when inactive"
- `isEntitled(Tenant $tenant, string $key): bool`
- `setOverride(Tenant $tenant, string $key, string $effect, array $options, ?PlatformUser $by = null): TenantFeature`: `$options` holds `starts_at`, `expires_at`, `reason`, `extra_amount`, `extra_currency_code` and `billed`. A grant also calls `ModuleActivationService::syncAutoModules()`.
- `removeOverride(Tenant $tenant, string $key): void`: deletes the row, so entitlement falls back to the plan
- `listEffectiveModules(Tenant $tenant): array`: every registry key with `{state, entitled, source: override|plan|none, activation, requires, dependents, missing_requirements, inactive_periods}`

`ModuleActivationService` (Landlord; called from the tenant context under §6.4):

- `enable(Tenant $tenant, string $key, User $actor): void`: requires entitlement and enabled requirements; writes the row; the first time, runs the module's `seedDefaults()` in the tenant context; calls `onEnabled()`
- `disable(Tenant $tenant, string $key, User $actor): void`: rejects when dependents are enabled or `disableBlockers()` returns reasons; writes the row; calls `onDisabled()`
- `syncAutoModules(Tenant $tenant): void`: inserts `enabled` rows for entitled `auto` modules that have no row. It runs at provisioning, when a plan change applies, and when a grant override is created.

`PlanLimitService` (Landlord):

- `getLimit(Tenant $tenant, string $limitKey): ?int`: an active, unexpired override first, then the plan value. `null` means unlimited. A missing plan row returns `0` and logs an error.
- `isWithinLimit(Tenant $tenant, string $limitKey, int $currentCount): bool`: returns `true` when unlimited, or when `currentCount < limit`
- `setLimitOverride(Tenant $tenant, string $limitKey, ?int $value, array $options = [], ?PlatformUser $by = null): TenantLimitOverride`: `$options` holds `extra_amount`, `extra_currency_code`, `billed`, `expires_at` and `reason`
- `removeLimitOverride(Tenant $tenant, string $limitKey): void`
- `getUsageSummary(Tenant $tenant): array`: `{"max_products": {"used": 42, "limit": 50}, ...}`. The "used" counts are gathered in the tenant context. Unlimited limits return `"limit": null`.

### 11.14 Initial Commercial Plans

`PlanCatalogueSeeder` ([§7.6](#76-landlord-seed-data)) creates the three plans below. Prices, trials, features and limits are **data**. No code branches on a plan name, a slug or an amount. A platform user edits them through §11.13.

**Plans.** All three are active and public. None is marked `is_recommended`, and none has a `marketing_badge`: those are for the platform to set once it has a reason.

| Slug | Name | Tagline | Sort order |
|---|---|---|---|
| `basic` | Basic | Sell online | 1 |
| `standard` | Standard | Run the whole store | 2 |
| `premium` | Premium | Scale across teams and channels | 3 |

**Prices** (`plan_prices`):

| Plan price | Currency | Interval | Amount | Trial days | Trial requires payment method |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic monthly | USD | monthly | 20.00 | null (platform default, seeded 7) | no |
| Basic yearly | USD | yearly | 200.00 | null (platform default, seeded 7) | no |
| Standard monthly | USD | monthly | 39.00 | 0 | no |
| Standard yearly | USD | yearly | 380.00 | 0 | no |
| Premium monthly | USD | monthly | 59.00 | 0 | no |
| Premium yearly | USD | yearly | 600.00 | 0 | no |

**Annual savings** (computed by `annualSavingsPercent()`, shown for transparency):

| Plan | 12 × monthly | Yearly | Saving | Exact | Displayed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | 240.00 | 200.00 | 40.00 | 16.67% | 16% |
| Standard | 468.00 | 380.00 | 88.00 | 18.80% | 18% |
| Premium | 708.00 | 600.00 | 108.00 | 15.25% | 15% |

The prices are kept exactly as requested. None of them is a 20% saving, so the product never displays a fixed "save 20%" label. It displays the computed value per plan. Round prices convert better than exact 20% prices ($192.00, $374.40 and $566.40) and are easier to quote. The one inconsistency, that Standard saves more than Premium, is a pricing choice for the platform owner. The mechanism handles any values.

**Features** (`plan_features`). Every plan includes the core platform and core commerce (§11.3), which have no feature keys. Each higher plan includes everything in the plan before it.

| Plan | Adds these feature keys | Packaging intent |
|---|---|---|
| Basic | `expenses`, `content_marketing` | A complete online store for one location, with simple bookkeeping and a blog |
| Standard | `pos`, `purchasing`, `accounting`, `multi_currency`, `gift_cards`, `reward_points`, `sales_quotations`, `back_in_stock_alerts`, `advanced_reporting`, `support`, `whatsapp`, `custom_email` | Online and in-store selling, procurement, real books, loyalty and customer service |
| Premium | `hr`, `hr_payroll`, `hr_recruitment`, `marketplace`, `installments`, `product_subscriptions`, `sales_agents`, `approval_workflows`, `project_management`, `ai_assistant`, `woocommerce`, `social_commerce`, `manufacturing`, `restaurant`, `booking`, `repair` | Teams, marketplaces, recurring revenue, integrations and every vertical |

Vertical modules and integrations are also sold as **billed add-ons** to Standard tenants through a `grant` override with `extra_amount` (§11.7, §14.5). Self-service purchase of add-ons is deferred (Appendix C).

**Limits** (`plan_limits`). `null` means unlimited, and it is seeded exactly once, for Premium order volume.

| Limit key | Basic | Standard | Premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_users` | 2 | 10 | 30 |
| `max_products` | 250 | 5,000 | 50,000 |
| `max_warehouses` | 1 | 3 | 10 |
| `max_orders_per_month` | 500 | 5,000 | `null` (unlimited: blocking checkout would stop a top-tier tenant trading) |
| `max_storage_mb` | 2,048 | 20,480 | 102,400 |
| `max_pos_registers` | 0 | 3 | 10 |
| `max_custom_domains` | 0 | 1 | 5 |
| `max_custom_fields` | 10 | 50 | 200 |
| `max_employees` | 0 | 0 | 100 |
| `max_sellers` | 0 | 0 | 100 |
| `max_api_requests_per_minute` | 600 | 1,500 | 3,000 |

A limit of `0` on a module the plan does not include is deliberate. When a platform user grants that module as an add-on, the override workflow also sets the matching limit override.

**Seed matrix** (features and limits belong to the plan, so both prices of a plan share them):

| Plan price | Price | Currency | Interval | Trial | Features | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic monthly | 20.00 | USD | monthly | 7 days | Basic row above | Basic column above |
| Basic yearly | 200.00 | USD | yearly | 7 days | Basic row above | Basic column above |
| Standard monthly | 39.00 | USD | monthly | none | Basic plus Standard rows | Standard column |
| Standard yearly | 380.00 | USD | yearly | none | Basic plus Standard rows | Standard column |
| Premium monthly | 59.00 | USD | monthly | none | All three rows | Premium column |
| Premium yearly | 600.00 | USD | yearly | none | All three rows | Premium column |
