## 12. Roles and Permissions

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (platform-user roles) and Tenant (staff roles) |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `Access` |
| **Depends on** | §10, §11 |

### 12.1 Two Separate Permission Systems

1. **Landlord permissions** control what platform users may do in the platform admin API. spatie/laravel-permission runs in the landlord database with guard `platform`.
2. **Tenant permissions** control what a tenant's staff users may do. spatie/laravel-permission runs inside **each tenant database** with guard `staff`. Its tables are isolated like every other tenant table.

Tenant access has two layers:

- **Layer 1: module access (features).** Does the module exist for this tenant at all ([§11](#11-modules-plans-features-and-usage-limits))? This is not a permission. It is checked first.
- **Layer 2: in-module permissions.** What may this staff user do inside a module the tenant already has? These are tenant-defined roles and permissions.

Customers, sellers and drivers have **no** roles or permissions. Their routes are restricted to their own records by policies ([§12.5](#125-policies-and-record-ownership)).

### 12.2 Landlord Roles

Default platform roles are seeded by the landlord `PlatformAccessSeeder` ([§7.6](#76-landlord-seed-data)):

| Role | Intended scope |
|---|---|
| `super-admin` | Every landlord permission. Cannot be deleted. Only this role holds the **sensitive platform permissions**: `payment-gateways.*` (credentials and the billing payment mode, §15.10), `platform-settings.update`, `platform-users.*` and publishing legal documents. |
| `support-staff` | Tenants (view), tenant registrations (view), platform support conversations, contact submissions, module notices, the operations dashboard section |
| `billing-admin` | Plans, prices, tenant module and limit overrides, subscriptions (including trial extension and refunds), payment transactions, platform coupons, affiliate payouts (generate and mark paid), and the revenue, subscription, payment and affiliate dashboard sections |
| `affiliate-manager` | Affiliates (review, approve, reject, suspend, rate overrides), referrals, commissions (approve, reject, reverse) and the affiliate dashboard section. It cannot mark payouts paid, so the person who approves commissions is not the person who releases money (§75 rule 23). |
| `content-editor` | Landlord website content (§24) and legal document drafts. Publishing a legal document stays with `super-admin`. |

`PlatformUserService` (Landlord):

- `createPlatformUser(array $data): PlatformUser`: sends `platform_user.invited`
- `updatePlatformUser(PlatformUser $user, array $data): PlatformUser`
- `deactivatePlatformUser(PlatformUser $user): void`
- `assignRole(PlatformUser $user, string $role): void`
- `revokeRole(PlatformUser $user, string $role): void`

```
platform_users  [DB: landlord]
id
name                 string
email                string            unique
password             string            hashed
email_verified_at    datetime nullable
is_active            bool              default true
preferences          json     nullable  display preferences {date_format, time_format} (§5.10)
last_login_at        datetime nullable
```

Landlord admin routes (group `landlord.admin`):

| Method | URI | Action (`Landlord\Access\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/platform-users` | `PlatformUserController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/platform-users` | `PlatformUserController@store` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/platform-users/{user}` | `PlatformUserController@update` |
| POST | `/api/admin/platform-users/{user}/deactivate` | `PlatformUserController@deactivate` |
| POST | `/api/admin/platform-users/{user}/roles` | `PlatformUserController@assignRole` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/platform-users/{user}/roles/{role}` | `PlatformUserController@revokeRole` |

### 12.3 Tenant Roles and Permissions

**Default tenant roles**, seeded at provisioning and kept current by the defaults sync (§12.6). Each role's starter set is defined as permission-name patterns in `config/permissions/tenant.php` (`roles` key), for example `accounting.*` or `products.view`, so the starter sets of newly provisioned tenants stay correct as the permission list grows, without a hand-maintained list.

| Role | Starter set | Protected |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | Every permission | Yes. Exactly one user holds it. It cannot be deleted, edited or assigned directly; it moves only by ownership transfer. |
| `admin` | Every permission except billing (`billing.*`), module activation (`modules.*`), ownership transfer and legal acceptance | Yes. It cannot be deleted or stripped of permissions. |
| `manager` | Day-to-day operations: catalogue, inventory, orders, returns, customers, promotions, CMS, reports | No |
| `staff` | Order processing, customers, catalogue view. Excludes money and stock-control permissions: refunds, manual payments, payouts, promotions and coupons, stock adjustments and journal entries (§75 rule 23). | No |
| `accountant` | Accounting, expenses, income, billers, payments (view), refunds (view), financial reports and exports | No |
| `sales` | Customers, orders, quotations, POS sales, gift card sale | No |
| `warehouse` | Inventory, stock movements, transfers, purchasing receipts, shipments and picking | No |
| `hr` | HR, payroll and recruitment | No |

- Starter sets include the permissions of modules the tenant cannot use yet. They have no effect until the module is `enabled`, because the feature check comes first, and they make a later upgrade work without role changes.
- Unprotected roles are starting points. After provisioning the tenant owns them: the sync never changes their permissions again, and the tenant may edit or delete them.
- **Ownership transfer.** `POST /api/admin/users/{user}/transfer-ownership` (owner only) moves the `owner` role to another active staff user, gives the previous owner `admin`, updates `tenants.owner_name` and `tenants.email` as the billing contact, and sends `staff.ownership_transferred` to both users. The owner cannot be deactivated or deleted without first transferring ownership.
- Tenants create and edit their own roles, and assign permissions to roles, through `RoleService`. Direct per-user permissions are allowed ([§25.2](#252-user-service)).
- The permission check applies only after the feature check.

`RoleService` (Tenant):

- `listRoles(): Collection`: includes permission counts
- `createRole(array $data): Role`
- `updateRole(Role $role, array $data): Role`
- `deleteRole(Role $role): void`: blocked for `owner` and `admin`, and for any role still assigned to a user
- `assignPermissionsToRole(Role $role, array $permissionNames): void`: sync; rejected for `owner` and `admin`
- `listPermissions(): Collection`: the canonical set, grouped by module. It includes every module whose state is `enabled`, `disabled` or `locked` (each group carries the state), so roles can be prepared before a module is re-enabled. `unavailable`, `available` and `suspended` modules are omitted.

Tenant admin routes (group `tenant.admin`, always available):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Access\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/roles` | `RoleController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/roles` | `RoleController@store` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/roles/{role}` | `RoleController@update` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/roles/{role}` | `RoleController@destroy` |
| PUT | `/api/admin/roles/{role}/permissions` | `RoleController@syncPermissions` |
| GET | `/api/admin/permissions` | `RoleController@permissions` |

### 12.4 Permission Naming and Derivation

Permission names are derived mechanically from the route tables in this document. Coding agents MUST NOT invent other names.

1. Take the route URI after `/api/admin/`.
2. Remove every `{parameter}` segment.
3. If the controller action is **not** one of `index`, `show`, `metrics`, `store`, `update` or `destroy`, the last remaining segment is the **ability**. Otherwise the ability is `view` (for `index`, `show` and `metrics`), `create` (for `store`), `update` (for `update`) or `delete` (for `destroy`). A `metrics` action ends in the segment `metrics`, which is dropped before the resource is formed: anyone who may list a resource may see its contextual KPIs ([§22.4](#224-contextual-kpis)).
4. The remaining segments, joined with `.`, form the **resource**.
5. Permission name = `{resource}.{ability}`.

Examples:

| Route | Action | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/admin/products` | `index` | `products.view` |
| `POST /api/admin/products/{product}/variants` | `store` | `products.variants.create` |
| `PATCH /api/admin/returns/{return}/approve` | `approve` | `returns.approve` |
| `POST /api/admin/hr/payroll-runs/{run}/finalize` | `finalize` | `hr.payroll-runs.finalize` |
| `POST /api/admin/pos/sessions/open` | `open` | `pos.sessions.open` |
| `GET /api/admin/tenants` (landlord) | `index` | `tenants.view` |
| `GET /api/admin/orders/metrics` | `metrics` | `orders.view` |
| `GET /api/admin/dashboard/{section}` | `show` | `dashboard.view`, plus the section's own data permission ([§22.3](#223-dashboard-sections-and-endpoints)) |

**Exceptions.** A route table row marked **"none"** in its Permission column requires authentication only. These are:

- self-service routes (own profile, own notification preferences, "My approvals", own attendance clock-in and clock-out)
- the platform support helpdesk for tenant staff
- `GET /api/admin/modules` and `GET /api/admin/onboarding`
- `/api/admin/auth/*`

**Canonical permission set.** `config/permissions/landlord.php` and `config/permissions/tenant.php` hold the canonical lists, grouped by feature key and generated from the route tables. They are the source of truth for `PermissionSyncService`.

The `permission:` middleware on each route uses the derived name. Route tables in this document show the Permission column only where it deviates from the rule, or where it is "none".

### 12.5 Policies and Record Ownership

- Customer routes MUST restrict every record to the authenticated customer. For guest-accessible routes, the record must match the guest token ([§39.6](#396-guest-order-access)).
- Seller routes MUST restrict records to the authenticated seller (`products.seller_id`, `order_items.seller_id`, own payouts).
- Affiliate routes MUST restrict records to the authenticated affiliate (own clicks, referrals, commissions and payouts). A referred tenant is shown to its affiliate only as a masked business name and a status, never as contact data (§21A.8).
- Driver routes MUST restrict records to the authenticated driver's `delivery_assignments`.
- Staff record visibility is further narrowed by `tenant_settings.staff_data_access_scope` ([§25.3](#253-staff-data-access-scope)).
- Policies live in each module's `Policies/` folder ([§73](#73-project-structure)).

### 12.6 Permission and Default Data Sync

**Problem.** When a release adds new permissions, notification templates, AI intents or system accounts, every existing tenant database needs the new rows without losing tenant customisations.

**Solution.** `TenantDefaultsSyncService` (Tenant context) is a versioned, **idempotent, additive-only** sync. Its single entry point, `sync(): void`, runs these steps in order:

1. `PermissionSyncService::syncPermissionsForTenant()`: inserts missing canonical permissions; creates any missing default role (§12.3) with its starter set; and ensures `owner` holds every permission and `admin` holds every permission of its pattern. It never deletes permissions and never alters the assignments of unprotected roles that already exist.
2. Notification template seeder: inserts missing template keys and channel rows ([§17.4](#174-default-templates-and-seeding)). It never overwrites customised templates.
3. System chart of accounts seeder: inserts missing system accounts ([§57.2](#572-account-categories-and-chart-of-accounts)).
4. Default unit, customer group, invoice template and storefront content seeders (§9.5): insert only if absent. The storefront content is inserted only at provisioning, never by a later sync, so a tenant that deleted it does not get it back. (The default warehouse and base currency are seeded by provisioning itself, §9.4 step 4, not by the sync.)
5. For every module that is currently `enabled`, the module's `seedDefaults()` (§11.4), which is additive in the same way. This is how new AI intents reach tenants with `ai_assistant` enabled ([§62](#62-ai-business-assistant)).

The sync runs:

- during provisioning ([§9.4](#94-provisioning-job) step 3)
- on each deployment, through the `SyncTenantDefaultsForAllTenants` job, which fans out one `SyncTenantDefaults` job per active tenant

After each sync, it updates `tenants.permissions_version` to the current value of `config('permissions.tenant.version')` (the `version` key of `config/permissions/tenant.php`, bumped by every release that changes any synced default). This lets operators find tenants that are still behind and re-run the sync selectively.

`PermissionSyncService`:

- `getCanonicalPermissionSet(): array`
- `syncPermissionsForTenant(Tenant $tenant): void`
- `syncPermissionsForAllTenants(): void`: dispatches the fan-out job

---

# Part 4: Platform Services and Shared Infrastructure

## 13. Settings

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (`platform_settings`, `tenant_platform_settings`) and Tenant (`tenant_settings`, `storefront_settings`, plus module settings tables) |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `Settings` |
| **Depends on** | §7, §8, §11 |

### 13.1 Four Settings Tiers

Settings follow the ceiling pattern (Principle 5). Each setting lives in exactly one of four places, chosen by **who needs to read or enforce it** and **who may see it**:

| Tier | Table | Database | Who reads it | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform settings (ceilings and the platform's own website identity) | `platform_settings` | Landlord | Landlord code; tenant code read-only; the landlord website through `GET /api/platform/config` (public keys only) | Platform users |
| Tenant platform-level settings | `tenant_platform_settings` | Landlord | Landlord code, and tenant code through `TenantPlatformSettingsService` | Platform users only |
| Tenant business settings | `tenant_settings` | Tenant | Tenant code only. Never exposed to the public. | Tenant staff (`settings.update`) |
| Tenant storefront settings | `storefront_settings` | Tenant | Tenant code, and the public storefront through `GET /api/storefront/config` | Tenant staff (`storefront-settings.update`) |

- Business and storefront settings are separate tables because every storefront key is public by definition, and business settings include secrets (for example `custom_mail_settings`). The public endpoint reads a table that cannot contain a secret, so no key filtering can go wrong.
- Usage limits (§11.8) are not settings. They come from the plan and its overrides.
- Module-specific configuration that needs structured rows (not key/value pairs) lives in module settings tables. See §13.6.

### 13.2 Platform Settings

Platform settings are the authoritative configuration of platform-wide behaviour. They are key/value rows, but every key is declared in one code registry, `config/platform_settings.php`, which gives each key its **group**, type, default, validation rules and whether it is **public**. `PlatformSettingsService` rejects any key not in the registry and validates every value against it, so the table can never hold an undocumented or malformed setting.

```
platform_settings  [DB: landlord]  audited
id
group                string            from the registry; used to read and edit settings a group at a time
key                  string            unique
value                text    nullable
type                 enum(string, bool, int, decimal, json)
index(group)
```

- **No secrets.** Nothing in this table is secret. Payment credentials live in `platform_payment_gateways` (encrypted, [§15.10](#1510-platform-gateway-configuration)); infrastructure secrets live in the environment.
- **Audited.** Every change records the old and new value and the platform user (§19.2). Changing `trials_enabled`, `tenant_registration_enabled`, `tenant_provisioning_enabled`, `affiliate_program_enabled`, `maintenance_mode` or any `custom_domain_*` key is additionally written to the landlord activity log with a required `reason`.
- **Effect is forward-only** wherever a value is snapshotted: trials (§11.6), affiliate commission rates (§21A.5) and coupon terms (§14.8) are copied onto the records they create, so a later change never rewrites history.
- **Groups that do not exist, on purpose.** *Security* (token lifetimes, rate limits, password rules) is code and environment configuration, because a runtime toggle must never be able to weaken security. *Storage* is the `max_storage_mb` plan limit (§11.8). *Notifications* are the template and channel matrix (§17). *Custom-domain records* are `domains` rows (§7.5).

The registry, by group. "Public" keys are returned by `GET /api/platform/config`.

**Not here, by design:** the announcement bar is a CMS banner of kind `announcement` (§24.5); policies are CMS pages with system keys (§24.2); navigation is CMS menus (§24.3); the home page layout is CMS page sections.

`GET /api/storefront/config` returns, in one cached response ([§74](#74-caching-strategy)):

- every `storefront_settings` key
- the public business identity: `store_name`, logo and favicon URLs, `store_contact_email`, `store_contact_phone`, `store_address`, `business_hours`
- formatting: `default_currency`, `default_currency_position`, `decimal_digits`, `locale`, `rtl_enabled`, `timezone`, and the effective `date_format` and `time_format` (§5.10)
- checkout switches: `guest_checkout_enabled` (effective value), `prices_include_tax`, and `payment_mode`, so the storefront can show a "test mode: no real payments" banner (§15.9)
- the active announcement banners and the `header` and `footer` menus (§24)
- the storefront-visible modules: which of `reward_points`, `gift_cards`, `multi_currency` (with the enabled currencies), `back_in_stock_alerts`, `installments`, `booking` and `content_marketing` are `enabled`, so the frontend can hide what the tenant does not use

### 13.7 Services

`PlatformSettingsService` (Landlord):

- `get(string $key, $default = null)`: the stored value, else the registry default
- `group(string $group): array`: every key of a group with its effective value
- `updateGroup(string $group, array $values, PlatformUser $by, ?string $reason = null): void`: validates every value against the registry, rejects keys of another group, keys changed only through their own routes (`billing_payment_mode`) and combinations that break an invariant (for example `custom_domains_enabled = true` with no routing target), writes the audit and activity entries, and busts the settings cache
- `isCommissionEnabled(): bool`
- `publicConfig(): array`: every key marked public, with media URLs

`TenantPlatformSettingsService` (Landlord):

- `get(Tenant $tenant, string $key, $default = null)`
- `set(Tenant $tenant, string $key, $value): void`
- `getEffectiveCommissionRate(Tenant $tenant): ?float`: returns null when `commission_enabled` is false, otherwise the override or `default_commission_rate`

`TenantSettingsService` (Tenant):

- `get(string $key, $default = null)`: applies the documented default and the platform ceilings (for example guest checkout)
- `set(string $key, $value): void`: validates the type, rejects keys that aren't registered, and rejects values that exceed a platform ceiling (for example `email_provider = custom` without `custom_email`)
- `all(): array`: every key, including the read-only `app_version` and the effective platform `commission_rate`
- `getMailConfig(): array`: the platform mailer, or the decrypted custom configuration (§16.2)

`StorefrontSettingsService` (Tenant):

- `get(string $key, $default = null)`, `set(string $key, $value): void`: validates each key's format (§13.5)
- `all(): array`
- `publicConfig(): array`: the `GET /api/storefront/config` response (§13.5)

All settings reads are cached per tenant and busted on write ([§74](#74-caching-strategy)). The storefront config cache is also busted when a banner, a menu, a module state or one of the business identity keys it includes changes.

|---|---|---|

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Settings\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/settings` | `Admin\TenantSettingsController@show` |

`commission_rate` is read-only in the tenant settings response. The tenant cannot write it. No landlord-only setting is ever returned by a tenant route, apart from the effective ceilings and defaults a tenant needs to configure itself (the effective guest checkout value, the platform default display formats).

### 13.9 Settings Precedence

Inheritance applies only where this table says so. **Entitlements, limits, permissions, billing terms and security rules are never settings and never inherit from one**: they come from plans, overrides and roles (§11, §12).

| Concern | Resolution (first match wins) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Display date and time format | user preference → tenant setting → platform default | Display only (§5.10). Customer-facing documents skip the user step. |
| Locale | tenant setting → platform default | No per-user locale in v1. |
| Business timezone | tenant setting (landlord: platform setting) | No inheritance at run time: the tenant value is seeded from the country at provisioning. |
| Store base currency | tenant setting | Seeded from registration. Independent of the billing currency (§14). |
| Trial length | platform `trials_enabled` switch → plan price `trial_days` → platform `default_trial_days` | Resolved once and snapshotted on the subscription (§11.6). |
| Guest checkout | platform ceiling AND tenant setting | Ceiling pattern: the tenant can only narrow. |
| Custom email provider | module entitlement (`custom_email`) AND tenant setting | A setting never grants a module. |
| Return window | tenant setting → platform default | |
| Platform commission rate | per-tenant override → platform default, only while `commission_enabled` | §13.3 |
| Affiliate commission rate | affiliate override → programme default | Snapshotted on each commission (§21A.5). |
| Payment mode | platform `billing_payment_mode` for platform billing; tenant `payment_mode` for tenant commerce | Two unrelated settings; neither inherits from the other (§15.9). |

---

## 14. Subscription Billing

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (records and services). Tenant domain (the tenant owner's billing routes). |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `Billing` |
| **Depends on** | §11, §13, §15 |

This section covers **tenants paying the platform**. Tenant storefront payments are covered in [§40](#40-order-payments). Customers subscribing to products are covered in [§55](#55-product-subscriptions).

### 14.1 Tables

```
subscriptions  [DB: landlord]
id
tenant_id                       string   fk -> tenants.id
plan_id                         fk -> plans
plan_price_id                   fk -> plan_prices
currency_code                   char(3)  billing currency (copied from plan_price)
billing_interval                enum(monthly, yearly)
gateway                         enum(flutterwave, paystack, stripe)  nullable while trialing/free
gateway_mode                    enum(test, live)  the platform billing_payment_mode when the subscription was created;
                                         never changes; every charge of this subscription uses this mode (§15.9)
gateway_plan_reference          string   nullable
gateway_subscription_reference  string   nullable  provider subscription id/code, used to cancel
authorization_reference         encrypted nullable  reusable payment authorization, when the platform charges renewals itself (§14.5)
status                          enum(incomplete, trialing, active, past_due, cancelled)
trial_days                      int      default 0  resolved trial length, snapshotted at creation (§11.6)
trial_ends_at                   datetime nullable
starts_at                       datetime
ends_at                         datetime nullable  set when cancelled (end of the paid period)
renews_at                       datetime nullable
scheduled_plan_id               fk -> plans  nullable  plan change waiting for next renewal (proration_mode = next_renewal)
scheduled_plan_price_id         fk -> plan_prices  nullable
cancelled_at                    datetime nullable
past_due_at                     datetime nullable  when the subscription last became past_due; the grace period
                                         (past_due_grace_days, §6.5) is measured from it; cleared on payment
index(tenant_id, status), index(status, renews_at)
```

**Governing subscription.** Plan entitlement (§11.9) and subscription access (§6.5) follow the latest subscription whose status is not `incomplete`, or the latest subscription when there is no other. A checkout started for a new plan therefore never displaces the plan the tenant already pays for until it succeeds.

A tenant has at most one subscription whose status is not `cancelled`. `SubscriptionService::getCurrentSubscription()` returns it.

```
payment_transactions  [DB: landlord]  audited
id
tenant_id              string   fk -> tenants.id
subscription_id        fk -> subscriptions
type                   enum(charge, authorization, refund, chargeback)  default charge
                                authorization = a payment-method check for a trial, never money collected (§11.6)
mode                   enum(test, live)  copied from subscriptions.gateway_mode; a webhook of the other mode never touches it
provider               enum(flutterwave, paystack, stripe)
reference              string   unique   our own reference, sent to the provider as idempotency key / merchant reference
provider_reference     string   nullable the provider's charge, refund or dispute id
amount                 money             positive for charges and authorizations; negative for refunds and chargebacks
currency_code          char(3)
status                 enum(pending, successful, failed)
                                refunds are separate rows; a charge is never re-labelled "refunded"
refund_of_payment_transaction_id  fk -> payment_transactions  nullable  set on refund and chargeback rows
is_first_paid_charge   bool     default false  true on the tenant's first successful live charge with amount > 0 (§21A.5)
line_items             json     nullable  charges: itemised lines (plan, module_addon, limit_override, coupon_discount, proration) (§14.5)
fee                    money    nullable  provider fee, when reported
failure_reason         string   nullable
reason                 string   nullable  refunds: why the platform refunded
refunded_by            fk -> platform_users  nullable
meta                   json     nullable  raw provider data used for reconciliation
paid_at                datetime nullable  when the row became successful
unique(mode, provider, provider_reference), index(tenant_id, type, status), index(paid_at)
```

- Only `successful` rows count as money moved. A refund or chargeback never edits the original charge; its effect is computed by summing the rows (the same ledger rule as tenant `order_payments`, §40.1).
- `is_first_paid_charge` is set inside `handleSuccessfulCharge()` under a lock on the tenant row, only when no earlier successful live `charge` with `amount > 0` exists for the tenant. It is the single definition of "first paid subscription payment" used by affiliates (§21A.5) and trial conversion metrics (§22.5), so the two can never disagree.
- Test-mode rows are kept for audit but excluded from every revenue metric (§22.5).

```
subscription_mrr_movements  [DB: landlord]  [no updated_at]
id
tenant_id              string   fk -> tenants.id
subscription_id        fk -> subscriptions
plan_id                fk -> plans, nullable   the subscription's plan after the movement (plan movement matrix, §22.6)
type                   enum(new, expansion, contraction, churn, reactivation)
currency_code          char(3)
mrr_before             money             normalised monthly recurring amount before the change
mrr_after              money
mrr_delta              money             mrr_after − mrr_before
reason                 string            first_payment, renewal, plan_change, reactivated, cancellation_effective, past_due_grace_expired
occurred_at            datetime
created_at             datetime
index(occurred_at), index(tenant_id, occurred_at), index(type, occurred_at)
```

This is the minimum history needed to report MRR movement correctly: current subscription rows show only the present. `SubscriptionService` writes one row whenever a live subscription's normalised recurring amount changes (§14.10). Rows are never updated.

### 14.2 Access Check Relationship

The feature and limit resolution in [§11](#11-modules-plans-features-and-usage-limits) always uses the plan of the **current subscription** (`subscriptions.plan_id`). While a plan change is scheduled but not yet applied, the old plan remains in effect.

### 14.3 Subscription Lifecycle

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | `incomplete`, `trialing` or `active` | Email verification, through `createInitialSubscription()` (§9.3), or `subscribeTenantToPlan()` after a cancellation |
| `incomplete` | `active` | First successful charge. A tenant in `awaiting_payment` then moves to `provisioning` (§9.3). |
| `incomplete` | `trialing` | Payment-method authorisation succeeds for a trial that requires one (§11.6) |
| `incomplete` | `cancelled` | The unpaid registration expires (§9.3) |
| `trialing` | `active` | First successful charge |
| `trialing` | `past_due` | Trial ended with no successful charge |
| `active` | `active` | Successful renewal (`renews_at` advances) |
| `active` | `past_due` | Failed charge |
| `past_due` | `active` | Successful retry or new charge |
| any except `cancelled` | `cancelled` | `cancelTenantSubscription()` or a provider cancellation webhook |

Notifications for these transitions are listed in [§17.9](#179-notification-event-catalog): `subscription.trial_ending_soon`, `subscription.payment_succeeded`, `subscription.payment_failed`, `subscription.renewing_soon`, `subscription.renewed`, `subscription.cancelled`, `subscription.plan_upgraded` and `subscription.plan_downgraded`.

What `past_due` means for tenant access is defined in [§6.5](#65-tenant-status-and-access). `incomplete` occurs only before provisioning, while the tenant is `awaiting_payment`.

**Trial extension.** A platform user may extend a `trialing` subscription through `extendTrial()`. `trial_ends_at` moves forward, and the provider-side first charge date is updated through the gateway driver when a payment method is on file. The extension is written to the landlord activity log with its reason. A `past_due` subscription whose trial ended without payment may also be extended while it is within `past_due_grace_days`: it returns to `trialing`.

### 14.4 Plan Changes and Proration

`platform_settings.proration_mode` applies to every tenant. It is not a per-tenant choice.

- **`immediate`:** an upgrade applies immediately, and a prorated charge for the rest of the current cycle is charged through the gateway.
- **`next_renewal`:** `scheduled_plan_id` and `scheduled_plan_price_id` are set. At the next renewal the subscription switches plan, and the scheduled fields are cleared.
- **Downgrades are always scheduled for the next renewal**, under either mode (decides UD-05). The tenant keeps the plan it paid for until the end of the cycle, so there is never a credit to refund or carry forward, and the platform holds no tenant balance. If the tenant's usage exceeds a limit of the lower plan when it takes effect, existing records are kept, and only new creations are blocked (§11.10).
- **Impact confirmation.** Every plan or interval change first calls `previewPlanChange()`, which returns the modules that would become `locked` and the limits current usage would exceed (§11.11). A change with a non-empty preview requires `confirm_impact = true`, or it returns 422 `plan_change_requires_confirmation` with the preview in `details`.
- **Interval changes** (monthly to yearly or back, on the same plan) apply at the next renewal, like a downgrade, so no proration is needed.

### 14.5 Billing for Module Add-ons and Negotiated Limit Overrides

- A module add-on (a `grant` in `tenant_features` with `extra_amount`) and a raised limit (a `tenant_limit_overrides` row with `extra_amount`) both **ride the tenant's existing billing cadence** (`subscriptions.billing_interval`). Neither is ever a separate one-off charge or its own subscription.
- `extra_amount` is the negotiated price per cycle, in the subscription currency. `billed = false` marks a goodwill override that adds nothing to the invoice. An override that is not yet in force (`starts_at` in the future) or has expired adds nothing.
- Workflow:
  1. The tenant asks, through the helpdesk (§21), for a module or a higher limit.
  2. A platform user negotiates a price with the tenant.
  3. The platform user calls `FeatureAccessService::setOverride()` or `PlanLimitService::setLimitOverride()` with the agreed `extra_amount`. A module add-on that has a matching limit at `0` (for example `pos` and `max_pos_registers`) needs both calls.
  4. The next invoice automatically includes a separate line for each billed override.
- Overrides granted or removed mid-cycle take effect under the same `proration_mode` rule as plan changes. With `next_renewal`, they are included from the next renewal onward.
- An add-on for a module that a later plan change includes stops being billed from the moment the plan includes it. `SubscriptionService` sets `billed = false` on it when the change applies, and records this in the activity log.

`SubscriptionBillingService` (Landlord):

- `calculateCycleTotal(Tenant $tenant, ?int $cycleNumber = null): array`: the base `plan_prices.amount` for the subscription currency and interval, plus the sum of `extra_amount` across the tenant's in-force `billed = true` module grants and limit overrides, minus the discount of an active platform coupon redemption for that cycle (§14.8). Returned itemised as `{lines: [{type: plan|module_addon|limit_override|coupon_discount, key, label, amount}], total, currency_code}`. The total is never negative.

  It is called whenever a charge is generated. **The platform's computed total is always what is charged.** When the provider can hold a recurring amount (a provider plan or subscription), the driver updates it whenever the total changes. When it cannot vary the amount per cycle (for example a coupon that applies to the first cycle only, on a provider whose plans have a fixed amount), the platform does not use provider-side recurrence: it stores `authorization_reference` from the first charge and charges each renewal itself through `chargeAuthorization()`, scheduled by `ProcessSubscriptionRenewal` (§72.2). Which path a subscription uses is internal to the driver and invisible to the rest of billing.

### 14.6 Routes

**Tenant domain: tenant owner billing** (group `tenant.admin`, always available):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Billing\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/billing/plans` | `BillingController@plans`: active plans priced in the tenant's billing currency |
| GET | `/api/admin/billing/subscription` | `BillingController@current` |
| POST | `/api/admin/billing/subscription` | `BillingController@subscribe`: body `{plan_id, billing_interval, gateway, coupon_code?}`. Returns a checkout URL. |
| POST | `/api/admin/billing/coupon-preview` | `BillingController@couponPreview`: body `{coupon_code, plan_id, billing_interval}`; returns the discount or the rejection `reason` (§14.8) |
| GET | `/api/admin/billing/subscription/plan-change-preview` | `BillingController@preview`: query `plan_id`, `billing_interval`; returns `previewPlanChange()` |
| POST | `/api/admin/billing/subscription/swap-plan` | `BillingController@swapPlan`: body `{plan_id, billing_interval?, confirm_impact?}` |

### 14.7 Service

`SubscriptionService` (Landlord; gateway-agnostic orchestration):

- `createInitialSubscription(Tenant $tenant, PlanPrice $price, ?PlatformCoupon $coupon = null): Subscription`: called at email verification (§9.3). Sets `gateway_mode` from `billing_payment_mode`, resolves and snapshots the trial (§11.6), sets `trial_consumed_at` when a trial starts, and reserves the coupon (§14.8)
- `subscribeTenantToPlan(Tenant $tenant, Plan $plan, string $interval, string $gateway, ?string $couponCode = null): array`: resolves the plan price (§11.6), reserves the coupon, calls `PaymentGatewayInterface::initiateSubscriptionCharge()` with the first-cycle total, creates or updates the subscription, and returns the checkout URL and reference
- `handleSuccessfulCharge(WebhookEvent $event): void`: under a lock on the tenant row, marks the `payment_transactions` row successful (idempotent by the row transition, §14.9), sets `is_first_paid_charge` when it applies, activates or renews the subscription, applies any scheduled plan change, activates the coupon redemption, records MRR movement (§14.10), calls the affiliate hook `AffiliateCommissionService::recordQualifyingPayment()` (§21A.5), and sends `subscription.payment_succeeded` or `subscription.renewed`
- `handleFailedCharge(WebhookEvent $event): void`: sets `past_due` (an `incomplete` subscription stays `incomplete`), writes the transaction, and sends `subscription.payment_failed`
- `refundTransaction(PaymentTransaction $charge, ?float $amount, string $reason, PlatformUser $by): PaymentTransaction`, `handleRefundEvent(WebhookEvent $event): void` and `handleDispute(WebhookEvent $event): void`: §14.9
- `cancelTenantSubscription(Tenant $tenant): void`: calls the gateway's `cancelSubscription()` and sets `cancelled` with `ends_at`
- `previewPlanChange(Tenant $tenant, Plan $newPlan, ?string $interval = null): array`: `{direction: upgrade|downgrade|interval_change, effective_at, modules_locked: [...], modules_unlocked: [...], limits_exceeded: [{key, used, new_limit}], addons_no_longer_billed: [...]}`
- `swapTenantPlan(Tenant $tenant, Plan $newPlan, ?string $interval = null, bool $confirmImpact = false): Subscription`: applies `proration_mode` and impact confirmation (§14.4), and sends `subscription.plan_upgraded` or `subscription.plan_downgraded`. When the change applies, it calls `ModuleActivationService::syncAutoModules()`.
- `extendTrial(Subscription $subscription, int $days, string $reason, PlatformUser $by): Subscription`: §14.3
- `getCurrentSubscription(Tenant $tenant): ?Subscription`

The `ProcessSubscriptionRenewal` job ([§72](#72-jobs-scheduling-events-and-broadcasting)) runs daily. For subscriptions renewed by the provider, it is a safety net: it calls `verifyTransaction()` if no webhook has arrived. For subscriptions the platform renews itself (§14.5), it creates the renewal `payment_transactions` row and charges it through `chargeAuthorization()`, with the row's `reference` as the provider idempotency key, so a rerun can never charge twice. It also sends `subscription.renewing_soon` and `subscription.trial_ending_soon` ahead of the dates.

### 14.8 Platform Subscription Coupons

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord |
| **Code module** | `Billing` |
| **Depends on** | §11.6, §14.1, §19.2 |

Platform coupons discount what a **tenant pays the platform**. They are a separate domain from tenant store promotions and coupons (§37): different database, different payer, different money, different lifecycle (per billing cycle, not per order). They share no table, service or code path. The tenant promotion engine is not reused, because its concepts (lines, targets such as categories and warehouses, flash-sale interaction, POS channels) do not exist in subscription billing.

```
platform_coupons  [DB: landlord]  audited
id
code                      string   unique   4 to 32 characters [A-Z0-9-], stored upper-cased, matched case-insensitively
name                      string            internal name
description               string   nullable shown to the tenant at checkout
discount_type             enum(percentage, fixed_amount)
discount_value            decimal(18,4)     percentage: 0 < v ≤ 100; fixed_amount: money in currency_code
currency_code             char(3)  nullable required for fixed_amount; the coupon then applies only to prices in that currency
duration                  enum(once, repeating)  once = the first paid cycle only; repeating = duration_cycles paid cycles
duration_cycles           int      nullable required when duration = repeating (2 to 36)
max_discount_amount       money    nullable cap per cycle, in the price currency (percentage coupons)
min_amount                money    nullable the plan price must be at least this (in currency_code; percentage coupons without a
                                            currency apply the rule only to prices in platform default_currency)
first_subscription_only   bool     default true  only a tenant's first subscription may use it
usage_limit_total         int      nullable null = unlimited
usage_limit_per_tenant    int      default 1     per tenant, and per owner email across tenants

```

```
unique(platform_coupon_id, target_type, target_id)
```

No target rows means every plan and price. With targets, the coupon applies when the chosen price, or its plan, is listed.

```
platform_coupon_redemptions  [DB: landlord]
id
platform_coupon_id        fk -> platform_coupons
tenant_id                 string   fk -> tenants.id
subscription_id           fk -> subscriptions
owner_email               string            lower-cased snapshot; enforces the per-email limit across tenants
code_snapshot             string
discount_type_snapshot    string
discount_value_snapshot   decimal(18,4)
max_discount_snapshot     money    nullable
cycles_total              int               1 for once; duration_cycles for repeating
cycles_applied            int      default 0
total_discount_amount     money    default 0
status                    enum(reserved, active, completed, released)
reserved_at               datetime
activated_at              datetime nullable
completed_at              datetime nullable
released_at               datetime nullable
unique(platform_coupon_id, subscription_id), index(tenant_id), index(owner_email, platform_coupon_id)
```

**Rules:**

- **Validation** (`PlatformCouponService::validate()`, used by registration, the tenant billing routes and the preview route) rejects with a `reason`: `not_found`, `inactive`, `not_started`, `expired`, `not_applicable_to_price`, `currency_mismatch`, `minimum_not_met`, `first_subscription_only`, `usage_limit_reached`, `tenant_limit_reached`.
- **One coupon per subscription.** A plan change keeps the redemption for its remaining cycles if the new price still qualifies; otherwise the redemption becomes `completed` early and an MRR `expansion` movement is recorded.
- **What it discounts.** Only the plan line of a cycle. Module add-ons and limit overrides are negotiated prices and are never discounted. Proration charges (§14.4) are not discounted.
- **Lifecycle.** `reserved` when the subscription is created or the checkout is started, under a lock on the coupon row (the same concurrency pattern as tenant promotions, so `usage_limit_total` can never be exceeded), incrementing `times_redeemed`. `active` on the first successful paid charge, which applies cycle 1. Each later successful charge applies the next cycle until `cycles_applied = cycles_total`, then `completed`. `released` (and `times_redeemed` decremented) when the reserving subscription is cancelled or the registration expires before any successful charge.
- **Trials.** A trial is not a paid cycle; the coupon starts with the first charge after the trial.
- **Refunds** do not restore coupon usage: a used coupon stays used.
- **Snapshots.** A redemption keeps the terms it was reserved with. Editing or deactivating a coupon affects only new redemptions. A coupon with redemptions cannot be deleted, only deactivated; `discount_type`, `discount_value`, `currency_code` and `duration` cannot change once redeemed.
- **Affiliate codes.** A coupon with `affiliate_id` is also an attribution touch (§21A.4). Commission is calculated on the amount actually charged, after the coupon (§21A.5).

`PlatformCouponService` (Landlord): `create()`, `update()`, `deactivate()`, `syncTargets()`, `validate(string $code, PlanPrice $price, ?Tenant $tenant, string $ownerEmail): array`, `validateForRegistration()`, `reserve(PlatformCoupon $coupon, Subscription $subscription): PlatformCouponRedemption`, `applyCycle(PlatformCouponRedemption $r, PaymentTransaction $charge): float`, `release(PlatformCouponRedemption $r)`, `usageStats(PlatformCoupon $coupon): array`.

| `landlord.public` (`auth-sensitive` limiter) | POST | `/api/platform-coupons/validate` | `PlatformCouponController@validate`: body `{code, plan_price_id}`; returns the first-cycle discount or the `reason` |
| `landlord.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/platform-coupons` | `Admin\PlatformCouponController@index`: filters `is_active`, `status` (scheduled, running, ended), `affiliate_id` |
| `landlord.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/platform-coupons` | `Admin\PlatformCouponController@store`: body includes `targets[]` |
| `landlord.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/platform-coupons/{coupon}` | `Admin\PlatformCouponController@show`: includes targets and usage stats |
| `landlord.admin` | PATCH | `/api/admin/platform-coupons/{coupon}` | `Admin\PlatformCouponController@update` |
| `landlord.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/platform-coupons/{coupon}/deactivate` | `Admin\PlatformCouponController@deactivate` |
| `landlord.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/platform-coupons/{coupon}/redemptions` | `Admin\PlatformCouponRedemptionController@index` |

### 14.9 Refunds and Chargebacks of Platform Payments

Platform billing uses the same two-phase refund discipline as tenant commerce (§40.4), on its own table.

1. **Refund.** `refundTransaction()` locks the original `charge` row, checks that `amount` (default: the remaining refundable amount) does not exceed `amount` minus the absolute sum of its `pending` and `successful` refund and chargeback rows, and inserts a `pending` `refund` row with a fresh `reference`. After commit it calls the driver's `refund()` with that reference as the provider idempotency key. The synchronous result, or the `refund.processed` / `refund.failed` webhook, performs the single `pending → successful | failed` transition.
2. **Chargeback.** `dispute.opened` creates a `pending` `chargeback` row that reserves the disputed amount; `dispute.lost` makes it `successful`; `dispute.won` makes it `failed`.
3. **Side effects of a successful refund or chargeback**, in the transition's transaction: the affiliate hook `AffiliateCommissionService::handlePaymentReversal()` (§21A.5), and an MRR movement only if the subscription is also cancelled. A refund never changes the subscription by itself; cancelling is a separate, explicit action.
4. A refund with an unknown outcome (no `provider_reference` after 1 hour) is never retried automatically; it is listed for review, as in §40.4.
5. Every transition is idempotent: a duplicated webhook or a repeated admin call finds the row already transitioned and does nothing. The admin refund route also requires `Idempotency-Key` (§70.11).

### 14.10 MRR Movements

`SubscriptionService::recordMrrMovement()` is called at the moments below, for `live` subscriptions only. The normalised amount is the recurring cycle total (§14.5, including the current coupon discount) divided by 1 for monthly and 12 for yearly subscriptions.

| Moment | Type |
|---|---|
| First successful paid charge (`is_first_paid_charge`) | `new` |
| A later change that raises the normalised amount (upgrade, add-on, limit override, coupon ending) | `expansion` |
| A change that lowers it (downgrade taking effect, add-on removed, coupon starting on a later cycle) | `contraction` |
| A cancelled subscription reaching `ends_at`, or a `past_due` subscription passing the grace period without payment | `churn` (to 0) |
| A churned tenant's next successful paid charge | `reactivation` |

Trials, authorizations and test-mode subscriptions never create movements. MRR at any date is the running sum of `mrr_delta` up to that date, per currency, which lets the dashboard report MRR history without a snapshot per day (§22.5).

---

## 15. Payment Gateway Architecture

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Shared code (`app/Shared/Payments`), used by the landlord (§14) and tenants (§40, §46, §47, §55) |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | none: shared infrastructure in `app/Shared/Payments` ([§73.1](#731-modular-monolith-layout)). Order payments are the `Payments` code module (§40). |
| **Depends on** | §5, §6 |

### 15.1 Two Uses, One Contract

| Use | Payment domain | Credentials | Mode selector | Records | Caller |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Platform subscription billing | **Platform billing payments** | The platform's own credentials in the landlord `platform_payment_gateways` table (encrypted, [§15.10](#1510-platform-gateway-configuration)) | `platform_settings.billing_payment_mode`, snapshotted per subscription | Landlord `payment_transactions` | `SubscriptionService`, `PlatformCouponService` |
| Tenant storefront payments | **Tenant commerce payments** | The tenant's own credentials in its `tenant_payment_settings` table (encrypted, §15.4) | `tenant_settings.payment_mode` | Tenant `order_payments` | `OrderPaymentService` (§40), `InstallmentPlanService` (§47), `ProductSubscriptionService` (§55) |

The two domains share only the driver code. They are separated structurally, not by convention:

- `PaymentGatewayFactory::forPlatform()` reads only `platform_payment_gateways` through the `landlord` connection; `forTenant()` reads only the current tenant's `tenant_payment_settings` and throws when tenancy is not initialised. Neither method accepts credentials from the caller, so platform billing can never be pointed at a tenant's account, and no tenant code path can obtain a platform secret.
- Platform gateway routes exist only on landlord domains, behind `landlord.admin` and super-admin permissions. Tenant routes never return, accept or reference platform gateway rows.
- Webhooks for the two domains have different URLs, different signing secrets and different log tables (§15.6).

Laravel Cashier is not used ([§4.4](#44-explicitly-not-used)).

### 15.2 PaymentGatewayInterface

```php
interface PaymentGatewayInterface
{
    // Subscription billing (landlord only)
    public function createPlan(PlanPrice $price): string;                       // provider plan reference
    public function initiateSubscriptionCharge(Tenant $tenant, PlanPrice $price, Subscription $subscription): array; // {checkout_url, reference}
    public function cancelSubscription(Subscription $subscription): bool;

    // One-off and stored-authorization charges (tenant storefront)
    public function initiateCharge(ChargeRequest $request): array;              // {checkout_url, reference}
    public function chargeAuthorization(string $authorizationToken, ChargeRequest $request): array; // {reference, status}

    // Both contexts
    public function verifyTransaction(string $reference): array;                // {status, amount, currency_code, fee, authorization_token}
    public function refund(string $providerReference, float $amount, string $refundReference): array; // {refund_reference, status: pending|successful|failed, amount}
    public function verifyWebhookSignature(string $rawPayload, array $headers): bool;
    public function parseWebhookEvent(array $payload): WebhookEvent;            // normalised event

    // Configuration (both contexts)
    public function validateCredentials(): array;                               // {valid, detected_mode: test|live|null, message}
}
```

- Every driver instance is built for exactly one mode (§15.9) and knows it. `validateCredentials()` makes one harmless authenticated call (for example fetching the account or balance) and reports the mode the provider says the keys belong to, from the key prefix or the API response (Stripe `sk_test_`/`sk_live_`, Paystack `sk_test_`/`sk_live_`, Flutterwave `FLWSECK_TEST-`).

- `ChargeRequest` is a DTO: `amount`, `currency_code`, `reference` (our own unique reference), `customer_email`, `customer_name`, `callback_url`, `metadata`, and `save_authorization` (bool: asks the provider to return a reusable authorization token).
- `WebhookEvent` is a DTO: `event_id` (the provider's unique event identifier), `type` (`charge.succeeded`, `charge.failed`, `subscription.cancelled`, `refund.processed`, `refund.failed`, `dispute.opened`, `dispute.won`, `dispute.lost`), `reference`, `provider_reference`, `status`, `amount`, `currency_code`, `fee`, `authorization_token`, `livemode` (bool or null: the provider's own test/live flag, where it sends one), `payment_method_fingerprint` (nullable: a provider-issued card fingerprint, used only for affiliate fraud checks, §21A.7), `occurred_at`, `raw`.
- Drivers **never** call application services. Routing a webhook to the right handler is the caller's job (§15.6).
- **Idempotency towards providers.** Every call that moves money (`initiateCharge`, `chargeAuthorization`, `refund`) sends our own reference as the provider's idempotency key or merchant reference, wherever the provider API supports one. A retried call can then never charge or refund twice.
- **Timeouts.** Driver HTTP calls use a 10-second connect and 30-second total timeout. A timeout is reported as `status = pending`, never as `failed`, because the provider may still have processed the call. The caller resolves it through verification (§40.2) or review (§40.4).

### 15.3 Drivers and Factory

| Driver | Billing (landlord) | Storefront (tenant) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FlutterwaveGateway` | Payment Plans API: one plan per `plan_prices` row and mode. The first charge references the plan, and later cycles are charged by Flutterwave, unless the cycle total varies (§14.5), in which case renewals are platform-charged through tokenised charges. Cancelled through the subscriptions cancel endpoint. | Standard checkout, tokenised charges, refunds | NGN and other African currencies |
| `PaystackGateway` | Plan API (`plan_code`). The customer completes an initial transaction, then a subscription is created with the customer and plan code. Cancelled through the disable-subscription endpoint. | Initialize transaction, `charge_authorization`, refunds | NGN and other African currencies |
| `StripeGateway` | Stripe Products and Prices plus Subscriptions (the equivalent flow) | Checkout or PaymentIntents, saved payment methods, refunds | International cards (USD, EUR, GBP and others) |

All three drivers are **first-class in v1**, for both billing and storefront use.

`PaymentGatewayFactory`:

- `forPlatform(string $provider, string $mode): PaymentGatewayInterface`: builds the driver from the enabled `platform_payment_gateways` row for that provider and mode. `$mode` is always the subscription's `gateway_mode` for existing subscriptions and `billing_payment_mode` for new ones; it is never taken from a request.
- `forTenant(string $provider, ?string $mode = null): PaymentGatewayInterface`: builds the driver with the current tenant's active `tenant_payment_settings` row for that provider and mode (default: the tenant's current `payment_mode`; the stored mode of an existing `order_payments` row when completing or refunding it). Throws when that row is missing or inactive.
- Both methods refuse `live` when `PAYMENTS_LIVE_ALLOWED` is false (§15.9).
- `supportedProvidersForCurrency(string $currencyCode, string $context): array`: for the platform, from each enabled gateway row's `supported_currencies`; for tenants, from `config/payments.php` (by default Stripe covers USD, EUR and GBP, and Flutterwave and Paystack cover NGN and other African currencies). Used to list options. The caller always passes an explicit provider when charging.

### 15.4 Tenant Gateway Credentials

```
tenant_payment_settings  [DB: tenant]  audited (secrets excluded)
id
provider             enum(flutterwave, paystack, stripe)
mode                 enum(test, live)
public_key           string   nullable
secret_key           encrypted
webhook_secret       encrypted nullable  secret hash / signing secret used to verify webhooks
is_active            bool     default false
enabled_for_online   bool     default true   usable by storefront checkout
credentials_verified_at datetime nullable  last successful validateCredentials() (§15.2)
unique(provider, mode)
```

There is no POS flag (decides UD-06). Online gateways are not offered at the counter in v1: POS card payments use terminal providers (§51.4). An unused flag would be a promise the system does not keep.

A tenant can have several active providers, for example Paystack for local customers and Stripe for international ones, and a separate credential set per mode for each. Only rows of the tenant's current `payment_mode` are offered at checkout (§15.5).

**Rules:**

- Saving credentials calls `validateCredentials()`. Keys that the provider reports as belonging to the other mode are rejected with 422 `payment_mode_mismatch`, so live keys can never be saved in the test slot or the reverse. A row can be activated only after successful validation.
- **Switching to live** (`PATCH /api/admin/payment-settings/mode`) requires at least one active, validated `live` row, and is refused while `PAYMENTS_LIVE_ALLOWED` is false. It is audited and sends `payments.mode_changed` to users holding `owner` or `admin`.
- **Switching back to test** is allowed at any time. Unpaid orders keep the mode they were created in: their payment attempts, verifications and refunds keep using that mode's credentials (§40.8).

`TenantPaymentSettingsService` (Tenant):

- `listGateways(): Collection`: both modes, secrets masked (`has_secret_key`, `has_webhook_secret`, the last four characters of the public key)
- `getActiveGateways(?string $mode = null): Collection`: default the current `payment_mode`
- `getOnlineGateways(): Collection`: active rows of the current mode with `enabled_for_online = true`
- `saveGatewayCredentials(string $provider, string $mode, array $credentials): TenantPaymentSetting`
- `testGateway(string $provider, string $mode): array`: `validateCredentials()` result
- `activateGateway(string $provider, string $mode): void`
- `deactivateGateway(string $provider, string $mode): void`
- `setOnlineAvailability(string $provider, string $mode, bool $enabled): void`
- `setPaymentMode(string $mode, User $by): void`: the rules above

Routes (group `tenant.admin`, always available):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Payments\Admin\...`) | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/payment-settings` | `PaymentSettingsController@index`: both modes and the current `payment_mode` | derived |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/payment-settings/mode` | `PaymentSettingsController@mode`: body `{mode}` | derived (`payment-settings.mode`, seeded to `owner` and `admin` only) |
| PUT | `/api/admin/payment-settings/{provider}/{mode}` | `PaymentSettingsController@update`: save credentials | derived |
| POST | `/api/admin/payment-settings/{provider}/{mode}/test` | `PaymentSettingsController@test` | derived |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/payment-settings/{provider}/{mode}/activate` | `PaymentSettingsController@activate` | derived |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/payment-settings/{provider}/{mode}/deactivate` | `PaymentSettingsController@deactivate` | derived |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/payment-settings/{provider}/{mode}/online-availability` | `PaymentSettingsController@onlineAvailability`: body `{enabled}` | derived |

### 15.5 Checkout Gateway Selection

At checkout, the customer chooses one of the tenant's active `enabled_for_online` providers **of the tenant's current payment mode** that supports the order currency ([§40.2](#402-online-gateway-payments)). If the tenant has exactly one eligible provider, it is used automatically. There is no automatic fallback to another provider after a failed attempt: retrying on a second provider could charge the customer twice. The customer chooses again.

### 15.6 Webhooks

| Context | Method | URI | Action | Identification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Landlord billing | POST | `/api/webhooks/{provider}/{mode}` | `Landlord\Billing\BillingWebhookController@handle` | Landlord domain |
| Tenant storefront | POST | `/api/webhooks/{tenant}/{provider}/{mode}` | `Tenant\Payments\PaymentWebhookController@handle` | Path (`InitializeTenancyByPath`) on a landlord domain |

`{provider}` is one of `flutterwave`, `paystack` or `stripe`, and `{mode}` is `test` or `live`. Each credential set is registered with its provider using its own URL, so a test event and a live event never arrive at the same endpoint. The settings screens show the exact URL to register for each provider and mode. Processing:

1. The `verify.webhook:{provider}` middleware calls `verifyWebhookSignature()` with the webhook secret of **that provider and mode**: from `platform_payment_gateways` (landlord) or the tenant's `tenant_payment_settings` (tenant), against the **raw** request body. A mode without configured credentials rejects every event with 401. An invalid signature is rejected with 401 and never processed. It is counted in metrics, but its payload is not stored. This check is a genuine security requirement and MUST NOT be skipped.
2. **Replay window.** Where the provider signs a timestamp (Stripe), events older than 5 minutes are rejected with 401. For every provider, replays are neutralised by step 4. **Mode check:** when the event carries the provider's own test/live flag (`WebhookEvent::livemode`) and it contradicts the URL's `{mode}`, the event is logged with `error = mode_mismatch`, acknowledged with 200 and never processed. When processing, a handler only matches records of the same mode (`payment_transactions.mode`, `order_payments.mode`); an event whose reference belongs to the other mode is ignored the same way.
3. For a valid signature, the controller stores the event in `webhook_logs` **in the database of the context it belongs to**: the landlord database for billing webhooks, and the tenant's own database for storefront webhooks. It then dispatches the queued `ProcessPaymentWebhook` job with the log ID after commit, and responds 200 immediately. Tenant payloads, which contain customer data, therefore never enter the landlord database.
4. **Deduplication.** `webhook_logs` has `unique(provider, provider_event_id)`. A duplicate delivery hits the unique key, is acknowledged with 200, and is not dispatched again.
5. The job calls `parseWebhookEvent()` and hands the event to `SubscriptionService` (landlord) or `OrderPaymentService::handleWebhookEvent()` (tenant). It then sets `processed_at`, or increments `attempts` and records `error` on failure. It retries 5 times with exponential backoff (1, 5, 15, 60 and 240 minutes). Business handling is also idempotent through the row transition rule ([§40.1](#401-order-payments-ledger)), so a webhook racing client verification is harmless.
6. Webhook routes are exempt from general throttling ([§70.5](#705-rate-limiting)). Tenant webhooks are still accepted and processed when the tenant is `suspended` or `closed`, or the platform is in maintenance mode ([§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode)).
7. **Retention.** Processed rows are pruned after 90 days by the daily maintenance jobs (§72.2). Rows with an `error` are kept until resolved.

```
webhook_logs  [DB: landlord and tenant; identical shape]
id
provider             string
mode                 enum(test, live)  from the URL
provider_event_id    string            the provider's event id; a hash of the raw body when the provider has none
event_type           string  nullable
provider_reference   string  nullable
payload              encrypted json    the parsed payload; encrypted because it carries customer data
received_at          datetime
processed_at         datetime nullable
attempts             int      default 0
error                text    nullable
unique(mode, provider, provider_event_id), index(provider, provider_reference), index(processed_at)
```

### 15.7 Refunds, Settlement and Payouts

- **Refunds.** Every storefront refund goes through `OrderPaymentService::refund()` ([§40](#40-order-payments)). It calls `PaymentGatewayInterface::refund()` on the provider that processed the original `order_payments` row. Refunds of payments recorded manually (cash, bank transfer) are recorded in the ledger only.
- **POS card terminals** use a separate contract, `PosTerminalGatewayInterface` ([§51.4](#514-terminal-providers)).
- **Provider settlement reconciliation** (matching provider payout batches to transactions) is deferred ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)).
- **Seller payouts** ([§50.5](#505-seller-payouts)), **sales agent commissions** ([§52](#52-sales-agents)) and **affiliate payouts** ([§21A.6](#21a6-payouts)) are paid outside the platform and recorded as paid. There is no gateway disbursement integration for any of them (Appendix C).

### 15.8 Platform Commission on Tenant Sales

- Controlled by `platform_settings.commission_enabled`, with the rate from `TenantPlatformSettingsService::getEffectiveCommissionRate()`.
- `OrderPaymentService::applyPlatformCommission(OrderPayment $payment)` is the single hook point. It is called after every successful **live** online gateway payment. It is a no-op when commission is disabled and for test orders (§40.8).
- **How** commission is collected (a split payment at charge time versus a post-transaction ledger entry), where the owed commission is recorded, and how it posts to tenant accounting, are UD-07. Interim: the hook computes the amount and records it only in `order_payments.meta.platform_commission`. Nothing is collected.

### 15.9 Payment Modes: Test and Live

Every payment provider offers separate test (sandbox) and live accounts. The platform uses one term throughout: **mode**, with the values `test` and `live`. "Sandbox", "environment" and "livemode" are not used as column or setting names.

**Where the mode lives:**

| Record | Mode column | Set from | Changes? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform gateway credentials | `platform_payment_gateways.mode` | Entered per row | No: one row per provider and mode |
| Tenant gateway credentials | `tenant_payment_settings.mode` | Entered per row | No |
| Subscription | `subscriptions.gateway_mode` | `billing_payment_mode` at creation | Never |
| Platform transaction | `payment_transactions.mode` | Its subscription | Never |
| Tenant order | `orders.is_test` | `tenant_settings.payment_mode` at creation (§40.8) | Never |
| Tenant payment row | `order_payments.mode` | The order (`is_test` → `test`) | Never |
| Webhook log | `webhook_logs.mode` | The webhook URL | Never |
| Plan price provider references | keys of `plan_prices.gateway_references` | Per mode | Added lazily |

**Safeguards** (each one is enforced in code and covered by tests, §76.3):

1. **Live is impossible outside production.** The environment variable `PAYMENTS_LIVE_ALLOWED` (default `true` only when `APP_ENV=production`) gates every live path: saving live credentials, switching either mode setting to `live`, and building a live driver in `PaymentGatewayFactory`. A staging copy of the production database therefore cannot charge a real card even though it holds live rows.
2. **Keys must match their slot.** `validateCredentials()` detects the mode of the keys; saving live keys in a test row, or the reverse, returns 422 `payment_mode_mismatch`.
3. **A record is completed only by its own mode.** Drivers are built from the record's stored mode, never the current setting. Webhooks arrive on mode-specific URLs and are matched only to records of that mode (§15.6).
4. **Mode changes are forward-only.** Switching `billing_payment_mode` affects new subscriptions only; switching a tenant's `payment_mode` affects new orders only. Existing subscriptions keep charging, renewing and refunding in their own mode.
5. **Switching platform billing to live** (`POST /api/admin/payment-gateways/mode`) requires super-admin, an explicit `confirm: true`, a `reason`, and at least one enabled, validated live gateway. It is audited and sends `platform.billing_mode_changed` to every super-admin.
6. **Test money is never reported as revenue.** Test transactions and test orders are excluded from every revenue metric, accounting posting, commission and limit (§22.5, §40.8, §21A.5).
7. **Idempotency, refunds, failed payments and chargebacks** follow the same rules in both modes (§14.9, §40); the mode only selects credentials and isolates records.

A subscription created in `test` mode stays a test subscription for life. When the platform goes live, super-admins cancel the test subscriptions listed under `GET /api/admin/subscriptions?mode=test`; they are never converted, because their provider references exist only in the test account.

### 15.10 Platform Gateway Configuration

The platform's own billing credentials are configured by a super-admin, per provider and per mode, instead of being fixed in environment variables. This lets the platform enable a provider, rotate a key or prepare live credentials without a deployment.

```
platform_payment_gateways  [DB: landlord]  audited (secret columns excluded)
id
provider                 enum(flutterwave, paystack, stripe)
mode                     enum(test, live)
public_key               string   nullable
secret_key               encrypted
webhook_secret           encrypted nullable
extra_credentials        encrypted json  nullable  provider-specific values (for example a Flutterwave encryption key)
is_enabled               bool     default false
is_default               bool     default false  at most one enabled default per mode; pre-selected at checkout
sort_order               int      default 0     display order of providers offered to tenants
supported_currencies     json               e.g. ["NGN", "GHS"]; validated against World currencies
supported_country_ids    json     nullable  null = every country; else offered only to tenants in these countries
credentials_verified_at  datetime nullable  last successful validateCredentials()
last_webhook_at          datetime nullable  updated on every verified webhook; shown so an admin can see the URL is registered
updated_by               fk -> platform_users  nullable
unique(provider, mode)
```

- **Offering providers to a tenant.** The billing checkout lists enabled gateways of the current `billing_payment_mode` whose `supported_currencies` contain the price currency and whose `supported_country_ids` include the tenant's country, ordered by `is_default` then `sort_order`. The tenant chooses; there is no automatic fallback after a failure, for the same double-charge reason as §15.5.
- **Secrets** are write-only. Responses return `has_secret_key`, `has_webhook_secret`, the masked public key, `credentials_verified_at` and the webhook URL to register. Updating a secret requires sending the new value; an omitted secret keeps the stored one.
- **Validation.** Saving credentials runs `validateCredentials()` (§15.2) and rejects a mode mismatch. Enabling a row requires `credentials_verified_at` within the last 24 hours.
- **Disabling** a gateway stops offering it for new checkouts. Existing subscriptions on it keep renewing with its credentials, which are never deleted while any non-cancelled subscription of that provider and mode exists (422 `gateway_in_use`).

`PlatformPaymentGatewayService` (Landlord): `list()`, `save(string $provider, string $mode, array $data, PlatformUser $by)`, `test(string $provider, string $mode): array`, `enable()`, `disable()`, `setDefault()`, `availableFor(Tenant|TenantRegistration $subject, string $currency): Collection`, `setBillingMode(string $mode, string $reason, PlatformUser $by)`.

Routes (group `landlord.admin`; permissions derived by §12.4 and held only by `super-admin`):

| Method | URI | Action (`Landlord\Billing\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/payment-gateways` | `PaymentGatewayController@index`: every provider and mode, secrets masked, plus the current `billing_payment_mode` |
| PUT | `/api/admin/payment-gateways/{provider}/{mode}` | `PaymentGatewayController@update`: credentials, currencies, countries, sort order |
| POST | `/api/admin/payment-gateways/{provider}/{mode}/test` | `PaymentGatewayController@test` |
| POST | `/api/admin/payment-gateways/{provider}/{mode}/enable` | `PaymentGatewayController@enable` |
| POST | `/api/admin/payment-gateways/{provider}/{mode}/disable` | `PaymentGatewayController@disable` |
| POST | `/api/admin/payment-gateways/{provider}/{mode}/set-default` | `PaymentGatewayController@setDefault` |
| POST | `/api/admin/payment-gateways/mode` | `PaymentGatewayController@mode`: body `{mode, confirm, reason}` (safeguard 5) |
