## 16. Message Delivery: Email, SMS, WhatsApp and Push

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (platform mailer and SMS configured by environment) and Tenant (tenant-configurable delivery) |
| **Feature key** | none for `database`, `email` (platform mailer), `sms` and `push`. A custom email provider requires `custom_email` (§16.2). The `whatsapp` channel requires `whatsapp` (§16.4). |
| **Code module** | `Messaging` |
| **Depends on** | §13 |

This section defines **how** messages are physically delivered. **What** is sent, and to whom, is defined in [§17](#17-notification-system).

### 16.1 Channels

The platform uses exactly five channels:

| Channel | Transport |
|---|---|
| `database` | Laravel database notifications (in-app) |
| `email` | §16.2 |
| `sms` | §16.3 |
| `whatsapp` | §16.4 |
| `push` | §16.5 |

### 16.2 Email

- **Landlord email** (platform to tenant owner, platform to platform user) always uses the platform mailer from the environment.
- **Tenant email** has two modes, set by `tenant_settings.email_provider`:
  1. `platform` (default): the platform's own mailer, the same SMTP or transactional-email service the landlord uses. The **From name** is the tenant's `store_name`. The reply-to is `store_contact_email`. The from address comes from the platform domain unless the tenant has a custom provider.
  2. `custom`: the tenant's own SMTP, sendmail or SES configuration from `tenant_settings.custom_mail_settings`. This requires the `custom_email` feature.
- At send time, `MailService` swaps the mailer configuration **per message** using Laravel's `Mail::build()` with the resolved configuration. The global mailer configuration is never mutated, so there is no cross-tenant leakage.

`MailService` (Tenant):

- `send(Mailable $mailable, $recipient): void`
- `resolveMailer(): Mailer`: platform or custom, based on the setting and the feature
- `testCustomConfig(array $config): bool`: sends a test message before the tenant saves the setting

Route (group `tenant.admin`):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Messaging\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/admin/settings/mail/test` | `MailSettingsController@test` |

### 16.3 SMS

```php
interface SmsGatewayInterface
{
    public function send(string $to, string $message): bool;
}
```

Termii and Africa's Talking are the recommended Nigerian providers, because they generally give better local delivery and pricing than Twilio for Nigerian numbers.

- Drivers in v1: `TermiiGateway` and `AfricasTalkingGateway`. Twilio is named as a possible provider, but its driver is deferred. Any other provider is added by writing one more driver class.
- `SmsGatewayFactory::forTenant(?string $provider = null)` resolves the named active gateway, or the tenant's **default** gateway when no provider is named. `SmsGatewayFactory::forPlatform()` uses the environment configuration for landlord SMS, such as driver OTPs sent before a tenant has configured a gateway.

```
sms_gateway_settings  [DB: tenant]
id
provider             enum(termii, africas_talking)   unique
credentials          encrypted json   provider-specific shape, e.g. {api_key, sender_id}
is_active            bool     default false
is_default           bool     default false  exactly one active row is the default
```

A tenant can configure more than one gateway. Only the default gateway is used, unless a caller targets a specific one.

`SmsGatewaySettingsService` (Tenant):

- `saveGatewayCredentials(string $provider, array $credentials): SmsGatewaySetting`
- `setDefaultGateway(string $provider): void`
- `activateGateway(string $provider): void`
- `deactivateGateway(string $provider): void`: blocked for the default gateway while other gateways are active
- `getDefaultGateway(): ?SmsGatewaySetting`
- `listGateways(): Collection`: credentials masked

Routes (group `tenant.admin`, always available):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Messaging\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/sms-gateway-settings` | `SmsGatewaySettingsController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/sms-gateway-settings` | `SmsGatewaySettingsController@store`: create or update by provider |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/sms-gateway-settings/{gateway}/set-default` | `SmsGatewaySettingsController@setDefault` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/sms-gateway-settings/{gateway}/activate` | `SmsGatewaySettingsController@activate` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/sms-gateway-settings/{gateway}/deactivate` | `SmsGatewaySettingsController@deactivate` |

### 16.4 WhatsApp

```php
interface WhatsAppGatewayInterface
{
    public function send(string $to, string $message, array $mediaUrls = []): bool;
}
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **Feature key** | `whatsapp` (integration, `manual` activation, §11.4) |
| **Disabled behaviour** | The `whatsapp` channel is skipped by delivery resolution (§17.3), so messages go out on the tenant's other enabled channels. Settings stay readable, and credentials are kept. |

- Driver in v1: `WhatsAppBusinessGateway` (Meta WhatsApp Business Cloud API).
- **Tenant credentials** (decides UD-08). A tenant may connect its own WhatsApp Business number. Otherwise its messages go out through the platform's number, configured in the environment. The `whatsapp` channel is available to a tenant when `whatsapp` is `enabled` **and** either number is configured. WhatsApp is gated because every message has a per-conversation cost to the platform or the tenant.

```
whatsapp_settings  [DB: tenant]  singleton (§5.9)
id
phone_number_id       string    nullable
business_account_id   string    nullable
access_token          encrypted nullable
is_active             bool      default false  true = send through the tenant's own number
verified_at           datetime  nullable       set by a successful test message
```

- `WhatsAppSettingsService`: `getSettings()`, `saveCredentials(array $data)`, `sendTestMessage(string $to): bool` (sets `verified_at`; activation requires it), `activate()`, `deactivate()`.
- Routes (group `tenant.admin`, `feature:whatsapp`; `Tenant\Messaging\Admin\...`): `GET /api/admin/whatsapp-settings` (`WhatsAppSettingsController@show`), `PUT /api/admin/whatsapp-settings` (`WhatsAppSettingsController@update`), `POST /api/admin/whatsapp-settings/test` (`WhatsAppSettingsController@test`), `POST /api/admin/whatsapp-settings/activate` (`WhatsAppSettingsController@activate`) and `POST /api/admin/whatsapp-settings/deactivate` (`WhatsAppSettingsController@deactivate`).

### 16.5 Push

- `PushNotificationService` (Firebase Cloud Messaging) is used for mobile and browser push. Unlike the passive `database` channel, push reaches the device even when the app is closed.
  - `sendToTenantUser(User $user, string $title, string $body, array $data = []): void`
  - `sendToDevice(string $fcmToken, string $title, string $body): void`
- FCM server credentials are platform-level (environment).
- **Device tokens** (decides UD-09). Apps register their FCM token after login, per actor:

```
push_device_tokens  [DB: tenant]
id
tokenable_type     string    morph type: User, Customer, Driver or Seller
tokenable_id       int
token              string    unique  the FCM registration token
platform           enum(ios, android, web)
last_used_at       datetime  nullable
index(tokenable_type, tokenable_id)
```

- Registering a token that already exists moves it to the current actor, because a shared device changes hands. An actor keeps at most 10 tokens, and the least recently used is deleted beyond that.
- A token that FCM reports as unregistered or invalid is deleted on the spot.
- Logout (§10) deletes the tokens registered with that access token's device, when the client sends the token on logout.
- `PushDeviceTokenService`: `register(Model $actor, string $token, string $platform)`, `unregister(Model $actor, string $token)`, `tokensFor(Model $actor): Collection`.
- Routes: `POST` and `DELETE` on `/api/admin/push-tokens` (`tenant.admin`), `/api/account/push-tokens` (`tenant.customer`), `/api/driver/push-tokens` (`tenant.driver`) and `/api/seller/push-tokens` (`tenant.seller`, which also requires `feature:marketplace`), all handled by `Tenant\Messaging\PushDeviceTokenController@store` and `@destroy`, with body `{token, platform}`. They are always available. Their Permission is "none" (self-service).

## 17. Notification System

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (platform-to-tenant and platform-to-platform-user) and Tenant (tenant-to-customer, tenant-to-staff, tenant-to-seller and supplier) |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `Notifications` |
| **Depends on** | §16 |

### 17.1 Two Scopes

| Scope | Database | Who sends | Who receives | Customisable by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Landlord | Landlord | The platform | Tenants (notifiable: `Tenant`, delivered to `tenants.email`), platform users and affiliates | Platform users |
| Tenant | Tenant | The tenant's own system | Customers, staff users, sellers, suppliers | Tenant staff (`notification-templates.update`) |

Both scopes use the **same table shapes** (§17.2). The landlord tables are platform-wide. The tenant tables live in each tenant database.

In-app (`database` channel) delivery of **landlord** notifications to tenant staff is UD-10. Interim: landlord notifications to tenants use `email` and `sms` only.

### 17.2 Tables

```
notification_templates  [DB: landlord and tenant; same shape]
id
key                  string            unique; from the event catalog (§17.9)
subject              string            nullable for channels without subjects
body                 text              supports {{placeholders}}
target_audience      json              array of audience values; tenant values: admin, customer, supplier,
                                       seller, sales_agent. Landlord values: tenant, platform_user, affiliate.
                                       An admin can widen or narrow the audience per event
                                       (e.g. also notify suppliers on purchase_order.received).
is_active            bool              default true
is_mandatory         bool              default false; true = non-optional (e.g. password reset,
                                       payment failure): cannot be deactivated and ignores preferences
is_customized        bool              default false; false = content equals the platform default
```

```
notification_template_channels  [DB: landlord and tenant]
id
notification_template_id  fk -> notification_templates
channel              enum(database, email, sms, whatsapp, push)
enabled              bool              default per config
unique(notification_template_id, channel)
```

This matrix replaces a single `channel` column. An admin settings screen can then show one event per row, with a checkbox per channel.

```
notification_preferences  [DB: tenant]
id
notifiable_type      string            morph alias: user | customer
notifiable_id        int
template_key         string   nullable null = this recipient's general preference for the channel
channel              enum(database, email, sms, whatsapp, push)
enabled              bool     default true
unique(notifiable_type, notifiable_id, template_key, channel)
```

`notifications` is the standard Laravel database notifications table, present in both databases.

### 17.3 Delivery Resolution

A notification is delivered on a channel only if **every** one of these is true:

1. `tenant_settings.notifications_enabled` is true. This is the tenant master kill switch and does not apply to the landlord scope.
2. The template `is_active`.
3. The `notification_template_channels` row for that channel is `enabled`. This is the tenant-level channel matrix.
4. The recipient's preferences allow the channel. The resolution order is:
   1. A row matching the recipient, `template_key` and channel.
   2. Otherwise, the recipient's row for the channel with `template_key = null`.
   3. Otherwise, enabled. This is an opt-out model: nobody starts silenced.
5. The channel's transport is configured ([§16](#16-message-delivery-email-sms-whatsapp-and-push)), and, for `whatsapp`, the `whatsapp` module is `enabled` (§16.4). Mandatory templates do not bypass this step.

Templates marked `is_mandatory` ignore steps 1 and 4 and cannot be deactivated (step 2 is enforced on write). Mandatory status is checked before preferences are consulted at all.

**Audience resolution (Assumption A-10).** Each value in `target_audience` resolves to recipients:

- `customer`: the customer on the triggering record. For a guest record, email and SMS go to the guest contact fields on the order or conversation.
- `admin`: all active staff users holding the `owner` or `admin` role. For `order.new_order_received`, `order_notification_email` is added. For `inventory.low_stock`, `low_stock_notification_recipients` is added. For events addressed to a specific staff user (for example `hr.leave_request_approved`, `approval.step_pending` or `project_task.assigned`), that user replaces the role-based list.
- `seller`: the seller on the triggering record. For events with no seller, it resolves to nobody.
- `supplier`: the supplier on the triggering record (email only). For events with no supplier, it resolves to nobody.
- `sales_agent`: the sales agent attributed to the triggering order (email or SMS). For events with no agent, it resolves to nobody.
- Landlord `tenant`: the `Tenant` notifiable (`tenants.email`).
- Landlord `platform_user`: the platform users named by the event.
- Landlord `affiliate`: the affiliate on the triggering record (email; `database` for the affiliate portal inbox).

### 17.4 Default Templates and Seeding

- Default content, default channels and the default audience for every key in §17.9 live in `config/notifications/landlord.php` and `config/notifications/tenant.php`.
- Seeding inserts one `notification_templates` row per key (`is_customized = false`) and one `notification_template_channels` row per channel. This happens at provisioning ([§9.4](#94-provisioning-job)) and on every defaults sync ([§12.6](#126-permission-and-default-data-sync)). It only inserts missing rows and never overwrites.
- `resetToDefault()` rewrites a row's content from config and sets `is_customized = false`.

### 17.5 Services

`NotificationTemplateService`. There is one implementation per context. Each binds to its own connection.

- `getTemplate(string $key): ?NotificationTemplate`
- `listTemplates(array $filters): Collection`
- `render(string $key, array $variables): array`: `[subject, body]` per channel, with placeholders substituted
- `updateTemplate(string $key, array $data): void`: sets `is_customized = true`
- `resetToDefault(string $key): void`: discards the customisation and restores the platform default

`NotificationMatrixService`. There is one implementation per context.

- `listMatrix(): array`: every template key with its channel checkboxes and `target_audience`, shaped for the settings screen
- `updateChannels(string $templateKey, array $channels): void`: for example `['database' => true, 'email' => true, 'sms' => false, 'whatsapp' => false, 'push' => true]`. Rejects disabling every channel of a mandatory template.
- `updateAudience(string $templateKey, array $audience): void`

`NotificationDispatchService`. There is one implementation per context.

- `dispatch(string $templateKey, $notifiable, array $variables, ?array $channels = null): void`: resolves the template. When `$channels` is null, it defaults them from `notification_template_channels`. It resolves the audience to recipients, filters channels through the delivery rules (§17.3) for each recipient, renders the content per channel, and queues one Laravel notification per recipient. `$notifiable` is either an explicit recipient or the triggering record from which the audiences are resolved.

`NotificationPreferenceService` (Tenant):

- `getPreferences($notifiable): Collection`: all preference rows for this user or customer
- `getEnabledChannels($notifiable, string $templateKey, array $defaultChannels): array`: applies the resolution order in §17.3
- `setPreference($notifiable, ?string $templateKey, string $channel, bool $enabled): void`: rejected when the template is mandatory
- `resetToDefault($notifiable, ?string $templateKey = null, ?string $channel = null): void`

### 17.6 Master Kill Switch

`tenant_settings.notifications_enabled` stops every tenant notification in one toggle, for example during a data migration. Mandatory templates are the only exception.

### 17.7 Routes

**Tenant** (always available):

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Notifications\...`) | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/notification-templates` | `Admin\NotificationTemplateController@index` | derived |
| `tenant.admin` | PATCH | `/api/admin/notification-templates/{key}` | `Admin\NotificationTemplateController@update` | derived |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/notification-templates/{key}/reset` | `Admin\NotificationTemplateController@reset` | derived |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/notifications/matrix` | `Admin\NotificationMatrixController@index` | derived |
| `tenant.admin` | PATCH | `/api/admin/notifications/matrix/{templateKey}` | `Admin\NotificationMatrixController@update`: body `channels` and/or `audience` | derived |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/notifications` | `Admin\InboxController@index`: own in-app notifications | none |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/notifications/{id}/read` | `Admin\InboxController@markRead` | none |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/notification-preferences` | `Admin\NotificationPreferenceController@index`: own staff preferences | none |
| `tenant.admin` | PATCH | `/api/admin/notification-preferences` | `Admin\NotificationPreferenceController@update`: body `template_key` (nullable), `channel`, `enabled` | none |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/notification-preferences/reset` | `Admin\NotificationPreferenceController@reset` | none |
| `tenant.customer` | GET | `/api/notification-preferences` | `NotificationPreferenceController@index` | n/a |
| `tenant.customer` | PATCH | `/api/notification-preferences` | `NotificationPreferenceController@update` | n/a |
| `tenant.customer` | POST | `/api/notification-preferences/reset` | `NotificationPreferenceController@reset` | n/a |
| `tenant.customer` | GET | `/api/notifications` | `InboxController@index` | n/a |
| `tenant.customer` | POST | `/api/notifications/{id}/read` | `InboxController@markRead` | n/a |

Staff and customers each manage only their own preferences, so the preference routes carry no permission.

**Landlord admin** (group `landlord.admin`). These are platform-owned messages. Platform users with the permission may edit them. Tenants cannot.

| Method | URI | Action (`Landlord\Notifications\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/notification-templates` | `NotificationTemplateController@index`: includes a rendered preview |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/notification-templates/{key}` | `NotificationTemplateController@update` |
| POST | `/api/admin/notification-templates/{key}/reset` | `NotificationTemplateController@reset` |
| GET | `/api/admin/notifications/matrix` | `NotificationMatrixController@index` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/notifications/matrix/{templateKey}` | `NotificationMatrixController@update` |

### 17.8 Placeholders

Each key in the catalog documents its variables in the config defaults, for example `{{customer_name}}`, `{{order_number}}`, `{{order_total}}` and `{{store_name}}`. `render()` MUST leave unknown placeholders untouched and log a warning.

### 17.9 Notification Event Catalog

This is the authoritative list of keys. "Trigger" names the service call that dispatches the notification. Keys marked **reserved** are seeded as templates, but have no trigger in v1 (see [Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)).

**Landlord scope**

| Key | Audience | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `tenant.registration_verification` | registrant (the registration email; there is no tenant yet) | `TenantRegistrationService::register()` and `resendVerification()` (mandatory; carries the code and link, §9.3) |

## 18. Module Notices and Maintenance Mode

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord (records and admin routes). Tenant (middleware and read route). |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `ModuleNotices` |
| **Depends on** | §11, §13, §17 |

### 18.1 Table

```
module_notices  [DB: landlord]
id
module_key           string            a feature key from §11.4 (the module key)
tenant_id            string   nullable fk -> tenants.id; null = platform-wide
type                 enum(update, maintenance, info)
behavior             enum(hard_block, read_only)  nullable; null = platform_settings.default_maintenance_behavior;
                                                   only meaningful when type = maintenance
title                string
message              text
starts_at            datetime
ends_at              datetime nullable
is_active            bool     default true
index(module_key, is_active)
```

### 18.2 Behaviour

- **`update` and `info`:** the request proceeds normally. The response carries `X-Module-Notice: {id}`, and the notice appears in the notices endpoint.
- **`maintenance` with effective behavior `hard_block`:** every request to that module's routes returns HTTP 503 with the notice's title and message.
- **`maintenance` with effective behavior `read_only`:** `GET` and `HEAD` requests pass. Every other method returns HTTP 503.
- A notice applies when `is_active`, `starts_at <= now()`, `ends_at` is null or in the future, and `tenant_id` is null or equals the current tenant.

### 18.3 Services and Middleware

`ModuleNoticeService` (Landlord):

- `createNotice(array $data): ModuleNotice`: dispatches `module_notice.published`
- `updateNotice(ModuleNotice $notice, array $data): ModuleNotice`
- `deactivateNotice(ModuleNotice $notice): void`
- `getActiveNoticesForModule(string $moduleKey, ?Tenant $tenant = null): Collection`
- `getActiveNoticesForTenant(Tenant $tenant): Collection`

The `module.notice:{key}` middleware ([§71](#71-middleware-reference)) is applied to **every** tenant route group, with that group's feature key. Always-available route groups use no module key and are not subject to module notices.

### 18.4 Global Maintenance

`platform_settings.maintenance_mode = true` makes the `platform.maintenance` middleware return HTTP 503 for every tenant-domain request. Tenant webhook routes are the exception: they are still accepted and queued. Landlord routes are unaffected.

### 18.5 Routes

**Landlord admin** (group `landlord.admin`):

| Method | URI | Action (`Landlord\ModuleNotices\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/module-notices` | `ModuleNoticeController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/module-notices` | `ModuleNoticeController@store` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/module-notices/{notice}` | `ModuleNoticeController@update` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/module-notices/{notice}` | `ModuleNoticeController@destroy` |

**Tenant** (group `tenant.public`, always available). Notices are not secret, so both the storefront and the admin can read them:

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\ModuleNotices\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/module-notices` | `ModuleNoticeController@index`: optional `?module=hr`. Returns the current tenant's active notices. |

## 19. Logging, Auditing and Media

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Both |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Depends on** | §4 |

### 19.1 Activity Log (spatie/laravel-activitylog)

- Records "who did what" feeds, for example "User X created product Y" or "User Z approved order W".
- Present in both databases.
- Inventory movements are **not** recorded here. They have their own transactional ledger ([§32.8](#328-inventory-movement-ledger)).
- Surfaced by the Activity Log report ([§61](#61-advanced-reporting)).
- **Retention.** Activity-log rows older than 365 days are pruned by the daily maintenance jobs (§72.2). Audits are kept for the life of the record (Assumption A-70).

### 19.2 Auditing (owen-it/laravel-auditing)

- Records field-level before and after values for sensitive models. Answers "what changed, from what to what, when, and by whom".
- Audited models:
  - Landlord: `Subscription`, `PaymentTransaction`, `Plan`, `PlanPrice`, `TenantFeature`, `TenantLimitOverride`, `TenantModule`, `TenantPlatformSetting`, `PlatformSetting`, `PlatformPaymentGateway` (secrets excluded), `PlatformCoupon`, `Domain`, `LegalDocument`, `Affiliate` (password and payout details excluded; a change of payout details is recorded as "payout details changed" without values), `AffiliateCommission`, `AffiliatePayout`
  - Tenant: `Order`, `OrderPayment`, `OrderReturn`, `Shipment`, `Product`, `ProductVariant`, `Promotion`, `Coupon`, `FlashSale`, `Customer`, `User`, `TenantPaymentSetting` (secrets excluded), `JournalEntry`, `SellerPayout`, `CustomFieldDefinition`, `StorefrontSetting`, `CmsPage`, `CmsBlogPost`
  - **Sensitive administrative actions** are also written to the activity log with the actor and a reason, because an audit row alone does not say why: switching a payment mode (platform or tenant), enabling or disabling a platform gateway, changing platform onboarding, trial, affiliate or custom-domain settings, approving, rejecting or suspending an affiliate, overriding an affiliate's rate, approving, rejecting or reversing a commission, generating, marking paid or failing a payout, refunding a platform payment, and creating or deactivating a platform coupon. This uses the existing activity log; there is no second audit system.
  - Custom-field value changes are recorded on the owning entity's audit trail (§23.2).
- Audits of `Product`, `ProductVariant`, `Promotion`, `Coupon` and `FlashSale` are the **price and promotion history**. "What was the price, or the promotion rule, on date X?" is answered from them. Order snapshots, not audits, are the record of what a customer actually paid.
- Audits never store secrets or full card or bank data. Encrypted attributes are excluded from auditing.

### 19.3 Media (spatie/laravel-medialibrary)

- Every image and file across both contexts. Storage is isolated per tenant by the filesystem bootstrapper ([§6.3](#63-tenancy-bootstrappers)).
- Collections are named in their owning sections, for example `gallery` and `featured` on `Product` ([§30.1](#301-product-images)).
- Every upload counts toward `max_storage_mb` ([§11.8](#118-limit-registry)).
- Controllers never touch storage paths. Services attach and read files only through the media library, which gives one media abstraction for local disks and object storage alike.
- **Upload safety.** Uploads are validated by MIME type (sniffed from content, not the file name), extension allow-list and size. Images are re-encoded when conversions are generated, which strips embedded metadata. SVG uploads are rejected. Private collections are never served from a public URL ([§75](#75-security) rule 10).

### 19.4 Asynchronous Exports

Every export that can exceed a few thousand rows runs in the background: report exports (§61), coupon code exports (§37.9), customer personal data (§26.4) and order exports. There is one mechanism for all of them.

An export of an optional module's data is allowed when `FeatureAccessService::canRead()` is true for that module, so a tenant can still export data from a `disabled` or `locked` module whose registry entry is "read when inactive" (§11.5). Exports include custom-field columns (§23.5). The customer personal-data export always includes every module's data about the customer, whatever the module states, because it answers a legal request.

```
data_exports  [DB: tenant]
id
export_type          string            e.g. report:sales, coupons, customer_personal_data, orders
parameters           json              validated filters
format               enum(csv, json, pdf)
status               enum(queued, processing, completed, failed, expired)  default queued
requested_by_type    string            morph type: User or Customer
requested_by_id      int
row_count            int      nullable
error                text     nullable
completed_at         datetime nullable
expires_at           datetime nullable  completed_at + 7 days; the file is deleted after this
(media: file)        private collection
index(requested_by_type, requested_by_id), index(status)
```

- `DataExportService::request(string $type, array $parameters, string $format, Model $requestedBy): DataExport` creates the row and dispatches `GenerateExport` on the `tenant-bulk` queue. The job streams rows in chunks (§6.6) into a file on the private disk. The requester is then notified: `export.ready` for staff, `account.data_export_ready` for a customer. Staff download through the authenticated download route below. A customer receives a signed link to `GET /api/exports/{export}/download` (group `tenant.public`, Laravel `signed` middleware, valid until `expires_at`). Both routes answer with a 302 to a 5-minute temporary URL on the private disk.
- The daily tenant maintenance job deletes expired files.
- A request with the same type, parameters and requester as a `queued` or `processing` export returns that export instead of creating a duplicate.
- **Imports** (bulk product, customer and stock uploads) are deferred (Appendix C). Bulk writes in v1 go through the bulk endpoints of §70.12.

`DataExportService` routes (group `tenant.admin`, always available; each export type also checks the permission and feature of the data it exports):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Exports\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/exports` | `DataExportController@index`: the caller's exports |
| POST | `/api/admin/exports` | `DataExportController@store`: body `{export_type, parameters, format}`; 202 |
| GET | `/api/admin/exports/{export}` | `DataExportController@show` |
| GET | `/api/admin/exports/{export}/download` | `DataExportController@download`: 302 to a temporary signed URL |

Customer download (group `tenant.public` with the `signed` middleware, always available): `GET /api/exports/{export}/download` routes to `Tenant\Exports\SignedExportDownloadController`.

## 20. World Reference Data

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord database. Read from both contexts. |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Code module** | `World` (lookups) |
| **Depends on** | §4 |

- `nnjeim/world` provides countries, states, cities, currencies, languages and timezones. It is installed and seeded **once, in the landlord database**. It is never copied per tenant.
- Tenant code reads World data through the `landlord` connection, and results are cached ([§74](#74-caching-strategy)). Tenant tables store `country_id`, `state_id` and `city_id` as plain columns ([§5.1](#51-keys-and-references)).
- Uses:
  - Registration (country and default currency, §9)
  - `plan_prices.currency_code` validation
  - Customer and shipping addresses (§26.2)
  - Warehouse and supplier addresses
  - Tax regions (§35)
  - Shipping zones (§36)
  - Tenant timezone and locale settings
- World data is exposed only through lookup endpoints ([§45](#45-lookup-endpoints)). States are always filtered by country, and cities by state.

## 21. Platform Support Helpdesk

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord database. The tenant-facing routes are on the tenant domain. |
| **Feature key** | none (every tenant, on every plan) |
| **Code module** | `PlatformSupport` |
| **Depends on** | §10, §17, §19, §72.4 (Reverb) |

This is tenant staff asking **the platform** for help: billing questions, bug reports, stuck provisioning, feature or limit requests. It is distinct from the tenant Customer Support module ([§59](#59-customer-support)), in which a tenant helps its own customers. The two modules share the same conversation and message shape, in separate tables.

### 21.1 Tables

```
platform_support_conversations  [DB: landlord]
id
tenant_id            string   fk -> tenants.id
raised_by_user_id    int      tenant-side users.id snapshot (no FK: different database)
raised_by_name       string   snapshot
raised_by_email      string   snapshot
subject              string
category             enum(billing, technical, feature_request, bug, other)
status               enum(open, pending, resolved, closed)
priority             enum(low, normal, high, urgent)   default normal
assigned_to          fk -> platform_users  nullable
last_message_at      datetime nullable
index(tenant_id, status)
```

```
platform_support_messages  [DB: landlord]
id
platform_support_conversation_id  fk -> platform_support_conversations
sender_type          enum(tenant, platform_user, system)
sender_id            int      nullable  tenant users.id snapshot or platform_users.id
sender_label         string   display-name snapshot
body                 text
is_internal_note     bool     default false  platform-staff-only
read_at              datetime nullable
```

```
platform_support_message_attachments  [DB: landlord]
id
platform_support_message_id  fk -> platform_support_messages
(media: attachment)
```

### 21.2 Real-Time

- The private channel is `platform-support-conversation.{id}`. The authorisation callback allows staff users of the conversation's tenant, and platform users with `platform-support.view`.
- Broadcast events: `PlatformSupportMessageSent` and `PlatformSupportConversationStatusChanged` ([§72.4](#724-broadcasting-and-real-time)).
- Everything uses the shared Reverb instance ([§77.4](#774-reverb)).

### 21.3 Services

`PlatformSupportConversationService` (Landlord):

- `openConversation(Tenant $tenant, array $raisedBy, array $data): PlatformSupportConversation`
- `assignToStaff(PlatformSupportConversation $c, PlatformUser $staff): void`
- `updateStatus(PlatformSupportConversation $c, string $status): void`
- `updatePriority(PlatformSupportConversation $c, string $priority): void`
- `listConversations(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`: platform inbox; filters are tenant, status, category and assignee
- `getForTenant(Tenant $tenant): Collection`

`PlatformSupportMessageService` (Landlord):

- `sendMessage(PlatformSupportConversation $c, array $data): PlatformSupportMessage`: persists the message, broadcasts it, and notifies the recipient when they are not connected
- `addInternalNote(PlatformSupportConversation $c, PlatformUser $staff, string $body): PlatformSupportMessage`
- `markRead(PlatformSupportMessage $m, $reader): void`

### 21.4 Routes

**Tenant domain** (group `tenant.admin`, no feature check, permission **none**: any authenticated staff user):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\PlatformSupport\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations` | `PlatformSupportController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations` | `PlatformSupportController@store` |
| GET | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations/{conversation}` | `PlatformSupportController@show` |
| POST | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations/{conversation}/messages` | `PlatformSupportController@sendMessage` |

**Landlord admin** (group `landlord.admin`):

| Method | URI | Action (`Landlord\PlatformSupport\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations` | `ConversationController@index` |
| GET | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations/{conversation}` | `ConversationController@show` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations/{conversation}` | `ConversationController@update`: status, priority, assignment |
| POST | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations/{conversation}/messages` | `ConversationController@sendMessage` |
| POST | `/api/admin/platform-support/conversations/{conversation}/notes` | `ConversationController@addNote` |

---

## 21A. Affiliate Marketing

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord only. No tenant database is read or written. |
| **Feature key** | none. A landlord platform module (§11.3), switched by `platform_settings.affiliate_program_enabled`. |
| **Code module** | `Affiliates` |
| **Depends on** | §9 (registration), §10 (the `affiliate` actor), §13.2 (`affiliates` settings group), §14 (billing, platform coupons, refunds), §17 (notifications), §19 (audit and activity log) |
| **Integration hooks** | Called by `TenantRegistrationService` (attribution) and `SubscriptionService` (qualifying payment, refunds, disputes). Calls nothing outside the landlord. |

The affiliate programme lets people outside the platform refer new **businesses** to the SaaS and earn a commission when a referred business first pays for a subscription. It is a platform acquisition channel. It is unrelated to anything a tenant sells: tenant marketplace sellers (§50), sales agents (§52) and platform commission on tenant sales (§15.8) are different concepts with different tables.

**Money flow in one line:** affiliate link → click → registration → trial (no commission) → **first paid subscription charge** → commission `pending` → hold period → `approved` → monthly payout (paid outside the platform) → `paid`. A refund or chargeback reverses or claws back the commission.

### 21A.1 Programme Switch and Scope

- `affiliate_program_enabled = false` (the seeded default) stops: new affiliate applications (503 `affiliate_program_unavailable`), new clicks (the click endpoint returns 404 for every code) and new referrals at registration.
- It does **not** stop obligations already made: referrals created while the programme was on still convert, and existing commissions still move through hold, approval, reversal and payout. Switching the programme off is not a way to avoid paying affiliates.
- Every rule of this section is enforced server-side. No client input can create, approve or size a commission: the client only ever passes a referral token or code, which the server validates, and commissions are created only by the billing webhook path.

### 21A.2 Affiliates

```
affiliates  [DB: landlord]  audited (password and payout_details excluded)
id
public_id                 uuid     unique   used in affiliate-facing URLs
name                      string
email                     string   unique
email_verified_at         datetime nullable
phone                     string   nullable
password                  string            hashed
company_name              string   nullable
website_url               string   nullable
country_id                int      nullable  World
promotion_methods         text     nullable  how the applicant intends to promote; reviewed at approval
referral_code             string   nullable unique  4 to 20 characters [A-Z0-9], assigned at approval; case-insensitive
status                    enum(pending, approved, rejected, suspended, closed)  default pending
commission_rate           percent  nullable  null = affiliate_default_commission_rate (§13.2)
rejection_reason          string   nullable
status_reason             string   nullable  suspension or closure reason
approved_at               datetime nullable
approved_by               fk -> platform_users  nullable
payout_method             enum(bank_transfer, paypal, other)  nullable
payout_details            encrypted json  nullable  e.g. {account_name, account_number, bank_name, bank_code, iban, swift, paypal_email}
payout_details_updated_at datetime nullable
last_login_at             datetime nullable
last_login_ip_hash        char(64) nullable  HMAC of the IP (§21A.7); the raw IP is never stored
index(status)
```

Totals such as referrals, conversions and earnings are **computed** from referrals and commissions (§21A.8), never stored as counters that could drift.

**Lifecycle:**

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| (new) | `pending` | `POST /api/affiliate/auth/apply` with name, email, password, promotion methods and `accepted_legal_document_ids` containing the current `affiliate_agreement` (§9.2, acceptance recorded with `context = affiliate_application`). The email must be verified before the application is shown for review. |
| `pending` | `approved` | `affiliate-manager` approves. A referral code is generated (or chosen by the manager) and `affiliate.approved` sends the referral link `https://{landlord website}/?ref={CODE}`. |
| `pending` | `rejected` | `affiliate-manager` rejects with a reason. Terminal; the email may re-apply after 90 days. |
| `approved` | `suspended` | `affiliate-manager` suspends with a reason. The code stops resolving immediately. |
| `suspended` | `approved` | `affiliate-manager` reinstates. |
| `approved`, `suspended` | `closed` | The affiliate asks to leave, or the manager closes the account. Terminal. |

**Effect of status on money:**

| Status | New clicks and referrals | Existing referrals convert | Commissions approved | Included in payouts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `approved` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `suspended` | No | No: a referral converting while its affiliate is suspended becomes `ineligible` (`affiliate_not_active`) | Only manually | No: the balance is held until reinstatement or a manual decision |
| `closed` | No | No (same as suspended) | Only manually | A final manual payout of the approved balance, at the manager's decision |

**Rate override.** `commission_rate` null means the programme default applies at the moment each commission is created. Setting a value (0 to 100) locks this affiliate to its own rate for future commissions. Changing either the default or the override never changes an existing commission: the applied rate is snapshotted (§21A.5). Rate changes require a reason and are written to the activity log.

**Payout details** are write-only for the affiliate and masked everywhere (last four characters of the account number). Changing them requires the affiliate's current password, sends `affiliate.payout_details_changed` to the affiliate's email, and makes the affiliate ineligible for automatic payout generation for 72 hours (§21A.6), which blunts account-takeover fraud.

### 21A.3 Clicks

```
affiliate_clicks  [DB: landlord]  [no updated_at]
id
affiliate_id              fk -> affiliates
visitor_id                uuid              random first-party identifier, created by the website on first visit
landing_path              string(512) nullable  path only; no query string beyond utm_* is stored
referrer_host             string   nullable
utm_source                string   nullable
utm_medium                string   nullable
utm_campaign              string   nullable
ip_hash                   char(64)          HMAC-SHA256 of the IP with an application key
user_agent                string(512) nullable
created_at                datetime
index(affiliate_id, created_at), index(visitor_id), index(ip_hash, created_at)
```

- The landlord website calls `POST /api/affiliate-clicks` whenever a page is opened with `?ref=CODE`. The server resolves the code (approved affiliate, programme enabled), records the click, and returns `{referral_token, visitor_id, expires_at}`.
- **Deduplication.** A second click by the same `visitor_id` on the same affiliate within 24 hours returns the existing click and a fresh token, without a new row. Click counts therefore mean unique visitor-days, not page loads.
- **Referral token.** An HMAC-signed, opaque value encoding `{click_id, affiliate_id, expires_at}`, where `expires_at = now + affiliate_cookie_days`. It cannot be forged, and it carries no personal data.
- **Cookie.** The website stores the token in a first-party cookie `aff_ref` on the landlord website domain (`Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, max-age `affiliate_cookie_days`). Because each click returns a new token that overwrites the cookie, the cookie always holds the **latest** click.
- **Retention.** Clicks not linked to a referral are deleted after 13 months by landlord maintenance (§72.2).

### 21A.4 Attribution

**Attribution model: last touch before registration, server-fixed at registration** (decides UD-35). Last-click is chosen because it rewards the affiliate who actually prompted the sign-up, it is the model affiliates expect, and it is exactly what the cookie mechanism produces. First-click and multi-touch models are not offered.

At `POST /api/register`, `AffiliateAttributionService::resolveForRegistration()` considers up to three touches and takes the first that is valid, in this order (each is more recent than the next):

1. **Affiliate coupon** (`coupon_code` belonging to a platform coupon with `affiliate_id`, when `affiliate_coupon_attribution_enabled`): the visitor typed it at registration, so it is the latest touch. `source = coupon`.
2. **`ref` code** in the registration request (from `/register?ref=CODE`): a click made on the registration page itself. A click row is created at this moment. `source = registration_code`.
3. **`referral_token`** from the cookie, unexpired and signature-valid: the latest earlier click. `source = link`.

A touch is valid only when its affiliate is `approved` and the programme is enabled. Invalid or expired values are ignored silently: attribution never blocks a registration.

**Multiple affiliates.** If a visitor clicks affiliate A's link and later affiliate B's link, the cookie holds B's token and B is attributed. If the visitor then registers with A's coupon, A is attributed, because the coupon is the latest touch. The rule is deterministic and documented in the affiliate agreement.

**Journey through onboarding.** The browser matters only until `POST /api/register`:

| Step | Where attribution lives |
|---|---|
| Landing page | `affiliate_clicks` row + `aff_ref` cookie |
| `POST /api/register` | `tenant_registrations.affiliate_click_id` (and `platform_coupon_id` for a coupon touch) |
| Email verification | `affiliate_referrals` row created with the new `tenant_id` (§9.3 step 2.4). From here on, the cookie is irrelevant. |
| Provisioning, trial, payment | `affiliate_referrals` (unchanged) |
| First paid charge | `affiliate_commissions` |

```
affiliate_referrals  [DB: landlord]
id
affiliate_id              fk -> affiliates
tenant_id                 string   unique   fk -> tenants.id; a tenant has at most one referral, ever
tenant_registration_id    fk -> tenant_registrations  nullable  nulled when the registration row is deleted
affiliate_click_id        fk -> affiliate_clicks  nullable
platform_coupon_id        fk -> platform_coupons  nullable
source                    enum(link, registration_code, coupon)
status                    enum(registered, converted, ineligible, rejected)  default registered
ineligible_reason         string   nullable  self_referral, existing_customer, conversion_window_expired,
                                             affiliate_not_active, first_payment_refunded
risk_flags                json     nullable  [{flag, detail, detected_at}] (§21A.7)
requires_review           bool     default false
attributed_at             datetime          the email-verification moment
conversion_deadline       datetime nullable attributed_at + affiliate_conversion_window_days; null = none
converted_at              datetime nullable
reviewed_by               fk -> platform_users  nullable
index(affiliate_id, status), index(status, conversion_deadline)
```

- `registered`: attributed, waiting for the first paid charge.
- `converted`: its commission has been created.
- `ineligible`: a rule excluded it; no commission will ever be created.
- `rejected`: an `affiliate-manager` rejected it (fraud); terminal.
- Daily landlord maintenance marks `registered` referrals past `conversion_deadline` as `ineligible` (`conversion_window_expired`).
- **Attribution is permanent.** Later clicks by the same person, a plan change, a cancellation or a re-subscription never move a tenant to another affiliate.

### 21A.5 Commissions

**Commission rule: one commission per referred tenant, on its first paid subscription charge only** (decides UD-36).

| Event | Commission? |
|---|---|
| Free sign-up, registration, provisioning | No |
| Trial start, trial extension, payment-method authorization | No |
| **First successful live charge with amount > 0** (`payment_transactions.is_first_paid_charge`, §14.1) | **Yes, once** |
| Renewals, upgrades, proration charges, add-on charges | No |
| A retried or duplicated webhook for the first charge | No (already processed) |
| Failed charges and their retries | No; only the charge that succeeds can be the first paid charge |
| Cancellation and later re-subscription | No; the tenant's first paid charge already happened |
| Test-mode charges | No, ever |

`is_first_paid_charge` is set under a lock on the tenant row inside `handleSuccessfulCharge()`, and `affiliate_commissions` has a unique commission per referral and per payment transaction, so no lifecycle path, retry or race can produce a second "first" commission. If the first paid charge is later fully refunded, the commission is reversed and **no later charge qualifies** (`first_payment_refunded`): this prevents refund-and-repay gaming.

```
affiliate_commissions  [DB: landlord]  audited
id
affiliate_id              fk -> affiliates
affiliate_referral_id     fk -> affiliate_referrals
tenant_id                 string   fk -> tenants.id
subscription_id           fk -> subscriptions
type                      enum(commission, clawback)
reverses_commission_id    fk -> affiliate_commissions  nullable  clawback rows only
payment_transaction_id    fk -> payment_transactions   the qualifying charge (commission) or the refund/chargeback row (clawback)
base_amount               money             the charge amount the commission is calculated on; negative on clawbacks
currency_code             char(3)           the charge currency
commission_rate_applied   percent           snapshot of the rate in force at creation
amount                    money             base_amount × rate ÷ 100, rounded (§5.3); negative on clawbacks
original_amount           money    nullable set when a partial refund reduced the amount before payout
status                    enum(pending, approved, rejected, reversed, paid)
requires_review           bool     default false  copied from the referral; set while a dispute is open
hold_until                datetime          paid_at of the qualifying charge + affiliate_commission_hold_days
approved_at               datetime nullable
approved_by               fk -> platform_users  nullable  null when approved automatically
rejected_at               datetime nullable
rejection_reason          string   nullable
reversed_at               datetime nullable
reversal_reason           string   nullable  refund, chargeback, manual
affiliate_payout_id       fk -> affiliate_payouts  nullable
paid_at                   datetime nullable
commission_referral_key   bigint   nullable generated: affiliate_referral_id when type = commission, else null
unique(payment_transaction_id, type), unique(commission_referral_key)
index(affiliate_id, status), index(status, hold_until), index(affiliate_payout_id)
```

**Commission base.** The amount actually collected by the qualifying charge (`payment_transactions.amount`), which already reflects any platform coupon (§14.8) and includes add-on lines, in the charge currency. Platform billing carries no tax in v1, so there is nothing to exclude.

**State machine** (the only allowed transitions; anything else is 422 `invalid_transition`):

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| (new) | `pending` | `recordQualifyingPayment()` |
| `pending` | `approved` | `affiliate-manager` approval, allowed only when `now ≥ hold_until` and `requires_review` is false (or cleared by the approver with a note). With `affiliate_commission_approval = automatic`, the daily job approves such rows. |
| `pending`, `approved` | `rejected` | `affiliate-manager`, with a reason (for example fraud). Only while not yet in a paid payout. Terminal. |
| `pending`, `approved` | `reversed` | The qualifying charge is fully refunded or charged back (`handlePaymentReversal()`), or an `affiliate-manager` reverses it manually with a reason. Terminal. |
| `approved` | `paid` | The payout containing it is marked paid (§21A.6). |

"Eligible" (pending and past the hold) and "payable" (approved and not in a payout) are **computed views**, not states, so the state machine has one meaning for each state.

**Refunds and chargebacks of the qualifying charge** (`handlePaymentReversal()`, called in the same transaction as the refund or chargeback row's `successful` transition, §14.9):

| Commission status | Full refund / lost chargeback | Partial refund |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` or `approved` | → `reversed` | `amount` reduced in proportion to the refunded share (`original_amount` kept); becomes `reversed` if it reaches 0 |
| `paid` | A **clawback** row: `type = clawback`, `status = approved`, `amount = −commission × refunded share`. It is netted against the affiliate's next payout. | Same, for the refunded share |
| `rejected` or `reversed` | Nothing | Nothing |

- `dispute.opened` on the qualifying charge sets `requires_review = true` on a commission that is not yet paid, which blocks approval and payout until the dispute resolves.
- Refunds of later (non-qualifying) charges never affect commissions.
- A clawback can make an affiliate's payable balance negative. A negative balance rolls forward and is recovered from future commissions; it is never collected from the affiliate by the platform (recovering it off-platform is a contractual matter).

### 21A.6 Payouts

```
affiliate_payouts  [DB: landlord]  audited (payout_details_snapshot excluded)
id
reference                 string   unique   our payout reference, e.g. AFP-202610-000123; shown on the bank transfer
affiliate_id              fk -> affiliates
currency_code             char(3)
amount                    money             sum of the included rows; always > 0
commission_count          int
period_start              date              first day of the payout period
period_end                date              last day of the payout period
status                    enum(pending, paid, failed, cancelled)  default pending
payout_method             string            snapshot
payout_details_snapshot   encrypted json    snapshot of the affiliate's details when generated
external_reference        string   nullable bank or provider transfer reference, required to mark paid
paid_at                   datetime nullable
paid_by                   fk -> platform_users  nullable
failed_at                 datetime nullable
failure_reason            string   nullable
cancelled_at              datetime nullable
created_by                fk -> platform_users  nullable  null = generated by the schedule
unique(affiliate_id, currency_code, period_end)
index(status)
```

**Generation** (`AffiliatePayoutService::generate(Carbon $periodEnd)`), by `GenerateAffiliatePayouts` on `affiliate_payout_day` for the previous calendar month (platform timezone) when the schedule is `monthly`, or by a `billing-admin` through the route. For each `approved` affiliate, in one transaction per affiliate, under a lock on the affiliate row:

1. Skip the affiliate when payout details are missing or were changed within the last 72 hours (the balance rolls forward, and the admin payout list shows why).
2. For each currency, sum the payable rows (`status = approved`, `affiliate_payout_id` null, `requires_review` false, `approved_at ≤ period_end`), commissions and clawbacks together.
3. If the sum is **at least** the currency's `affiliate_minimum_payout` threshold, create a `pending` payout and attach the rows. If the sum is below the threshold, zero or negative, or the currency has no threshold, create nothing: the balance rolls forward to the next period. Tiny payouts are never created.

The unique key `(affiliate_id, currency_code, period_end)` makes a rerun of the same period a no-op, so a retried job can never create two payouts for one period.

**Paying.** Money is sent outside the platform (bank transfer or the chosen method). Then:

| From | To | Trigger | Effect on the included rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pending` | `paid` | `POST .../mark-paid` with `external_reference`, by `billing-admin`; `Idempotency-Key` required | → `paid`, `paid_at` set. `affiliate.payout_paid` sent. |
| `pending` | `failed` | `POST .../mark-failed` with a reason (for example rejected bank details) | Detached (`affiliate_payout_id = null`), so they are payable again next period. `affiliate.payout_failed` sent. |
| `pending` | `cancelled` | `POST .../cancel` | Detached. |
| `paid` | `failed` | `POST .../mark-failed` when the transfer is returned by the bank (super-admin only) | Back to `approved` and detached. |

Every transition locks the payout row and checks its current status, so a double click, a retried request or two admins acting at once produce one transition and a 409 `state_conflict` for the rest. Automated disbursement through a provider API is deferred (Appendix C).

### 21A.7 Fraud and Abuse Controls

Practical, server-side and explainable. There is no device fingerprinting or invasive tracking: IP addresses are stored only as keyed hashes, and emails are compared only for the rules below.

**Hard rules** (the referral becomes `ineligible`; no commission is ever created):

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| Self-referral | The registration owner email equals the affiliate's email after normalisation (lower-case; `+tag` removed; dots removed for Gmail addresses). |
| Existing customer | The normalised owner email belongs to any existing or previous tenant, in any status. Affiliates are paid for new customers only. |
| Inactive affiliate | The affiliate is not `approved` at attribution or at conversion. |
| Conversion window | The first paid charge happens after `conversion_deadline`. |

**Review flags** (recorded in `risk_flags`; the referral and its commission get `requires_review`, which blocks automatic approval and payout until a manager clears or rejects it; `affiliate.referral_flagged` is sent):

| Flag | Check |
|---|---|
| `affiliate_ip_match` | The registration IP hash equals the affiliate's `last_login_ip_hash` or an affiliate login IP hash from the last 30 days. |
| `email_domain_match` | The owner email domain equals the affiliate's email domain, and the domain is not a public mail provider (list in `config/affiliates.php`). |
| `shared_payment_method` | The qualifying charge's `payment_method_fingerprint`, when the provider supplies one, matches the qualifying charge of another tenant referred by the same affiliate. |
| `velocity` | More than 10 referrals for one affiliate in 24 hours, or more than 3 referrals from one IP hash in 24 hours (thresholds in `config/affiliates.php`). |
| `rapid_refund` | Set on the affiliate (not a referral) when more than 30% of its converted referrals in the last 90 days were refunded; its new commissions require review. |

**Manual controls:** reject a referral or commission, reverse a commission, suspend the affiliate. Every such action requires a reason and is written to the activity log.

**Programme terms.** The affiliate agreement is a `legal_documents` type (`affiliate_agreement`, §9.2), versioned and accepted at application, so there is one source of truth for the programme's rules. It covers at least: the attribution model (§21A.4), the first-paid-charge commission rule and hold period (§21A.5), payout schedule and threshold (§21A.6), refund and chargeback reversals and clawbacks, self-referral and existing-customer exclusions, prohibited methods (bidding on the platform's brand terms, spam, cookie stuffing or forced clicks, misleading claims, publishing coupons not assigned to the affiliate), the disclosure requirement for paid endorsements, and termination. The machine-enforced rules are exactly those in this section; the rest are enforced by manual review. Publishing a new agreement version with `requires_reacceptance` asks existing affiliates to accept it on their next login (the same mechanism as §9.2).

### 21A.8 Affiliate Portal

What an affiliate sees (MVP). Figures are computed by `AffiliateMetricsService` over the affiliate's own rows, for a standard date range (§22.1):

| KPI | Definition |
|---|---|
| Clicks | `affiliate_clicks` rows in range (unique visitor-days, §21A.3) |
| Sign-ups | `affiliate_referrals` with `attributed_at` in range (verified registrations) |
| Trials | Those referrals whose tenant's first subscription started `trialing` |
| Paid conversions | `affiliate_commissions` of type `commission` created in range |
| Conversion rate | Paid conversions among referrals attributed in range ÷ referrals attributed in range (a cohort rate, so it is never above 100%) |
| Pending commission | Σ `amount` with status `pending`, per currency |
| Approved / payable commission | Σ `amount` of approved rows not in a payout (includes clawbacks), per currency |
| Paid commission | Σ `amount` of `paid` rows, per currency, in range by `paid_at` |
| Reversed commission | Σ `original_amount` or `amount` of `reversed` rows plus Σ clawbacks, per currency |
| Lifetime earnings | Σ `paid` rows, per currency |

Lists: referrals (the referred business shown only as a masked name, for example "Ac*** Stores", with status and dates, never contact details), commissions, and payouts. **Deferred:** marketing assets, campaign and sub-ID reports, charts, postback URLs and multi-tier programmes (Appendix C).

### 21A.9 Services

- `AffiliateService`: `apply(array $data, Request $request)`, `approve(Affiliate $a, ?string $code, PlatformUser $by)`, `reject(Affiliate $a, string $reason, PlatformUser $by)`, `suspend()`, `reinstate()`, `close()`, `setCommissionRate(Affiliate $a, ?float $rate, string $reason, PlatformUser $by)`, `changeReferralCode(Affiliate $a, string $code, PlatformUser $by)` (the old code stops resolving; existing tokens keep working because they carry the affiliate ID), `updateProfile()`, `updatePayoutDetails(Affiliate $a, array $details, string $currentPassword)`
- `AffiliateTrackingService`: `recordClick(string $code, array $context, Request $request): array`, `issueToken(AffiliateClick $click): string`, `parseToken(string $token): ?AffiliateClick`
- `AffiliateAttributionService`: `resolveForRegistration(array $input, ?PlatformCoupon $validatedCoupon, Request $request): ?array`, `attachToTenant(TenantRegistration $r, Tenant $t): ?AffiliateReferral`, `expireStaleReferrals(): int`
- `AffiliateCommissionService`: `recordQualifyingPayment(PaymentTransaction $charge): ?AffiliateCommission`, `handlePaymentReversal(PaymentTransaction $refundOrChargeback): void`, `handleDisputeOpened(PaymentTransaction $charge): void`, `approve()`, `reject()`, `reverse()`, `approveEligible(): int` (automatic mode), `balances(Affiliate $a): array`
- `AffiliatePayoutService`: `generate(Carbon $periodEnd, ?PlatformUser $by = null): Collection`, `markPaid(AffiliatePayout $p, string $externalReference, PlatformUser $by)`, `markFailed()`, `cancel()`
- `AffiliateFraudService`: `evaluateReferral(AffiliateReferral $r, Request $registrationRequest): void`, `evaluateCommission(AffiliateCommission $c): void`, `clearFlags(AffiliateReferral $r, PlatformUser $by, string $note)`
- `AffiliateMetricsService`: the affiliate portal KPIs (§21A.8) and the landlord affiliate dashboard section (§22.6)
