## 32. Warehouses and Inventory

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Inventory` |
| **Depends on** | §25, §27, §28 |
| **Integration hooks** | Back-in-stock alerts (§56) and low-stock notifications (§17) are called from `InventoryService` |

### 32.1 Inventory Model

- **One store per tenant; many warehouses.** Warehouses are internal stock locations. Customers never see or choose a warehouse. The storefront shows only aggregate availability.
- **The `inventory` table is the single source of truth for stock.** No product or variant column holds stock.
- Stock is tracked per `(product, variant, warehouse)`:
  - simple products use `product_variant_id = null`
  - variable products use one row per variant
  - bundles, digital products and service products have no inventory rows ([§28.1](#281-product-types))
- **Available stock** = `quantity - reserved_quantity`.

The full trace: product, then variant, then warehouse, then inventory. Stock then moves through these operations:

- adjustments (§33.2)
- transfers (§33.1)
- purchase receipts and purchase returns (§49)
- reservations (§32.5)
- orders (§39)
- fulfilment (§36)
- returns (§41)
- manufacturing (§64)
- repair parts (§67)

Every movement goes through `InventoryService` (§32.6).

### 32.2 Warehouses

```
warehouses  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string
code                 string   nullable unique
address_line         string   nullable
city_id              int      nullable  World
state_id             int      nullable  World
country_id           int      nullable  World
phone                string   nullable
is_active            bool     default true
```

### 32.3 Warehouse Staff Assignment

```
warehouse_user  [DB: tenant]  [no timestamps]
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses
user_id              fk -> users
unique(warehouse_id, user_id)
```

This table is used by `staff_data_access_scope = warehouse` ([§25.3](#253-staff-data-access-scope)). Assignments are managed through `PUT /api/admin/users/{user}/warehouses` ([§25.4](#254-routes)).

### 32.4 Inventory Table and Fulfilment Warehouse

```
inventory  [DB: tenant]
id
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
variant_key          int      generated: COALESCE(product_variant_id, 0)  (for uniqueness with nullable variant)
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses
quantity             qty      default 0   on hand; never negative
reserved_quantity    qty      default 0   never negative; never greater than quantity
unique(product_id, variant_key, warehouse_id)
```

**Choosing the fulfilment warehouse** for each physical order line:

1. **POS sales:** the register's warehouse ([§51](#51-point-of-sale)).
2. **Orders created by other services** use the rule in item 3, unless the caller passes a `warehouse_id` per line. Callers include order duplication (§39), sales-quotation conversion (§53), repair invoicing (§67), product-subscription renewals (§55) and channel imports (§68, §69).
3. **Online checkout:** `InventoryService::selectFulfillmentWarehouse()` picks the active warehouse with the lowest `id` that has enough available stock for the **whole** line quantity. A line is never split across warehouses in v1 (Assumption A-15). If no single warehouse can fulfil the line, checkout rejects that line as out of stock.
4. Before the line ships, staff can move it to another warehouse through `PATCH /api/admin/orders/{order}/items/{item}/warehouse` ([§39.7](#397-routes)). This releases the reservation at the old warehouse and reserves at the new one, inside one transaction.

### 32.5 Stock Lifecycle: Reservation, Deduction and Release

| Event | Effect | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Online order placed, not yet fully paid | `reserved_quantity += qty` at the line warehouse | `reserveStock()` |
| Order confirmed ([§39.4](#394-confirmation-payment-status-and-order-status)): fully paid, or released to fulfilment by the installment policy | `quantity -= qty`, `reserved_quantity -= qty` | `deductStock(fromReservation: true)` |
| Payment attempt failed (§40.2) | None. The reservation is kept so the customer can retry payment on the same order. | none |
| Unpaid order expired (`payment_expires_at` passed, §39.5), or cancelled before confirmation | `reserved_quantity -= qty` | `releaseReservedStock()` |
| Order cancelled after confirmation, before shipment | `quantity += qty` (reason `order_cancelled`) | `adjustStock()` |
| POS sale (§51), paid at the counter | `quantity -= qty`, with no reservation | `deductStock(fromReservation: false)` |
| Restaurant table order (§65.4): items added per round; settled at the end | Reserved when each round is added; deducted from the reservation on settlement; released if the table order is voided | `reserveStock()`, then `deductStock()` or `releaseReservedStock()` |
| Installment order (§47) | Reserved at placement. Deducted when released to fulfilment under `installments_fulfillment_policy`. | `reserveStock()`, then `deductStock()` |
| Resellable return received (§41) | `quantity += qty` | `adjustStock()` |
| Purchase order received (§49) | `quantity += qty` | `adjustStock()` |
| Purchase return approved (§49) | `quantity -= qty` | `adjustStock()` |
| Transfer dispatched or received (§33.1) | Source `quantity -= sent`; destination `quantity += received` | `adjustStock()` |
| Stock adjustment submitted (§33.2) | `quantity += / -=` per line | `adjustStock()` |
| Work order completed (§64) | Components minus, finished goods plus | `adjustStock()` |
| Repair part consumed or removed (§67) | Minus or plus | `adjustStock()` |

Bundle lines expand to their children for every operation ([§28.3](#283-bundles)). Digital and service lines skip inventory entirely.

**Reservation expiry** (decides UD-14). A reservation lives exactly as long as its unpaid order. Unpaid online orders expire at `payment_expires_at` = `placed_at + tenant_settings.unpaid_order_expiry_minutes` (default 60). The delayed `ExpireUnpaidOrder` job then cancels the order with reason `payment_timeout`, which releases its stock, flash-sale claims and promotion reservations ([§39.5](#395-order-service)). No reservation outlives its order, so there is no separate reservation expiry clock. Orders that are not paid through the online flow do not expire, because staff manage them: `admin`, `woocommerce`, `social`, installment and restaurant table orders. The daily tenant maintenance job (§72.2) lists reservations older than 7 days on unconfirmed orders in `inventory.stale_reservations` for staff review.

### 32.6 Inventory Service

`InventoryService` (Tenant). Every mutating method runs in a database transaction (joining the caller's transaction when there is one) and locks the affected `inventory` rows with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, which prevents overselling. Every mutating method writes one `inventory_movements` row per affected inventory row ([§32.8](#328-inventory-movement-ledger)) and runs the post-mutation hooks ([§32.7](#327-stock-alerts-and-hooks)) after commit.

**Lock ordering.** A multi-line operation (checkout, a POS sale, a transfer, an adjustment, a work order) first expands bundles, then locks every affected `inventory` row in ascending `(warehouse_id, product_id, variant_key)` order, in one query, before changing any of them. Every caller uses the same order, so two concurrent operations on overlapping stock can wait on each other but never deadlock. A deadlock that the database still reports (for example from gap locks) is retried up to 3 times by the transaction helper.

- `getStockForProduct(Product $product, ?ProductVariant $variant = null): array`: `{total_quantity, total_reserved, total_available, warehouses: [{warehouse_id, quantity, reserved_quantity, available}]}`
- `getAvailableStock(Product $product, ?ProductVariant $variant = null, ?Warehouse $warehouse = null): ?float`: across all warehouses when no warehouse is given. Bundles use derived availability. Returns `null`, meaning "not tracked", for digital and service products.
- `selectFulfillmentWarehouse(Product $product, ?ProductVariant $variant, float $qty): ?Warehouse`
- `adjustStock(Warehouse $w, Product $p, ?ProductVariant $v, float $delta, string $reason, ?Model $reference = null): Inventory`: creates the row if missing. Rejects any result where `quantity < 0` or `quantity < reserved_quantity`.
- `reserveStock(Warehouse $w, Product $p, ?ProductVariant $v, float $qty, Model $reference): void`: throws `InsufficientStockException` when available stock is less than `$qty`
- `releaseReservedStock(Warehouse $w, Product $p, ?ProductVariant $v, float $qty, Model $reference): void`
- `deductStock(Warehouse $w, Product $p, ?ProductVariant $v, float $qty, Model $reference, bool $fromReservation = true): void`
- `moveReservation(OrderItem $item, Warehouse $to): void`
- `rebuildBalance(Inventory $row): Inventory`: operational repair from the ledger (§32.8)
- `getLowStockProducts(?Warehouse $warehouse = null): Collection`
- `getOutOfStockProducts(?Warehouse $warehouse = null): Collection`

There is no direct warehouse-to-warehouse transfer method. All transfers go through `StockTransferService` ([§33.1](#331-stock-transfers)).

### 32.7 Stock Alerts and Hooks

After each mutation, `InventoryService` compares the product's (or variant's) **total available stock** before and after:

- If it crossed to at or below `tenant_settings.low_stock_threshold`: dispatch `inventory.low_stock`.
- If it reached `0`: dispatch `inventory.out_of_stock`.
- If it went from `0` to a positive value and `back_in_stock_alerts` is enabled: call `BackInStockService::checkAndNotify()` ([§56](#56-back-in-stock-alerts)).

The `CheckExpiringProducts` job runs daily. It dispatches `inventory.product_expiring_soon` for products whose `expiry_date` falls within `tenant_settings.expiring_product_alert_days`. It does nothing when that setting is null.

### 32.8 Inventory Movement Ledger

`inventory_movements` is the append-only ledger of every stock change (decides UD-15). `inventory.quantity` and `reserved_quantity` are a materialised balance of this ledger. The balance is written in the same transaction as the movement, so the two can never drift. An activity log is unsuitable for this role: it is not transactional with the stock row, it is not typed, and it is pruned.

```
inventory_movements  [DB: tenant]  [no updated_at]
id
inventory_id         fk -> inventory
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses          denormalised for reporting
product_id           fk -> products            denormalised
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable  denormalised
movement_type        enum(reserve, release, deduct, restock_return, restock_cancel, purchase_receipt,
                          purchase_return, transfer_out, transfer_in, adjustment_in, adjustment_out,
                          work_order_consume, work_order_output, repair_consume, repair_return, reservation_move)
quantity_delta       qty               change to quantity (signed; 0 for reserve and release)
reserved_delta       qty               change to reserved_quantity (signed)
quantity_after       qty               balance after this movement
reserved_after       qty
unit_cost_snapshot   money    nullable  cost for valuation (adjustments, receipts, restocks)
reference_type       string            morph type: Order, OrderReturn, StockTransfer, StockAdjustment,
                                         PurchaseOrder, PurchaseReturn, WorkOrder, RepairJob
reference_id         int
reason               string   nullable
user_id              fk -> users  nullable  null = system
created_at           datetime
index(inventory_id, id), index(product_id, created_at), index(reference_type, reference_id)
```

- Rows are never updated or deleted ([§5.2](#52-timestamps-soft-deletes-and-immutability)).
- `InventoryService::rebuildBalance(Inventory $row)` recomputes a row from the ledger. The weekly `inventory:verify` check (§77.6) compares the two and reports any difference. It never auto-corrects.
- Stock history, valuation-at-date and the stock movement report (§61) are queries over this table.
- The `Inventory` model is not audited separately. The ledger is its audit trail.
- Movements are listed through `GET /api/admin/inventory/movements` ([§32.10](#3210-routes)).

### 32.9 Warehouse Service

`WarehouseService` (Tenant):

- `createWarehouse(array $data): Warehouse`: enforces `max_warehouses`
- `updateWarehouse(Warehouse $warehouse, array $data): Warehouse`
- `deactivateWarehouse(Warehouse $warehouse): void`: blocked while `reserved_quantity > 0` anywhere in the warehouse
- `deleteWarehouse(Warehouse $warehouse): void`: allowed only when the warehouse has no inventory rows with `quantity > 0`, and no orders, transfers, POS registers or purchase orders reference it. Deactivate it otherwise.
- `listWarehouses(array $filters = []): Collection`

### 32.10 Routes

Group `tenant.admin`, core. There are no customer-facing warehouse routes.

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Inventory\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/warehouses` | `WarehouseController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/warehouses` | `WarehouseController@store` (`usage.limit:max_warehouses`) |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/warehouses/{warehouse}` | `WarehouseController@update` |

| DELETE | `/api/admin/warehouses/{warehouse}` | `WarehouseController@destroy` |
| GET | `/api/admin/warehouses/{warehouse}/inventory` | `InventoryController@warehouse` |
| GET | `/api/admin/products/{product}/inventory` | `InventoryController@product`: per-warehouse breakdown |

## 33. Stock Transfers and Stock Adjustments

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Inventory` |
| **Depends on** | §32 |
| **Integration hooks** | Approval workflows (§60) MAY gate adjustment submission |

### 33.1 Stock Transfers

```
stock_transfers  [DB: tenant]
id
from_warehouse_id    fk -> warehouses
to_warehouse_id      fk -> warehouses   must differ from from_warehouse_id
status               enum(draft, in_transit, received, cancelled)
notes                text     nullable
created_by           fk -> users
dispatched_at        datetime nullable
received_at          datetime nullable
```

```
stock_transfer_items  [DB: tenant]
id
stock_transfer_id    fk -> stock_transfers
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
quantity_sent        qty
quantity_received    qty      default 0   supports partial receipt
```

Rules:

- **Dispatch** (`draft` to `in_transit`) decrements `quantity` at the source immediately. While a transfer is in transit, its stock is not countable at either location, which reflects the real state of goods on the road. A line cannot dispatch more than the source's available stock.
- **Receive** increments `quantity` at the destination for the received quantity of each line. Partial receipts are allowed. The status becomes `received` only once every line is fully received.
- **Cancel** is allowed from `draft` or `in_transit`. From `in_transit`, the not-yet-received remainder of each line (`quantity_sent - quantity_received`) is returned to the source.

`StockTransferService`:

- `createTransfer(Warehouse $from, Warehouse $to, array $items, ?string $notes = null): StockTransfer`
- `updateTransfer(StockTransfer $t, array $items, ?string $notes = null): StockTransfer`: draft only
- `dispatchTransfer(StockTransfer $t): void`
- `receiveTransfer(StockTransfer $t, array $receivedItems): void`
- `cancelTransfer(StockTransfer $t): void`
- `listTransfers(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`
- `getTransfer(StockTransfer $t): StockTransfer`

### 33.2 Stock Adjustments

Stock adjustments are the operator-facing, batch-oriented workflow for correcting stock at one warehouse: stock-take corrections, damage, loss, found stock and miscounts. Submitting an adjustment calls `InventoryService::adjustStock()` once per line, inside a single transaction.

```
stock_adjustments  [DB: tenant]
id
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses
status               enum(draft, submitted)
notes                text     nullable  reason for the whole batch
attachment_media_id  int      nullable  e.g. a photo of damaged stock or a signed stock-take sheet
created_by           fk -> users
submitted_at         datetime nullable
```

```
stock_adjustment_items  [DB: tenant]
id
stock_adjustment_id  fk -> stock_adjustments
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
action               enum(addition, subtraction)
quantity             qty
unit_cost_snapshot   money    nullable  product/variant cost_price captured when the line is added
notes                text     nullable  per-line note
```

Rules:

- A draft can be edited freely.
- Submitting is final and all-or-nothing. After submission the record is immutable ([§5.2](#52-timestamps-soft-deletes-and-immutability)).
- Submission records a `postStockAdjustment()` request in the accounting outbox (§57.3), so shrinkage and write-offs reach the profit and loss statement.
- A mistake is corrected with a new, opposite adjustment.
- When `approval_workflows` is enabled and an active workflow exists for `module_key = stock_adjustment`, submission creates an approval request. The adjustment is applied only when that request is approved ([§60](#60-approval-workflow-engine)).

`StockAdjustmentService`:

- `createAdjustment(Warehouse $warehouse, ?string $notes = null, ?UploadedFile $attachment = null): StockAdjustment`
- `addItem(StockAdjustment $a, Product $p, string $action, float $quantity, ?ProductVariant $v = null, ?string $notes = null): StockAdjustmentItem`
- `updateItem(StockAdjustmentItem $item, array $data): StockAdjustmentItem`
- `removeItem(StockAdjustmentItem $item): void`
- `submitAdjustment(StockAdjustment $a): void`
- `getAdjustment(StockAdjustment $a): StockAdjustment`
- `listAdjustments(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`
- `lookupProducts(Warehouse $warehouse, string $search): Collection`: matches the name, SKU or barcode of products and variants. Returns name, code, `cost_price` and current quantity at that warehouse.

### 33.3 Routes

Group `tenant.admin`, core:

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Inventory\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/stock-transfers` | `StockTransferController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/stock-transfers` | `StockTransferController@store` |
| GET | `/api/admin/stock-transfers/{transfer}` | `StockTransferController@show` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/stock-transfers/{transfer}` | `StockTransferController@update` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/stock-transfers/{transfer}/dispatch` | `StockTransferController@dispatch` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/stock-transfers/{transfer}/receive` | `StockTransferController@receive` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/stock-transfers/{transfer}/cancel` | `StockTransferController@cancel` |
| GET | `/api/admin/stock-adjustments` | `StockAdjustmentController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/stock-adjustments` | `StockAdjustmentController@store` |
| GET | `/api/admin/stock-adjustments/{adjustment}` | `StockAdjustmentController@show` |
| POST | `/api/admin/stock-adjustments/{adjustment}/items` | `StockAdjustmentItemController@store` |

## 34. Per-Warehouse Pricing

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) (per-product opt-in through `products.has_warehouse_pricing`) |
| **Code module** | `Inventory` |
| **Depends on** | §27, §32 |

Most products sell at one price across the tenant. A product can opt in (`has_warehouse_pricing = true`, a plain checkbox on the product edit screen) to be priced differently per warehouse, for example because local costs are higher at one location.

```
warehouse_product_prices  [DB: tenant]
id
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable  null = applies to the product / all its variants
variant_key          int      generated: COALESCE(product_variant_id, 0)
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses
price                money
compare_at_price     money    nullable
unique(product_id, variant_key, warehouse_id)
```

- When `has_warehouse_pricing = false`, this table is never read.
- When it is true and the fulfilling warehouse has no row, pricing falls back to the base price. Turning the flag on therefore never requires pricing every warehouse immediately.
- The price is resolved once the fulfilling warehouse is known, at checkout ([§38.4](#384-price-resolution)).

`WarehousePricingService`:

- `setWarehousePrice(Product $p, Warehouse $w, float $price, ?float $compareAtPrice = null, ?ProductVariant $v = null): WarehouseProductPrice`
- `removeWarehousePrice(WarehouseProductPrice $price): void`
- `getPriceForWarehouse(Product $p, Warehouse $w, ?ProductVariant $v = null): ?float`: looks up the variant row first, then the product row, and returns null when there is none
- `listWarehousePrices(Product $p): Collection`

Routes (group `tenant.admin`, core):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Inventory\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/products/{product}/warehouse-prices` | `WarehousePriceController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/products/{product}/warehouse-prices` | `WarehousePriceController@store` |

## 35. Tax

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce). Tax is core to checkout. It has no feature flag of its own. |
| **Code module** | `Tax` |
| **Depends on** | §20, §27, §32 |

### 35.1 Tax Rates

```
tax_rates  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "VAT", "Sales Tax"
country_id           int               World
state_id             int      nullable World; null = country-level rate
tax_class            enum(standard, reduced)  default standard
rate_percentage      percent
is_active            bool     default true
unique(country_id, state_id, tax_class)
```

### 35.2 Calculation Rules

- Tax depends on the **customer's address**, not the tenant's location, because a tenant can sell across regions.
  - For orders that need shipping: the shipping address.
  - For orders with no shippable lines: the billing address, falling back to the customer's default address.
  - For POS sales: the register warehouse's country and state (Assumption A-16).
- For each line, the rate is chosen by the product's `tax_class`:
  - `exempt` means no tax.
  - Otherwise, the active rate matching the country, state and class is used. If there is none, the active country-level rate for the class (`state_id = null`) is used. If there is none of those either, the tax is 0.
- The tax base is the line's `line_net`: the line amount after every promotion discount on it, including its allocated share of order-level discounts (§38.5, Assumption A-19).
- **Tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive prices** (decides UD-16) are a tenant setting, `tenant_settings.prices_include_tax` (default false):
  - `false`: catalogue prices exclude tax. Tax is `line_net × rate / 100`, added on top.
  - `true`: catalogue prices include tax. Tax is extracted: `line_net × rate / (100 + rate)`. The customer pays the shelf price.
  - The setting is snapshotted on `orders.prices_include_tax`. It can be changed at any time, and existing orders are unaffected. The formulas are in [§38.5](#385-order-totals).
- **Shipping tax.** When `tenant_settings.tax_shipping` is true, net shipping is taxed at the destination's `standard` class rate. Otherwise shipping is untaxed.
- The rate and amount are **snapshotted** on each order line (`order_items.tax_rate_applied`, `tax_amount`), and the total on `orders.tax_amount`. Past orders never change when rates change later.

### 35.3 India GST and Saudi ZATCA

- When `india_gst_enabled` is on:
  - Products carry an `hsn_code`.
  - Each line stores a `tax_breakdown` JSON:
    - **intra-state** (the fulfilling warehouse's state equals the destination state): `{cgst: half, sgst: half}`
    - otherwise: `{igst: full}`
  - When the fulfilling warehouse has no state, IGST is used.
- ZATCA QR generation for Saudi invoices is described in [§43.2](#432-invoice-rendering-and-compliance).

### 35.4 Service and Routes

`TaxService` (Tenant):

- `createTaxRate(array $data): TaxRate`
- `updateTaxRate(TaxRate $rate, array $data): TaxRate`
- `deleteTaxRate(TaxRate $rate): void`
- `listTaxRates(array $filters): Collection`
- `getTaxRateForAddress(array $address, string $taxClass): ?TaxRate`
- `calculateForLines(array $lines, array $address, ?Warehouse $origin = null, float $netShipping = 0): array`: `{lines: [{tax_rate_applied, tax_amount, tax_breakdown}], shipping_tax_amount, total}`. Applies `prices_include_tax` and `tax_shipping`.

Routes (group `tenant.admin`, core). There are no customer routes: tax appears as line items in cart and order responses.

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Tax\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/tax-rates` | `TaxRateController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/tax-rates` | `TaxRateController@store` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/tax-rates/{rate}` | `TaxRateController@update` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/tax-rates/{rate}` | `TaxRateController@destroy` |

## 36. Shipping and Delivery

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce). Shipping is bundled into core commerce. |
| **Code module** | `Shipping` |
| **Depends on** | §10 (driver authentication), §20, §32, §39 |

An order is priced with one shipping method, but it is **fulfilled through shipments**. A shipment is one physical parcel or delivery run from one warehouse. An order whose lines sit in two warehouses, or that ships in stages, has several shipments. Each shipment uses one of two fulfilment paths:

- **Courier:** a third-party carrier with its own tracking number.
- **In-house delivery:** the tenant's own driver is assigned, picks up the goods and delivers them. It has its own status trail.

Both paths are modelled as `shipping_methods` with a `fulfillment_type`, so one checkout dropdown can offer "DHL Express" next to "Standard Delivery (in-house)".

### 36.1 Zones and Methods

```
shipping_zones  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string
is_active            bool     default true

shipping_zone_regions  [DB: tenant]
id
shipping_zone_id     fk -> shipping_zones
country_id           int               World
state_id             int      nullable World; null = whole country
unique(shipping_zone_id, country_id, state_id)

shipping_methods  [DB: tenant]
id
shipping_zone_id     fk -> shipping_zones
name                 string            e.g. "Standard", "Express", "In-House Delivery"
fulfillment_type     enum(courier, in_house)
courier_provider     string   nullable  e.g. "DHL"; courier only
cost                 money             flat cost per order in base currency (Assumption A-17)
estimated_days       int      nullable
is_active            bool     default true
```

An address resolves to a zone through the most specific region match: a state match first, then a country-level match.

The shipping columns on orders (`shipping_method_id`, `shipping_address`, `shipping_amount`, `shipping_discount_amount` and `shipping_tax_amount`) are defined in [§39.1](#391-orders-table).

### 36.2 Shipments, Drivers and Delivery Assignments

```
shipments  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
order_id             fk -> orders
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses     every item in the shipment ships from this warehouse
shipping_method_id   fk -> shipping_methods  nullable  defaults to the order's method; staff may override
fulfillment_type     enum(courier, in_house)           copied from the method
carrier              string   nullable  courier name
tracking_number      string   nullable  courier only
tracking_url         string   nullable
status               enum(pending, dispatched, in_transit, delivered, failed, cancelled)  default pending
dispatched_at        datetime nullable
delivered_at         datetime nullable
created_by_user_id   fk -> users  nullable
index(order_id), index(status)
```

```
shipment_items  [DB: tenant]
id
shipment_id          fk -> shipments
order_item_id        fk -> order_items   its warehouse_id must equal shipments.warehouse_id
quantity             qty
unique(shipment_id, order_item_id)
```

Rules:

- A shipment can be created only for a confirmed order. Its items are physical lines. For each line, Σ `shipment_items.quantity` over non-cancelled shipments MUST NOT exceed `order_items.quantity`. This is checked under a lock on the order row.
- `order_items.quantity_shipped` is updated when a shipment becomes `dispatched`, and reduced if that shipment is later `cancelled` before delivery.
- Stock has already been deducted at confirmation (§32.5). A shipment moves goods, not stock balances.
- A digital or service line never appears in a shipment.

```
drivers  [DB: tenant]
id
user_id              fk -> users   nullable  set when the driver is also a staff user
name                 string
phone                string   unique
phone_verified_at    datetime nullable
pin_hash             string   nullable
vehicle_type         string   nullable  e.g. "motorbike", "van"
status               enum(active, inactive)  default active
is_available         bool     default true
```

```
delivery_assignments  [DB: tenant]
id
shipment_id          fk -> shipments   unique (one current assignment per shipment)
driver_id            fk -> drivers
status               enum(assigned, picked_up, en_route, delivered, failed)
assigned_at          datetime
picked_up_at         datetime nullable
delivered_at         datetime nullable
delivery_notes       text     nullable  e.g. reason for a failed delivery
(media: proof_of_delivery)
```

- OTP codes for driver login are held in the cache with a short TTL. They are never stored in a table (Assumption A-18).
- A driver can be assigned only to a shipment with `fulfillment_type = in_house`.

**Shipment status from delivery events:**

| Event | Shipment status |
|---|---|
| Courier: staff set the tracking number and mark dispatched. In-house: `picked_up` | `dispatched` |
| Courier `in_transit`; in-house `en_route` | `in_transit` |
| Courier `delivered`; in-house `delivered` | `delivered` |
| In-house `failed` | `failed`. `delivery.assignment_failed` is sent, and the shipment can be reassigned, which returns it to `pending`. |

**Effect on `orders.status`** (applied by `ShipmentService` after every shipment change, §39.4):

- Some physical quantity dispatched, some not: `partially_shipped`.
- Every physical line fully dispatched: `shipped`.
- Every non-cancelled shipment delivered and every physical line fully shipped: `delivered`. `order.delivered` is sent once, on this transition.

`order.shipped` is sent by `markDispatched()` for **each** shipment, with that shipment's items and tracking data, so a customer with a split order is told about every parcel.

### 36.3 Services

`ShippingZoneService`:

- `createZone(array $data): ShippingZone`: includes `regions[]`
- `updateZone(ShippingZone $zone, array $data): ShippingZone`
- `deleteZone(ShippingZone $zone): void`
- `listZones(): Collection`
- `resolveZoneForAddress(array $address): ?ShippingZone`

`ShippingMethodService`:

- `createMethod(array $data): ShippingMethod`
- `updateMethod(ShippingMethod $m, array $data): ShippingMethod`
- `deleteMethod(ShippingMethod $m): void`
- `listMethodsForZone(ShippingZone $zone): Collection`

`ShippingService`:

- `getAvailableMethods(array $address): Collection`: the resolved zone's active methods, courier and in-house together
- `calculateShippingCost(ShippingMethod $method, array $lines): float`: the flat method cost in v1. Returns 0 when no line needs shipping.
- `getTracking(Order $order): array`: one entry per shipment, with its items, status, carrier, tracking number and URL, and, for in-house shipments, the assignment's status trail

`ShipmentService`:

- `createShipment(Order $order, Warehouse $warehouse, array $items, array $data = []): Shipment`: `items` are `[{order_item_id, quantity}]`
- `createShipmentsForOrder(Order $order): Collection`: one shipment per warehouse covering every unshipped quantity. This is the one-click default.
- `updateTracking(Shipment $s, array $data): Shipment`: courier only; carrier, tracking number and URL
- `markDispatched(Shipment $s): void`
- `markInTransit(Shipment $s): void`
- `markDelivered(Shipment $s): void`
- `cancelShipment(Shipment $s): void`: allowed only before `delivered`
- `listShipments(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`

`DriverService`:

- `createDriver(array $data): Driver`
- `updateDriver(Driver $d, array $data): Driver`
- `deactivateDriver(Driver $d): void`
- `setAvailability(Driver $d, bool $isAvailable): void`
- `listAvailableDrivers(): Collection`
- `listDriverDeliveries(Driver $d, array $filters): Collection`: the "my deliveries today" view

`DeliveryAssignmentService`:

- `assignDriver(Shipment $shipment, Driver $driver): DeliveryAssignment`
- `reassignDriver(DeliveryAssignment $a, Driver $newDriver): void`
- `markPickedUp(DeliveryAssignment $a): void`
- `markEnRoute(DeliveryAssignment $a): void`: sends `order.out_for_delivery`
- `markDelivered(DeliveryAssignment $a, ?UploadedFile $proof = null): void`
- `markFailed(DeliveryAssignment $a, string $reason): void`
- `getAssignmentForShipment(Shipment $shipment): ?DeliveryAssignment`

Each assignment method updates its shipment through `ShipmentService`, which then derives the order status.

Driver authentication is defined in [§10.3](#103-authentication-services).

## 37. Promotions: Coupons and Flash Sales

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Promotions` |
| **Depends on** | §26, §27, §28, §32 |
| **Integration hooks** | Marketplace (seller-funded promotions, §50), POS (§51), reports (§61) |

This module owns every price reduction that is not a unit price. It contains the **discount engine** (`PromotionEngine`), which is the only code that decides which discounts apply to a basket and how much each is worth. Cart quotes (§38), checkout (§38.6), POS sales (§51) and back-office order creation all call it. Controllers never compute discounts.

### 37.1 Model and Rationale

A five-level model (Promotion → Discount Plan → Discount → Coupon Plan → Coupon) was considered and **rejected**. Each extra level would duplicate the same rule fields, and none adds behaviour that the smaller model cannot express. The model has three concepts and one ledger:

| Concept | Table | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Promotion** | `promotions` | The rule: what is discounted, by how much, when, for whom, how often, and how it combines with other promotions. A promotion is either **automatic** (applies whenever eligible) or **coupon-triggered** (applies only when one of its codes is entered). It replaces both "discount plan" and "discount". A reusable template is simply an inactive promotion that is copied with the duplicate route. |
| **Promotion target** | `promotion_targets` | Normalised include and exclude rows that restrict a promotion to products, variants, categories, brands, sellers, warehouses, customers or customer groups. |
| **Coupon** | `coupons` | A code that unlocks a coupon-triggered promotion. One promotion owns any number of codes: one public code ("SAVE20"), or thousands of generated single-use codes. The promotion therefore plays the role of the "coupon plan". |
| **Redemption** | `promotion_redemptions` | The append-only record of one promotion applied to one order, with a snapshot of the rule and the amount. It drives usage limits, the redemption lifecycle, reporting and audit. |

What each rejected level would have added, and where that need is met instead:

- **Discount plan vs discount:** a plan reused by several discounts. Met by duplicating a promotion. Sharing live rule rows between campaigns would make a change to one campaign silently alter another.
- **Coupon plan vs coupon:** code-generation settings. These are parameters of the generate route (§37.9), not stored state.

Flash sales (§37.7) stay separate. They are a **price layer**: they change the unit price that is shown on the product page and carry a stock-like quantity cap. Promotions are **discounts**: they reduce an already-priced basket.

**Discount types in v1** are percentage, fixed amount and free shipping. Buy-X-get-Y, tiered ("spend more, save more") and bundle-price promotions are deferred (Appendix C). They would add a `discount_type` value and a rule payload to `promotions` and a strategy inside `PromotionEngine`, without new tables. The model does not need to change to add them later.

Customer-group discounts and seller-funded discounts are promotions with the matching targets (§37.3, §37.6). They are not separate mechanisms.

### 37.2 Promotions Table

```
promotions  [DB: tenant]  soft deletes, audited
id
name                      string            internal name
public_label              string   nullable customer-facing text, e.g. "20% off shoes"; falls back to name
description               text     nullable internal notes
trigger                   enum(automatic, coupon)
scope                     enum(line, order, shipping)
discount_type             enum(percentage, fixed_amount, free_shipping)
discount_value            decimal(18,4) nullable  percentage: 0 < v ≤ 100; fixed_amount: money in base currency;
                                                 null for free_shipping
max_discount_amount       money    nullable  cap on the discount this promotion gives one order (base currency)
min_subtotal_amount       money    nullable  eligible subtotal must be at least this (base currency)
max_subtotal_amount       money    nullable  eligible subtotal must be at most this (base currency)
min_eligible_quantity     qty      nullable  eligible quantity must be at least this
max_eligible_quantity     qty      nullable  eligible quantity must be at most this
starts_at                 datetime nullable  null = immediately
ends_at                   datetime nullable  null = open-ended
valid_days_of_week        tinyint  nullable  bitmask, ISO order: Mon=1, Tue=2, Wed=4, Thu=8, Fri=16, Sat=32, Sun=64;
                                             null = every day
valid_time_from           time     nullable  tenant timezone; both or neither of the two time columns are set
valid_time_to             time     nullable  a window that wraps midnight (22:00 to 02:00) is allowed
applies_to_online         bool     default true   storefront checkout, admin, WooCommerce and social orders
applies_to_pos            bool     default true   POS sales, including restaurant table orders
applies_to_sale_items     bool     default false  whether lines priced by a flash sale are eligible
first_order_only          bool     default false
usage_limit_total         int      nullable  null = unlimited
usage_limit_per_customer  int      nullable  null = unlimited
times_redeemed            int      default 0  reserved + committed redemptions (§37.5); never edited by hand
is_exclusive              bool     default false  when applied, no other promotion applies to the order (§37.6)
priority                  int      default 0      higher is evaluated first
seller_id                 fk -> sellers  nullable  set = seller-funded (§37.6, §50.4)
is_active                 bool     default true
created_by_user_id        fk -> users  nullable
index(is_active, trigger), index(starts_at), index(ends_at)
```

**Field naming rule.** Every threshold is named `min_*` or `max_*` for what it bounds, and `max_discount_amount` is the only field that bounds the discount itself. The request "20% off, minimum order ₦20,000, maximum discount ₦10,000" is stored as `discount_type = percentage`, `discount_value = 20`, `min_subtotal_amount = 20000`, `max_discount_amount = 10000`. A ₦30,000 basket gets ₦6,000 off. A ₦80,000 basket gets ₦10,000 off (20% would be ₦16,000, capped). A ₦15,000 basket is not eligible.

**Validation** (`PromotionService`, rejected with 422):

- `scope = shipping` if and only if `discount_type = free_shipping`. Partial shipping discounts are not supported.
- `discount_value` is required unless `discount_type = free_shipping`. A percentage must satisfy `0 < v ≤ 100`.
- When both are set: `min_subtotal_amount ≤ max_subtotal_amount`, `min_eligible_quantity ≤ max_eligible_quantity`, and `starts_at < ends_at`.
- At least one of `applies_to_online` and `applies_to_pos` is true.
- A promotion with `seller_id` may target only that seller's products. Its `promotion_targets` MUST include `seller = seller_id` and MUST NOT include products of other sellers.
- `usage_limit_total` cannot be lowered below `times_redeemed`.
- Once a promotion has redemptions, `scope`, `discount_type`, `discount_value` and `trigger` cannot change. Staff end it and create a new promotion. Redemption snapshots already protect history, but this rule keeps reports meaningful.

**Days of week: representation trade-off.** A bitmask in one `tinyint` is used, not a JSON array or a pivot table.

- It is one column, needs no join, and a "valid now" check is a single `valid_days_of_week & :todayBit` expression.
- It cannot hold invalid or duplicate days.
- Its cost is readability in raw SQL. The model casts it to and from an array of ISO day numbers (`[1, 5]` = Monday and Friday), and the API accepts and returns that array. The bitmask is never exposed.
- A pivot table would only be justified if days carried their own data (per-day time windows). They do not. A promotion with different hours on different days is two promotions.

**Money and currency.** Money columns are in the base currency. For a basket in another currency (§48), the engine converts the basket's amounts to the base currency at the rate used for pricing that basket when it checks thresholds, and converts fixed amounts and caps into the basket currency when it computes the discount. Currency conversion itself is §48.

**Time evaluation.** Windows and days are evaluated in `tenant_settings.timezone`, at the moment of the quote or of the checkout commit. A time window that has `valid_time_from > valid_time_to` wraps midnight: it is valid when `now ≥ from OR now < to`, and the day-of-week check uses the day on which the window started.

### 37.3 Promotion Targets

```
promotion_targets  [DB: tenant]
id
promotion_id         fk -> promotions
target_type          enum(product, product_variant, category, brand, seller, warehouse, customer, customer_group)
target_id            int               id in the table named by target_type
mode                 enum(include, exclude)
unique(promotion_id, target_type, target_id)
index(target_type, target_id)
```

`target_id` is polymorphic by a fixed enum, not a morph type, because the set of types is closed. The service validates that the row exists.

**Matching rules:**

- **Line dimensions** are `product`, `product_variant`, `category`, `brand`, `seller` and `warehouse`. A line is **eligible** when:
  - for every line dimension that has at least one `include` row, the line matches at least one of them. Dimensions are ANDed; rows within a dimension are ORed.
  - the line matches no `exclude` row of any line dimension. Exclusion always wins.
  - A promotion with no line-dimension include rows applies to every line, subject to exclusions.
- **Category** matches a product in that category or in any descendant category, across all of the product's categories, not only the primary one.
- **Product** matches every variant of the product. **Product variant** matches one variant only.
- **Warehouse** matches the line's fulfilling warehouse. Before a warehouse is chosen (cart quotes, §38.3), warehouse-targeted promotions are not applied. They are applied at checkout and POS, where the warehouse is known.
- **Buyer dimensions** are `customer` and `customer_group`. Include rows restrict the promotion to those buyers. Exclude rows block them. A guest belongs to no customer and to the default customer group. A customer with no group belongs to the default group (§26.3).
- Bundles are matched by the bundle product itself, never by their children.
- Gift-card purchase lines and `exchange_credit` value are never eligible for any promotion.

**A limit per customer group** is expressed as a promotion that includes that group, with `usage_limit_total`. Different limits for different groups are different promotions. There is no per-group limit column.

### 37.4 Coupons

```
coupons  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
promotion_id          fk -> promotions      promotions.trigger must be coupon
code                  string   unique       stored trimmed and upper-cased; matched case-insensitively
usage_limit           int      nullable     per-code cap; 1 = single-use; null = only the promotion's limits apply
times_redeemed        int      default 0    reserved + committed redemptions of this code
assigned_customer_id  fk -> customers  nullable  set = only this customer may use the code
expires_at            datetime nullable     effective end = the earlier of this and promotions.ends_at
is_active             bool     default true
index(promotion_id)
```

- A cart holds at most one coupon (`carts.coupon_id`, §38.1). A coupon and a gift card can be used on the same order. A gift card is a tender, not a promotion (§46).
- A coupon is valid only when its promotion is valid. Every rule of the promotion applies, plus the coupon's own `usage_limit`, `assigned_customer_id`, `expires_at` and `is_active`.
- A code must be 4 to 32 characters from `A–Z`, `0–9` and `-`. Generated codes exclude the ambiguous characters `0`, `O`, `1` and `I`.
- A coupon with redemptions cannot be deleted. It can only be deactivated (409 otherwise).

### 37.5 Redemptions and the Redemption Lifecycle

```
promotion_redemptions  [DB: tenant]
id
promotion_id               fk -> promotions
coupon_id                  fk -> coupons  nullable  set for coupon-triggered promotions
order_id                   fk -> orders
customer_id                fk -> customers  nullable
customer_email             string   nullable  lower-cased snapshot; enforces per-customer limits for guests
promotion_name_snapshot    string
public_label_snapshot      string   nullable
coupon_code_snapshot       string   nullable
scope_snapshot             string
discount_type_snapshot     string
discount_value_snapshot    decimal(18,4) nullable
discount_amount            money             order currency
base_discount_amount       money             base currency, at orders.exchange_rate_used
seller_id                  fk -> sellers  nullable  snapshot of promotions.seller_id
status                     enum(reserved, committed, released, reversed)
over_limit                 bool     default false  offline POS sale synced after the limit was reached (§51.6)
committed_at               datetime nullable
released_at                datetime nullable  set for released and reversed
unique(promotion_id, order_id)
index(promotion_id, status), index(customer_id, promotion_id), index(customer_email, promotion_id)
```

**Lifecycle:**

| Event | Redemption status | `times_redeemed` on promotion and coupon | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cart quote, coupon applied to cart | none. Carts never consume usage. | unchanged | §38.3 |
| Checkout commit (order created) | `reserved` | +1 | §38.6 |
| Payment attempt fails | stays `reserved`, so the customer can retry the same order | unchanged | §40.2 |
| Order confirmed (§39.4) | `committed`, with `committed_at` | unchanged | §39.4 |
| Unpaid order expires, or is cancelled before confirmation | `released` | −1 | §39.5 |
| Confirmed order cancelled before completion | `reversed` | −1 | §39.5 |
| Return or refund after completion | stays `committed`. Usage stays consumed. | unchanged | §41 |

Because an unpaid order either gets paid or expires (§32.5, `unpaid_order_expiry_minutes`), a failed or abandoned checkout never consumes usage permanently. `times_redeemed` is always equal to the count of `reserved` and `committed` rows. `promotions:recount` (§77.6) recomputes it for support purposes.

**Concurrency-safe reservation** (`PromotionRedemptionService::reserve()`, called inside the checkout or POS commit transaction, §38.6):

1. Lock the promotion rows applied by the engine, `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` in ascending `id` order, then the coupon row. Ascending order across every caller prevents deadlocks.
2. Re-check under the lock, against the locked values:
   - `is_active`, not soft-deleted, time window, days and channel
   - `usage_limit_total IS NULL OR times_redeemed < usage_limit_total`
   - coupon `usage_limit IS NULL OR coupon.times_redeemed < usage_limit`, `is_active`, `expires_at` and `assigned_customer_id`
   - `usage_limit_per_customer`: the count of this promotion's `reserved` and `committed` redemptions for the same `customer_id`, or, for guests, the same `customer_email`
   - `first_order_only`: the buyer, by `customer_id` or by `customer_email`, has no other order whose status is not `cancelled`
3. If any check fails, the whole commit rolls back and the API returns **409** `promotion_unavailable` with the promotion's ID in `details`. The client re-quotes the cart. No order is created.
4. Otherwise, increment `times_redeemed` on the promotion and the coupon, and insert one `reserved` redemption per applied promotion.

The promotion row lock serialises every redemption of that promotion, so the per-customer and first-order counts in step 2 cannot race. With `usage_limit_total = 100`, the 101st concurrent commit waits for the lock, sees `times_redeemed = 100`, and fails. The lock is held only for the remainder of the commit transaction, which never contains network calls (§38.6).

`PromotionRedemptionService` also provides `commit(Order)` (called by `confirmOrder()`), `release(Order)` (called by cancellation and expiry before confirmation) and `reverse(Order)` (called by cancellation after confirmation). Each locks the same rows in the same order, is idempotent by redemption status, and adjusts `times_redeemed` exactly once.

### 37.6 Discount Engine

`PromotionEngine::evaluate(PricingContext $context): PromotionResult` is a **pure** evaluation. It reads promotions and writes nothing. The same input gives the same output.

- **`PricingContext`** carries:
  - each line: product, variant, category IDs including ancestors, brand, seller, warehouse (nullable), quantity, the resolved unit price and its `source` (§38.4)
  - the buyer: customer ID, customer group, normalised email and whether this is a first order
  - the channel (`online` or `pos`), the basket currency and its rate, the coupon code (nullable), the shipping amount (nullable) and the evaluation time
- **`PromotionResult`** carries:
  - per line: `discount_amount` and `seller_funded_discount_amount`
  - the order-level `discount_amount` and `shipping_discount_amount`
  - the applied promotions, each with its amount
  - for a coupon that did not apply, a `coupon_rejection_reason` (§37.8)

**Algorithm:**

1. **Candidates.** All active automatic promotions whose window contains the evaluation time, plus the promotion of the entered coupon when the coupon is valid. The automatic set is read from the per-tenant promotion cache (§74).
2. **Buyer and channel eligibility.** Remove candidates that fail the day and time checks, the channel flag, buyer targets, `first_order_only`, remaining `usage_limit_total`, or `usage_limit_per_customer`. These checks are advisory here. The authoritative check is under lock at commit (§37.5).
3. **Eligible lines** per candidate, by the matching rules (§37.3). Lines whose price `source = flash_sale` are removed unless `applies_to_sale_items` is true.
4. **Thresholds.** The eligible subtotal is Σ `unit_price × quantity` over the eligible lines, before any discount. The eligible quantity is Σ `quantity` over them. Both must lie within the promotion's `min_*` and `max_*` bounds. A candidate with no eligible lines, or outside the bounds, is removed.
5. **Raw amount.**
   - `percentage`: the eligible base × `discount_value` / 100.
   - `fixed_amount`: `discount_value`, capped at the eligible base.
   - `free_shipping`: the shipping amount, or 0 when no shipping amount is known yet.

   Then cap at `max_discount_amount`, and round (§5.3). For `line` promotions, the eligible base is the eligible lines' amounts. For `order` promotions, it is those amounts **after** line promotions from step 6. The threshold in step 4 still uses the pre-discount basket, so "minimum order ₦20,000" always means the basket value the customer sees.
6. **Selection** (the conflict rules). Rank candidates by `priority` desc, then raw amount desc (largest wins), then `id` asc. Walk the ranking and apply a candidate only when all of these hold:
   1. no already-applied promotion has `is_exclusive = true`
   2. the candidate is not exclusive, or nothing has been applied yet
   3. its **slot** is free:
      - at most **one line promotion per line**. A line promotion claims its eligible lines, and a later line promotion is re-evaluated (steps 4 and 5) on the lines that are still unclaimed.
      - at most **one order promotion**
      - at most **one shipping promotion**
   4. at most **one coupon-triggered promotion** per order. This follows from one coupon per cart.

   So the maximum is one discount per line, plus one order discount, plus free shipping. Every rule is deterministic, and the result is independent of database row order.
7. **Allocation.** The order-level discount is allocated to its eligible lines in proportion to their post-line-discount amounts, by the largest-remainder method at the currency's minor unit. Ties go to the lower line position. Each line's `discount_amount` is its line promotion plus its share of the order promotion. `seller_funded_discount_amount` is the part that came from promotions with `seller_id` set.
8. **Never negative.** No line's discount exceeds its `unit_price × quantity`. The shipping discount never exceeds `shipping_amount`.

**Interaction with other layers** (the full chain is §38.4 and §38.5):

- Flash-sale and warehouse prices are unit prices, resolved before the engine runs.
- Tax is calculated **after** discounts, on each line's discounted amount (§35.2).
- Free shipping reduces the shipping charge, never line amounts.
- Reward points (§54) are applied after promotions. Gift cards (§46) are a tender after the total.

**Who funds a discount.** A discount from a promotion with `seller_id` is seller-funded: it reduces the seller's ledger gross (§50.4). Every other discount is tenant-funded: the seller's gross is computed before it, and the tenant absorbs the cost.

**Previews.** `PromotionEngine::previewForProducts(Collection $products, ?Customer $customer): array` returns, per product, the automatic line promotions the current buyer would receive with no threshold conditions. Storefront product responses use it for "20% off" badges. Checkout always re-evaluates the whole basket.

### 37.7 Flash Sales

```
flash_sales  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
name                 string
starts_at            datetime
ends_at              datetime
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
flash_sale_products  [DB: tenant]
id
flash_sale_id        fk -> flash_sales
product_id           fk -> products
sale_price           money             base currency; applies to every variant of the product
quantity_limit       qty      nullable  null = unlimited
quantity_claimed     qty      default 0  quantity on reserved or confirmed orders
unique(flash_sale_id, product_id)
```

- A product MUST NOT be in two flash sales whose windows overlap. This is validated on `addProduct` (Assumption A-20).
- A flash sale is a price layer (§38.4 step 3). It applies only while `quantity_claimed < quantity_limit`.
- **Claiming** uses the same pattern as promotion reservation. In the commit transaction, `FlashSaleService::claim()` locks each affected `flash_sale_products` row in ascending `id` order, checks `quantity_claimed + line quantity ≤ quantity_limit`, and increments. If the check fails, the commit fails with **409** `price_changed` and the client re-quotes. **Release** (`FlashSaleService::release()`) decrements on unpaid expiry and on cancellation before completion, exactly like `PromotionRedemptionService::release()`.
- A line is claimed only when its price source is `flash_sale`. A line quantity is never split between the sale price and the regular price.

### 37.8 Services

`PromotionService` (Tenant; administration):

- `createPromotion(array $data): Promotion`: accepts `targets[]` and applies the §37.2 validation
- `updatePromotion(Promotion $p, array $data): Promotion`
- `syncTargets(Promotion $p, array $targets): void`
- `duplicatePromotion(Promotion $p): Promotion`: copies the rule and targets. The copy is inactive, with `times_redeemed = 0` and no coupons.
- `deletePromotion(Promotion $p): void`: a soft delete. Redemptions keep their snapshots.
- `listPromotions(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`
- `getUsageStats(Promotion $p): array`: redemptions by status, total discount and orders

`CouponService` (Tenant):

- `createCoupon(Promotion $p, array $data): Coupon`
- `generateCoupons(Promotion $p, int $count, array $options): int`: `options` are `prefix`, `length` (default 10) and `usage_limit`. At most 1,000 codes are generated synchronously. Larger batches (up to 100,000) run as the queued `GenerateCouponCodes` job (§72). Uniqueness is guaranteed by the unique index, and a collision is retried.
- `updateCoupon(Coupon $c, array $data): Coupon`
- `deleteCoupon(Coupon $c): void`: blocked when redemptions exist
- `findByCode(string $code): ?Coupon`: normalises the code
- `validateForCart(string $code, Cart $cart): array`: `{valid, reason, discount_amount}`. It runs the engine with the code and reports whether the coupon's promotion was applied. `reason` is one of: `not_found`, `inactive`, `not_started`, `expired`, `not_valid_now`, `channel_not_allowed`, `customer_not_eligible`, `first_order_only`, `usage_limit_reached`, `customer_limit_reached`, `minimum_not_met`, `maximum_exceeded`, `no_eligible_items`, `not_combinable`.

`PromotionEngine` (Tenant; §37.6):

- `evaluate(PricingContext $context): PromotionResult`
- `previewForProducts(Collection $products, ?Customer $customer): array`

`PromotionRedemptionService` (Tenant; §37.5):

- `reserve(Order $order, PromotionResult $result): void`
- `commit(Order $order): void`
- `release(Order $order): void`
- `reverse(Order $order): void`
- `recount(Promotion $promotion): void`: operational repair only (§77.6)

`FlashSaleService` (Tenant):

- `createFlashSale(array $data): FlashSale`
- `updateFlashSale(FlashSale $s, array $data): FlashSale`
- `deleteFlashSale(FlashSale $s): void`: blocked while any product has `quantity_claimed > 0`. Staff end the sale instead.
- `addProduct(FlashSale $s, Product $p, float $salePrice, ?float $qtyLimit = null): FlashSaleProduct`
- `removeProduct(FlashSale $s, Product $p): void`

## 38. Cart, Pricing and Checkout

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Cart` (cart and pricing), `Checkout` |
| **Depends on** | §26, §27, §28, §32, §34, §35, §36, §37, §39 |
| **Integration hooks** | Gift cards (§46), installments (§47), multi-currency (§48), sales agents (§52), reward points (§54) |

### 38.1 Tables

```
carts  [DB: tenant]
id
customer_id              fk -> customers  nullable unique  (one active cart per customer)
guest_token              string   nullable unique          opaque random token (UUID)
currency_code            char(3)           base currency unless multi_currency (§48)
coupon_id                fk -> coupons     nullable  at most one coupon (§37.4)
gift_card_id             fk -> gift_cards  nullable  (§46)
reward_points_to_redeem  int      nullable           (§54)
last_activity_at         datetime
index(last_activity_at)
```

Exactly one of `customer_id` and `guest_token` is set on a cart.

```
cart_items  [DB: tenant]
id
cart_id              fk -> carts
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
variant_key          int      generated: COALESCE(product_variant_id, 0)
quantity             qty
unique(cart_id, product_id, variant_key)
```

Carts never store prices, discounts or reservations. Totals are recalculated on every read, and a cart never holds stock or promotion usage.

### 38.2 Guest Carts and Merge

- A shopper's first cart action with no customer token and no `X-Guest-Token` creates a guest cart with a freshly generated `guest_token`. The token is returned in the response body and in the `X-Guest-Token` response header. The client stores it (for example in local storage) and sends it on every later cart, checkout and order request. This makes the cart survive reloads before the shopper ever registers.
- Guest carts with no activity for 30 days are deleted by the daily tenant maintenance job (§72.2). Their tokens stop working at that point (Assumption A-66).
- **Merge on login and registration:** when `POST /api/auth/login` or `POST /api/auth/register` carries `X-Guest-Token`, the guest cart's items are merged into the customer's cart (or the guest cart becomes it). Quantities of overlapping items are summed. The guest cart row is then deleted. This happens automatically inside the authentication flow, so there is no separate merge endpoint.

### 38.3 Cart Service

`CartService` (Tenant):

- `getOrCreateCart(?Customer $customer, ?string $guestToken): Cart`: the single entry point
- `mergeGuestCartIntoCustomer(string $guestToken, Customer $customer): Cart`
- `addItem(Cart $cart, Product $p, float $qty, ?ProductVariant $v = null): CartItem`: validates `is_active`, the unit's decimal rules, and availability
- `updateItemQuantity(CartItem $item, float $qty): CartItem`
- `removeItem(Cart $cart, CartItem $item): void`
- `clearCart(Cart $cart): void`
- `applyCoupon(Cart $cart, string $code): array`: stores the coupon only when `CouponService::validateForCart()` reports it valid. Otherwise it returns 422 with the rejection `reason` (§37.8).
- `removeCoupon(Cart $cart): void`
- `applyGiftCard(Cart $cart, string $code): array`: requires `gift_cards`; delegates to `GiftCardService` (§46)
- `removeGiftCard(Cart $cart): void`
- `setCurrency(Cart $cart, string $currencyCode): Cart`: requires `multi_currency`. Removes an applied gift card whose currency no longer matches (§46.3).
- `applyRewardPoints(Cart $cart, int $points): array`: requires `reward_points` and a customer cart; delegates validation to `RewardPointService` (§54)
- `getTotals(Cart $cart, ?array $address = null, ?ShippingMethod $method = null): array`: a **quote** built by `CheckoutService::quote()` (§38.6 steps 1 to 8), with no writes. It returns lines with their prices and discounts, the applied promotions, subtotal, discounts, tax, shipping, reward points discount, gift card applied, total, amount due and `quote_hash`. Tax and shipping are null when no address is given. A coupon that no longer applies (for example, the basket fell below the minimum) stays on the cart and is reported with its rejection `reason`.

### 38.4 Price Resolution

`PricingService::resolveUnitPrice(Product $p, ?ProductVariant $v, ?Warehouse $w, string $currencyCode): PriceResult`

`PriceResult` contains `unit_price`, `compare_at_price`, `currency_code`, `source` (`base`, `warehouse`, `currency` or `flash_sale`) and `is_estimated`.

This method is the **only** place a unit price is computed. Cart, checkout, POS, the storefront listing and filters, and reports all call it. A unit price is resolved through these layers, in this order:

1. **Base price:** `variant.price`, falling back to `product.price`. For a marketplace product, this is the price the seller set.
2. **Warehouse price:** if `has_warehouse_pricing` is set and `$w` is given, `WarehousePricingService::getPriceForWarehouse()` replaces the base when it returns a price.
3. **Currency** (only when `$currencyCode` differs from the base currency and `multi_currency` is enabled):
   - If an explicit `product_prices` row exists for the currency (a variant row first, then the product row), it **replaces** the result of steps 1 and 2 (`source = currency`). An explicit currency price is the tenant's deliberate price for that market, so warehouse prices do not adjust it.
   - Otherwise, the result of steps 1 and 2 is converted with `CurrencyService` at the current reference rate (`is_estimated = true`).
4. **Flash sale:** if an active flash sale with remaining quantity covers the product (§37.7), its `sale_price`, converted to `$currencyCode` when needed, becomes the unit price **only if it is lower** than the result of step 3 (`source = flash_sale`). A sale never raises a price.
5. **Rounding:** the unit price is rounded to the currency's minor unit (§5.3).

This ordering resolves UD-17. It is deterministic, and it has only one currency conversion.

**Not unit-price layers.** These act on the priced basket, in this order, and never change `unit_price`:

| Order | Layer | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | Promotions (line, then order, then shipping), including customer-group and seller-funded promotions | §37.6 |
| 7 | Reward points discount | §54 |
| 8 | Tax, on each line's discounted amount, and on shipping when `tax_shipping` is on | §35.2 |
| 9 | Shipping charge, less any free-shipping discount | §36.3 |
| 10 | Gift card, as a tender against the total | §46 |

Per-channel price lists (a different POS and online price for the same SKU) are not supported. A channel-specific price is expressed as a promotion with `applies_to_online` or `applies_to_pos` (§37.2).

### 38.5 Order Totals

These definitions are authoritative for carts, orders, POS sales and every module that derives an amount from an order. All amounts are in `orders.currency_code`.

**Lines:**

- `line_subtotal` = `unit_price × quantity`, rounded
- `discount_amount` = the engine's per-line discount (§37.6): the line promotion plus the line's share of the order promotion
- `line_net` = `line_subtotal − discount_amount`
- `tax_amount` = the line tax on `line_net` (§35.2)
  - When prices exclude tax: `line_net × rate / 100`
  - When prices include tax (`tenant_settings.prices_include_tax`): `line_net × rate / (100 + rate)`
  - Rounded per line
- `line_total` = `line_net + tax_amount` when prices exclude tax, or `line_net` when prices include tax

**Order:**

- `subtotal` = Σ `line_subtotal`
- `discount_amount` = Σ line `discount_amount`
- `shipping_amount` = the chosen method's charge (§36.3)
- `shipping_discount_amount` = the free-shipping discount (§37.6)
- `shipping_tax_amount` = tax on `shipping_amount − shipping_discount_amount` when `tax_shipping` is on, computed like a line in the `standard` tax class. It is 0 otherwise.
- `tax_amount` = Σ line `tax_amount` + `shipping_tax_amount`
- `reward_points_discount_amount` comes from §54
- `total`:
  - When prices exclude tax: `subtotal − discount_amount + shipping_amount − shipping_discount_amount + tax_amount − reward_points_discount_amount`
  - When prices include tax: `subtotal − discount_amount + shipping_amount − shipping_discount_amount − reward_points_discount_amount`. The tax is contained in the amounts.
- `gift_card_amount_applied` is a payment instrument, not a discount ([§46](#46-gift-cards))
- **Amount due through other payments** = `total − gift_card_amount_applied`

**Derived amounts used by other modules:**

- **Net merchandise amount** = Σ (`line_total − tax_amount`) over the lines. This is the value of goods sold, excluding tax and shipping and after promotions. It is the revenue base (§57.3), the commission base for sales agents (§52) and the points-earning base (§54), each converted to the base currency at `exchange_rate_used`.
- **Net shipping amount** = `shipping_amount − shipping_discount_amount`, less `shipping_tax_amount` when prices include tax.

**Rounding.** Every stored amount is rounded half-up to the currency's minor unit when it is computed (§5.3). Order amounts are sums of rounded line amounts. They are never recomputed from unrounded intermediates, so `total` always equals the sum of its stored parts.

Reward points reduce the total but not the tax base (Assumption A-67).

### 38.6 Checkout Flow

`CheckoutService` (Tenant):

- `quote(Cart $cart, array $checkoutData): Quote`: steps 1 to 8 below, with no writes. It backs `getTotals()` and is re-run by `placeOrder()`.
- `placeOrder(Cart $cart, array $checkoutData): Order`: backs `POST /api/orders`

`POST /api/orders` requires an `Idempotency-Key` header ([§70.11](#7011-idempotency)). A retry with the same key returns the original response and never creates a second order.

1. **Resolve the buyer.** An authenticated customer, or a guest. A guest requires the effective `guest_checkout_enabled` (tenant setting AND platform ceiling) and a `guest_email`. `guest_phone` is optional.
2. **Validate lines.** Every product and variant must be active, and every quantity must satisfy its unit's rules.
3. **Shipping.** If any line is physical (simple, variable or bundle): require a shipping address (a customer `address_id`, or an inline address for guests) and a `shipping_method_id` that is available for the address's zone. Otherwise, shipping is skipped.
4. **Pick fulfilment warehouses** for physical lines ([§32.4](#324-inventory-table-and-fulfilment-warehouse)). Quotes use the same selection, so a quote and the checkout price the same warehouse unless stock has moved in between.
5. **Price every line** ([§38.4](#384-price-resolution)) in `carts.currency_code`, using the chosen warehouse.
6. **Promotions:** `PromotionEngine::evaluate()` with the cart's coupon and `channel = online` (§37.6).
7. **Reward points:** the requested points are validated against the balance and the cap (§54).
8. **Tax, shipping and totals** ([§38.5](#385-order-totals)).
9. **Price guard.** The client sends the `quote_hash` it displayed. If the recomputed quote differs, the request fails with **409** `totals_changed`, and `details` carries the fresh quote. The customer is never charged an amount they did not see.
10. **Optional inputs:**
    - `sales_agent_code`, when `sales_agents` is enabled (§52)
    - `installment_plan` choice, when `installments` is enabled (§47)
    - `gateway`, the payment provider for the online payment
11. **Commit** in one short database transaction. It contains **no network calls**:
    1. `OrderService::createOrder()` ([§39.5](#395-order-service)). It enforces `max_orders_per_month`, snapshots prices, discounts, costs and taxes, stores the request's key in `orders.idempotency_key` (a duplicate returns the existing order, §70.11), and reserves stock for each physical line (§32.5).
    2. `FlashSaleService::claim()` (§37.7).
    3. `PromotionRedemptionService::reserve()` (§37.5).
    4. `GiftCardService::redeemGiftCard()`, which locks the card row and records an `order_payments` row with `payment_method = gift_card` (§40.1).
    5. `RewardPointService::redeemPoints()`, which locks the balance row (§54).
    6. `OrderService::recalculatePaymentStatus()`. When the amount due is 0, this marks the order paid and confirms it (§39.4).
    7. `CartService::clearCart()`.

    Any failure in steps 11.1 to 11.7 rolls back everything. Stock (409 `stock_conflict`), flash-sale quantity (409 `price_changed`) and promotion usage (409 `promotion_unavailable`) are all re-checked under row locks here. Locks are always taken in this order: inventory rows, flash-sale rows, promotion rows, coupon rows, gift card row, reward points row. Within each table, rows are locked in ascending `id` order (§32.6).
12. **After commit:** if the order is unpaid, `ExpireUnpaidOrder` is dispatched with a delay of `tenant_settings.unpaid_order_expiry_minutes` (§39.5). `order.new_order_received` is dispatched by `createOrder()` after commit.
13. Respond with the order. If the order is not paid, the client continues with `POST /api/orders/{order}/pay` ([§40.2](#402-online-gateway-payments)).

### 38.7 Routes

Group `tenant.storefront`, core. This group uses `auth.as.optional:customer` plus `guest.token`, so an authenticated customer or a guest carrying `X-Guest-Token` can call these routes.

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Cart\...` / `Tenant\Checkout\...`) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/cart` | `CartController@show` | Includes the quote; `?address_id=` or inline address and `?shipping_method_id=` add tax and shipping |
| POST | `/api/cart/items` | `CartItemController@store` | Issues a guest token when there is none |
| PATCH | `/api/cart/items/{item}` | `CartItemController@update` | |
| DELETE | `/api/cart/items/{item}` | `CartItemController@destroy` | |
| POST | `/api/cart/apply-coupon` | `CartCouponController@store` | 422 with `reason` when the coupon does not apply |
| DELETE | `/api/cart/coupon` | `CartCouponController@destroy` | |
| POST | `/api/cart/apply-gift-card` | `CartGiftCardController@store` | `feature:gift_cards` |
| DELETE | `/api/cart/gift-card` | `CartGiftCardController@destroy` | `feature:gift_cards` |
| POST | `/api/cart/apply-reward-points` | `CartRewardPointController@store` | `feature:reward_points`; customer only |
| PATCH | `/api/cart/currency` | `CartCurrencyController@update` | `feature:multi_currency`; body `currency_code`, which must be an active tenant currency (§48.3) |
| POST | `/api/orders` | `Checkout\CheckoutController@store` | Places an order (§38.6). `idempotency` middleware; body includes `quote_hash`. |
