## 39. Orders

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Orders` |
| **Depends on** | §26, §27, §28, §32, §35, §36, §37, §38 |
| **Integration hooks** | Gift cards (§46), installments (§47), multi-currency (§48), marketplace (§50), POS (§51), sales agents (§52), reward points (§54), accounting (§57), restaurant (§65). These columns are defined here and used by their modules. |

An order is the single record of a sale, whatever its origin. Online checkout, POS, sales-quotation conversion, repair invoicing, product-subscription renewals, WooCommerce and social-commerce imports, and exchanges all create orders through `OrderService::createOrder()`. No module inserts `orders` rows directly.

Two independent enums classify an order:

- `order_source` records **where** the order came from.
- `order_type` records **what kind** of order it is.

For example, a gift-card purchase can have `order_source = online` or `pos`.

### 39.1 Orders Table

```
orders  [DB: tenant]  soft deletes, audited
id
order_number               string   unique       generated (§39.3)
invoice_number             string   nullable unique  assigned on confirmation (§43.1)
customer_id                fk -> customers  nullable  null = guest or walk-in
guest_token                string   nullable index    copied from the cart for guest orders (§39.6)
customer_name              string   nullable  snapshot
customer_email             string   nullable  snapshot; required for guest online orders
customer_phone             string   nullable  snapshot
status                     enum(pending, processing, partially_shipped, shipped, delivered, completed,
                                cancelled, refunded)
payment_status             enum(unpaid, partially_paid, paid, failed, partially_refunded, refunded)  default unpaid
order_type                 enum(standard, gift_card_purchase, exchange_replacement)  default standard
order_source               enum(online, pos, woocommerce, social, admin)  default online
                                     admin = created by a staff back-office flow (Assumption A-21)
is_test                    bool     default false  true when created while tenant_settings.payment_mode = test (§40.8); never changes
currency_code              char(3)
prices_include_tax         bool               snapshot of tenant_settings.prices_include_tax (§38.5)
subtotal                   money
discount_amount            money    default 0  Σ order_items.discount_amount (§38.5)
shipping_amount            money    default 0
shipping_discount_amount   money    default 0  free-shipping promotion (§37.6)
shipping_tax_amount        money    default 0  (§38.5)
tax_amount                 money    default 0  lines plus shipping tax
reward_points_redeemed     int      default 0          (§54)
reward_points_discount_amount money default 0          (§54)
gift_card_amount_applied   money    default 0          (§46)
total                      money                        formula in §38.5
base_currency_amount       money    nullable            total converted to base currency (§48)
exchange_rate_used         rate     nullable            (§48)
shipping_method_id         fk -> shipping_methods  nullable
shipping_address           json     nullable  snapshot {name, phone, line1, line2, city_id, state_id, country_id, postal_code}
billing_address            json     nullable  snapshot, same shape
payment_gateway            string   nullable  provider chosen for online payment (§40.2)
sales_agent_id             fk -> sales_agents  nullable       (§52)
pos_session_id             fk -> pos_sessions  nullable       set only when order_source = pos (§51)
restaurant_table_id        fk -> restaurant_tables nullable   (§65)
replaces_order_return_id   fk -> order_returns nullable       set only when order_type = exchange_replacement (§41)
created_by_user_id         fk -> users  nullable  staff who created it (POS cashier, back-office flows)
idempotency_key            string   nullable unique  checkout Idempotency-Key (§70.11), POS offline sync (§51.6) and channel imports
customer_note              text     nullable  captured at checkout
placed_at                  datetime
payment_expires_at         datetime nullable  unpaid online orders: placed_at + unpaid_order_expiry_minutes (§39.5)
confirmed_at               datetime nullable  (§39.4)
paid_at                    datetime nullable  when payment_status first became paid
completed_at               datetime nullable  when the order first reached delivered or completed
cancelled_at               datetime nullable
cancellation_reason        string   nullable  free text, or payment_timeout for expired orders
index(status), index(payment_status), index(customer_id), index(placed_at), index(customer_email),
index(is_test, confirmed_at)  dashboard and report ranges (§22.7, §44)
```

- `orders.currency_code` is the only currency column. No `currency` column exists.
- Applied promotions are recorded in `promotion_redemptions` (§37.5), not on the order. The applied coupon code is `promotion_redemptions.coupon_code_snapshot`.
- Shipment and tracking data lives in `shipments` (§36.2). There are no tracking columns on orders.
- Foreign keys to optional-module tables (`sales_agents`, `pos_sessions`, `restaurant_tables`) are created by the core migration as nullable columns **without** a foreign-key constraint. The owning module's migration adds the constraint. This keeps the tenant schema identical for every tenant (§8) while still letting the core migration run first.

### 39.2 Order Items Table

```
order_items  [DB: tenant]
id
order_id              fk -> orders
product_id            fk -> products  nullable  null only for non-product lines (e.g. repair labour, §67)
product_variant_id    fk -> product_variants  nullable
name_snapshot         string            product name plus variant label, or the line description
sku_snapshot          string   nullable
seller_id             fk -> sellers  nullable  snapshot of products.seller_id (§50)
warehouse_id          fk -> warehouses  nullable  fulfilling warehouse; null for digital, service and non-product lines
quantity              qty
quantity_shipped      qty      default 0  maintained by shipments (§36.2)
unit_price            money             resolved price (§38.4), in orders.currency_code
price_source          string            PriceResult.source snapshot: base, warehouse, currency, flash_sale, quotation,
                                         subscription or manual
unit_cost_snapshot    money    nullable products.cost_price at order time, in base currency (COGS, §57)
discount_amount       money    default 0  every discount on this line (§38.5)
seller_funded_discount_amount money default 0  part of discount_amount funded by the seller (§37.6)
tax_rate_applied      percent  default 0
tax_amount            money    default 0
tax_breakdown         json     nullable  GST split (§35.3)
line_total            money             §38.5
kitchen_status        enum(pending, preparing, ready, served)  nullable  restaurant only (§65)
kitchen_ready_at      datetime nullable  when kitchen_status became ready; preparation time = kitchen_ready_at − created_at (§65)
stock_already_deducted bool    default false  true = the originating module already moved the stock
                                               (repair parts, §67.3); reservation and deduction skip the line
```

- Bundle lines are stored as **one** order item for the bundle. Inventory operations expand them to their children ([§28.3](#283-bundles)).
- Snapshots (`name_snapshot`, `sku_snapshot`, `unit_price`, `price_source`, `unit_cost_snapshot`, the discount and tax fields) never change after creation ([§5.8](#58-snapshots)).
- Modules that set their own line price (sales quotations §53, product subscriptions §55, repair §67) pass it with its `price_source`. The discount they apply is recorded in `discount_amount`, like any other discount.

### 39.3 Order Numbering

- `order_number` is generated by `OrderService::generateOrderNumber()` from a per-tenant sequence, formatted as a zero-padded integer starting at `100001` (Assumption A-22). It is assigned at creation and never reused. The sequence is a locked counter row, so concurrent checkouts never collide.
- `invoice_number` is a separate, template-driven number assigned on confirmation ([§43.1](#431-invoice-templates)).

### 39.4 Confirmation, Payment Status and Order Status

**Confirmation** is the point at which an order becomes a committed sale. It happens exactly once, in `OrderService::confirmOrder()`, which locks the order row and returns immediately when `confirmed_at` is already set. Callers:

- `markPaid()`, when the order becomes fully paid
- `PosSaleService::createSale()` (§51), because POS sales are paid at the counter
- `InstallmentPlanService`, when the `on_first_payment` fulfilment policy releases an order after its first installment (§47)

Confirmation performs, in one transaction:

1. Sets `confirmed_at`, and clears `payment_expires_at`.
2. Converts reservations to deductions. For one-pass POS sales, it deducts directly ([§32.5](#325-stock-lifecycle-reservation-deduction-and-release)).
3. Commits promotion redemptions: `PromotionRedemptionService::commit()` (§37.5).
4. Assigns `invoice_number` (§43.1).
5. Runs the tenant-database integration hooks, each only when its feature is enabled:
   - `SellerLedgerService::recordOrderLines()` (§50.4)
   - `SalesAgentCommissionService::calculateCommission()` (§52.2)
   - `BookingService::confirmForOrder()` for a prepaid booking (§66.2)
6. Records the accounting posting request for `postOrderSale()` in the accounting outbox (§57.3), when `accounting` is enabled. Seller commission postings are recorded the same way by `SellerLedgerService`.

After the transaction commits, `order.confirmed` is dispatched.

For `gift_card_purchase` orders, confirmation also calls `GiftCardService::issueGiftCard()` (§46).

**Payment status** is derived from the `order_payments` ledger (§40). Let `net_paid` be the sum of `amount_paid` over rows with `status = successful`. Refunds and chargebacks count as negative:

| Condition | `payment_status` |
|---|---|
| No successful payment, and the last gateway attempt failed | `failed` |
| `net_paid = 0` and no refunds or chargebacks | `unpaid` |
| `0 < net_paid < total`, no refunds or chargebacks | `partially_paid` |
| `net_paid ≥ total` | `paid` |
| Refunds or chargebacks exist, `net_paid > 0` | `partially_refunded` |
| Refunds or chargebacks exist, `net_paid ≤ 0` | `refunded` |

`OrderService::recalculatePaymentStatus()` applies this table after every ledger change, under a lock on the order row. When the status first becomes `paid`, it sets `paid_at` and calls `markPaid()`.

**Order status** tracks fulfilment. The initial status is:

- online orders: `tenant_settings.default_order_status` (`pending` or `processing`)
- `admin`, `woocommerce` and `social` orders: `pending`
- POS orders: `completed`
- restaurant table orders (POS orders opened against a table, §65.4): `pending` until settled

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | `processing` | Staff, via `updateOrderStatus()` |
| `pending` | `completed` | Restaurant table order settled (§65.4) |
| `pending`, `processing`, `partially_shipped` | `partially_shipped` | A shipment is dispatched, and some physical quantity is still unshipped (§36.2) |
| `pending`, `processing`, `partially_shipped` | `shipped` | A shipment is dispatched, and every physical line is fully shipped (§36.2) |
| `shipped` | `delivered` | Every shipment of the order is delivered (§36.2), or staff |
| `pending`, `processing` | `delivered` | Automatic on confirmation when the order has no physical lines (digital, service or gift-card-only) |
| `pending`, `processing` | `cancelled` | `cancelOrder()` or `expireUnpaidOrder()` |
| any except `cancelled` | `refunded` | Automatic when `payment_status` becomes `refunded` |

- `completed` is used only for POS orders and is terminal.
- `delivered` and `completed` are the **completion** states. Reaching one for the first time sets `completed_at`, triggers `RewardPointService::earnPoints()` (§54), opens the return window (§41), and starts the seller hold period (§50.4).
- Invalid transitions are rejected with HTTP 422.

### 39.5 Order Service

`OrderService` (Tenant):

- `createOrder(array $data): Order`: the only order-creation primitive. It enforces `max_orders_per_month`, generates `order_number`, snapshots every line (§39.2) and totals (§38.5), and dispatches `order.new_order_received` after commit. For every order except one-pass POS sales it reserves stock at the line warehouses, in the same transaction (§32.5). One-pass POS sales are deducted on confirmation instead. Restaurant table orders reserve like online orders. For unpaid online orders it sets `payment_expires_at`.
- `appendItems(Order $order, array $lines): Order`: adds lines to an open restaurant table order (`order_source = pos`, `restaurant_table_id` set, not yet confirmed) (§65.4). It snapshots and reserves the new lines and recalculates totals, including promotions. It is rejected for every other order.
- `getOrder(Order $order): Order`
- `listOrders(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`: admin. Applies `staff_data_access_scope` (§25.3).
- `listOrdersForCustomer(Customer $customer): LengthAwarePaginator`
- `recalculatePaymentStatus(Order $order): void`
- `markPaid(Order $order): void`: calls `confirmOrder()` when the order is not yet confirmed
- `markFailed(Order $order): void`: sets `payment_status = failed` and dispatches `order.payment_failed` and `order.payment_failed_staff_alert`. It does **not** release stock, flash-sale claims or promotion reservations: the customer can retry payment on the same order until `payment_expires_at`.
- `confirmOrder(Order $order): void`: see §39.4
- `updateOrderStatus(Order $order, string $status): void`: validates the transition and dispatches `order.status_changed`, or the specific key (`order.shipped`, `order.delivered`)
- `cancelOrder(Order $order, string $reason, bool $byCustomer = false): void`:
  - Allowed only while the status is `pending` or `processing`. Once any shipment has been dispatched, the order cannot be cancelled. Unshipped items are handled by staff through a return or a direct refund (partial line cancellation is deferred, Appendix C).
  - A customer may cancel only while `payment_status` is `unpaid` or `failed` (Assumption A-23).
  - Staff may cancel paid orders. Stock is restocked (§32.5), but no refund is issued automatically. Staff refund explicitly through `refundOrder()`.
  - In one transaction: releases reservations (unconfirmed) or restocks deductions (confirmed); calls `PromotionRedemptionService::release()` (unconfirmed) or `reverse()` (confirmed); calls `FlashSaleService::release()`; reverses the gift-card redemption through `GiftCardService::reverseRedemption()` (§46); and restores redeemed reward points (§54); and cancels a linked `pending_payment` booking through `BookingService::cancelForOrder()` (§66.2). For a confirmed order, it writes seller ledger `reversal` entries for every seller line (§50.4) and records a `reverseEntry()` request for the sale posting in the accounting outbox (§57.3).
  - Dispatches `order.cancelled`.
- `expireUnpaidOrder(Order $order): void`: called by the `ExpireUnpaidOrder` job (§72.3). It re-reads the order under lock and does nothing unless the order is still unconfirmed, `payment_status` is `unpaid` or `failed`, no gateway payment row is `pending`, and `payment_expires_at` has passed. Otherwise it calls `cancelOrder($order, 'payment_timeout')` as the system. When a payment row is still pending, it first calls `OrderPaymentService::verifyOrderPayment()` for that row, and reschedules itself if the provider still reports it pending.
- `refundOrder(Order $order, ?float $amount, string $reason, ?array $lineAllocations = null): void`: a direct refund with no return, for example goodwill or a shipping-fee adjustment. It refunds successful payments newest first, through `OrderPaymentService::refund()` (§40.4), until `$amount` (default: `net_paid`) is covered. When the order has seller lines, the refunded amount is attributed to lines: by the explicit `lineAllocations` (`[{order_item_id, amount}]`) when given, otherwise pro rata to `line_total`. Seller lines then receive `reversal` entries for their share (§50.4).
- `duplicateOrder(Order $order): Order`: clones the customer and every line's product, variant and quantity into a new `pending`, `unpaid` order with `order_source = admin`. Prices and promotions are re-resolved at the current values. Payments, shipments and returns are not copied. This is used to re-sell the same basket without re-picking every line.
- `changeLineWarehouse(OrderItem $item, Warehouse $warehouse): OrderItem`: see §32.4. Allowed only while `quantity_shipped = 0`.
- `getOrderItemsForSeller(Seller $seller, Order $order): Collection`: one order can span several sellers (§50)
- `getPendingOrders(): Collection`: used by the AI assistant (§62)
- `generateOrderNumber(): string`

### 39.6 Guest Order Access

- A guest order stores the cart's `guest_token`.
- A storefront request carrying a matching `X-Guest-Token` header may show, pay, track and cancel that order, and view its invoice.
- Once a guest registers or logs in with that token, the auth flow sets `customer_id` on their guest orders whose `customer_email` matches the account email (Assumption A-24).

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Orders\...`) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/orders` | `OrderController@index` | Authenticated customer only |
| GET | `/api/orders/{order}` | `OrderController@show` | |
| POST | `/api/orders/{order}/cancel` | `OrderController@cancel` | Subject to A-23 |
| GET | `/api/orders/{order}/invoice` | `OrderDocumentController@invoice` | §43.2 |

## 40. Order Payments

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Payments` |
| **Depends on** | §15, §39 |
| **Integration hooks** | Accounting (§57), platform commission (§15.8), installments (§47), POS (§51), product subscriptions (§55) |

This is the tenant's own storefront accepting money from **its** customers. It is separate from subscription billing (§14). It reuses the same gateway drivers (§15), built with the **tenant's** credentials.

### 40.1 Order Payments Ledger

Every movement of money against an order is one `order_payments` row, however it was collected: gateway charge, cash, bank transfer, gift card, POS terminal, a refund or a chargeback. An order's payment history is therefore always in one place.

```
order_payments  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
order_id                   fk -> orders
kind                       enum(payment, refund, chargeback)  default payment
payment_method             enum(gateway, cash, card_terminal, bank_transfer, cheque, gift_card,
                                exchange_credit, other)   refunds and chargebacks copy the original's method
provider                   string   nullable  flutterwave | paystack | stripe (gateway);
                                               moniepoint | opay | stripe_terminal (card_terminal)
mode                       enum(test, live)  test when the order is a test order (§40.8); selects gateway credentials
status                     enum(pending, successful, failed)  manual rows are created as successful
reference                  string   unique    our own reference, sent to the provider (charge or refund)
idempotency_key            string   nullable  the request's Idempotency-Key (§70.11), for rows created by an API call
provider_reference         string   nullable  the provider's transaction, refund or dispute id
amount_due                 money    nullable  order balance at the moment of payment
amount_received            money    nullable  amount tendered, e.g. a larger cash note
amount_paid                money              amount applied to the order; negative for refunds and chargebacks
change_given               money    nullable  amount_received − amount_paid (cash)
currency_code              char(3)
exchange_rate_used         rate     nullable  when paid in a non-base currency (§48)
account_id                 fk -> chart_of_accounts  nullable  where the money landed (§57); defaulted per method
refund_of_order_payment_id fk -> order_payments  nullable  set on refund and chargeback rows
installment_payment_id     fk -> installment_payments  nullable  (§47; constraint added by that module)
pos_session_id             fk -> pos_sessions  nullable        (§51; constraint added by that module)
recorded_by_user_id        fk -> users  nullable  null = system (gateway, checkout)
paid_at                    datetime nullable  when the row became successful
notes                      text     nullable
meta                       json     nullable  provider fee, platform_commission (§15.8), failure reason, raw summary
index(order_id), unique(mode, kind, provider, provider_reference), unique(order_id, kind, idempotency_key),
index(kind, status, paid_at)  dashboard and report ranges
```

- **Only `successful` rows count** towards `net_paid` (§39.4). `pending` refunds and chargebacks still reserve refundable capacity (§40.4).
- A row's `status` moves only `pending → successful` or `pending → failed`, exactly once, under a lock on the row. That transition is the idempotency point for webhooks, client verification and retries. Every side effect (posting, commission, status recalculation) runs only in the transaction that performs the transition.
- The `wallet` payment method from earlier drafts is not supported. Store credit and deposits are deferred (Appendix C).
- `exchange_credit` records the value of returned goods applied to an exchange replacement order (§41.5).

### 40.2 Online Gateway Payments

`POST /api/orders/{order}/pay`, with body `{gateway}` and an `Idempotency-Key` header ([§70.11](#7011-idempotency)):

1. The order must belong to the caller (§39.6), must not be `cancelled`, and `payment_status` must be `unpaid`, `partially_paid` or `failed`. When `payment_expires_at` has passed, the request fails with 409 `order_expired`.
2. The gateway must be one of the tenant's active `enabled_for_online` providers **of the order's mode** (`test` for a test order, otherwise `live`) that supports `orders.currency_code` (§15.5, §40.8).
3. **One attempt at a time.** If the order already has a `pending` gateway row, it is first verified with the provider (`verifyOrderPayment()`). If the provider still reports it pending, the request returns 409 `payment_in_progress` with that attempt's `checkout_url`. Otherwise the earlier row is resolved first. This prevents two parallel charges for one order. Stock, flash-sale claims and promotion reservations are still held from checkout, because a failed payment does not release them (§39.5).
4. `OrderPaymentService::initiateOrderPayment()` creates a `pending` row with a fresh `reference` and commits it. It then calls `PaymentGatewayFactory::forTenant($gateway, $payment->mode)->initiateCharge()` outside any transaction. The amount is the outstanding balance. `save_authorization` is set when the order starts an installment plan (§47) or a product subscription (§55).
5. It dispatches `VerifyOrderPayment` for the row, delayed 15 minutes (§72.3).
6. The response returns `{checkout_url, reference}`. The client redirects the customer.

Payment completion is confirmed by **any** of three paths. All three converge on `OrderPaymentService::completeGatewayPayment()`, which performs the `pending → successful | failed` transition under a row lock, so the outcome is applied exactly once:

- **Webhook:** `POST /api/webhooks/{tenant}/{provider}/{mode}` (§15.6), then `OrderPaymentService::handleWebhookEvent()`.
- **Client verification:** after the redirect back, the client calls `POST /api/payments/verify` with `{reference}`. This calls `verifyOrderPayment()`, which calls `verifyTransaction()` on the provider.
- **Delayed verification:** `VerifyOrderPayment` calls `verifyOrderPayment()`. While the provider reports the payment pending, it re-dispatches itself at 1 hour and then 6 hours. After 24 hours it marks the row `failed` with `meta.failure_reason = verification_timeout` (Assumption A-25).

The provider's reported amount and currency MUST equal the row's `amount_paid` and `currency_code`. A mismatch marks the row `failed` with `meta.failure_reason = amount_mismatch`, and dispatches `order.payment_needs_review` to staff. It never confirms the order.

**On success**, in one transaction: the row becomes `successful` with `paid_at`, `provider_reference` and `meta.fee` set, and then:

- `applyPlatformCommission()` runs (§15.8).
- Posting requests for `postOrderPayment()`, and for `postGatewayFee()` when the provider reports a fee, are recorded in the accounting outbox (§57.3), when `accounting` is enabled.
- When `installment_payment_id` is set, `InstallmentPlanService` is notified (§47).
- `OrderService::recalculatePaymentStatus()` runs, which may confirm the order.
- If `net_paid` now exceeds `total` (for example a manual payment and a gateway payment both landed), `order.overpaid` is dispatched to staff, who refund the difference. The system never refunds automatically.

**On failure**, the row becomes `failed` and `OrderService::markFailed()` is called. A success reported later for a `failed` row (a late webhook after a timeout) is applied as a new `successful` row with the same provider reference, recorded as `kind = payment`, and handled like any other success. Money the provider actually captured is never ignored.

### 40.3 Order Payment Service

`OrderPaymentService` (Tenant):

- `initiateOrderPayment(Order $order, string $provider): array`
- `verifyOrderPayment(string $reference): array`
- `completeGatewayPayment(OrderPayment $payment, array $verifiedResult): void`: the single transition point (§40.2)
- `handleWebhookEvent(WebhookEvent $event): void`: routes by `reference` to the `order_payments` row, or by `provider_reference` for refund and dispute events. Unknown references are logged and acknowledged.
- `chargeStoredAuthorization(Order $order, string $provider, string $authorizationToken, float $amount, ?InstallmentPayment $installment = null): OrderPayment`: a merchant-initiated charge used by installments (§47) and product-subscription renewals (§55). Calls `chargeAuthorization()` with our `reference` as the provider idempotency key.
- `refund(OrderPayment $payment, float $amount, string $reason, ?OrderReturn $return = null): OrderPayment`: see §40.4
- `handleDispute(WebhookEvent $event): void`: see §40.5
- `applyPlatformCommission(OrderPayment $payment): void`: see §15.8

### 40.4 Refunds

`OrderPaymentService::refund()` is the **only** refund path. It is used by direct refunds (§39.5), returns (§41) and exchanges.

| Original `payment_method` | Refund mechanism |
|---|---|
| `gateway` | `PaymentGatewayFactory::forTenant(provider)->refund(provider_reference, amount, refund reference)` |
| `card_terminal` | `PosTerminalGatewayFactory` refund (§51.4) |
| `gift_card` | `GiftCardService::reverseRedemption()` credits the balance back to the card (§46) |
| `cash`, `bank_transfer`, `cheque`, `other` | Ledger only. Staff return the money outside the system. |
| `exchange_credit` | Not refundable. The exchange is reversed through the return (§41). |

**Two-phase refund:**

1. **Reserve (one transaction).** Lock the original payment row with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. Its refundable capacity is `amount_paid` minus the absolute sum of its `pending` and `successful` refund and chargeback rows. If `$amount` exceeds the capacity, the refund fails with 422 `refund_exceeds_payment`. Otherwise insert a `kind = refund` row with a fresh `reference`, `refund_of_order_payment_id` set and a negative `amount_paid`. The row is `pending` for gateway and terminal refunds, and `successful` immediately for gift-card and manual methods.
2. **Execute (outside the transaction)**, for `pending` rows only. Call the provider, passing our refund `reference` as the provider's idempotency key or merchant reference. Drivers MUST do this wherever the provider supports it (§15.2).
3. **Complete.** A synchronous success or failure performs the row transition immediately. A provider that processes refunds asynchronously is completed by the `refund.processed` or `refund.failed` webhook. A `failed` refund frees its capacity.
4. **Side effects of a successful refund**, in the transition's transaction:
   - a `postRefund()` request in the accounting outbox (§57.3)
   - `recalculatePaymentStatus()`
   - seller ledger reversals for the attributed lines (§39.5, §41)
   - `return.refunded` when triggered by a return, or `order.refunded` otherwise

A `pending` gateway refund with no `provider_reference` one hour after creation means the provider call's outcome is unknown, for example because the process crashed. It is **never retried automatically**, because a retry could refund twice on a provider that ignores idempotency keys. `order.refund_needs_review` is dispatched to staff, who check the provider dashboard and resolve the row through `POST /api/admin/order-payments/{payment}/resolve-refund`. This check runs in the daily tenant maintenance job and in a delayed `VerifyRefund` job dispatched when the refund is created (§72.3).

`refund()` routes require an `Idempotency-Key` header ([§70.11](#7011-idempotency)).

### 40.5 Chargebacks

A chargeback (dispute) is money the provider takes back on the cardholder's behalf. It is recorded, not initiated.

| Webhook event (§15.2) | Effect |
|---|---|
| `dispute.opened` | Creates a `kind = chargeback`, `status = pending` row against the disputed payment for the disputed amount, with the dispute ID as `provider_reference`. The row reserves refundable capacity, so staff cannot also refund the disputed money. Dispatches `order.payment_disputed` to staff. |
| `dispute.lost` | The row becomes `successful`. It is then treated like a refund: a `postChargeback()` outbox request, `recalculatePaymentStatus()`, and seller ledger reversals pro rata to `line_total`. Stock is not restocked, and promotion redemptions stay committed. A dispute fee reported by the provider is posted with `postGatewayFee()`. |
| `dispute.won` | The row becomes `failed`, and its capacity is freed. |

Events are idempotent by the row transition (§40.1). A `dispute.lost` for an unknown dispute creates the row and completes it in one step.

### 40.6 Manual Payment Ledger

Payments collected outside the gateway flow are recorded by hand. Examples are cash at a counter, a bank transfer confirmed manually, or a partial deposit. This supports simple ad hoc partial payments without the installment module.

`OrderPaymentLedgerService` (Tenant):

- `recordPayment(Order $order, array $data): OrderPayment`: `payment_method` must be `cash`, `bank_transfer`, `cheque` or `other`. Creates a `successful` row, records the `postOrderPayment()` outbox request, and calls `recalculatePaymentStatus()`.
- `updatePayment(OrderPayment $payment, array $data): OrderPayment`: manual rows only. Reverses and re-posts the accounting entry.
- `deletePayment(OrderPayment $payment): void`: manual rows only, and only when the row has no refunds. Reverses the accounting posting through `reverseEntry()`.
- `resolveRefund(OrderPayment $refund, string $outcome, ?string $providerReference = null): void`: staff resolution of a refund whose outcome is unknown (§40.4). `outcome` is `successful` or `failed`.
- `getPayment(OrderPayment $payment): OrderPayment`
- `listPaymentsForOrder(Order $order): Collection`
- `getBalanceForOrder(Order $order): float`: `total − net_paid`

Gateway, gift-card, terminal, refund and chargeback rows are system-generated. They cannot be edited or deleted.

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Payments\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.storefront` | POST | `/api/orders/{order}/pay` | `OrderPaymentController@store` (`idempotency`) |
| `tenant.storefront` | POST | `/api/payments/verify` | `OrderPaymentController@verify`: body `{reference}` |
| `tenant.storefront` | GET | `/api/payment-methods` | `OrderPaymentController@methods`: eligible providers for `?currency=` |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/order-payments/metrics` | `Admin\OrderPaymentController@metrics`: contextual KPIs (§44.4) |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/order-payments` | `Admin\OrderPaymentController@index`: every payment, refund and chargeback row across orders; filters `kind`, `status`, `payment_method`, `provider`, `mode`, date range |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/orders/{order}/payments` | `Admin\OrderPaymentLedgerController@index` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/orders/{order}/payments` | `Admin\OrderPaymentLedgerController@store` (`idempotency`) |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/orders/{order}/balance` | `Admin\OrderPaymentLedgerController@balance` |
| `tenant.admin` | PATCH | `/api/admin/order-payments/{payment}` | `Admin\OrderPaymentLedgerController@update` |
| `tenant.admin` | DELETE | `/api/admin/order-payments/{payment}` | `Admin\OrderPaymentLedgerController@destroy` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/order-payments/{payment}/resolve-refund` | `Admin\OrderPaymentLedgerController@resolveRefund`: body `{outcome, provider_reference}` |

These routes are core (no feature key). Webhook routes are defined in §15.6.

### 40.8 Test Orders

A tenant starts in `payment_mode = test` (§13.4) so that it can rehearse its whole flow (checkout, payment with the provider's test cards, fulfilment, returns) before taking real money. Every order created while the mode is `test` is a **test order**: `orders.is_test = true`, and its `order_payments` rows have `mode = test`. This is the single definition; other sections refer here.

A test order behaves like any order for **operations**: stock is reserved and deducted, shipments, returns, notifications and documents work (invoices and receipts carry a "TEST" watermark), so the rehearsal is real. Staff cancel test orders to restock.

A test order is **excluded** from everything that represents real money or real usage:

| Excluded from | Section |
|---|---|
| `max_orders_per_month` | §11.8 |
| Dashboards, contextual KPIs and reports (unless a report is explicitly filtered to `is_test = true`) | §44, §61 |
| Accounting postings: `AccountingOutbox::record()` is a no-op for test orders and their payments | §57.3 |
| Platform commission | §15.8 |
| Seller ledger and payouts | §50.4 |
| Sales-agent commissions | §52 |
| Earning reward points (redeeming is also refused for test orders) | §54 |
| Gift cards: a test gift-card purchase issues no card; test orders cannot be paid with a real card | §46 |
| Tenant usage snapshots reported to the landlord | §22.6 |

- Manual payment methods (cash, bank transfer) on a test order are recorded with `mode = test` too; nothing about a test order becomes live.
- POS sales follow the same rule: a POS sale made in test mode is a test order. Card-terminal providers (§51.4) have no test mode in v1, so `card_terminal` payments are refused (422 `payment_mode_mismatch`) while the tenant is in test mode; cash and the other manual methods are recorded as test rows. This prevents a rehearsal from charging a real card.
- Switching to `live` does not convert existing test orders. Unpaid test orders can still be paid in test mode until they expire (§39.5).
- Orders imported from WooCommerce or social channels (§68, §69) are **always live**: they represent money collected outside the tenant's test setup, so they ignore `payment_mode`.
- Renewal and installment orders (§47, §55) inherit `is_test` from the order that created the stored authorization, because a test authorization can only be charged with test credentials. A test product subscription therefore stays a test subscription.

## 41. Returns, Refunds and Exchanges

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce). Returns are bundled into core commerce. |
| **Code module** | `Returns` |
| **Depends on** | §32, §39, §40 |
| **Integration hooks** | Approval workflows (`module_key = return`, §60), accounting (§57) |

A refund on its own (§39.5) is not a return. A return is a request, approval and restock workflow: the customer asks to return items and says why; the tenant approves or rejects; the goods optionally come back before any money moves; and stock is restocked according to condition. The workflow reuses the refund path (§40.4) and never duplicates payment logic.

### 41.1 Tables

```
return_reasons  [DB: tenant]
id
label                string            e.g. "Wrong item received", "Item defective"
requires_photo       bool     default false
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
order_returns  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
order_id                 fk -> orders
customer_id              fk -> customers  nullable  null for guest orders
return_reason_id         fk -> return_reasons
resolution_type          enum(refund, exchange)   chosen by the customer
status                   enum(requested, approved, rejected, awaiting_return_shipment, received,
                              refunded, exchanged, closed)
requires_physical_return bool              set on approval
customer_note            text     nullable
admin_note               text     nullable  internal
rejection_reason         string   nullable
refund_amount            money    nullable  set when refunded
requested_at             datetime
resolved_at              datetime nullable
(media: photos)
```

```
order_return_items  [DB: tenant]
id
order_return_id                   fk -> order_returns
order_item_id                     fk -> order_items
quantity                          qty
condition                         enum(resellable, damaged, missing_parts)  nullable  set on receipt
restocked                         bool     default false
exchange_for_product_id           fk -> products  nullable  exchange only
exchange_for_product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable  exchange only
```

The PHP model names are `OrderReturn` and `OrderReturnItem`, because `return` is a reserved word.

### 41.2 Eligibility

- The order's status must be `delivered` or `completed`.
- The request must fall within the return window. The window is `return_window_days`, falling back to `default_return_window_days`. It is counted from `orders.completed_at` (§39.4). When both settings are null, no window is enforced.
- The quantity per line cannot exceed the line's quantity (`quantity_shipped` for physical lines) minus quantities in earlier returns that were not rejected. The check runs under a lock on the order row, so two concurrent return requests cannot both claim the same units.
- When the reason `requires_photo`, at least one photo is required.

### 41.3 Workflow

1. **Request.** The customer picks items and quantities, a reason, a resolution type (with a replacement product or variant per item for exchanges), an optional note and photos. The status is `requested`. `return.requested` goes to the customer and `return.new_request` goes to staff.
2. **Approval gate.** When an active approval workflow matches `module_key = return` (§60), the return waits in `requested` until the workflow resolves. Otherwise, staff act directly.
3. **Approve or reject.**
   - `approveReturn()` sets `requires_physical_return`, defaulting to `requires_physical_return_by_default`. Staff may override it per return.
   - For exchanges, replacement stock must be available before approval.
   - If a physical return is required, the status becomes `awaiting_return_shipment`. Otherwise it becomes `approved`.
   - `rejectReturn()` records a reason, sets `rejected` and dispatches `return.rejected`.
4. **Receipt.** When a physical return is required, `markReceived()` records each line's condition. The status becomes `received` and `return.received` is dispatched.
5. **Resolution.** For a return that did not require a physical return, resolution is allowed directly from `approved`. This is the instant-refund path for low-value items.
   - **Refund:** `processRefund()` (§41.4)
   - **Exchange:** `ExchangeService::processExchange()` (§41.5)
6. **Restock.** When the return is resolved, lines with `condition = resellable` are restocked into their original line warehouse through `InventoryService::adjustStock()` (reason `return_restock`), and `restocked` is set. Damaged lines, missing-parts lines and lines never physically returned are not restocked. When `accounting` is enabled, `AccountingService::postReturnRestock()` reverses the cost of goods sold for the restocked quantity (§57).
7. **Close.** `refunded` and `exchanged` returns move to `closed` through `closeReturn()`. So do rejected returns, when staff archive them.

### 41.4 Refund Resolution

`processRefund()` computes the refund amount. For each returned line, that is the line's `line_total` pro-rated by the returned quantity, rounded (§5.3). Because `line_total` is after discounts, the customer is refunded what they actually paid for the line, and a promotion's value is never refunded twice. Shipping is not refunded (Assumption A-26). Staff may pass an explicit, lower amount. The amount is refunded through `OrderPaymentService::refund()` (§40.4) against the order's successful payments, newest first. It runs under a lock on the return row, and only from `approved` or `received`, so a repeated call cannot refund twice. The status becomes `refunded` once the refund rows succeed. Promotion redemptions stay `committed` (§37.5).

### 41.5 Exchange Resolution

`ExchangeService::processExchange()`:

1. Creates a replacement order through `OrderService::createOrder()`, with `order_type = exchange_replacement`, `replaces_order_return_id` set, the same customer and addresses, and one line per requested replacement, priced at the current price (§38.4).
2. Records an `order_payments` row on the replacement order, with `payment_method = exchange_credit` and an amount of `min(returned value, replacement total)`. The returned value is computed as in §41.4.
3. When the replacement costs **more**, the difference remains due on the replacement order. The customer pays it through the normal payment flow (§40.2), or staff record it (§40.6).
4. When the replacement costs **less**, the difference is refunded on the original order through `OrderPaymentService::refund()`.
5. Runs the restock step (§41.3, step 6) and sets the status to `exchanged`.

The replacement order is confirmed when it becomes fully paid, as for any other order (§39.4).

- `rejectReturn(OrderReturn $return, string $reason): void`

## 42. Reviews and Wishlist

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Reviews`, `Wishlist` |
| **Depends on** | §26, §27, §38, §39 |
| **Integration hooks** | Approval workflows (`module_key = review`, §60), back-in-stock alerts (§56) |

### 42.1 Product Reviews

```
product_reviews  [DB: tenant]
id
product_id              fk -> products
customer_id             fk -> customers
order_id                fk -> orders  nullable  set when the customer has a completed order containing the product
rating                  tinyint           1 to 5
title                   string   nullable
body                    text
status                  enum(pending, approved, rejected)
rejection_reason        string   nullable
is_verified_purchase    bool     default false  true when order_id is set
index(product_id, status)
```

- Only authenticated customers can submit reviews.
- Who may review is a tenant setting (decides UD-18). When `tenant_settings.reviews_require_verified_purchase` is true, only customers with a completed order containing the product may review it (422 `verified_purchase_required` otherwise). When it is false (the default), any authenticated customer may review. A customer may review a product at most once, and updating the review replaces it. `order_id` and `is_verified_purchase` are set automatically when the customer has a `delivered` or `completed` order containing the product, which lets the storefront show a "verified buyer" badge.
- When `review_moderation_required` is true, new reviews start as `pending`. Otherwise they are `approved` immediately.
- When an active approval workflow matches `module_key = review` (§60), approval runs through that workflow instead of a single staff decision.
- `products.rating_average` and `products.rating_count` are recalculated from approved reviews whenever a review is approved, rejected or deleted.
- `review.approved` is sent to the customer, and `review.pending_moderation` to staff.

`ReviewService` (Tenant):

- `submitReview(Customer $customer, Product $product, array $data): ProductReview`
- `approveReview(ProductReview $review): void`
- `rejectReview(ProductReview $review, string $reason): void`
- `deleteReview(ProductReview $review): void`
- `getReviewsForProduct(Product $product, array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`: approved reviews only
- `listReviews(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`: admin
- `getAverageRating(Product $product): float`
- `recalculateAggregates(Product $product): void`

```
created_at           datetime
unique(customer_id, product_id)
```

The keys `wishlist_item.back_in_stock` and `wishlist_item.price_drop` are reserved (§17.9). Explicit back-in-stock subscriptions are handled by §56.

## 43. Documents and Printing

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce) |
| **Code module** | `Documents` |
| **Depends on** | §13.4, §27, §32, §39 |
| **Integration hooks** | POS receipts (§51) |

Documents are rendered with the libraries chosen in [§4.5](#45-document-rendering-libraries). Every renderer in this section sits behind a `DocumentRenderer` interface, so the library choice is isolated to one binding.

### 43.1 Invoice Templates

A tenant can define several named invoice templates, for example an A4 paper invoice and a thermal receipt. `tenant_settings.invoice_format` selects the family of fields (`standard` or `gst`). The template is the per-layout design layer on top of it.

```
invoice_templates  [DB: tenant]
id
name                          string            the template's own name
description                   string   nullable
invoice_type                  enum(a4, 58mm, 80mm)
is_default                    bool     default false  exactly one row is the default
prefix                        string   nullable  e.g. "INV-"
numbering_type                enum(sequential, random)
start_number                  int      default 1
last_number                   int      nullable  last sequential number issued (Assumption A-27)
header_text                   text     nullable
footer_text                   text     nullable
payment_notes                 text     nullable
sales_notes                   text     nullable
logo_media_id                 int      nullable  overrides store_logo_media_id
logo_height                   decimal(8,2) nullable  display dimensions
logo_width                    decimal(8,2) nullable
primary_color                 string   nullable  hex
date_format                   string   nullable  overrides tenant_settings.date_format
show_barcode                  bool     default false
show_qr_code                  bool     default false
show_description              bool     default true
show_amount_in_words          bool     default false
show_warehouse_info           bool     default false
show_bill_to_info             bool     default true
show_payment_details          bool     default true
show_payment_notes            bool     default false
show_reference_number         bool     default false
show_generated_invoice_number bool     default true
show_total_due                bool     default true
show_registration_number      bool     default false
show_sales_notes              bool     default false
show_customer_name            bool     default true
signature_enabled             bool     default false
```

- Provisioning seeds one default A4 template, named "Default", with the prefix `INV-` and sequential numbering ([§9.4](#94-provisioning-job)).
- **Invoice numbering.** On confirmation (§39.4), `orders.invoice_number` is assigned from the **default** template:
  - `sequential`: prefix + `max(start_number, last_number + 1)`, zero-padded to 6 digits. The template row is locked while `last_number` is incremented.
  - `random`: prefix + 8 random digits, retried until unique.
- The earlier `tenant_settings.invoice_prefix` key does not exist. The template prefix is the only invoice prefix.
- Targeting a non-default template per warehouse or per order type is deferred (Appendix C). In v1, rendering uses the default template unless a `template_id` is passed explicitly.

### 43.2 Invoice Rendering and Compliance

`InvoiceTemplateService::renderInvoice(Order $order, ?InvoiceTemplate $template = null): string` returns a PDF, or printable HTML for thermal sizes. It applies:

- every `show_*` flag on the template
- `invoice_format = gst` and `india_gst_enabled`: GSTIN, `hsn_code` per line, and the CGST/SGST/IGST breakdown from `order_items.tax_breakdown` (§35.3)
- `saudi_zatca_enabled`: a ZATCA QR code, TLV-encoded and then base64-encoded, containing the seller name, `vat_registration_number`, the invoice timestamp, the invoice total and the VAT total. Rendering is refused with a validation error while `vat_registration_number` is empty.
- the currency formatting keys (`default_currency_position`, `decimal_digits`) and the effective date format

Invoices are rendered on demand and are not stored.

### 43.3 Packing Slips

When `packing_slip_enabled` is true, `GET /api/admin/orders/{order}/packing-slip` renders a stock-only pick list for warehouse staff. It lists line names, SKUs, quantities and the fulfilling warehouse. It has no prices, and it groups lines by warehouse. When the setting is false, the route returns 404.

### 43.4 Barcode Sticker Settings

These are named sticker-sheet layouts for different label stock and printers.

```

name                     string
description              string   nullable

is_default               bool     default false
top_margin_inches        decimal(6,3)
left_margin_inches       decimal(6,3)
sticker_width_inches     decimal(6,3)
sticker_height_inches    decimal(6,3)

paper_height_inches      decimal(6,3)
stickers_per_row         int

```

`BarcodeSettingsService` (Tenant):

- `createSetting(array $data): BarcodeSetting`

- `generateStickerSheet(array $items, ?BarcodeSetting $setting = null, array $labelOptions = []): string`: lays barcodes out on the sheet, using the given setting or the default. `$items` is `[{product_id, product_variant_id, quantity}]`. The barcode value is the variant barcode when set, then the product barcode.

### 43.5 Print Barcode

This is the day-to-day label-printing screen. It prints onto a layout from §43.4.

- **Product search** uses the same lookup shape as `StockAdjustmentService::lookupProducts()` (§33.2). It searches by name, SKU or barcode, and returns the name, the on-hand quantity and the current price.
- **Quantity per product.** The batch table defaults each product's label count to its on-hand quantity, summed across warehouses, or at `?warehouse_id=` when given. Staff edit the counts per row. When the product `has_warehouse_pricing` and a warehouse is given, the price comes from that warehouse (§34).
- **Per-label content toggles**, each with its own font size:
  - `show_product_name` (`name_font_size`)
  - `show_price` (`price_font_size`)
  - `show_promotional_price` (`promotional_price_font_size`): the active flash-sale price
  - `show_business_name` (`business_name_font_size`): `store_name`
  - `show_brand` (`brand_font_size`)
  - `show_size` (`size_font_size`): the variant's size option value, when present
  - `show_barcode_value`: the human-readable code under the barcode
- **Paper size.** The staff member picks a saved `barcode_settings` layout. The default is the `is_default` layout.

`PrintBarcodeService` (Tenant):

- `searchProducts(string $query, ?Warehouse $warehouse = null): Collection`
- `generateLabels(array $items, ?BarcodeSetting $setting = null, array $labelOptions = []): string`: delegates the sheet layout to `BarcodeSettingsService::generateStickerSheet()`

### 43.6 Receipt Printers

A receipt printer is assigned to a warehouse, so POS receipts print directly to the device instead of through the browser's print dialog.

```
receipt_printers  [DB: tenant]
id
name                  string
warehouse_id          fk -> warehouses
connection_type       enum(network, usb, bluetooth)
capability_profile    string            ESC/POS capability profile, e.g. "default", "simple"
characters_per_line   int               e.g. 42 or 48
ip_address            string   nullable required when connection_type = network
port                  int      nullable required when connection_type = network
is_active             bool     default true
```

- At most one active printer per warehouse is used. `getPrinterForWarehouse()` returns the active printer with the lowest `id`.
- A warehouse with no active printer falls back to browser printing.
- The API returns the ESC/POS payload and the printer connection details. Delivery to the device is the POS client's job, because the server cannot reach a USB or Bluetooth printer (Assumption A-28).

## 44. Tenant Dashboard and Metrics

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none (core commerce). Sections and contextual KPIs of optional modules follow their module's state (§44.3). |
| **Code module** | `Dashboard` (composition); each module's own `Metrics/` provider computes its figures (§22.1) |
| **Depends on** | §22.1 to §22.4, §22.7, §32, §37, §39, §40, §41, §42 |

The tenant's admin dashboard and the KPI strips on its list screens. Everything uses the shared architecture, KPI shape, date ranges and caching of §22. Every figure is computed from the **current tenant's database only**.

### 44.1 Scope Rules

- **Included orders.** Sales figures count orders that are confirmed (`confirmed_at` set) **in the range**, not test orders (§40.8), not `cancelled`, and of `order_type = standard`. Gift-card purchases are liabilities, not sales (they appear in the gift-card section), and exchange replacements are part of their original sale.
- **Currency.** Amounts are in the base currency, converted with each order's `exchange_rate_used` where the order currency differs (§48).
- **Timezone.** The tenant timezone (§5.10).
- **Disabled modules.** A section or KPI of an optional module is returned only while the module is readable (§11.5); the section list (§22.3) omits the rest, so nothing is shown for a module the tenant does not use.

### 44.2 Metric Definitions

**Sales** (all tax-exclusive unless stated; for orders with `prices_include_tax`, a line's tax-exclusive value is its amount ÷ (1 + `tax_rate_applied` ÷ 100))

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| Gross sales | Σ tax-exclusive `line_subtotal` of included orders: merchandise at the resolved unit price, before discounts |
| Discounts | Σ tax-exclusive line `discount_amount` (every promotion, including the allocated order-level share) + Σ `reward_points_discount_amount` |
| Returns | Tax-exclusive value of successful refund and chargeback rows (`order_payments`, live) with `paid_at` in the range, using the tax-share rule of §57.3 (Assumption A-44); refunds of gift-card purchases excluded. Dated by the refund, not the order. |
| **Net sales** | Gross sales − discounts − returns. When `accounting` is enabled this equals Sales Revenue less Sales Returns for the same period (§57.3), which is the reconciliation check. |
| Tax | Σ `tax_amount` of included orders (lines and shipping) |
| Shipping revenue | Σ net shipping amount (§38.5) of included orders |
| Total sales | Σ `total` of included orders: what customers were charged, including tax and shipping |
| Refunds | Σ \|`amount_paid`\| of successful live `refund` rows with `paid_at` in the range (money returned, including tax and shipping); chargebacks reported separately |
| Orders | Count of included orders |
| Average order value (AOV) | (Gross sales − line discounts) ÷ orders: net merchandise value per order, excluding tax and shipping |
| Units sold | Σ `quantity` of lines of included orders |
| Gross profit | (Gross sales − line discounts) − Σ `unit_cost_snapshot × quantity`; lines without a cost snapshot are excluded and counted in a "cost unknown" note |

**Orders** (by `placed_at` in the range, test orders excluded): total, and counts by `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `partially_shipped` and `shipped`, `delivered` and `completed`, `cancelled`, `refunded`), plus **returned**: orders with a return in `received`, `refunded`, `exchanged` or `closed`. Outstanding balance: Σ (`total` − `net_paid`) of confirmed, non-cancelled orders with a balance, as of now.

**Customers**

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| Total customers | Customers not anonymised (§26.4) |
| New customers | Customers created in the range |
| First-time buyers | Customers whose first included order is in the range |
| Returning customers | Customers with an included order in the range and one before the range start |
| Repeat purchase rate | Returning customers ÷ customers with an included order in the range |
| Active / inactive customers | With / without an included order in the last 90 / 180 days |

**Catalogue and inventory**

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| Products / active / inactive | Products not deleted / storefront-visible (`is_active` and moderation allows, §50.3) / `is_active = false`. "Inactive" is the catalogue's draft state; there is no separate draft status. |
| Total SKUs | Active simple, bundle, digital and service products + active variants |
| Low stock / out of stock | As `InventoryService::getLowStockProducts()` / `getOutOfStockProducts()` (§32.6), tracked products only |
| Inventory value | Σ `inventory.quantity × current cost_price` (variant, else product), labelled "at current cost"; SKUs without a cost are excluded and counted |
| Stock movements / adjustments | `inventory_movements` by `movement_type` in the range; stock adjustments submitted in the range |
| Pending transfers | Stock transfers `in_transit` |

**Promotions**: running, scheduled and ended promotions (by window, now); active coupons; committed redemptions in the range; discount given = Σ `base_discount_amount` of committed redemptions in the range (§37.5).

**Payments** (`order_payments` of live orders, created in the range): successful, failed and pending counts and sums of `kind = payment`; refunds; gateway success rate = successful ÷ (successful + failed) gateway payments.

**Module figures** use their owning section's definitions: receivables (§57.6), payables and supplier balances (§49.4), commissions (§52), seller balances (§50.4), gift-card liability (§46), points balances (§54), installment balances (§47), and so on.

### 44.3 Dashboard Sections

## 45. Lookup Endpoints

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Landlord and Tenant |
| **Feature key** | none for the endpoints themselves. Module-specific lookups carry their module's `feature:{key}`. |
| **Code module** | `Lookups` |
| **Depends on** | Every section whose enums or tables are exposed |

Lookup endpoints fill dropdowns and filters without the frontend hardcoding lists or fetching full resources.

**Response shape:** `[{"value": "...", "label": "...", "meta": {...}}]`. `meta` is optional, for example a colour, a sort order, a parent ID for nesting, or a group. Lookups never return full resources.

**Implementation:** one generic `LookupController@show`, with a whitelist map from lookup key to an enum class or a query, serves the simple lookups. Lookups that need business logic have dedicated methods, for example nested categories and permissions grouped by module. Enum-backed lookups are generated from the PHP backed enums (§5.5), so the lists can never drift from validation.

Lookups carry no permission check beyond their group's authentication (Assumption A-29).

# Part 7: Optional Commerce Modules

Every module in this part has its own feature key and lifecycle ([§11.4](#114-module-registry), [§11.5](#115-module-lifecycle-and-disabled-behaviour)). Each builds on core commerce, which is always present, so none lists core commerce as a requirement. Admin route groups use `feature:{key}` and `module.notice:{key}`. When a module is not `enabled`, its integration hooks in core commerce are skipped.

## 46. Gift Cards

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `gift_cards` |
| **Code module** | `GiftCards` |
| **Depends on** | §38, §39, §40 |
| **Integration hooks** | Accounting (§57.3): a gift-card sale credits Gift Card Liability, not revenue; a redemption debits it |

A gift card is different from a coupon. A coupon is a promotional discount rule the tenant gives away. A gift card is a **stored-money instrument**: usually bought by one customer, redeemed by whoever holds the code, and spendable across several orders until its balance runs out. Redeeming a gift card is a **payment**, not a discount (§38.5).

### 46.1 Tables

```
gift_cards  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
code                      string   unique   generated, 16 characters, excluding ambiguous characters
initial_value             money
current_balance           money             never negative
currency_code             char(3)
purchased_by_customer_id  fk -> customers  nullable  null = issued directly by staff (e.g. goodwill)
source_order_id           fk -> orders  nullable unique  the gift_card_purchase order that paid for it
recipient_email           string   nullable  "buy as a gift, email it to someone"
recipient_message         string   nullable
status                    enum(active, redeemed, expired, disabled)
issued_by_user_id         fk -> users  nullable  staff-issued cards
issued_at                 datetime
expires_at                datetime nullable  null = never expires
```

```
gift_card_redemptions  [DB: tenant]
id
gift_card_id              fk -> gift_cards
order_id                  fk -> orders
order_payment_id          fk -> order_payments   the ledger row for this redemption or its reversal
amount                    money    positive = redeemed; negative = reversed back onto the card
created_at                datetime
```

`current_balance` is the source of truth. `gift_card_redemptions` is its audit trail. `current_balance` always equals `initial_value` minus the sum of `amount`.

### 46.2 Purchasing a Gift Card

1. `POST /api/gift-cards/purchase` with body `{amount, recipient_email?, recipient_message?}` creates an order through `OrderService::createOrder()`. The order has `order_type = gift_card_purchase` and a single non-product line (`product_id = null`, `name_snapshot = "Gift card"`). It has no shipping and no tax (Assumption A-30).
2. The customer pays through the normal flow (§40.2). A gift-card purchase cannot itself be paid with a gift card.
3. On confirmation (§39.4), `issueGiftCard()` creates the card in the order currency, with `source_order_id` set. A test order (§40.8) issues no card. `gift_card.issued` is sent to the `recipient_email`, falling back to the purchaser.

A POS sale can also sell a gift card, using the same order type (§51).

### 46.3 Redemption Rules

- A card applies to a cart through `POST /api/cart/apply-gift-card` (§38.7). The cart stores `gift_card_id`.
- The card must be `active` and unexpired, and its `currency_code` must equal the cart currency. Cross-currency redemption is out of scope in v1, and the request returns 422 `gift_card_currency_mismatch`.
- At checkout, the amount applied is `min(current_balance, total)` (§38.6). A card can be combined with a coupon on the same order.
- When `current_balance` reaches 0, the status becomes `redeemed`.
- The `ExpireGiftCards` job runs daily and moves cards past `expires_at` to `expired`.
- Reversal: cancelling an order (§39.5), or refunding a `gift_card` payment (§40.4), calls `reverseRedemption()`. This credits the amount back to the card and returns a `redeemed` card to `active`.

### 46.4 Service

`GiftCardService` (Tenant):

- `issueGiftCard(array $data): GiftCard`: used for purchases (called on confirmation) and for direct staff issue
- `validateForCart(string $code, Cart $cart): array`: `{valid, balance, applicable_amount, reason}`
- `redeemGiftCard(GiftCard $card, Order $order, float $amount): OrderPayment`: locks the card row, validates the balance and status, decrements `current_balance`, records the redemption and an `order_payments` row (`payment_method = gift_card`, `status = successful`), and sets `orders.gift_card_amount_applied`
- `reverseRedemption(OrderPayment $payment, ?float $amount = null): void`
- `checkBalance(string $code): array`: `{balance, currency_code, status, expires_at}`. Safe for public use.
- `disableGiftCard(GiftCard $card): void`: for example on suspected fraud
- `getGiftCard(GiftCard $card): GiftCard`
- `listGiftCards(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`

### 46.5 Routes

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\GiftCards\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.storefront` | POST | `/api/gift-cards/purchase` | `GiftCardPurchaseController@store` (`idempotency`) |
| `tenant.public` | GET | `/api/gift-cards/{code}/balance` | `GiftCardBalanceController@show`: `auth-sensitive` limiter |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/gift-cards` | `Admin\GiftCardController@index` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/gift-cards` | `Admin\GiftCardController@store`: direct issue (`idempotency`) |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/gift-cards/{card}` | `Admin\GiftCardController@show`: includes redemptions |
| `tenant.admin` | PATCH | `/api/admin/gift-cards/{card}/disable` | `Admin\GiftCardController@disable` |

Every route carries `feature:gift_cards`. The cart routes are in §38.7.

## 47. Installment Payments

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `installments` |
| **Code module** | `Installments` |
| **Depends on** | §39, §40 |

Installments let a customer pay for an order in several scheduled payments. This is the tenant's **own** in-house payment plan, similar to layaway: the tenant extends the credit and bears the risk. Third-party "buy now, pay later" credit, such as Klarna-style underwriting, is out of scope (Appendix C).

Two gates apply:

1. The `installments` feature, which decides whether the plan permits the module.
2. `tenant_settings.installments_enabled`, which decides whether the tenant offers it.

When either is off, the option is never offered, and the plan-creation route returns 403.

### 47.1 Tables

```
installment_plans  [DB: tenant]
id
order_id                  fk -> orders  unique
total_amount              money             the order total at plan creation
currency_code             char(3)           = orders.currency_code
number_of_installments    int               at least 2
frequency                 enum(weekly, biweekly, monthly)
status                    enum(active, completed, defaulted, cancelled)
starts_at                 date              first due date = plan creation date
payment_provider          string   nullable provider holding the stored authorization
authorization_token       encrypted nullable reusable authorization from the first gateway payment
consecutive_overdue_count int      default 0
```

```
installment_payments  [DB: tenant]
id
installment_plan_id       fk -> installment_plans
sequence                  int               1, 2, 3 ...
amount_due                money
due_date                  date
amount_paid               money    default 0
paid_at                   datetime nullable
status                    enum(pending, paid, overdue, failed)
unique(installment_plan_id, sequence)
```

Amounts are split evenly. Rounding differences are added to the last installment.

### 47.2 Settings

The following tenant settings apply (§13.4):

- `installments_enabled`
- `installments_minimum_order_amount`: orders below this total are not eligible
- `installments_fulfillment_policy`:
  - `on_full_payment` (the default): the order is confirmed and released only when fully paid, which behaves like true layaway
  - `on_first_payment`: the order is confirmed after the first installment clears. This is more common in retail, and riskier.
- `installments_default_after_overdue_count`

Stock is reserved at order creation under both policies. Only the confirmation gate differs ([§39.4](#394-confirmation-payment-status-and-order-status)).

### 47.3 Flow

1. **Opt in.** The customer chooses installments at checkout (the `installment_plan` input, §38.6), or later through `POST /api/orders/{order}/installment-plan`. This is allowed while the order has no payments.
2. **First installment.** The customer pays installment 1 through `POST /api/installment-payments/{payment}/pay`. This follows the gateway flow in §40.2, with `installment_payment_id` set on the ledger row and `save_authorization = true`. The returned authorization is stored on the plan.
3. **Each successful installment payment** updates `amount_paid`, `paid_at` and `status = paid` on the installment, resets `consecutive_overdue_count`, and runs `recalculatePaymentStatus()` on the order. Under `on_first_payment`, the first paid installment calls `confirmOrder()`.
4. **Scheduled charges.** The `ChargeDueInstallments` job runs daily. It charges `pending` installments due today through `OrderPaymentService::chargeStoredAuthorization()`. A failure sets `failed`, and the customer can still pay manually.
5. **Overdue.** The `MarkOverdueInstallments` job runs daily. It sets `pending` and `failed` installments whose `due_date` has passed to `overdue`, and increments `consecutive_overdue_count`. When the count reaches `installments_default_after_overdue_count`, the plan becomes `defaulted`. This is a business-status flag for staff to act on, for example by contacting the customer or cancelling the order. It never cancels anything automatically.
6. When every installment is paid, the plan becomes `completed`.

### 47.4 Service

`InstallmentPlanService` (Tenant):

- `isEligible(Order $order): bool`: checks the setting, the minimum amount, and that no payments exist yet
- `createPlan(Order $order, int $installments, string $frequency): InstallmentPlan`: rejects when not eligible
- `payInstallment(InstallmentPayment $payment, string $provider): array`: a customer-initiated payment. Returns `{checkout_url, reference}`.
- `chargeInstallment(InstallmentPayment $payment): void`: charges through the stored authorization
- `handleInstallmentPaid(InstallmentPayment $payment, OrderPayment $ledgerRow): void`: called by `OrderPaymentService` (§40.2)
- `markOverdue(InstallmentPayment $payment): void`
- `markPlanDefaulted(InstallmentPlan $plan): void`
- `cancelPlan(InstallmentPlan $plan): void`: stops future charges. Payments already made stay on the order.
- `getPlanForOrder(Order $order): ?InstallmentPlan`
- `listPlans(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Installments\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.storefront` | GET | `/api/orders/{order}/installment-eligibility` | `InstallmentController@eligibility` |
| `tenant.storefront` | POST | `/api/orders/{order}/installment-plan` | `InstallmentController@store`: body `number_of_installments`, `frequency` |
| `tenant.storefront` | GET | `/api/orders/{order}/installment-plan` | `InstallmentController@show` |

Every route carries `feature:installments`. Storefront routes are restricted to the order's owner (§39.6).

## 48. Multi-Currency

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `multi_currency`. This key replaces the inconsistent `multi-currency` spelling in earlier drafts. |
| **Code module** | `Currency` |
| **Depends on** | §13.4, §20, §38.4, §39 |
| **Integration hooks** | Accounting (§57) |

Every tenant has one base currency (`tenant_settings.default_currency`). This module lets a tenant sell in more currencies at **fixed, tenant-set prices**, the same deliberate pattern as `plan_prices` (§11.6). It does not use live FX pricing, which keeps prices predictable. Exchange rates are used only as a fallback estimate for products without an explicit price, and for converting amounts to the base currency.

### 48.1 Tables

```
tenant_currencies  [DB: tenant]
id
currency_code        char(3)  unique   ISO 4217
is_base              bool     default false  exactly one row is true; mirrors tenant_settings.default_currency
is_active            bool     default true   retire a currency without deleting history
display_symbol       string   nullable  e.g. "KSh" instead of the ISO code
```

```
product_prices  [DB: tenant]
id
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
variant_key          int      generated: COALESCE(product_variant_id, 0)
currency_code        char(3)
price                money
compare_at_price     money    nullable
unique(product_id, variant_key, currency_code)
```

```
currency_exchange_rates  [DB: tenant]
id
base_currency_code   char(3)
target_currency_code char(3)
rate                 rate              1 base = rate target
fetched_at           datetime
unique(base_currency_code, target_currency_code)
```

Provisioning seeds the base `tenant_currencies` row even when the feature is off, so the invariant always holds (§9.4).

### 48.2 Rules

- **Pricing.** Prices resolve through `PricingService` step 4 ([§38.4](#384-price-resolution)).
  - An explicit `product_prices` row is authoritative.
  - Otherwise, the price is converted at the stored reference rate and flagged `is_estimated = true`.
  - Exchange rates never reprice a product that has an explicit price for the currency.
- **Storefront.** Catalogue endpoints accept `?currency=` (§31). The cart currency is set through `PATCH /api/cart/currency` (§38.7).
- **Orders.** `orders.currency_code` is the currency the customer checked out in. For non-base currencies, `exchange_rate_used` and `base_currency_amount` are captured at order creation and are never recomputed. For base-currency orders, both are null.
- **Payment.** The chosen gateway must support the order currency (§15.3).
- **Currency-bound instruments.** Gift cards (§46), installment plans (§47) and product subscriptions (§55) stay in the currency of their originating order, and are never converted automatically.
- **Accounting.** Every journal entry is posted in the base currency. Postings from non-base records use `convertToBaseCurrency()` with the rate already captured on the record, never a fresh lookup (§57.3).
- **Base currency changes.** `setBaseCurrency()` is blocked once any order, purchase order or journal entry exists, because historical base amounts would otherwise become ambiguous (Assumption A-31).
- **Exchange-rate source.** The FX rate provider is UD-19. The `RefreshExchangeRates` job runs daily and fetches only the pairs between the base currency and the tenant's active currencies.

### 48.3 Service

`CurrencyService` (Tenant):

- `addTenantCurrency(string $code, bool $isActive = true): TenantCurrency`
- `deactivateTenantCurrency(TenantCurrency $currency): void`: blocked for the base currency
- `listTenantCurrencies(): Collection`
- `setBaseCurrency(TenantCurrency $currency): void`: flips `is_base` and updates `tenant_settings.default_currency` in one transaction. Subject to A-31.
- `setProductPrice(Product $product, string $currencyCode, float $price, ?float $compareAtPrice = null, ?ProductVariant $variant = null): ProductPrice`
- `deleteProductPrice(ProductPrice $price): void`
- `getPriceForCurrency(Product $product, string $currencyCode, ?ProductVariant $variant = null): array`: `{price, compare_at_price, is_estimated}`
- `refreshExchangeRates(): void`
- `convertToBaseCurrency(float $amount, string $fromCurrency, ?float $rateOverride = null): float`
- `getCurrencyExposure(): array`: outstanding order, gift-card and installment balances, grouped by currency

### 48.4 Routes

Group `tenant.admin` with `feature:multi_currency`:

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Currency\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/currencies` | `CurrencyController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/currencies` | `CurrencyController@store` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/currencies/{currency}/deactivate` | `CurrencyController@deactivate` |
| POST | `/api/admin/currencies/{currency}/set-base` | `CurrencyController@setBase` |
| GET | `/api/admin/products/{product}/prices` | `ProductPriceController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/products/{product}/prices` | `ProductPriceController@store` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/products/{product}/prices/{price}` | `ProductPriceController@update` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/products/{product}/prices/{price}` | `ProductPriceController@destroy` |
| GET | `/api/admin/accounting/reports/currency-exposure` | `CurrencyExposureController@show`: also requires `feature:accounting` |
