## 49. Suppliers and Purchasing

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `purchasing` |
| **Code module** | `Purchasing` |
| **Depends on** | §20, §27, §32 |
| **Integration hooks** | Accounting (§57), approval workflows (`module_key = purchase_order`, §60), multi-currency (§48) |

A supplier is upstream of the tenant: someone the tenant **buys** stock from. A seller (§50) is downstream: someone who sells **through** the tenant. Receiving a purchase order is what increases warehouse stock. This module is entirely back-office, with no customer-facing or seller-facing routes.

Billers are lightweight payees for expenses. They belong to Accounting (§57.4), not to this module.

### 49.1 Suppliers

```
suppliers  [DB: tenant]  soft deletes
id
name                 string
contact_name         string   nullable
email                string   nullable
phone                string   nullable
address_line         string   nullable
country_id           int      nullable  World
state_id             int      nullable  World
city_id              int      nullable  World
payment_terms        string   nullable  free text, e.g. "Net 30"
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
supplier_products  [DB: tenant]
id
supplier_id          fk -> suppliers
product_id           fk -> products
supplier_sku         string   nullable  the supplier's own reference
cost_price           money    nullable
lead_time_days       int      nullable
unique(supplier_id, product_id)
```

A product can be linked to several suppliers, each with its own cost.

### 49.2 Purchase Orders

```
purchase_orders  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
supplier_id          fk -> suppliers
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses     destination
status               enum(draft, submitted, partially_received, received, cancelled)
currency_code        char(3)              default_purchase_order_currency, falling back to default_currency
exchange_rate_used   rate     nullable     captured on submit for non-base currencies
order_date           date
expected_date        date     nullable
notes                text     nullable
created_by           fk -> users
```

```
purchase_order_items  [DB: tenant]
id
purchase_order_id    fk -> purchase_orders
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable  (Assumption A-32)
quantity_ordered     qty
quantity_received    qty      default 0
unit_cost            money
```

- The purchase-order total is `Σ quantity_ordered × unit_cost`. It is computed, not stored.
- **Submit.**
  - `draft` becomes `submitted`.
  - When an active approval workflow matches `module_key = purchase_order` (§60), receiving is blocked until the approval request is `approved`.
  - A rejected approval sets the purchase order to `cancelled`.
  - With no matching workflow, a submitted purchase order can be received immediately.
- **Receive.** `receiveStock()` accepts a partial set of lines and quantities. For each line it:
  - increments `quantity_received`
  - calls `InventoryService::adjustStock()` at the destination warehouse (reason `purchase_received`)
  - calls `AccountingService::postPurchaseOrderReceived()` for the received value (§57.3)

  The status becomes `partially_received` or `received`. `purchase_order.received` is dispatched.
- Only `draft` and `submitted` purchase orders with nothing received can be cancelled.
- **Duplicate** clones the supplier, warehouse and lines into a new `draft`, with `quantity_received = 0`. Payments and approval requests are not copied.

### 49.3 Supplier Quotations

Supplier quotations are an optional request-for-pricing step before a purchase order. They let a tenant compare quotes from several suppliers.

```
quotation_requests  [DB: tenant]
id
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses   destination
status               enum(draft, sent, received, converted, cancelled)
notes                text     nullable
requested_at         datetime
created_by           fk -> users

quotation_request_items  [DB: tenant]
id
quotation_request_id fk -> quotation_requests
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
quantity_requested   qty

supplier_quotations  [DB: tenant]
id
quotation_request_id fk -> quotation_requests
supplier_id          fk -> suppliers
status               enum(pending, received, accepted, rejected, expired)
valid_until          date     nullable
notes                text     nullable
received_at          datetime nullable
unique(quotation_request_id, supplier_id)

supplier_quotation_items  [DB: tenant]
id
supplier_quotation_id     fk -> supplier_quotations
quotation_request_item_id fk -> quotation_request_items
unit_price                money
lead_time_days            int      nullable
```

- Sending a request creates one `pending` supplier quotation per supplier and dispatches `quotation_request.sent` to each supplier.
- Staff enter each supplier's pricing. The request becomes `received` when the first quote is recorded.
- Accepting a quotation creates a `draft` purchase order with the supplier, warehouse, and every line's product, variant, quantity and unit price. It also rejects the sibling quotations and sets the request to `converted`.
- The `ExpireSupplierQuotations` job runs daily and expires `pending` and `received` quotations past `valid_until`.

### 49.4 Supplier Payments

Suppliers are paid outside the platform, by bank transfer, cash or cheque. This ledger records those payments. It has no gateway integration.

```
supplier_payments  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
supplier_id          fk -> suppliers
purchase_order_id    fk -> purchase_orders  nullable  null = a bulk payment across orders
purchase_return_id   fk -> purchase_returns nullable  set on refund rows (§49.5)
amount_due           money    nullable  balance being settled at the time
amount_received      money    nullable  the amount the supplier invoiced, when it differs
amount_paid          money              negative = money refunded by the supplier
change_given         money    nullable  cash overpayment handed back
payment_method       enum(cash, bank_transfer, cheque, card, other)
account_id           fk -> chart_of_accounts  nullable  the account the money came from (§57)
currency_code        char(3)
exchange_rate_used   rate     nullable
paid_at              datetime
reference            string   nullable  transfer reference or cheque number
notes                text     nullable
recorded_by_user_id  fk -> users
```

- Recording, updating or deleting a payment posts, re-posts or reverses `AccountingService::postSupplierPayment()` (§57.3).
- **Purchase-order balance** = the purchase-order total − Σ `amount_paid` for that order − the value of approved purchase returns against it.
- **Supplier balance** = the same calculation across all the supplier's purchase orders, minus unallocated payments. This is a simple running balance, with no aging buckets.

### 49.5 Purchase Returns

A purchase return sends received stock back to the supplier. It mirrors the order-return pattern (§41).

```
purchase_return_reasons  [DB: tenant]
id
label                string            e.g. "Damaged on arrival", "Wrong item shipped"
is_active            bool     default true

purchase_returns  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
purchase_order_id          fk -> purchase_orders
supplier_id                fk -> suppliers
warehouse_id               fk -> warehouses   stock leaves from here
purchase_return_reason_id  fk -> purchase_return_reasons
status                     enum(requested, approved, rejected, shipped_back, refunded, closed)
resolution                 enum(refund, credit_note)  nullable  set when resolved
note                       text     nullable
rejection_reason           string   nullable
requested_at               datetime
resolved_at                datetime nullable

purchase_return_items  [DB: tenant]
id
purchase_return_id       fk -> purchase_returns
purchase_order_item_id   fk -> purchase_order_items
quantity                 qty      at most the line's quantity_received minus earlier returns
unit_cost                money    copied from the purchase-order line at creation
```

- Return reasons are curated separately from customer `return_reasons`.
- **Approve.** The returned quantity is deducted from the warehouse immediately through `adjustStock()` (reason `purchase_return`). The tenant already knows the stock is leaving, so there is no inspection step. When `accounting` is enabled, `AccountingService::postPurchaseReturn()` runs: Dr Accounts Payable, Cr Inventory Asset.
- **Resolve.** `processSupplierRefund()` sets `status = refunded` and records `resolution`:
  - `refund`: records a negative `supplier_payments` row (money back, with `purchase_return_id` set). This posts Dr Cash/Bank, Cr Accounts Payable.
  - `credit_note`: records nothing further. Payables were already reduced on approval, so the credit is consumed by future purchase-order balances.

## 50. Marketplace: Sellers, Seller Groups and Payouts

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `marketplace` |
| **Code module** | `Marketplace` |
| **Depends on** | §10 (seller authentication), §27, §39, §40 |
| **Integration hooks** | Accounting (§57), approval workflows (`module_key = seller_application`, §60), product questions (§29.7) |

In marketplace mode, a tenant runs its own official store **and** lets third-party vendors (sellers) list their products under the tenant's storefront, similar to Jumia or Amazon. A seller is its own business entity. It is not a staff user and not a customer, and it authenticates with its own guard (§10).

There are two commission layers, and they must not be confused:

| Commission | Who pays whom | Configured by | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Platform commission** | Tenant pays the platform | `platform_settings`, `tenant_platform_settings` | §15.8 |
| **Seller commission** | Seller pays the tenant (deducted from payouts) | seller, seller group, `tenant_settings.default_seller_commission_rate` | §50.3 |

### 50.1 Tables

```
sellers  [DB: tenant]  soft deletes
id
seller_group_id      fk -> seller_groups  nullable
business_name        string
contact_name         string   nullable
email                string   unique
phone                string   nullable
password             string            hashed
email_verified_at    datetime nullable
status               enum(pending, approved, rejected, suspended)  default pending
rejection_reason     string   nullable
commission_rate      percent  nullable  per-seller override
approved_at          datetime nullable
last_login_at        datetime nullable
```

```
seller_groups  [DB: tenant]
id
name                     string            e.g. "Standard", "Verified", "Premium"
description              text     nullable
default_commission_rate  percent  nullable  applies to members without their own rate
```

- Seller groups let a tenant offer better terms to trusted sellers without editing rates one by one. They are also the natural place for future group perks.
- A seller with no group falls through to the tenant default rate. No default group is seeded.

### 50.2 Seller Lifecycle

1. **Register.** `POST /api/seller/auth/register` creates a `pending` seller and dispatches `seller.new_seller_application`.
2. **Approval gate.** When an active approval workflow matches `module_key = seller_application` (§60), it gates approval. Otherwise, staff approve or reject directly. `seller.application_approved` or `seller.application_rejected` is dispatched.
3. **Login.** Only `approved` sellers can log in (§10.3).
4. **Suspend.** Suspension revokes the seller's tokens and sets the seller's products to `is_active = false`. Reactivation (approving again) does not re-activate products automatically.

### 50.3 Seller Products and Orders

- A seller creates and manages products with `seller_id` set to itself. The `max_products` limit counts these too.
- Sellers cannot set:
  - `seller_id`
  - `has_warehouse_pricing`
  - `is_bookable`
  - `is_subscribable`
  - `social_commerce_excluded_channels`
- **Moderation** (decides UD-11). When `tenant_settings.seller_product_approval_required` is true, a product created by a seller gets `products.moderation_status = pending` and is hidden from the storefront until staff approve it. `seller.new_product_pending_approval` is dispatched to staff. Approval or rejection (with `moderation_note`) dispatches `seller.product_approved` or `seller.product_rejected` to the seller. Edits to an approved product do not re-trigger moderation (Assumption A-68). Tenant-created products always have `moderation_status = not_required`. Storefront visibility requires `is_active = true` **and** `moderation_status` in (`not_required`, `approved`).
- **Fulfilment model** (decides UD-20). The marketplace is **tenant-fulfilled (consignment)**. Seller products are stocked in, and fulfilled from, the tenant's warehouses by tenant staff, using the normal inventory model (§32). Sellers never mutate stock or shipments. This keeps one inventory ledger and one fulfilment flow for B2C and marketplace alike. Seller-managed fulfilment is deferred (Appendix C).
- **Seller-funded promotions.** Staff may create a promotion with `seller_id` set on a seller's behalf (§37.2). Only such promotions reduce the seller's earnings. Seller self-service promotions are deferred (Appendix C).
- **Isolation from B2C.** Every marketplace behaviour is gated by `feature:marketplace`. With the feature off, `seller_id` is always null, no seller routes exist, and the order, promotion and accounting flows skip every seller branch. Enabling the marketplace never changes how tenant-owned products are sold.
- `order_items.seller_id` snapshots the product's seller. A seller sees only its own order lines, through `OrderService::getOrderItemsForSeller()`.
- Sellers answer questions about their own products (§29.7).

**Effective commission rate:** the seller's `commission_rate`, else the group's `default_commission_rate`, else `tenant_settings.default_seller_commission_rate`.

### 50.4 Seller Ledger

The earlier single `seller_payouts` design mixed per-line earnings with payout batches. It is split into two tables:

```
seller_ledger_entries  [DB: tenant]
id
seller_id                fk -> sellers
order_id                 fk -> orders
order_item_id            fk -> order_items
entry_type               enum(sale, reversal)
source_type              string   nullable  morph type of the reversal cause: OrderReturn, OrderPayment (refund or
                                            chargeback) or Order (cancellation); null for sale entries
source_id                int      nullable
gross_amount             money    seller's line gross excluding tax, in base currency (rule below); negative for reversals
commission_rate_applied  percent
commission_amount        money    negative for reversals
net_payable              money    gross_amount − commission_amount; negative for reversals
available_at             datetime nullable  when the entry becomes payable; null until the order completes
seller_payout_id         fk -> seller_payouts  nullable  set once included in a payout
created_at               datetime
unique(order_item_id, entry_type, source_type, source_id)
index(seller_id, seller_payout_id, available_at)
```

- **Seller gross** = `line_subtotal − seller_funded_discount_amount`, excluding tax, converted to the base currency (§38.5, §39.2). Tenant-funded discounts do not reduce it: the tenant pays for its own promotions.
- On confirmation (§39.4), `SellerLedgerService::recordOrderLines()` writes one `sale` entry per seller line, with `available_at = null`. Test orders (§40.8) write nothing.
- When the order reaches completion (§39.4), `available_at` is set to `completed_at + seller_payout_hold_days` (or the effective return window when that setting is null) on its sale entries. Earnings are therefore never paid out while a return is still possible.
- A **reversal** entry is written for the refunded share of a seller line by every path that gives money back: a return refund (`ReturnService::processRefund()`), a direct refund with its line attribution (§39.5), a lost chargeback (§40.5), and cancellation of a confirmed order (§39.5). A reversal's amounts are the sale entry's amounts × the refunded proportion, rounded. Its `available_at` is its creation time, so it is netted in the next payout. The unique key makes each cause idempotent.

### 50.5 Seller Payouts

```
seller_payouts  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
seller_id            fk -> sellers
period_start         date
period_end           date
gross_amount         money
commission_amount    money
net_payable          money
status               enum(pending, paid)
paid_at              datetime nullable
reference            string   nullable  bank transfer reference
notes                text     nullable
created_by           fk -> users
```

- Staff generate a payout for a seller and a period. In one transaction, it locks the seller row, then collects every unassigned ledger entry, sale or reversal, whose `available_at` lies within the period, and sets their `seller_payout_id`. The seller row lock makes two concurrent payout requests for the same seller impossible, so an entry can never be paid twice.
- A payout whose `net_payable` would be zero or negative is not created. The entries stay unassigned and are netted against later earnings.
- Payouts are paid **outside the platform** and marked paid (§15.7).
- When `accounting` is enabled:
  - On confirmation, `AccountingService::postSellerCommission()` reclassifies each seller line from Sales Revenue into Commission Revenue (the tenant's cut) and Accounts Payable – Sellers (the seller's net).
  - `markPaid()` calls `postSellerPayout()`: Dr Accounts Payable – Sellers, Cr Cash/Bank.

- `approveSeller(Seller $seller): void`: enforces `max_sellers` (approved sellers, §11.8). Pending applications do not count, so sign-ups are never blocked; only approval is.

## 51. Point of Sale

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `pos` |
| **Code module** | `Pos` |
| **Depends on** | §25, §32, §38.4, §39, §40, §43.6 |
| **Integration hooks** | Gift cards (§46), sales agents (§52), reward points (§54), restaurant (§65), accounting (§57) |

POS is in-person selling at a physical counter. It is built **on top of** the catalogue, inventory, order and payment ledger. It is not a parallel system. A POS sale **is** an order (`order_source = pos`), so it appears in the same order history, dashboards and inventory flows. What POS adds is the register, cash-handling and offline-tolerant sale layer.

Cashiers are staff users. They use the `tenant.admin` group, and their actions are governed by the derived `pos.*` permissions. There is no separate guard.

### 51.1 Registers and Sessions

```
pos_registers  [DB: tenant]
id
warehouse_id           fk -> warehouses     stock is sold from, and deducted at, this warehouse
name                   string               e.g. "Front Counter", "Till 2"
terminal_provider      enum(moniepoint, opay, stripe_terminal)  nullable  null = no card terminal
terminal_credentials   encrypted json  nullable  provider-specific (API key, terminal ID, merchant code)
is_active              bool     default true
```

```
pos_sessions  [DB: tenant]
id
pos_register_id        fk -> pos_registers
opened_by_user_id      fk -> users
closed_by_user_id      fk -> users  nullable
opening_cash_float     money
closing_cash_float     money    nullable  counted at close
expected_cash          money    nullable  calculated at close
cash_variance          money    nullable  closing_cash_float − expected_cash
status                 enum(open, closed)
opened_at              datetime
closed_at              datetime nullable
```

- A register has at most one `open` session at a time.
- Creating a register enforces the `max_pos_registers` limit (§11.8) and the operational ceiling `platform_settings.max_pos_registers_per_warehouse` (§13.2).
- A session is the shift boundary. A cashier opens a session at the start of a shift and closes it at the end, and every sale in between is tied to it.
- When `pos_settings.cash_register_enabled` is false, sessions are not required. Sales then have `pos_session_id = null`. This suits card-only tenants.

### 51.2 POS Payments

POS payments are rows in the **same** `order_payments` ledger (§40.1), with `pos_session_id` set. There is no separate `pos_payments` table. Split tender, for example part cash and part card, is several rows.

| POS method | `order_payments.payment_method` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cash` | `cash` | Records `amount_received` and `change_given` |
| `card_terminal` | `card_terminal` | `provider` = the register's `terminal_provider`; `provider_reference` = the terminal reference (RRN) |
| `bank_transfer` | `bank_transfer` | Confirmed manually by the cashier |
| `cheque` | `cheque` | |
| `gift_card` | `gift_card` | Requires `gift_cards` (§46) |
| `reward_points` | none: applied as the `reward_points_discount_amount` discount | Requires `reward_points` (§54) and a real customer |
| `credit_sale` | none: the balance remains due | Requires a real customer (not the default walk-in). The order is confirmed with `payment_status` `unpaid` or `partially_paid`. It is settled later through §40.6. |

- `pos_settings.enabled_payment_methods` is a subset of the values in this table. It only filters what the POS screen offers. Credentials are never entered here.
- Methods listed in earlier drafts that have no driver in this specification (`upi`, `razorpay`, `paypal`, `mpesa`, `mtn_momo`, `payoneer`, `stripe` as an online gateway at the counter, `moyasar`) are deferred (Appendix C).
- `deposit`, `wallet` and POS `installment` are deferred (Appendix C). Store credit needs its own liability ledger, and nothing else in v1 depends on it.
- Online payment gateways are not offered at the counter (§15.4).

### 51.3 Sale Flow

`PosSaleService::createSale()`:

1. **Session.** When `cash_register_enabled` is true, an open session on the register is required.
2. **Lines.** Products are added by scan or search. `GET /api/admin/pos/products/lookup?barcode=` checks `product_variants.barcode` first, then `products.barcode`. Barcodes are unique across both tables (§28.2). Prices come from `PricingService` at the register warehouse. Promotions come from `PromotionEngine::evaluate()` with `channel = pos`, including a coupon the cashier enters (§37.6). Tax uses the register warehouse's location (§35.2). The screen shows the quote from `PosSaleService::quote()` before payment.
3. **Customer.** The cashier can pick a customer. Otherwise, `pos_settings.default_customer_id` is used, which is an ordinary customer record, for example "Walk-in Customer". If that is also null, the customer is null.
4. **Payments.** The card-terminal charge is initiated and verified before the sale is submitted (§51.4). The service re-verifies every `card_terminal` reference.
   - Payments must cover the total, unless `credit_sale` is used.
   - Overpayment is allowed only in cash, and becomes `change_given`.
5. **Commit.** One database transaction:
   1. `OrderService::createOrder()` with `order_source = pos`, `status = completed`, `pos_session_id`, `idempotency_key`, `created_by_user_id` (the cashier), and optional `sales_agent_id`
   2. `FlashSaleService::claim()` and `PromotionRedemptionService::reserve()`, with the same locks and 409 outcomes as online checkout (§38.6)
   3. the `order_payments` rows
   4. the reward points and gift card redemptions
   5. `OrderService::confirmOrder()`, which deducts stock directly at the register warehouse (§32.5) and commits the redemptions

   A failure part-way rolls back everything, so stock is never deducted without a completed order.
6. **Receipt.** `generateReceipt()` returns structured receipt data. It is printed through the warehouse's receipt printer when one is configured (§43.6), otherwise by the browser. It is emailed or sent by SMS when `send_sms_after_sale` is set and contact details exist.

`createSale()` is a **one-pass** sale: lines and payment are submitted together. Restaurant table orders, which stay open across several rounds and are paid at the end, use the open-order flow in §65.4 instead. They reuse the same session, payment and receipt mechanics.

**Void.** `voidSale()` is allowed only while the sale's session is still open (Assumption A-34). It refunds every payment through `OrderPaymentService::refund()` (§40.4), which reverses card-terminal payments through the terminal driver. It restocks every line through `adjustStock()` (reason `pos_void`) and records the reason. The order ends in `refunded`. After the session closes, the normal return flow (§41) applies.

### 51.4 Terminal Providers

A card terminal is a physical device transaction, not a redirect-and-webhook flow. It therefore has its own contract, alongside `PaymentGatewayInterface`:

```php
interface PosTerminalGatewayInterface
{
    public function initiateCharge(float $amount, string $currencyCode, array $meta = []): array; // {reference}
    public function verifyCharge(string $reference): array;   // {status, amount, card_last4?}
    public function refund(string $reference, ?float $amount = null): array;
}
```

- Drivers: `MoniepointTerminalGateway` and `OpayTerminalGateway` for Nigeria, and `StripeTerminalGateway` for other countries.
- `PosTerminalGatewayFactory::forRegister(PosRegister $register)` builds the driver from the register's `terminal_provider` and `terminal_credentials`.
- Terminal charges are initiated and verified through dedicated routes (§51.8) before the sale is submitted (Assumption A-35).
- Reconciling terminal settlement reports is deferred (Appendix C).

### 51.5 Session Close

`closeSession()`:

- `expected_cash` = `opening_cash_float` + Σ cash `amount_paid` in the session, where cash refunds count as negative.
- `cash_variance` = `closing_cash_float − expected_cash`.
- When `|cash_variance|` exceeds `pos_cash_variance_threshold`, `pos.session_variance_flagged` is dispatched.
- Card-terminal totals are summarised the same way, for information only.

### 51.6 Offline Resilience

- The POS client queues sales locally when offline and syncs them through `POST /api/admin/pos/sales` when back online. Each sale carries a client-generated `idempotency_key`.
- A request whose `idempotency_key` already exists returns the existing order with 200. It never creates a duplicate.
- The client caches stock and prices, and refreshes them periodically.
- If stock is insufficient when a queued sale syncs, the API responds 409 `stock_conflict` with the affected lines. Stock is never allowed to go negative (§32.4). The client keeps the sale flagged for staff, who adjust stock or edit the sale and then retry. Conflicts are never dropped silently.
- An offline sale carries the discount the customer was actually given. When it syncs, promotions are re-evaluated at the client-recorded sale time, which becomes `orders.placed_at`. If a promotion's usage limit has since been exhausted, the sale is **still accepted**: the goods and money have already changed hands. The redemption is recorded as `committed` beyond the limit with `promotion_redemptions.over_limit = true`, and `promotion.limit_exceeded_offline` is dispatched to staff. Online checkout never exceeds a limit. Only offline POS can, by necessity (Assumption A-69).

### 51.7 POS Settings

```
pos_settings  [DB: tenant]  singleton (§5.9)
id
default_warehouse_id          fk -> warehouses  nullable  pre-selected on the POS screen
default_customer_id           fk -> customers   nullable  the standing "Walk-in Customer" record
default_cashier_user_id       fk -> users       nullable  pre-selected attribution on shared kiosk terminals
products_per_page             int      default 20
touchscreen_keyboard_enabled  bool     default false
table_management_enabled      bool     default false  used by restaurant (§65)
send_sms_after_sale           bool     default false
cash_register_enabled         bool     default true
print_receipt_by_default      bool     default true
play_sound_on_sale            bool     default false
enabled_payment_methods       json     default ["cash"]  subset of the POS methods in §51.2
```

On a shared terminal, the sale's `created_by_user_id` is the authenticated user. The optional `cashier_user_id` request field defaults to `default_cashier_user_id`, and overrides the attribution when present.

### 51.8 Services and Routes

`PosRegisterService`: `createRegister()`, `updateRegister()`, `setTerminal(PosRegister $register, ?string $provider, ?array $credentials)`, `deactivateRegister()`, `listRegisters()`.

`PosSessionService`:

- `openSession(PosRegister $register, User $cashier, float $openingCash): PosSession`
- `closeSession(PosSession $session, float $closingCash): PosSession`
- `getCurrentSession(PosRegister $register): ?PosSession`
- `getSessionSummary(PosSession $session): array`: totals by method, sale count and variance
- `listSessions(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`

`PosSaleService`:

- `quote(PosRegister $register, array $lines, ?Customer $customer = null, ?string $couponCode = null): Quote`: prices, promotions, tax and total, with no writes
- `createSale(?PosSession $session, array $lines, array $payments, ?Customer $customer = null, array $options = []): Order`
- `voidSale(Order $order, string $reason): void`
- `generateReceipt(Order $order): array`
- `lookupProduct(string $barcode): ?array`
- `initiateTerminalCharge(PosRegister $register, float $amount): array`
- `verifyTerminalCharge(PosRegister $register, string $reference): array`
- `listSales(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`

`PosSettingsService`: `getSettings()`, `updateSettings(array $data)`.

## 52. Sales Agents

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `sales_agents` |
| **Code module** | `SalesAgents` |
| **Depends on** | §25, §39 |

A sales agent is credited, and earns commission, for driving a sale that the **tenant** fulfils. This is a referral or commission-rep model. It is distinct from a seller (§50), who lists and fulfils its own products. Agent commissions and seller earnings are separate tables and are never summed together in reports.

### 52.1 Tables

```
sales_agents  [DB: tenant]
id
user_id              fk -> users  nullable  set when the agent is also a staff user; null = external agent with no login
name                 string
phone                string
email                string   nullable
agent_code           string   unique  short code used for attribution
commission_rate      percent  nullable  per-agent override
status               enum(active, inactive)  default active
```

Earlier drafts had both `status` and `is_active`. Only `status` exists.

```
sales_agent_commissions  [DB: tenant]
id
sales_agent_id       fk -> sales_agents
order_id             fk -> orders  unique
gross_amount         money    the commission base, in base currency
commission_rate_applied percent
commission_amount    money
status               enum(pending, approved, paid)
earned_at            datetime
paid_at              datetime nullable
```

### 52.2 Rules

- **Attribution** sets `orders.sales_agent_id` before confirmation. It can happen:
  - at checkout, through `sales_agent_code`, which must belong to an `active` agent (§38.6)
  - at the POS or by staff, through `sales_agent_id`
- **Commission base** = the order's net merchandise amount (§38.5), converted to the base currency. It excludes tax and shipping, and is after every promotion discount (Assumption A-36).
- **Effective rate** = the agent's `commission_rate`, else `tenant_settings.default_sales_agent_commission_rate`.
- **Trigger.** On confirmation (§39.4), `SalesAgentCommissionService::calculateCommission()` creates a `pending` commission. Test orders (§40.8) earn none.
- **Payment.** Staff approve a commission (`approved`), then mark it paid once paid outside the platform (`paid`). There is no gateway integration (§15.7).
- **Refunds** do not adjust commissions automatically in v1. Staff simply do not approve affected commissions (Appendix C).

### 52.3 Services and Routes

`SalesAgentService`:

- `createAgent(array $data): SalesAgent`
- `updateAgent(SalesAgent $agent, array $data): SalesAgent`
- `deactivateAgent(SalesAgent $agent): void`
- `listAgents(array $filters): Collection`
- `getAgentByCode(string $code): ?SalesAgent`
- `attributeOrder(Order $order, SalesAgent $agent): void`: rejected after confirmation

`SalesAgentCommissionService`:

- `calculateCommission(Order $order): ?SalesAgentCommission`
- `approveCommission(SalesAgentCommission $commission): void`
- `markPaid(SalesAgentCommission $commission): void`
- `getCommissionsForAgent(SalesAgent $agent, array $filters): Collection`
- `getOutstandingBalance(SalesAgent $agent): float`: approved and unpaid commissions

Routes (group `tenant.admin` with `feature:sales_agents`). There is no agent-facing surface in v1: the agent code is just a field on checkout and POS.

| GET | `/api/admin/sales-agents` | `SalesAgentController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/sales-agents` | `SalesAgentController@store` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/sales-agents/{agent}` | `SalesAgentController@update` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/sales-agents/{agent}` | `SalesAgentController@destroy`: deactivates the agent |
| GET | `/api/admin/sales-agents/{agent}/commissions` | `SalesAgentCommissionController@index` |
| GET | `/api/admin/sales-agents/{agent}/balance` | `SalesAgentCommissionController@balance` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/sales-agent-commissions/{commission}/approve` | `SalesAgentCommissionController@approve` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/sales-agent-commissions/{commission}/mark-paid` | `SalesAgentCommissionController@markPaid` |

## 53. Sales Quotations

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `sales_quotations` |
| **Code module** | `SalesQuotations` |
| **Depends on** | §26, §38.4, §39 |
| **Integration hooks** | Sales agents (§52), multi-currency (§48) |

A sales quotation is the mirror image of a supplier quotation (§49.3). A customer, or staff or an agent on the customer's behalf, requests a formal price quote before ordering. This is common for B2B, bulk or negotiated prices. It is optional: customers can always check out directly.

### 53.1 Tables

```
sales_quotation_requests  [DB: tenant]
id
customer_id          fk -> customers  nullable  null = a walk-in or phone enquiry started by staff
sales_agent_id       fk -> sales_agents  nullable
status               enum(draft, sent, quoted, accepted, rejected, expired, converted, cancelled)
currency_code        char(3)          base currency unless multi_currency
notes                text     nullable
requested_at         datetime
created_by_user_id   fk -> users  nullable  null = customer self-service

sales_quotation_request_items  [DB: tenant]
id
sales_quotation_request_id  fk -> sales_quotation_requests
product_id                  fk -> products
product_variant_id          fk -> product_variants  nullable
quantity_requested          qty

sales_quotations  [DB: tenant]
id
sales_quotation_request_id  fk -> sales_quotation_requests  unique  (one quote per request)
status               enum(draft, sent, accepted, rejected, expired)
valid_until          date     nullable
notes                text     nullable
sent_at              datetime nullable
converted_order_id   fk -> orders  nullable

sales_quotation_items  [DB: tenant]
id
sales_quotation_id               fk -> sales_quotations
sales_quotation_request_item_id  fk -> sales_quotation_request_items
unit_price                       money
discount_amount                  money    nullable
```

**Status mapping.**

| Event | Request status | Quotation status |
|---|---|---|
| Customer or staff submit the request | `sent` | none yet |
| Staff send the quote | `quoted` | `sent` |
| Quote accepted | `converted` | `accepted` |
| Quote rejected | `rejected` | `rejected` |
| `valid_until` passes | `expired` | `expired` |
| Request cancelled | `cancelled` | none |

A staff-started request can sit in `draft` before it is submitted.

### 53.2 Rules

- **Stock check.** When `allow_quotation_without_stock` is false, `sendQuotation()` rejects lines with no available stock. A quotation is a price commitment, not a stock reservation.
- **Acceptance** converts the quote to an order through `OrderService::createOrder()`:
  - The customer, and each line's product, variant, quantity, quoted `unit_price` and quoted `discount_amount`, are copied over, with `price_source = quotation` (§39.2). The quoted price replaces `PricingService`. Promotions are **not** applied to a converted quotation: the quote is the negotiated price.
  - Tax is calculated at conversion (§35).
  - The order starts at `pending`. `order_source` is `online` when the customer accepts from the storefront, and `admin` when staff accept.
  - Stock is reserved as for any order.
  - The customer pays through the normal flow (§40).
- `sales_quotation.sent` is dispatched to the customer when one is attached.
- The `ExpireSalesQuotations` job runs daily.

### 53.3 Service and Routes

`SalesQuotationService`:

- `createRequest(?Customer $customer, array $items, ?SalesAgent $agent = null): SalesQuotationRequest`
- `sendQuotation(SalesQuotationRequest $request, array $items, ?Carbon $validUntil = null): SalesQuotation`
- `acceptQuotation(SalesQuotation $quotation): Order`
- `rejectQuotation(SalesQuotation $quotation): void`
- `cancelRequest(SalesQuotationRequest $request): void`
- `getRequest(SalesQuotationRequest $request): SalesQuotationRequest`
- `listRequests(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\SalesQuotations\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.customer` | GET | `/api/quotation-requests` | `QuotationRequestController@index` |
| `tenant.customer` | POST | `/api/quotation-requests` | `QuotationRequestController@store` |
| `tenant.customer` | GET | `/api/quotation-requests/{request}` | `QuotationRequestController@show`: includes the quote once sent |
| `tenant.customer` | POST | `/api/quotation-requests/{request}/accept` | `QuotationRequestController@accept` |
| `tenant.customer` | POST | `/api/quotation-requests/{request}/reject` | `QuotationRequestController@reject` |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/sales-quotation-requests` | `Admin\SalesQuotationRequestController@index` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/sales-quotation-requests` | `Admin\SalesQuotationRequestController@store` |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/sales-quotation-requests/{request}` | `Admin\SalesQuotationRequestController@show` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/sales-quotation-requests/{request}/send` | `Admin\SalesQuotationRequestController@send` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/sales-quotation-requests/{request}/cancel` | `Admin\SalesQuotationRequestController@cancel` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/sales-quotations/{quotation}/accept` | `Admin\SalesQuotationController@accept` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/sales-quotations/{quotation}/reject` | `Admin\SalesQuotationController@reject` |

Every route carries `feature:sales_quotations`. The customer-facing `/api/quotation-requests` routes are unrelated to the supplier-side `/api/admin/quotation-requests` routes (§49.7).

## 54. Reward Points

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `reward_points` |
| **Code module** | `RewardPoints` |
| **Depends on** | §26, §38, §39 |

Reward points are a loyalty programme. Customers earn points automatically from spending, and redeem them against later orders. This is not a coupon: points accrue from spend and carry a running balance per customer.

Two gates apply: the `reward_points` feature, and `reward_point_settings.is_active`.

### 54.1 Tables

```
reward_point_settings  [DB: tenant]  singleton (§5.9)
id
is_active                         bool     default false
amount_per_point                  money             spend (base currency) that earns one point
minimum_order_amount_to_earn      money    nullable
point_expiry_days                 int      nullable  null = never expire
redeem_amount_per_point           money             order value of one point when redeeming
minimum_order_total_to_redeem     money    nullable
minimum_redeem_points             int      nullable
maximum_redeem_points_per_order   int      nullable
```

The earn rate and the burn rate are deliberately separate.

```
customer_reward_points  [DB: tenant]
id
customer_id          fk -> customers  unique
points_balance       int      default 0   denormalised; never negative

reward_point_transactions  [DB: tenant]
id
customer_id          fk -> customers
order_id             fk -> orders  nullable  null for manual adjustments and expiry
type                 enum(earned, redeemed, expired, adjusted)
points               int      positive for earned or adjusted up; negative for redeemed, expired or adjusted down
balance_after        int      snapshot
expires_at           datetime nullable  earned rows only, when point_expiry_days is set
notes                string   nullable
created_at           datetime
```

### 54.2 Rules

- **Earning** happens when a non-test order (§40.8) reaches a completion state (`delivered` or `completed`, §39.4) and has a customer:
  - The eligible amount is the net merchandise amount (§38.5) minus `reward_points_discount_amount`, in the base currency (Assumption A-37).
  - No points are earned below `minimum_order_amount_to_earn`.
  - Points = `floor(eligible amount ÷ amount_per_point)`.
  - Earning is idempotent per order.
- **Redemption** requires an authenticated customer, online or at the POS with a real customer.
  - Validation checks `minimum_redeem_points`, `maximum_redeem_points_per_order`, `minimum_order_total_to_redeem` and the available balance.
  - The discount is `points × redeem_amount_per_point`, capped at the order total before the discount.
  - It is recorded on `orders.reward_points_redeemed` and `reward_points_discount_amount` (§38.5).
- **Cancellation** of an order restores its redeemed points as an `adjusted` transaction (§39.5). Points already earned on orders that are later refunded are not clawed back in v1 (Appendix C).
- **Expiry.** The `ExpireRewardPoints` job runs daily. For each earned row past `expires_at` that has not yet been processed, it expires `min(row points, current balance)` (Assumption A-38).

### 54.3 Service and Routes

`RewardPointService`:

- `getSettings(): RewardPointSettings`
- `updateSettings(array $data): RewardPointSettings`
- `earnPoints(Order $order): void`
- `validateRedemption(Customer $customer, int $points, float $orderTotal): array`: used by `CartService::applyRewardPoints()`
- `redeemPoints(Order $order, int $points): float`: returns the discount
- `restorePoints(Order $order): void`
- `getBalance(Customer $customer): int`
- `getTransactionHistory(Customer $customer): Collection`
- `adjustPoints(Customer $customer, int $points, string $reason): void`
- `expirePoints(): void`

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\RewardPoints\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.customer` | GET | `/api/account/reward-points/balance` | `RewardPointController@balance` |
| `tenant.customer` | GET | `/api/account/reward-points/history` | `RewardPointController@history` |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/reward-points/settings` | `Admin\RewardPointSettingsController@show` |
| `tenant.admin` | PUT | `/api/admin/reward-points/settings` | `Admin\RewardPointSettingsController@update` |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/customers/{customer}/reward-points` | `Admin\CustomerRewardPointController@show` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/customers/{customer}/reward-points/adjust` | `Admin\CustomerRewardPointController@adjust` |

Every route carries `feature:reward_points`. The earlier `/api/customer/reward-points/*` prefix is replaced by the customer account prefix `/api/account` (§26.5).

## 55. Product Subscriptions

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `product_subscriptions`. This key replaces the ambiguous `subscriptions` key of earlier drafts. |
| **Code module** | `ProductSubscriptions` |
| **Depends on** | §26, §27, §39, §40 |

A customer subscribes to receive a **product** on a recurring schedule, for example "coffee beans every 4 weeks" ("subscribe and save"). This has nothing to do with the tenant's own SaaS subscription (§14). Every renewal is a normal order, created by a scheduled job instead of a checkout.

### 55.1 Tables

Product columns `is_subscribable` and `subscription_discount_percent` are defined in §27.

```
product_subscription_plans  [DB: tenant]
id
product_id           fk -> products
interval             enum(weekly, biweekly, monthly, quarterly)
interval_count       int      default 1   e.g. monthly × 2 = every two months
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
customer_subscriptions  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
customer_id                   fk -> customers
product_id                    fk -> products
product_variant_id            fk -> product_variants  nullable
product_subscription_plan_id  fk -> product_subscription_plans
quantity                      qty
address_id                    fk -> addresses        delivery address for renewals
shipping_method_id            fk -> shipping_methods nullable  required when the product is physical
currency_code                 char(3)
status                        enum(pending_payment, active, paused, cancelled, payment_failed)
payment_provider              string   nullable
payment_method_token          encrypted nullable  reusable gateway authorization
next_billing_date             date     nullable
failed_renewal_count          int      default 0
cancelled_at                  datetime nullable
```

```
customer_subscription_orders  [DB: tenant]
id
customer_subscription_id  fk -> customer_subscriptions
order_id                  fk -> orders  unique
created_at                datetime
```

- `payment_method_token` is the reusable authorization returned by `verifyTransaction()` or a webhook when the first payment is made with `save_authorization = true`. The platform has no general "saved cards" module. The token exists only for this purpose (and installments, §47).
- The tables are renamed from the earlier `subscription_orders` and `SubscriptionService` to avoid confusion with SaaS billing.

### 55.2 Flow

1. **Create.** `POST /api/account/product-subscriptions` validates `is_subscribable`, the plan, the address and the shipping method.
   - It creates the subscription in `pending_payment`.
   - It creates the first order through `OrderService::createOrder()` (`order_source = online`), linked in `customer_subscription_orders`, with `subscription_discount_percent` applied as a line discount (`discount_amount`, `price_source = subscription`, §39.2). Automatic promotions are not combined with the subscription discount.
   - The response returns the order. The customer pays it through `POST /api/orders/{order}/pay`, and `save_authorization` is set automatically (§40.2) (Assumption A-39).
2. **Activate.** When that first payment succeeds and returns an authorization token, the subscription stores the token, becomes `active`, and sets `next_billing_date` = today + the interval. If no token is returned, the subscription stays `pending_payment` and the customer is told that the chosen gateway cannot store the payment method.
3. **Renew.** The `ProcessProductSubscriptionRenewals` job runs daily. It selects `active` subscriptions with `next_billing_date ≤ today` and calls `processRenewal()` for each. It catches failures per subscription, so one failure never blocks the batch.
   - `processRenewal()` creates an order at the product's current price, resolved by `PricingService`, minus `subscription_discount_percent` as a line discount, and charges it through `OrderPaymentService::chargeStoredAuthorization()`.
   - **On success:** `next_billing_date` advances one interval and `failed_renewal_count` resets.
   - **On failure:** the status becomes `payment_failed`, `failed_renewal_count` increments, and `product_subscription.payment_failed` is dispatched. The renewal is retried on the next run. When the count reaches `product_subscription_max_failed_renewals`, the subscription is `cancelled`.
4. **Pause and resume.** Pausing skips renewals. Resuming sets `next_billing_date` to today + one interval, not the date it was paused at.

### 55.3 Service and Routes

`ProductSubscriptionService`:

- `createSubscription(Customer $customer, Product $product, ProductSubscriptionPlan $plan, array $data): array`: `{subscription, order}`
- `activateFromPayment(CustomerSubscription $sub, OrderPayment $payment, string $token): void`
- `pauseSubscription(CustomerSubscription $sub): void`
- `resumeSubscription(CustomerSubscription $sub): void`
- `cancelSubscription(CustomerSubscription $sub): void`
- `updateQuantityOrVariant(CustomerSubscription $sub, array $data): void`
- `processRenewal(CustomerSubscription $sub): Order`
- `listCustomerSubscriptions(Customer $customer): Collection`
- `listSubscriptions(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`

`ProductSubscriptionPlanService`: `createPlan(Product $product, array $data)`, `deactivatePlan(ProductSubscriptionPlan $plan)`, `listPlansForProduct(Product $product)`.

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\ProductSubscriptions\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.public` | GET | `/api/products/{product}/subscription-plans` | `SubscriptionPlanController@index` |
| `tenant.customer` | GET | `/api/account/product-subscriptions` | `SubscriptionController@index` |
| `tenant.customer` | POST | `/api/account/product-subscriptions` | `SubscriptionController@store` (`usage.limit:max_orders_per_month`) |
| `tenant.customer` | PATCH | `/api/account/product-subscriptions/{subscription}` | `SubscriptionController@update`: quantity or variant |
| `tenant.customer` | PATCH | `/api/account/product-subscriptions/{subscription}/pause` | `SubscriptionController@pause` |
| `tenant.customer` | PATCH | `/api/account/product-subscriptions/{subscription}/resume` | `SubscriptionController@resume` |
| `tenant.customer` | DELETE | `/api/account/product-subscriptions/{subscription}` | `SubscriptionController@destroy`: cancels the subscription |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/products/{product}/subscription-plans` | `Admin\SubscriptionPlanController@index` |
| `tenant.admin` | POST | `/api/admin/products/{product}/subscription-plans` | `Admin\SubscriptionPlanController@store` |
| `tenant.admin` | DELETE | `/api/admin/products/{product}/subscription-plans/{plan}` | `Admin\SubscriptionPlanController@destroy`: deactivates the plan |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/product-subscriptions` | `Admin\SubscriptionController@index` |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/product-subscriptions/{subscription}` | `Admin\SubscriptionController@show` |
| `tenant.admin` | PATCH | `/api/admin/product-subscriptions/{subscription}/cancel` | `Admin\SubscriptionController@cancel` |

## 56. Back-in-Stock Alerts

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `back_in_stock_alerts` |
| **Code module** | `BackInStock` |
| **Depends on** | §17, §32.7 |

Back-in-stock alerts are a storefront "notify me when available" option on out-of-stock products. They reuse the inventory hooks and notifications, and add no separate stock tracking.

```
back_in_stock_subscriptions  [DB: tenant]
id
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable  variant-specific alert, e.g. one size
customer_id          fk -> customers  nullable  guests subscribe by email alone
email                string
notified_at          datetime nullable  set when the alert fires, so nobody is notified twice for the same restock
created_at           datetime
index(product_id, product_variant_id, notified_at)
```

- **Uniqueness** is enforced in the service: there is at most one un-notified row per product, variant and email. A repeat request is a no-op.
- **Trigger.** `InventoryService` calls `checkAndNotify()` when total available stock goes from 0 to a positive value ([§32.7](#327-stock-alerts-and-hooks)). There is no polling job. Every un-notified subscription for the product and variant receives `back_in_stock.available`, and `notified_at` is stamped.

`BackInStockService`:

- `subscribe(Product $product, string $email, ?Customer $customer = null, ?ProductVariant $variant = null): BackInStockSubscription`: rejected when the item is in stock
- `checkAndNotify(Product $product, ?ProductVariant $variant = null): void`
- `listPendingForProduct(Product $product): Collection`: shows staff the demand, so restocking can be prioritised

| Group | Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\BackInStock\...`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.storefront` | POST | `/api/products/{product}/back-in-stock-alert` | `AlertController@store`: body `email`, `product_variant_id`. No authentication is required. |
| `tenant.admin` | GET | `/api/admin/products/{product}/back-in-stock-subscribers` | `Admin\AlertController@index` |

Both routes carry `feature:back_in_stock_alerts`.
