## 57. Accounting

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `accounting` |
| **Code module** | `Accounting` |
| **Depends on** | §5, §8, §13.4, §19 |
| **Integration hooks** | Called by orders (§39.4), order payments (§40), returns (§41), gift cards (§46), multi-currency (§48), suppliers and purchasing (§49), marketplace (§50), POS (§51), expenses and income (§57.4) and HR payroll (§58.5) |

**Finance architecture.** Money is handled by one ledger and several operational modules that feed it. No module except `accounting` writes journal entries, and no module depends on `accounting` being enabled to work.

| Concern | Where it lives | Feature key |
|---|---|---|
| Customer invoices | Renderings of orders (§43). Not a separate receivable document. | core |
| Customer payments and refunds | Order payments (§40) and returns (§41) | core |
| Receivables | Unpaid order balances and installment schedules (§40, §47). With `accounting`, the `accounts_receivable` account. | core, `installments` |
| Payables to suppliers | Purchase orders and supplier payments (§49). With `accounting`, `accounts_payable`. | `purchasing` |
| Expenses, other income and billers | §57.4 | `expenses` |
| Taxes | Tax rates and order tax lines (§35). With `accounting`, `tax_payable`. Tax filing is out of scope. | core |
| Seller commissions, settlements and payouts | Seller ledger and payouts (§50.4) | `marketplace` |
| Sales-agent commissions | §52 | `sales_agents` |
| Payroll | §58.5 | `hr_payroll` |
| Gateway settlement and fees | Payment gateway reporting (§15.7). Reconciliation against bank statements is deferred (Appendix C). | core |
| Platform commission on tenant sales | §15.8 (landlord) | none |
| The general ledger, financial statements and fiscal periods | This section | `accounting` |

### 57.1 Principles

1. **Lightweight, but real double-entry.** The goal is that a tenant, or its accountant, can see where money went without exporting raw order data. Every money-moving event defined elsewhere in this document gets a balanced debit/credit posting. Adding accounting never changes how those flows work.
2. **`journal_entry_lines` is the general ledger.** The ledger and trial balance are queries over this table. There is no separate ledger table and no `account_transactions` table, so nothing can drift out of sync.
3. **Base currency only.** Every journal entry is in the tenant's base currency. A posting from a record in another currency converts it with the rate already captured on that record, never with a fresh lookup ([§48](#48-multi-currency)). Payments against an order are converted at the order's `exchange_rate_used`, so clearing Accounts Receivable never produces an exchange difference. Realised FX gain and loss is deferred ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)) (Assumption A-40).
4. **Postings are defined once, in `AccountingService`.** Other services call a named `post*()` method at the point where they already change status. They never build journal lines themselves.
5. **No retroactive postings.** When `accounting` is enabled for a tenant that already trades, only events from that moment on are posted. Opening balances are entered as a manual journal entry (Assumption A-41).

### 57.2 Account Categories and Chart of Accounts

```
account_categories  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Current Assets", "Operating Expenses"
account_type         enum(asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense)
is_system            bool     default false  seeded categories cannot be deleted
sort_order           int      default 0
```

```
chart_of_accounts  [DB: tenant]
id
code                 string   unique   e.g. "4000"
name                 string
account_category_id  fk -> account_categories   the account type is read through the category, never duplicated
parent_account_id    fk -> chart_of_accounts  nullable  sub-accounts
system_key           string   nullable unique  stable identifier used by automatic postings (table below)
is_system            bool     default false  system accounts can be renamed but not deleted or deactivated
is_active            bool     default true
description          text     nullable
```

The model is `Account` (table `chart_of_accounts`). Every foreign key to it is named `account_id`, or `{purpose}_account_id` where a table has more than one.

**Normal balance.** Asset and expense accounts are debit-normal. Liability, equity and revenue accounts are credit-normal. "Sales Returns and Allowances" is a debit-normal contra-revenue account.

**Seeded categories** (by `TenantDefaultsSyncService`, [§12.6](#126-permission-and-default-data-sync)): Current Assets and Fixed Assets (asset), Current Liabilities and Long-Term Liabilities (liability), Equity (equity), Revenue (revenue), Expenses (expense). Tenants can add more categories under any type.

**Seeded system accounts.** All of them are seeded for every tenant, whether or not the related module is enabled. An unused account simply has a zero balance (Assumption A-42).

| `system_key` | Code | Name | Category |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cash_bank` | 1000 | Cash/Bank | Current Assets |
| `accounts_receivable` | 1100 | Accounts Receivable | Current Assets |
| `inventory_asset` | 1200 | Inventory Asset | Current Assets |
| `accounts_payable` | 2000 | Accounts Payable (suppliers) | Current Liabilities |
| `accounts_payable_sellers` | 2010 | Accounts Payable – Sellers | Current Liabilities |
| `gift_card_liability` | 2020 | Gift Card Liability | Current Liabilities |
| `tax_payable` | 2100 | Tax Payable | Current Liabilities |
| `payroll_liabilities` | 2200 | Payroll Liabilities | Current Liabilities |
| `sales_revenue` | 4000 | Sales Revenue | Revenue |
| `shipping_revenue` | 4010 | Shipping Revenue | Revenue |
| `commission_revenue` | 4020 | Commission Revenue | Revenue |
| `sales_returns` | 4100 | Sales Returns and Allowances | Revenue (contra) |
| `other_income` | 4900 | Other Income | Revenue |
| `cost_of_goods_sold` | 5000 | Cost of Goods Sold | Expenses |
| `inventory_adjustments` | 5010 | Inventory Adjustments (shrinkage and write-offs) | Expenses |
| `payment_processing_fees` | 5100 | Payment Processing Fees | Expenses |
| `salaries_wages` | 5200 | Salaries and Wages Expense | Expenses |
| `general_expenses` | 5900 | General Expenses | Expenses |

Tenants may add their own accounts, including sub-accounts under system accounts. A tenant that wants POS cash tracked separately from online settlement creates its own asset account (for example "POS Till") and selects it as the `account_id` when recording POS and manual payments (§57.3).

### 57.3 Journal Entries and Automatic Postings

```
fiscal_years  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "FY2026"
starts_on            date
ends_on              date
status               enum(open, closed)  default open
closed_at            datetime nullable
```

```
fiscal_periods  [DB: tenant]
id
fiscal_year_id       fk -> fiscal_years
name                 string            e.g. "January 2026"
starts_on            date
ends_on              date
status               enum(open, closed)  default open
closed_at            datetime nullable
closed_by_user_id    fk -> users  nullable
```

Periods (normally monthly) are what entries close against day to day. The fiscal year is the roll-up used for year-on-year reporting. Periods MUST lie within their year and MUST NOT overlap.

```
journal_entries  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
entry_date                 date
fiscal_period_id           fk -> fiscal_periods   resolved from entry_date at creation; never chosen by hand
description                string
source                     enum(system, manual, reversal)
reference_type             string   nullable  morph type of the business record that caused it
reference_id               int      nullable
posting_key                string   nullable unique  idempotency key for system postings, e.g. "order_sale:123"
cash_flow_category         enum(operating, investing, financing)  default operating
reverses_journal_entry_id  fk -> journal_entries  nullable  set on reversal entries
reversed_at                datetime nullable  set on the original when it is reversed
created_by_user_id         fk -> users  nullable  null = system posting
index(reference_type, reference_id)
```

```
journal_entry_lines  [DB: tenant]
id
journal_entry_id     fk -> journal_entries
account_id           fk -> chart_of_accounts
type                 enum(debit, credit)
amount               money             always positive
description          string   nullable
index(account_id)
```

```
account_balances  [DB: tenant]
id
account_id           fk -> chart_of_accounts
fiscal_period_id     fk -> fiscal_periods
opening_balance      money    default 0
debit_total          money    default 0
credit_total         money    default 0
closing_balance      money    default 0
unique(account_id, fiscal_period_id)
```

**Entry rules.**

- Every entry has at least two lines, and total debits MUST equal total credits. `AccountingService` enforces this before anything is persisted.
- Every entry is posted on creation. There are no draft entries. Once created, an entry and its lines are immutable ([§5.2](#52-timestamps-soft-deletes-and-immutability)). A correction is a reversal (an equal and opposite entry) plus a new entry.
- `account_balances` is a read cache for balance lookups, updated as entries post. It is never the source of truth and can always be rebuilt from `journal_entry_lines` by `recalculateAccountBalance()`.
- Entries are posted in the base currency (§57.1).

**How system postings run: the accounting outbox (Assumption A-43).** A calling service never builds journal entries inside its own transaction, so an accounting problem can never block a sale. But the **request** to post is written inside the caller's transaction, so it can never be lost. A crash between the business commit and a queue dispatch cannot drop a posting.

```
accounting_posting_requests  [DB: tenant]
id
posting_key          string   unique   e.g. "order_sale:123", "order_payment:88", "order_payment:88:v2"
method               string            the AccountingService method, e.g. postOrderSale, reverseEntry
reference_type       string            morph type of the business record
reference_id         int
event_date           date              the business event's date (confirmed_at, paid_at, …) in the tenant timezone
payload              json     nullable extra arguments, e.g. receivedValue for purchase receipts
status               enum(pending, posted, skipped, failed)  default pending
attempts             int      default 0
last_error           text     nullable
journal_entry_id     fk -> journal_entries  nullable
processed_at         datetime nullable
index(status, id)
```

1. **Record.** Inside its transaction, the caller calls `AccountingOutbox::record($method, $record, $eventDate, $postingKey, $payload)`. It inserts one row, and does nothing when `accounting` is not enabled for the tenant or when the record belongs to a test order (§40.8). The unique `posting_key` makes a duplicate request a no-op. Wherever another section says a service "calls", "runs" or "records" an `AccountingService::post*()` or `reverseEntry()` method, it means exactly this.
2. **Dispatch.** `record()` registers an after-commit dispatch of `PostAccountingEntry` with the request ID, on the `tenant-default` queue.
3. **Post.** `PostAccountingEntry` locks the request row. It exits when the status is not `pending` or `failed`. Otherwise it builds and inserts the journal entry, and marks the request `posted` with `journal_entry_id`, in one transaction. `journal_entries.posting_key` is unique, so even a concurrent duplicate job cannot post twice.
4. **Dates and periods.** `entry_date` is `event_date`, never the time the job runs. If no **open** fiscal period covers it, the request becomes `failed` with `last_error`, and `accounting.posting_failed` is dispatched to admins ([§17.9](#179-notification-event-catalog)). It is not silently posted into another period. Once staff create or reopen the period, `php artisan accounting:retry-postings` (or `POST /api/admin/accounting/posting-requests/retry`) re-dispatches every `failed` request.
5. **Recovery.** The daily tenant maintenance job (§72.2) re-dispatches `pending` requests older than 10 minutes, which covers a lost dispatch.
6. `skipped` is used only when the referenced record no longer qualifies, for example an order that was never confirmed.

Only `PostAccountingEntry` and manual journal entries invoke `AccountingService` posting methods directly.

**Rounding and currency.** Each line amount is converted to the base currency at the record's snapshotted rate, and rounded to the base currency's minor unit (§5.3). The balancing line (Accounts Receivable in `postOrderSale()`) is the sum of the other converted lines, not an independent conversion of `total`. An entry is therefore balanced by construction, and `orders.base_currency_amount` is defined as that same sum.

**Automatic postings.** "Cash" means the payment row's `account_id` when set, otherwise the `cash_bank` system account.

| Method | Called by | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| `postOrderSale(Order $order)` | `OrderService::confirmOrder()` (§39.4) | **Standard and exchange-replacement orders:** Cr Sales Revenue for the net merchandise amount minus `reward_points_discount_amount`. Cr Shipping Revenue for the net shipping amount. Cr Tax Payable `tax_amount`. Dr Accounts Receivable for the sum of those credits, which equals `total` (§38.5). Revenue is recorded net of promotion discounts. There is no separate discount account. Then, for physical lines: Dr Cost of Goods Sold, Cr Inventory Asset, for Σ `unit_cost_snapshot × quantity`. **Gift-card purchase orders:** Dr Accounts Receivable, Cr Gift Card Liability, for `total`. There is no cost-of-goods line. |
| `reverseOrderSale(Order $order)` | `OrderService::cancelOrder()` for a confirmed order (§39.5) | Calls `reverseEntry()` on the order's sale entry, and on its seller commission entries |
| `postOrderPayment(OrderPayment $payment)` | `OrderPaymentService` on success (§40.2), `OrderPaymentLedgerService::recordPayment()` (§40.6), POS payments (§51), installment charges (§47) | Credit Accounts Receivable for `amount_paid`. The debit depends on `payment_method`: `gift_card` debits Gift Card Liability; `exchange_credit` debits Sales Returns and Allowances; every other method debits Cash. |
| `postGatewayFee(OrderPayment $payment)` | Same point as `postOrderPayment()`, when `meta.fee` is reported | Dr Payment Processing Fees, Cr Cash |
| `postRefund(OrderPayment $refund)` | `OrderPaymentService::refund()` (§40.4) | Dr Sales Returns and Allowances for the net-of-tax amount, Dr Tax Payable for the tax share, Cr Cash. A `gift_card` refund credits Gift Card Liability instead of Cash. For a refund of a gift-card purchase order, Gift Card Liability is debited instead of Sales Returns. Tax share: for a return refund, the refunded lines' `tax_amount` pro-rated by quantity. For a direct refund, `refund × tax_amount / total` of the order (Assumption A-44). |
| `postChargeback(OrderPayment $chargeback)` | `OrderPaymentService::handleDispute()` on `dispute.lost` (§40.5) | The same lines as `postRefund()` for the chargeback amount, with the direct-refund tax share. Nothing is restocked. |
| `postReturnRestock(OrderReturn $return)` | `ReturnService`, on restock (§41) | Dr Inventory Asset, Cr Cost of Goods Sold, for the restocked quantity × `unit_cost_snapshot` |
| `postStockAdjustment(StockAdjustment $adjustment)` | `StockAdjustmentService::submitAdjustment()` (§33.2) | For subtraction lines: Dr Inventory Adjustments (shrinkage), Cr Inventory Asset. For addition lines: the reverse. Each line is valued at `quantity × unit_cost_snapshot`. Lines with no cost snapshot are not posted and are listed in the entry description. |
| `postSellerCommission(Order $order)` | `SellerLedgerService::recordOrderLines()` (§50.4) | For each seller line: Dr Sales Revenue for the line net, Cr Commission Revenue for the tenant's commission, Cr Accounts Payable – Sellers for the seller's net payable |
| `postSellerCommissionReversal(SellerLedgerEntry $entry)` | A seller ledger reversal entry (§50.4) | The opposite of the corresponding `postSellerCommission()` lines, for the reversed amount |
| `postSellerPayout(SellerPayout $payout)` | `SellerPayoutService::markPaid()` (§50.5) | Dr Accounts Payable – Sellers, Cr Cash, for `net_payable` |
| `postPurchaseOrderReceived(PurchaseOrder $order, float $receivedValue)` | `PurchaseOrderService::receiveStock()` (§49.2) | Dr Inventory Asset, Cr Accounts Payable |
| `postSupplierPayment(SupplierPayment $payment)` | `SupplierPaymentService` (§49.4) | Dr Accounts Payable, Cr Cash. A negative `amount_paid` (a supplier refund) reverses the sides. |
| `postPurchaseReturn(PurchaseReturn $return)` | `PurchaseReturnService::approveReturn()` (§49.5) | Dr Accounts Payable, Cr Inventory Asset |
| `postExpense(Expense $expense)` | `ExpenseService::markPaid()` (§57.4) | Dr the expense category's account (or `general_expenses` when the category has none), Cr the paid-from account (default `cash_bank`) |
| `postIncome(IncomeEntry $income)` | `IncomeService::markReceived()` (§57.4) | Dr the received-into account (default `cash_bank`), Cr the income category's account (or `other_income` when the category has none) |
| `postPayroll(HrPayrollRun $run)` | `HrPayrollService::markPayrollRunPaid()` (§58.5) | One entry for the whole run: Dr Salaries and Wages Expense `total_gross`, Cr Cash `total_net`, Cr Payroll Liabilities `total_deductions` |

**Update and delete of manual source records.** When a manual order payment or supplier payment is edited or deleted, the calling service reverses its original entry through `reverseEntry()`, and for an edit, posts a fresh one. The `posting_key` of a re-post carries a version suffix (for example `order_payment:88:v2`).

**Not posted in v1:** stock transfers (they move value between locations of the same Inventory Asset account, so there is nothing to post), manufacturing (a work order moves component value into finished goods at cost, inside Inventory Asset), sales-agent commissions, and platform commission (UD-07). See [Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items).

### 57.4 Billers, Expenses and Income

| | |
|---|---|
| **Feature key** | `expenses` (module, `auto` activation; included from Basic, §11.14) |
| **Code module** | `Expenses` |
| **Integration hooks** | Calls `accounting` (`postExpense()`, `postIncome()`) when it is `enabled`; `purchasing` (supplier as payee); `approval_workflows` (expense approval, §60) |
| **Disabled behaviour** | Admin reads and exports stay available. New entries, edits and mark-paid are rejected. Nothing is deleted. |

Expenses are a separate module from `accounting` because every business, including one that never keeps double-entry books, needs to record what it spends. The tables live here because the ledger is their main consumer. When `accounting` is not `enabled`, marking an expense paid or income received writes no posting, and enabling `accounting` later does not back-post them (§57.1 rule 5). Employee expense claims are deferred (Appendix C).

**Billers** are lightweight payees for bills that have nothing to do with buying stock: rent, electricity, internet, a one-off vendor invoice. They are separate from suppliers because a biller has none of a supplier's product and purchase-order machinery.

```
billers  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string
phone                string   nullable
email                string   nullable
category             enum(utility, rent, landlord, vendor, other)
account_reference    string   nullable  the tenant's own account or meter number with this biller
notes                text     nullable
is_active            bool     default true
```

**Expenses** are ad hoc or recurring spending that is not a purchase order (purchase orders are for stock only). Entering an expense is the normal way into accounting for everything that is not posted automatically. An admin never hand-builds a journal entry for a routine expense.

```
expense_categories  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Rent", "Utilities", "Marketing"
account_id           fk -> chart_of_accounts  nullable  an expense-type account; null posts to general_expenses
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
expenses  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
expense_category_id  fk -> expense_categories
biller_id            fk -> billers    nullable
supplier_id          fk -> suppliers  nullable  a one-off non-stock vendor cost, e.g. a repair invoice
amount               money
currency_code        char(3)           must equal the base currency unless multi_currency is enabled
exchange_rate_used   rate     nullable  captured at creation for non-base currencies (§48)
expense_date         date
description          text     nullable
status               enum(pending, paid)  default pending
paid_at              datetime nullable
paid_from_account_id fk -> chart_of_accounts  nullable  defaults to cash_bank
created_by_user_id   fk -> users
(media: receipt)
```

At most one of `biller_id` and `supplier_id` is set. Neither is set for an expense without a payee, such as a bank charge. `supplier_id` can be used only when `purchasing` is enabled.

**Income** is money received that is not a customer order (orders post automatically): interest, a one-off asset sale, a grant, other revenue.

```
income_categories  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Interest Income", "Asset Sale"
account_id           fk -> chart_of_accounts  nullable  a revenue-type account; null posts to other_income
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
income_entries  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
income_category_id   fk -> income_categories
source               string   nullable  who or what it came from
amount               money
currency_code        char(3)
exchange_rate_used   rate     nullable
received_date        date
description          text     nullable
status               enum(pending, received)  default pending
received_at          datetime nullable
received_into_account_id fk -> chart_of_accounts  nullable  defaults to cash_bank
created_by_user_id   fk -> users
```

`markPaid()` and `markReceived()` are one-way. A paid expense or received income entry cannot be edited. A correction is a reversal of its journal entry plus a new record.

### 57.5 Fiscal Period Close

- Closing a fiscal period locks it. No new entry may be dated inside it. A correction discovered later is posted into the current open period, or made as a reversal.
- Closing finalises the period's `account_balances` and carries each account's closing balance forward as the next period's opening balance.
- `reopenFiscalPeriod()` is an admin override for correcting a late-discovered error. It is allowed only while the period's fiscal year is open (Assumption A-45).
- Closing a fiscal year requires every one of its periods to be closed. No closing entries are generated. The balance sheet shows accumulated earnings as a computed line: cumulative revenue minus cumulative expenses up to the report date (Assumption A-46).

### 57.6 Financial Reports

Reports are generated on demand. None are stored.

| Report | Definition |
|---|---|
| Profit and Loss | Revenue accounts minus expense accounts, for a date range, optionally scoped to a fiscal period or year |
| Balance Sheet | Assets, liabilities and equity as of a date, grouped by account category, plus the computed accumulated-earnings line (§57.5) |
| General Ledger | Every line for one account, with a running balance, for a date range |
| Trial Balance | Every account's debit and credit totals as of a date. Proves the books balance. |
| Cash Flow Statement | For a date range, the lines posted to asset accounts in the Current Assets category that represent cash (`cash_bank`, its sub-accounts, and any account the tenant created under it), grouped by `journal_entries.cash_flow_category`. Every automatic posting is `operating`. Investing and financing activity comes only from manual entries tagged accordingly, so those buckets have thin coverage in v1. |

The currency-exposure report is owned by multi-currency ([§48](#48-multi-currency)).

### 57.7 Services

`AccountingService` (Tenant): every `post*()` method in §57.3, plus:

- `postManualEntry(array $data): JournalEntry`: at least two lines, balanced, and the resolved period must be open. `cash_flow_category` may be set.
- `reverseEntry(JournalEntry $entry, ?string $reason = null): JournalEntry`: posts the equal and opposite entry dated today, sets `reverses_journal_entry_id` on it and `reversed_at` on the original. An entry can be reversed only once.
- `getProfitAndLoss(Carbon $from, Carbon $to): array`
- `getBalanceSheet(Carbon $asOf): array`
- `getGeneralLedger(Account $account, Carbon $from, Carbon $to): Collection`
- `getTrialBalance(Carbon $asOf): array`
- `getCashFlowStatement(Carbon $from, Carbon $to): array`
- `recalculateAccountBalance(Account $account, FiscalPeriod $period): AccountBalance`

`ChartOfAccountsService` (Tenant):

- `listAccounts(array $filters): Collection`
- `createAccount(array $data): Account`: non-system accounts only
- `updateAccount(Account $account, array $data): Account`: system accounts allow `name` and `description` only
- `deactivateAccount(Account $account): void`: blocked for system accounts and for accounts referenced by an active expense or income category
- `listCategories(): Collection`
- `createCategory(array $data): AccountCategory`
- `updateCategory(AccountCategory $category, array $data): AccountCategory`

Accounts are never deleted once any journal line references them.

`FiscalPeriodService` (Tenant):

- `createFiscalYear(array $data): FiscalYear`
- `createFiscalPeriod(FiscalYear $year, array $data): FiscalPeriod`
- `closeFiscalPeriod(FiscalPeriod $period): void`
- `reopenFiscalPeriod(FiscalPeriod $period): void`
- `closeFiscalYear(FiscalYear $year): void`
- `getCurrentPeriod(): ?FiscalPeriod`
- `listFiscalYears(): Collection`
- `listPeriodsForYear(FiscalYear $year): Collection`

The following three services belong to the `Expenses` code module (§57.4). They call `AccountingService` only through the accounting outbox, and only when `accounting` is `enabled`.

`BillerService` (Tenant): `createBiller()`, `updateBiller()`, `deactivateBiller()`, `listBillers(array $filters)`.

`ExpenseService` (Tenant):

- `createCategory(array $data): ExpenseCategory`
- `updateCategory(ExpenseCategory $category, array $data): ExpenseCategory`
- `listCategories(): Collection`
- `createExpense(array $data): Expense`
- `updateExpense(Expense $expense, array $data): Expense`: `pending` only
- `deleteExpense(Expense $expense): void`: `pending` only
- `markPaid(Expense $expense, ?Account $fromAccount = null): void`: dispatches the `postExpense()` posting
- `listExpenses(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`
- `getTodayExpenses(): array`: total and list of expenses dated today in the tenant timezone (used by the AI assistant, §62)

`IncomeService` (Tenant): the same shape. `createCategory()`, `updateCategory()`, `listCategories()`, `createIncome()`, `updateIncome()` and `deleteIncome()` (both `pending` only), `markReceived(IncomeEntry $income, ?Account $intoAccount = null)`, and `listIncome(array $filters)`.

## 58. Human Resources

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `hr`, with submodules `hr_payroll` (§58.5) and `hr_recruitment` (§58.7), which both require `hr` |
| **Code module** | `Hr` |
| **Depends on** | §19 (media), §25 (staff users) |
| **Integration hooks** | Accounting (`postPayroll()`, §57.3), approval workflows (`module_key = leave_request`, §60), tenant dashboard (`hr` section and contextual KPIs, §44.3, §44.4) |
| **Usage limit** | `max_employees` on employee create and reactivate (§11.8) |

HR covers departments, employees, documents, attendance, leave, payroll, appraisals and recruitment.

**What is in HR, and what is not.** `hr` itself holds the people records and the everyday processes: departments, employees and documents, attendance, leave and appraisals. Payroll is a submodule because it carries money and statutory risk, and many small employers run payroll elsewhere. Recruitment is a submodule because it exposes public careers routes and collects applicants' personal data. Staff logins and permissions are not HR (§25). Business expenses are not HR (§57.4). Employee expense claims and reimbursements are deferred (Appendix C). Sales-agent commissions are `sales_agents` (§52), not payroll. Every table is prefixed `hr_`. Inside the module, foreign keys drop the prefix: `employee_id` references `hr_employees`, `department_id` references `hr_departments`, and so on. This is the owning-section exception allowed by [§5.1](#51-keys-and-references).

### 58.1 Employee and Staff User Link

An `hr_employees` row optionally links to a staff user through `user_id` (same tenant database):

- The link avoids duplicating identity data. `users` holds login, authentication and permissions. `hr_employees` holds HR data: department, salary, leave balances, hire date.
- Enabling or disabling HR never changes `users` or authentication.
- Enabling HR needs no retroactive migration. Existing users simply have no employee record until one is created.
- Not every employee has a user account. For example, factory-floor staff who never log in exist as standalone employees with `user_id = null`.
- An employee who **is** a system user MUST reference that user through `user_id` rather than re-entering the name and email. For a linked employee, `name` and `email` come from `users`, and the employee's own `first_name`, `last_name` and `email` columns stay null.

### 58.2 Employees, Departments and Documents

```
hr_departments  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string
description          text     nullable
is_active            bool     default true
```

```

employment_type      enum(full_time, part_time, contract, internship)
hire_date            date

status               enum(active, inactive)  default active
```

```
id
```


Document types are a managed lookup, not free text. The columns of `hr_departments`, `hr_employees`, `hr_document_types` and `hr_employee_documents` are the minimum the services in §58.8 need. Earlier drafts named these tables without defining their columns (Assumption A-47).

### 58.3 HR Settings and Attendance

```
hr_settings  [DB: tenant]
id
department_id              fk -> hr_departments  nullable unique  null = the tenant-wide default row
expected_clock_in_time     time               e.g. 09:00
expected_clock_out_time    time               e.g. 17:00
late_grace_minutes         int      default 0 minutes after expected_clock_in_time before a clock-in is late
early_leave_grace_minutes  int      default 0 the same idea for clocking out early
```

`hr_settings` is HR's own settings home. Future HR-wide configuration (for example a default leave policy or a payroll cut-off day) belongs here, not in `tenant_settings`. It is not a singleton: the tenant-wide row can be overridden per department. The tenant-wide row is created on first access with 09:00 and 17:00 and zero grace minutes.

```
hr_attendance  [DB: tenant]
id
employee_id          fk -> hr_employees
work_date            date              in the tenant timezone
clock_in_at          datetime
clock_out_at         datetime nullable
is_late              bool     default false  computed at clock-in
is_early_leave       bool     default false  computed at clock-out
notes                string   nullable
unique(employee_id, work_date)
```

- One attendance row per employee per day (Assumption A-48). A second clock-in on the same day is rejected with 422.
- `is_late` and `is_early_leave` are computed against `HrSettingsService::getApplicableSettings()`: the employee's department row if it exists, otherwise the tenant-wide row.
- **Self-service clock-in and clock-out** act on the employee linked to the authenticated user. A user with no linked employee gets 422. A user holding the `hr.attendance.record` permission may pass `employee_id` to record for someone else, for example at a shared kiosk.

### 58.4 Leave

```
hr_leave_types  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Annual", "Sick", "Unpaid"
days_per_year        decimal(5,1)      default entitlement
is_paid              bool     default true
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
hr_leave_balances  [DB: tenant]
id
employee_id          fk -> hr_employees
leave_type_id        fk -> hr_leave_types
year                 int
entitled_days        decimal(5,1)
used_days            decimal(5,1)  default 0
unique(employee_id, leave_type_id, year)
```

```
hr_leave_requests  [DB: tenant]
id
employee_id          fk -> hr_employees
leave_type_id        fk -> hr_leave_types
start_date           date
end_date             date
days                 decimal(5,1)
reason               text     nullable
status               enum(pending, approved, rejected, cancelled)  default pending
rejection_reason     string   nullable
decided_by_user_id   fk -> users  nullable
decided_at           datetime nullable
```

- The balance is `entitled_days − used_days`. A balance row is created on first access for a year, with `entitled_days = days_per_year` (Assumption A-49).
- A request is validated against the remaining balance. Approval adds `days` to `used_days`.
- A request is submitted for the authenticated user's linked employee, or, with the `hr.leave-requests.create` permission, for any employee through `employee_id`.
- **Approval gate.** When an active approval workflow matches `module_key = leave_request` ([§60](#60-approval-workflow-engine)), approval runs through it. Otherwise staff approve or reject directly.
- Notifications: `hr.leave_request_submitted`, `hr.leave_request_approved` and `hr.leave_request_rejected` ([§17.9](#179-notification-event-catalog)).

### 58.5 Payroll

| | |
|---|---|
| **Feature key** | `hr_payroll` (submodule; requires `hr`) |
| **Disabled behaviour** | Finalized runs, payslips and salary history stay readable. New runs, salary changes and finalization are rejected. |

A single figure per employee per run is not enough. Payroll uses line items, so that payslips are itemised and auditable.

```
hr_salary_structures  [DB: tenant]
id
employee_id          fk -> hr_employees
base_salary          money
currency_code        char(3)           the base currency (Assumption A-50)
effective_from       date
effective_to         date     nullable  null = current
```

Salary changes are tracked historically, never overwritten in place. Creating a new structure closes the previous one (`effective_to` = the day before `effective_from`).

```
hr_payroll_runs  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
period_start         date
period_end           date
status               enum(draft, processing, finalized, paid)  default draft
run_date             date
total_gross          money    default 0
total_deductions     money    default 0  Σ over items of (total_deductions + tax_amount)
total_net            money    default 0
finalized_at         datetime nullable
finalized_by_user_id fk -> users  nullable
paid_at              datetime nullable
```

```
hr_payroll_items  [DB: tenant]
id
payroll_run_id       fk -> hr_payroll_runs
employee_id          fk -> hr_employees
base_salary          money             snapshot from the salary structure
total_allowances     money    default 0  Σ allowance, bonus and reimbursement lines
gross_pay            money    default 0  base_salary + total_allowances
total_deductions     money    default 0  Σ deduction lines
tax_amount           money    default 0  Σ tax lines
net_pay              money    default 0  gross_pay − total_deductions − tax_amount
status               enum(pending, paid)  default pending
paid_at              datetime nullable
unique(payroll_run_id, employee_id)
```

```
hr_payroll_item_lines  [DB: tenant]
id
payroll_item_id      fk -> hr_payroll_items
type                 enum(allowance, deduction, tax, bonus, reimbursement)
label                string            e.g. "Housing Allowance", "PAYE Tax"
amount               money             the computed amount
is_percentage        bool     default false  true = computed as a percentage of base_salary
percentage           percent  nullable  set when is_percentage
```

**Run lifecycle.**

| From | Action | To |
|---|---|---|
| `draft` | `generatePayrollItemsForRun()`: one item per active employee with a current salary structure | `processing` |
| `processing` | Lines are added or removed. Each change calls `recalculatePayrollItem()`, then the run totals are recalculated. | `processing` |
| `processing` | `finalizePayrollRun()`: locks the run. No line edits after this ([§5.2](#52-timestamps-soft-deletes-and-immutability)). | `finalized` |
| `finalized` | `markPayrollRunPaid()`: marks every item paid, and posts `postPayroll()` when `accounting` is enabled | `paid` |

`markPayrollItemPaid()` marks a single item paid. When every item is paid, the run becomes `paid` and posts as above. A run posts exactly once.

### 58.6 Appraisals

Reusable templates mean an appraisal cycle does not start from a blank form.

```
hr_appraisal_templates  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Annual Review", "Probation Review"
description          text     nullable
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
hr_appraisal_template_criteria  [DB: tenant]
id
appraisal_template_id fk -> hr_appraisal_templates
label                string            e.g. "Communication", "Quality of Work"
weight               percent           a template's weights MUST sum to 100 before it can be used
max_score            decimal(5,2)
sort_order           int      default 0
```

```
hr_appraisals  [DB: tenant]
id
employee_id          fk -> hr_employees
appraisal_template_id fk -> hr_appraisal_templates
reviewer_user_id     fk -> users
period_start         date
period_end           date
status               enum(draft, submitted, acknowledged)  default draft
overall_score        decimal(5,2) nullable  set on submit
overall_comments     text     nullable
submitted_at         datetime nullable
acknowledged_at      datetime nullable
```

```
hr_appraisal_scores  [DB: tenant]
id
appraisal_id                  fk -> hr_appraisals
appraisal_template_criterion_id fk -> hr_appraisal_template_criteria
score                         decimal(5,2)   0 ≤ score ≤ max_score
comments                      text     nullable
unique(appraisal_id, appraisal_template_criterion_id)
```

- `submitAppraisal()` requires a score for every criterion. It sets `overall_score` = Σ(`score / max_score × weight`), which gives a value from 0 to 100.
- `acknowledgeAppraisal()` records that the employee has seen it. It is performed by the employee's linked user, or by staff with the permission on behalf of a standalone employee.

### 58.7 Careers and Recruitment

| | |
|---|---|
| **Feature key** | `hr_recruitment` (submodule; requires `hr`) |
| **Disabled behaviour** | The public careers routes return 403, so no new applications arrive. Postings and applications stay readable to staff. |

Public job postings, plus the internal pipeline for reviewing applicants. Postings and applications are intentionally public: applicants are not staff, customers or sellers.

```
hr_job_postings  [DB: tenant]
id
title                string
slug                 string   unique   spatie/laravel-sluggable
department_id        fk -> hr_departments  nullable
description          text
requirements         text     nullable
location             string   nullable
employment_type      enum(full_time, part_time, contract, internship)
status               enum(draft, open, closed)  default draft
application_deadline date     nullable
posted_at            datetime nullable
closed_at            datetime nullable
```

```
hr_candidates  [DB: tenant]
id
first_name           string
last_name            string
email                string   unique
phone                string   nullable
linkedin_url         string   nullable
source               string   nullable  e.g. "career page", "referral"
(media: resume)
```

A candidate is its own lightweight entity. Candidates never log in, so they have no guard. `findOrCreateByEmail()` avoids duplicate candidates across several applications.

```
hr_job_applications  [DB: tenant]
id
job_posting_id       fk -> hr_job_postings
candidate_id         fk -> hr_candidates
cover_letter         text     nullable
status               enum(applied, shortlisted, interviewing, offered, hired, rejected)  default applied
status_changed_at    datetime nullable
notes                text     nullable  internal, staff only; never returned on public routes
applied_at           datetime
converted_employee_id fk -> hr_employees  nullable  set by convertToEmployee()
unique(job_posting_id, candidate_id)
```

- Public applications are accepted only for `open` postings before `application_deadline`.
- `convertToEmployee()` requires `status = hired`. It creates a standalone employee from the candidate's name and contact details plus the supplied employee data.

## 59. Customer Support

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `support` |
| **Code module** | `Support` |
| **Depends on** | §17 (notifications), §19 (media), §26 (customers) |

Support is ongoing two-way conversation with a customer. It has two channels that share one thread and message model:

- **Tickets** are asynchronous, like email. They can stay open for hours or days.
- **Live chat** is real-time, with both sides present. A chat that goes quiet for a few minutes is treated by the customer as ended. It is not literally closed until staff close it.

Tenant-to-platform support is a separate landlord helpdesk ([§21](#21-platform-support-helpdesk)).

### 59.1 Tables

```
support_conversations  [DB: tenant]
id
customer_id          fk -> customers  nullable  null = a guest
guest_token          string   nullable index  the storefront guest token for guest conversations (§38.2)
guest_name           string   nullable
guest_email          string   nullable  required for guest tickets
channel              enum(ticket, chat)
subject              string   nullable  required for tickets
status               enum(open, pending, resolved, closed)  default open
priority             enum(low, normal, high)  nullable  tickets only; default normal
assigned_to_user_id  fk -> users  nullable
last_message_at      datetime nullable  sorts the inbox by recency
index(status, channel), index(customer_id)
```

```
support_messages  [DB: tenant]
id
support_conversation_id fk -> support_conversations
sender_type          enum(customer, guest, staff, system)
sender_id            int      nullable  customers.id or users.id depending on sender_type
body                 text
is_internal_note     bool     default false  staff-only; never shown to the customer
read_at              datetime nullable  read by the other side
```

```
support_message_attachments  [DB: tenant]
id
support_message_id   fk -> support_messages
(media: attachment)
```

- A guest may open a chat or ticket before creating an account. Guest conversations are bound to the same `X-Guest-Token` as the guest cart. When the guest registers or logs in with that token, `customer_id` is set on their guest conversations (the same rule as guest orders, [§39.6](#396-guest-order-access)).
- `sender_id` is a plain integer resolved through `sender_type`, not a morph relation.

### 59.2 Real-Time

- Real-time delivery uses Laravel Reverb. One shared Reverb deployment serves every tenant ([§77.4](#774-reverb)). Channel names are tenant-prefixed by the broadcasting layer ([§72.4](#724-broadcasting-and-real-time)).
- **Private channel per conversation:** `support-conversation.{id}`. The authorisation callback allows the owning customer (or the guest whose token matches), and staff users holding `support.conversations.view`.
- **Events:** `SupportMessageSent` (a new message in either direction; internal notes are broadcast only on the staff channel), `SupportConversationStatusChanged`, and client whispers `typing` (not persisted; typing indicators need no database row).
- **Presence channel** `support-agents-online` lets the admin inbox show which agents are online, using Reverb presence rather than a polled "last seen" column.
- Tickets use the same events. A customer with the ticket page open sees a staff reply appear live, but neither side is expected to be watching.

### 59.3 Services

`SupportConversationService` (Tenant):

- `startTicket(?Customer $customer, array $data): SupportConversation`
- `startChat(?Customer $customer, array $data = []): SupportConversation`: opens empty; the first message is added separately
- `assignToAgent(SupportConversation $conversation, User $agent): void`
- `updateStatus(SupportConversation $conversation, string $status): void`
- `updatePriority(SupportConversation $conversation, string $priority): void`
- `listConversations(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`: admin inbox; filters are status, channel and assignee
- `getForCustomer(Customer $customer): Collection`
- `getForGuest(string $guestToken): Collection`

`SupportMessageService` (Tenant):

- `sendMessage(SupportConversation $conversation, array $data): SupportMessage`: persists the message and its attachments, updates `last_message_at`, and broadcasts `SupportMessageSent`. If the recipient is not connected to the channel, it dispatches `support.reply_received` (to the customer) or `support.message_received` (to staff) ([§17.9](#179-notification-event-catalog)). A customer reply to a `resolved` conversation reopens it.
- `addInternalNote(SupportConversation $conversation, User $staff, string $body): SupportMessage`
- `markRead(SupportMessage $message, $reader): void`

Typing indicators are client whispers over the private channel. They need no API route.

## 60. Approval Workflow Engine

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `approval_workflows` (a workflow only applies when its module's feature is also enabled) |
| **Code module** | `Approvals` |
| **Depends on** | §12 (roles), §17 (notifications), §25 (staff users) |
| **Integration hooks** | Stock adjustments (§33), returns (§41), reviews (§42), product questions (§29.7), purchase orders (§49), seller applications (§50), leave requests (§58.4) |

The engine is for tenants that need more than one person's yes or no. For example: a purchase order over a certain value needs the warehouse manager and then finance; a high-value return needs a second sign-off; a leave request needs both the manager and HR. It is built once, generically, and configured entirely through the API. Adding an approval level is a data change, not a code change.

**It is layered on top of existing module actions.** Every approvable module keeps its own simple single-step approve and reject action as the default. A module is only routed through the engine when an active workflow matches the record. If none matches, the module's own flow runs unchanged.

### 60.1 Module Key Registry

`config/approvals.php` maps each `module_key` to its model, its owning service's callback, and the trigger condition keys it supports:

| `module_key` | Record (model) | Held in state | Supported `trigger_conditions` | Owning section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `purchase_order` | `PurchaseOrder` | `submitted` (receiving blocked) | `min_amount` (purchase-order total, base currency) | §49.2 |
| `return` | `OrderReturn` | `requested` | `min_amount` (requested refund value) | §41 |
| `stock_adjustment` | `StockAdjustment` | not applied | none | §33 |
| `review` | `ProductReview` | `pending` | none | §42 |
| `product_question` | `ProductQuestion` | `pending` | none | §29.7 |
| `seller_application` | `Seller` | `pending` | none | §50 |
| `leave_request` | `HrLeaveRequest` | `pending` | `min_days` | §58.4 |

`min_amount` comes from the original requirements. `min_days` is the leave equivalent. Other modules accept only `trigger_conditions = null`, meaning "every record" (Assumption A-51). The owning service implements `App\Contracts\Approvable` with `onApprovalGranted($record)` and `onApprovalRejected($record, ?string $note)`. The engine drives the gate. The module still owns what "approved" means.

### 60.2 Tables

```
approval_workflows  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "High Value Purchase Orders"
module_key           string            a key from §60.1
trigger_conditions   json     nullable  e.g. {"min_amount": 500000}; null = applies to every record
is_active            bool     default true
sort_order           int      default 0  lower first; the first matching workflow wins
index(module_key, is_active)
```

```
approval_steps  [DB: tenant]
id
approval_workflow_id fk -> approval_workflows
step_order           int               1, 2, 3 ... resequenced on removal and reorder
name                 string            e.g. "Manager Review", "Finance Sign-off"
approval_mode        enum(any_one, all)  default any_one
unique(approval_workflow_id, step_order)
```

```
approval_step_approvers  [DB: tenant]
id
approval_step_id     fk -> approval_steps
approver_type        enum(role, user)
role_id              fk -> roles  nullable  spatie role; set when approver_type = role
user_id              fk -> users  nullable  set when approver_type = user
```

```
approval_requests  [DB: tenant]
id
approval_workflow_id fk -> approval_workflows
approvable_type      string            morph map
approvable_id        int
requested_by_user_id fk -> users  nullable  null when raised by a customer or seller
current_step_order   int      default 1
status               enum(pending, approved, rejected, cancelled)  default pending
resolved_at          datetime nullable
index(approvable_type, approvable_id)
```

```
approval_actions  [DB: tenant]
id
approval_request_id  fk -> approval_requests
approval_step_id     fk -> approval_steps
approved_by_user_id  fk -> users
decision             enum(approved, rejected)
note                 text     nullable
decided_at           datetime
unique(approval_request_id, approval_step_id, approved_by_user_id)
```

Workflow configuration (workflows, steps and approvers) is hard-deleted. A workflow with requests is deactivated instead of deleted, and its steps cannot be changed while it has `pending` requests.

### 60.3 Execution

1. **Match.** The owning service creates the record as usual. Before moving it to its own "awaiting staff action" state, it calls `ApprovalWorkflowService::findMatchingWorkflow($moduleKey, $record)`. This returns `null` when `approval_workflows` is disabled. Otherwise it evaluates active workflows for the key in `sort_order`, and the first whose `trigger_conditions` match wins.
2. **Start.** On a match, `ApprovalRequestService::startApproval()` creates the request at step 1. The record is held in the state listed in §60.1, and `approval.step_pending` is sent to the step's eligible approvers. The module's own direct approve and reject routes return 409 while a `pending` request exists for the record.
3. **Eligibility.** A user is eligible at a step when they are named in a `user` approver row, or hold the role of a `role` approver row, at the moment they act.
4. **Decide.**
   - A **rejection** at any step rejects the whole request. The engine calls `onApprovalRejected()`, and `approval.request_rejected` is sent to the requester.
   - Under **`any_one`**, one approval completes the step.
   - Under **`all`**, every approver row must be satisfied: a `user` row by that user, and a `role` row by any one holder of that role (Assumption A-52).
   - When a step completes, `current_step_order` advances and `approval.step_pending` is sent for the new step.
5. **Resolve.** When the final step completes, the request becomes `approved`, the engine calls `onApprovalGranted()`, and `approval.request_approved` is sent.
6. **Cancel.** When the underlying record is cancelled first (for example a purchase order), the owning service calls `cancelApproval()`.

### 60.4 Services

`ApprovalWorkflowService` (Tenant):

- `createWorkflow(array $data, array $steps): ApprovalWorkflow`: steps include their approvers, in one call
- `updateWorkflow(ApprovalWorkflow $workflow, array $data): ApprovalWorkflow`
- `addStep(ApprovalWorkflow $workflow, array $stepData): ApprovalStep`
- `removeStep(ApprovalStep $step): void`: resequences `step_order`
- `reorderSteps(ApprovalWorkflow $workflow, array $orderedStepIds): void`
- `deactivateWorkflow(ApprovalWorkflow $workflow): void`
- `deleteWorkflow(ApprovalWorkflow $workflow): void`: only when it has no requests
- `findMatchingWorkflow(string $moduleKey, $record): ?ApprovalWorkflow`
- `listWorkflows(array $filters): Collection`

`ApprovalRequestService` (Tenant):

- `startApproval(ApprovalWorkflow $workflow, $approvable, ?User $requestedBy = null): ApprovalRequest`
- `approveStep(ApprovalRequest $request, User $approver, ?string $note = null): void`
- `rejectStep(ApprovalRequest $request, User $approver, ?string $note = null): void`
- `cancelApproval(ApprovalRequest $request): void`
- `getPendingApprovalsForUser(User $user): Collection`: everything currently at a step this user is eligible for, across all modules. This powers a single "My Approvals" inbox.
- `getHistory(ApprovalRequest $request): Collection`

### 60.5 Routes

Group `tenant.admin` with `feature:approval_workflows`.

**Configuration** (derived permissions):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Approvals\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/approval-workflows` | `WorkflowController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/approval-workflows` | `WorkflowController@store` |
| GET | `/api/admin/approval-workflows/{workflow}` | `WorkflowController@show` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/approval-workflows/{workflow}` | `WorkflowController@update` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/approval-workflows/{workflow}` | `WorkflowController@destroy` |
| POST | `/api/admin/approval-workflows/{workflow}/deactivate` | `WorkflowController@deactivate` |
| POST | `/api/admin/approval-workflows/{workflow}/steps` | `WorkflowStepController@store` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/approval-workflows/{workflow}/steps/{step}` | `WorkflowStepController@destroy` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/approval-workflows/{workflow}/steps/reorder` | `WorkflowStepController@reorder` |

**Acting on approvals** (permission **none**; eligibility is checked per step, not by a separate permission):

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Approvals\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/approvals/my-pending` | `ApprovalController@myPending` |
| GET | `/api/admin/approvals/{request}` | `ApprovalController@show`: includes the action history. Visible to eligible approvers, the requester, and users with `approval-workflows.view`. |
| POST | `/api/admin/approvals/{request}/approve` | `ApprovalController@approve` |
| POST | `/api/admin/approvals/{request}/reject` | `ApprovalController@reject` |

Earlier drafts placed these under `/api/approvals/*`. Every staff route in this document lives under `/api/admin/`, so these do too.

## 61. Advanced Reporting

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `advanced_reporting` |
| **Code module** | `Reporting` |
| **Depends on** | §32, §39, §40, §44 |
| **Integration hooks** | Reports over optional modules also require that module's feature (table below) |

Advanced reporting is a **read-only** module. Every report queries existing data: orders, order items, products, customers, suppliers, warehouses, payments, expenses and the activity log. It owns no business tables. It replaces the small report set of earlier drafts.

### 61.1 Rules

- **Profit** is the sale amount minus the `unit_cost_snapshot` captured at the time of sale ([§5.8](#58-snapshots)). It is never recomputed from a product's current cost.
- **Sales figures** (gross sales, discounts, returns, net sales, AOV and the rest) use exactly the definitions of [§44.2](#442-metric-definitions): included orders only, test orders excluded, in the base currency. A report and the dashboard can never disagree about the same figure.
- **Shared filters.** Every report accepts the applicable subset of `from`, `to`, `warehouse_id`, `customer_id`, `supplier_id`, `category_id`, `brand_id`, `tag_id`, `payment_method`, `order_source` and `user_id`.
- **Export.** Every report is exported through the asynchronous export mechanism ([§19.4](#194-asynchronous-exports)) with `export_type = report:{reportKey}`. `ReportService::streamReport(string $reportKey, array $filters)` yields the rows in chunks for `GenerateExport`. `csv` and `pdf` are available (§4.5).
- **Read replica.** Reports and exports read from the tenant server's read replica when one is configured (§6.6).
- A `report_snapshots` cache table for very large tenants is deferred ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)).

### 61.2 Report Catalogue

All methods are on `ReportService` (Tenant). The report key is the URI segment after `/api/admin/reports/`.

| Area | Method | Route (`GET /api/admin/reports/...`) | Extra feature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | `getDailySalesReport($date)`: revenue, order count and average order value for one day | `sales/daily` | |
| Sales | `getMonthlySalesReport($year, $month)`: with a day-by-day breakdown | `sales/monthly` | |
| Sales | `getSalesReport($from, $to, array $filters)` | `sales` | |
| Sales | `getSalesReportChart($from, $to, $groupBy)`: day, week or month buckets | `sales/chart` | |
| Purchases | `getDailyPurchaseReport($date)` | `purchases/daily` | `purchasing` |
| Purchases | `getMonthlyPurchaseReport($year, $month)` | `purchases/monthly` | `purchasing` |
| Purchases | `getPurchaseReport($from, $to, array $filters)` | `purchases` | `purchasing` |
| Profit | `getProfitLossReport($from, $to)`: revenue, cost of goods sold and gross profit | `profit-loss` | |
| Profit | `getProfitByProduct($from, $to)` | `profit-by-product` | |
| Profit | `getProfitByCategory($from, $to)` | `profit-by-category` | |
| Profit | `getProfitByBrand($from, $to)` | `profit-by-brand` | |
| Profit | `getProfitByCustomer($from, $to)` | `profit-by-customer` | |
| Profit | `getProfitByLocation($from, $to)`: by fulfilment warehouse | `profit-by-location` | |
| Profit | `getProfitByInvoice($from, $to)`: per order | `profit-by-invoice` | |
| Products and stock | `getBestsellerReport($from, $to, $limit)` | `bestsellers` | |
| Products and stock | `getProductReport(array $filters)`: units sold, revenue and current stock per product | `products` | |
| Products and stock | `getStockReport(array $filters)`: on-hand and available stock across warehouses | `stock` | |
| Products and stock | `getProductExpiryReport($withinDays)`: products near or past `expiry_date` | `product-expiry` | |
| Products and stock | `getProductQuantityAlertReport()`: products at or below `low_stock_threshold`; the same query as `InventoryService::getLowStockProducts()` with report filtering and export | `product-quantity-alerts` | |
| Products and stock | `getWarehouseStockReport(array $filters)` | `warehouse-stock` | |
| Products and stock | `getWarehouseStockChart(int $warehouseId)` | `warehouse-stock/chart` | |
| Tags | `getTagReport(array $filters)`: sales rolled up by product tag | `tags` | |
| Payments | `getPaymentReport($from, $to, array $filters)`: by payment method and provider | `payments` | |
| Payments | `getCashRegisterReport($from, $to, array $filters)`: expected versus counted cash, over or short per session | `cash-register` | `pos` |
| Payments | `getInstallmentReport(array $filters)` | `installments` | `installments` |
| Customers | `getCustomerReport(array $filters)`: order count, revenue and average order value per customer | `customers` | |
| Customers | `getCustomerGroupReport(array $filters)` | `customer-groups` | |
| Customers | `getCustomerDealReport(array $filters)`: accepted sales quotations per customer, quoted versus list price | `customer-deals` | `sales_quotations` |
| Suppliers | `getSupplierReport(array $filters)`: purchase volume and spend per supplier | `suppliers` | `purchasing` |
| Suppliers | `getSupplierDealReport(array $filters)`: `supplier_products.cost_price` versus actual purchase-order unit cost | `supplier-deals` | `purchasing` |
| People | `getUserReport(array $filters)`: per staff user, orders created and POS sales made | `users` | |
| People | `getBillerReport(array $filters)`: expense totals per biller | `billers` | `expenses` |
| Activity | `getActivityLogReport(array $filters)`: the spatie activity log, filterable by user, subject type, date range and event | `activity-log` | |
| Promotions | `getPromotionReport($from, $to, array $filters)`: per promotion and coupon, redemptions by status, discount given, orders and net revenue of those orders | `promotions` | |
| Inventory | `getStockMovementReport(array $filters)`: `inventory_movements` by type, product, warehouse and period, with valuation where cost is known | `stock-movements` | |

Export: `POST /api/admin/reports/{reportKey}/export` with body `{filters, format}` routes to `ReportController@export`. It returns 202 with the `data_exports` record, and needs the same extra feature as the report.

**Changes from earlier drafts.**

- A "biller" is an expense payee (§57.4). It is never a seller of goods. So the biller report sums expenses per biller, and `biller_id` is not a sales filter (Assumption A-53).
- Customer-specific prices come from sales quotations (§53), so the customer-deal report is built on them. Customer-group pricing is a promotion (§26.3), and appears in the promotions report.
- The "daily sales objective" report is deferred, because the architecture has no sales-target entity ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)).

### 61.3 Routes

Group `tenant.admin` with `feature:advanced_reporting`, plus the extra feature shown in §61.2. Every report route is `ReportController@{method}`, with the method name derived from the route. Permissions follow the derivation rule. For example, `GET /api/admin/reports/profit-by-product` requires `reports.profit-by-product.view`.

## 62. AI Business Assistant

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `ai_assistant` |
| **Code module** | `AiAssistant` |
| **Depends on** | §32, §39, §44 |
| **Integration hooks** | Intents over optional modules require that module's feature |

The assistant is a structured natural-language query layer over the tenant's own data: "what were today's sales", "show me low stock", "today's expenses". It answers from this platform's database. It does **not** call an external AI API and needs no paid subscription.

It works by **intent matching against a fixed catalogue** of predefined queries, not by free-text LLM generation. Every answerable question maps to an existing service method. This keeps it free to run, and it cannot invent numbers: it only reports what the underlying service returns.

### 62.1 Tables

```
ai_assistant_intents  [DB: tenant]
id
intent_key           string   unique   e.g. "today_sales"
sample_phrases       json              phrasings to match, e.g. ["today's sales", "how much did we sell today"]
handler              string            a key in the handler registry (§62.2); never a raw class or method name
required_feature     string   nullable  feature key the handler needs; null = catalog only
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
ai_assistant_query_logs  [DB: tenant]
id
user_id              fk -> users
raw_query            text              the typed or dictated text
matched_intent_key   string   nullable  null = no match
response_summary     string   nullable  a short text of what was returned
created_at           datetime          [no updated_at]
```

### 62.2 Handler Registry and Seeded Intents

`config/ai_assistant.php` maps each `handler` key to a service method. The API can never cause an arbitrary method to be invoked: only registry entries run.

| `intent_key` | Handler (service method) | `required_feature` |
|---|---|---|
| `today_sales` | `SalesMetrics::summary(DateRange::today())` (§44.2 definitions) | none |
| `daily_snapshot` | `SalesMetrics::summary(DateRange::today())`, combined with the purchases, expenses and pending-orders handlers the tenant can access | none |
| `top_selling_products` | `SalesMetrics::topProducts(DateRange::lastDays(30))` | none |
| `pending_orders` | `OrderService::getPendingOrders()` | none |
| `low_stock` | `InventoryService::getLowStockProducts()` | none |
| `out_of_stock` | `InventoryService::getOutOfStockProducts()` | none |
| `today_purchases` | `PurchaseOrderService::listPurchaseOrders(['order_date' => today])` totals | `purchasing` |
| `outstanding_supplier_payments` | `SupplierPaymentService::getOutstandingBalances()` | `purchasing` |
| `today_expenses` | `ExpenseService::getTodayExpenses()` | `expenses` |

Seeded intents are inserted by the `ai_assistant` module's `seedDefaults()` the first time the module is enabled, and kept current by the defaults sync while it is enabled ([§12.6](#126-permission-and-default-data-sync)). Adding an intent is a registry entry plus a seeded row. No architecture change is needed. Handlers call the same metric providers as the dashboard (§22.1, §44.5), so the assistant and the dashboard always report the same numbers.

### 62.3 Matching and Service

- A question is matched by normalised keyword and phrase matching against `sample_phrases`. No external NLP service is used. Matching is deliberately basic, in keeping with the no-paid-subscription requirement.
- An intent is a candidate only when `is_active` is true and its `required_feature` (if any) is enabled.
- When nothing matches, the answer is a clarifying message: "I can help with sales, purchases, expenses, stock and order questions. Try asking about one of those." The assistant never guesses.
- The handler runs with the asking user's permissions. If the user lacks the view permission the equivalent report route would need, the answer is a permission message, not data.

`AiAssistantService` (Tenant):

- `askQuestion(string $rawQuery, User $user): array`: matches, calls the handler, logs the query, and returns `{matched, intent_key, answer, data}`
- `listIntents(): Collection`
- `toggleIntent(AiAssistantIntent $intent, bool $active): void`
- `getQueryLogs(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`: shows unmatched questions, so an admin can decide whether a new intent is worth adding

### 62.4 Routes

Group `tenant.admin` with `feature:ai_assistant`:

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\AiAssistant\Admin\...`) | Permission |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/admin/ai-assistant/ask` | `AssistantController@ask` | derived (`ai-assistant.ask`) |
| GET | `/api/admin/ai-assistant/intents` | `IntentController@index` | |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/ai-assistant/intents/{intent}/toggle` | `IntentController@toggle` | |
| GET | `/api/admin/ai-assistant/query-logs` | `QueryLogController@index` | |

## 63. Project Management

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `project_management` |
| **Code module** | `Projects` |
| **Depends on** | §17 (notifications), §25 (staff users), §26 (customers) |

An internal project and task tracker for tenants doing client or internal work alongside their store. A project belongs to a category, may be linked to a customer, has several assigned staff users, and breaks down into tasks. Each task has one assignee, hours and a notification setting. "Employees" in this module are staff **users**, not `hr_employees`. The module does not require `hr`.

### 63.1 Tables

```
project_categories  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string
status               enum(active, inactive)  default active
```

```
projects  [DB: tenant]
id
title                string
project_category_id  fk -> project_categories
customer_id          fk -> customers  nullable  null = an internal project
start_date           date     nullable
end_date             date     nullable
priority             enum(low, medium, high, urgent)  default medium
status               enum(not_started, in_progress, on_hold, completed, cancelled)  default not_started
notify_assigned_employees_whatsapp  bool  default false
notify_customer_whatsapp            bool  default false
description          text     nullable
created_by_user_id   fk -> users
```

```
project_user  [DB: tenant]  [no timestamps]
project_id           fk -> projects
user_id              fk -> users
unique(project_id, user_id)
```

```
project_tasks  [DB: tenant]
id
project_id           fk -> projects
title                string
start_date           date     nullable
end_date             date     nullable
estimated_hours      decimal(8,2) nullable
assigned_user_id     fk -> users  nullable  a task's single assignee, separate from the project's assigned users
status               enum(not_started, in_progress, on_hold, completed, cancelled)  default not_started
send_whatsapp_notification bool   default false
description          text     nullable
```

### 63.2 Notifications

The WhatsApp toggles do not send messages directly. Each maps to a notification event ([§17.9](#179-notification-event-catalog)), so the content stays editable and delivery follows the normal audience and channel matrix:

| Toggle | Event | When |
|---|---|---|
| `projects.notify_assigned_employees_whatsapp` | `project.assigned` | Users are assigned to the project |
| `projects.notify_customer_whatsapp` | `project.customer_update` | The project status changes and a customer is linked |
| `project_tasks.send_whatsapp_notification` | `project_task.assigned` | A task is created with, or reassigned to, a user |

When a toggle is set, the event is dispatched with its `whatsapp` channel enabled for that dispatch. Other channels follow the matrix. When the toggle is off, the event is not dispatched.

### 63.3 Services

- `ProjectCategoryService`: `createCategory()`, `updateCategory()`, `deleteCategory()` (blocked while projects use it), `listCategories(array $filters)`
- `ProjectService`: `createProject(array $data, array $userIds)`, `updateProject()`, `assignEmployees(Project $project, array $userIds)` (sync), `updateStatus(Project $project, string $status)`, `deleteProject()`, `listProjects(array $filters)` (filters are category, customer, status, priority and assigned user), `getProject()`
- `ProjectTaskService`: `createTask(Project $project, array $data)`, `updateTask()`, `updateStatus(ProjectTask $task, string $status)`, `deleteTask()`, `listTasks(Project $project, array $filters)`

Staff data-access scope ([§25.3](#253-staff-data-access-scope)) applies: a narrowed user sees only projects they are assigned to, and tasks assigned to them.

# Part 9: Vertical and Integration Modules

Vertical modules serve a specific industry. Integration modules connect external sales channels. Each has its own feature key ([§11.4](#114-module-registry)). Each is built **on top of** core commerce: a manufactured item, a menu item, a bookable service and a repair part are all ordinary `products` rows, and every stock change goes through `InventoryService` ([§32.6](#326-inventory-service)). No module in this part keeps a second copy of prices or stock.

---

## 64. Manufacturing

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `manufacturing` |
| **Code module** | `Manufacturing` |
| **Depends on** | §27, §28, §32 |

For tenants that produce finished goods from raw materials or components, rather than buying and reselling stock as-is. A manufactured item gains a recipe (a bill of materials) and a production workflow (work orders). Work orders consume component stock and add finished-good stock through the same inventory primitives as everything else.

### 64.1 Tables

```
bill_of_materials  [DB: tenant]
id
product_id           fk -> products             the finished product; simple or variable
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
name                 string            a product may have several BOMs (alternate recipes)
is_default           bool     default false  at most one default per product and variant
yield_quantity       qty      default 1  finished units one batch produces
notes                text     nullable
```

```
bill_of_material_items  [DB: tenant]
id
bill_of_material_id           fk -> bill_of_materials
component_product_id          fk -> products   a physical, non-bundle product
component_product_variant_id  fk -> product_variants  nullable
quantity_required             qty              per one yield_quantity batch
unit_cost_snapshot            money    nullable  component cost when the line was saved, for estimation
```

```
work_orders  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
bill_of_material_id  fk -> bill_of_materials
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses     components are drawn from, and finished goods added to, this warehouse
quantity_to_produce  qty
status               enum(planned, in_progress, completed, cancelled)  default planned
scheduled_start_date date     nullable
scheduled_end_date   date     nullable
started_at           datetime nullable
completed_at         datetime nullable
created_by_user_id   fk -> users
notes                text     nullable
```

```
work_order_materials  [DB: tenant]
id
work_order_id                 fk -> work_orders
component_product_id          fk -> products
component_product_variant_id  fk -> product_variants  nullable
quantity_required             qty              BOM quantity × quantity_to_produce / yield_quantity
quantity_consumed             qty      nullable  set on completion
```

### 64.2 Work Order Lifecycle

| From | Action | Stock effect | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| `planned` | `startWorkOrder()` | Checks that every component has enough **available** stock at the warehouse, then reserves it (`reserveStock()`, reference = the work order). A shortfall is rejected with 409 up front, not discovered mid-production. | `in_progress` |
| `in_progress` | `completeWorkOrder()` | One transaction: every component is deducted from its reservation (`deductStock(fromReservation: true)`), `quantity_consumed = quantity_required`, and `quantity_to_produce` of the finished product is added (`adjustStock()`, reason `work_order`). All or nothing. | `completed` |
| `planned` | `cancelWorkOrder()` | None | `cancelled` |
| `in_progress` | `cancelWorkOrder()` | Releases the component reservations | `cancelled` |

Components are reserved at start, not deducted, because the stock physically leaves only when production completes. This is what "cancelling reverses any reserved stock" means (Assumption A-54). Consumption that differs from the recipe (for example scrap) is recorded afterwards as a stock adjustment ([§33.2](#332-stock-adjustments)).

### 64.3 Cost Roll-Up

`ManufacturingCostService::calculateUnitCost(BillOfMaterial $bom): float` sums each item's `quantity_required` × the component's current `cost_price` (the variant's, falling back to the product's), and divides by `yield_quantity`.

The result is written to the finished product's (or variant's) `cost_price` when a default BOM is saved and when a work order on the default BOM completes. Margins on manufactured goods therefore reflect the recipe rather than a hand-typed figure. Historical orders keep their `unit_cost_snapshot` ([§5.8](#58-snapshots)). Manufacturing makes no accounting postings in v1 ([§57.3](#573-journal-entries-and-automatic-postings)).

### 64.4 Services and Routes

`BillOfMaterialService`: `createBom(Product $product, array $items, array $data)`, `updateBom(BillOfMaterial $bom, array $items, array $data)`, `deleteBom()` (blocked while work orders reference it), `setDefaultBom()`, `listBoms(Product $product)`, `getBom()`.

`WorkOrderService`: `createWorkOrder(BillOfMaterial $bom, Warehouse $warehouse, float $quantity, array $data)` (computes `work_order_materials`), `startWorkOrder()`, `completeWorkOrder()`, `cancelWorkOrder()`, `listWorkOrders(array $filters)`, `getWorkOrder()`.

Group `tenant.admin` with `feature:manufacturing`:

| Method | URI | Action (`Tenant\Manufacturing\Admin\...`) |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/admin/products/{product}/bill-of-materials` | `BillOfMaterialController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/products/{product}/bill-of-materials` | `BillOfMaterialController@store` |
| GET | `/api/admin/bill-of-materials/{bom}` | `BillOfMaterialController@show`: includes the calculated unit cost |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/bill-of-materials/{bom}` | `BillOfMaterialController@update` |
| DELETE | `/api/admin/bill-of-materials/{bom}` | `BillOfMaterialController@destroy` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/bill-of-materials/{bom}/set-default` | `BillOfMaterialController@setDefault` |
| GET | `/api/admin/work-orders` | `WorkOrderController@index` |
| POST | `/api/admin/work-orders` | `WorkOrderController@store` |
| GET | `/api/admin/work-orders/{order}` | `WorkOrderController@show` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/work-orders/{order}/start` | `WorkOrderController@start` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/work-orders/{order}/complete` | `WorkOrderController@complete` |
| PATCH | `/api/admin/work-orders/{order}/cancel` | `WorkOrderController@cancel` |
