## 65. Restaurant

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `restaurant` (requires `pos`) |
| **Code module** | `Restaurant` |
| **Depends on** | §39, §40, §51 |

The restaurant module is a layer on top of POS, not a separate checkout. A restaurant sale **is** a POS order (`order_source = pos`). It adds a floor plan of tables, reservations, modifier-based menu options, and a kitchen display that tracks each dish between "sent to kitchen" and "served". Table features are active when `pos_settings.table_management_enabled` is true ([§51.7](#517-pos-settings)).

### 65.1 Floors, Tables and Reservations

```
restaurant_floors  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Main Hall", "Patio"
warehouse_id         fk -> warehouses  the location (and therefore POS registers) this floor belongs to
sort_order           int      default 0
```

```
restaurant_tables  [DB: tenant]
id
restaurant_floor_id  fk -> restaurant_floors
name                 string            e.g. "Table 4"
seats                int
status               enum(available, occupied, reserved, cleaning)  default available
```

```
restaurant_reservations  [DB: tenant]
id
restaurant_table_id  fk -> restaurant_tables
customer_id          fk -> customers  nullable  a phone-in reservation may have no customer record
customer_name        string
customer_phone       string   nullable
party_size           int
reservation_time     datetime
status               enum(confirmed, seated, completed, cancelled, no_show)  default confirmed
order_id             fk -> orders  nullable  the table order opened on seating
notes                text     nullable
```

**Table status.**

- A table becomes `reserved` 30 minutes before a `confirmed` reservation's time. Confirming a reservation dispatches `MarkTableReserved` with a delay to that moment. The job re-reads the reservation and does nothing when it is no longer `confirmed` or its time has moved (a rescheduled reservation dispatches a new job) (Assumption A-55).
- Opening a table order sets `occupied`. Settling or voiding it sets `available`. Staff may set `cleaning` and `available` by hand.
- Reservations are not checked for overlap in v1 ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)).
- `seatReservation()` sets the reservation to `seated` and opens a table order (§65.4). The reservation becomes `completed` when that order is settled.

### 65.2 Modifiers

A menu item is an ordinary product. Modifiers add structured, optional customisation that variants do not suit: variants model fixed SKU combinations (size, colour), not add-ons.

```
modifier_groups  [DB: tenant]
id
name                 string            e.g. "Spice Level", "Add-ons"
selection_type       enum(single, multiple)
is_required          bool     default false
```

```
modifier_options  [DB: tenant]
id
modifier_group_id    fk -> modifier_groups
name                 string            e.g. "Extra Cheese", "No Onions"
price_adjustment     money    default 0  in the base currency
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
product_modifier_group  [DB: tenant]  [no timestamps]
product_id           fk -> products
modifier_group_id    fk -> modifier_groups
unique(product_id, modifier_group_id)
```

```
order_item_modifiers  [DB: tenant]
id
order_item_id              fk -> order_items
modifier_option_id         fk -> modifier_options
name_snapshot              string
price_adjustment_snapshot  money       in orders.currency_code
```

- A group is reused across many products instead of being redefined per product.
- Validation: a `single` group accepts at most one option, and a required group needs at least one.
- A line's `unit_price` is the product's resolved price plus Σ the selected `price_adjustment` values, converted to the order currency. The selections are snapshotted in `order_item_modifiers` ([§5.8](#58-snapshots)).
- Modifiers are available on restaurant table orders and one-pass POS sales. The online cart does not support modifiers in v1 (Assumption A-56).

### 65.3 Kitchen Display

- `order_items.kitchen_status` and `order_items.kitchen_ready_at` are defined in [§39.2](#392-order-items-table). Status is tracked per line, so the kitchen can mark dishes ready independently within one ticket.
- A line added to a table order enters the kitchen queue at `kitchen_status = pending`. It is visible as soon as it is sent, not only once paid.
- Line status moves `pending` → `preparing` → `ready` → `served`. Reaching `ready` sets `kitchen_ready_at`.
- `KitchenDisplayService::getActiveTickets()` returns open restaurant orders grouped by table, each with its lines and their status.
- `KitchenDisplayService::getMetrics(array $filters)` returns the average preparation time (`kitchen_ready_at − created_at`), open tickets, tickets completed today and the busiest hours. This kitchen view is separate from the sales dashboard.

### 65.4 Table Orders

A table order stays open while items are added across rounds (starters, then mains), and is paid once at the end. This differs from the one-pass retail sale in [§51.3](#513-sale-flow).

`RestaurantTableOrderService` (Tenant):

- `openTableOrder(RestaurantTable $table, ?PosSession $session, array $lines = [], array $options = []): Order`: creates the order through `OrderService::createOrder()` with `order_source = pos`, `status = pending`, `restaurant_table_id` and `created_by_user_id`. The initial lines may be empty. Lines are reserved at the floor's warehouse like online orders ([§32.5](#325-stock-lifecycle-reservation-deduction-and-release)). The table becomes `occupied`.
- `addItems(Order $order, array $lines): Order`: one round. Calls `OrderService::appendItems()` ([§39.5](#395-order-service)) with modifier selections. The new lines enter the kitchen queue.
- `settle(Order $order, array $payments): Order`: records the payments as `order_payments` rows with `pos_session_id`, using the POS payment rules ([§51.2](#512-pos-payments), [§51.3](#513-sale-flow)). When fully paid, `confirmOrder()` deducts from the reservations, and the order becomes `completed`. The table becomes `available`. The receipt comes from `PosSaleService::generateReceipt()`.
- `voidTableOrder(Order $order, string $reason): void`: allowed before settlement. Cancels the order through `OrderService::cancelOrder()`, which releases the reservations. The table becomes `available`.
- `getCurrentOrder(RestaurantTable $table): ?Order`

When `cash_register_enabled` is true, `settle()` requires an open session. Payment methods, split tender, receipts and session reconciliation are otherwise the standard POS mechanics.

### 65.5 Services and Routes

- `RestaurantFloorService`: `createFloor()`, `updateFloor()`, `deleteFloor()` (blocked while it has tables), `listFloors()`
- `RestaurantTableService`: `createTable(RestaurantFloor $floor, array $data)`, `updateTable()`, `updateStatus()`, `deleteTable()` (blocked while it has an open order), `listTables(array $filters)` (filters are floor and status)
- `RestaurantReservationService`: `createReservation()`, `updateReservation()`, `seatReservation(): Order`, `cancelReservation()`, `markNoShow()`, `listReservations(array $filters)`
- `ModifierGroupService`: `createGroup()`, `updateGroup()`, `deleteGroup()`, `addOption()`, `updateOption()`, `deleteOption()`, `attachToProduct()`, `detachFromProduct()`, `listGroups()`
- `KitchenDisplayService`: `getActiveTickets()`, `updateItemStatus(OrderItem $item, string $status)`, `getMetrics(array $filters)`
- `RestaurantTableOrderService`: §65.4

## 66. Booking

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `booking` |
| **Code module** | `Booking` |
| **Depends on** | §25, §26, §27, §28, §39 |
| **Integration hooks** | Repair drop-off slots (§67) |

Booking turns the `service` product type ([§28](#28-product-types-variants-bundles-digital-and-service)) into an appointment system, for tenants selling bookable time: a consultant's hourly slots, a salon chair, a repair bay. `products.is_bookable` and `products.duration_minutes` are defined in [§27](#27-catalogue-categories-brands-and-products). Only service products may be bookable, and a bookable product requires `duration_minutes`.

### 66.1 Tables

```
booking_staff  [DB: tenant]
id
user_id              fk -> users  unique  the staff user who can be booked
is_active            bool     default true
```

```
product_booking_staff  [DB: tenant]  [no timestamps]
product_id           fk -> products
booking_staff_id     fk -> booking_staff
unique(product_id, booking_staff_id)
```

```
booking_availability  [DB: tenant]
id
booking_staff_id     fk -> booking_staff
day_of_week          int               0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday
start_time           time
end_time             time
```

```
booking_time_off  [DB: tenant]
id
booking_staff_id     fk -> booking_staff
start_datetime       datetime
end_datetime         datetime
reason               string   nullable
```

```
bookings  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
product_id           fk -> products
booking_staff_id     fk -> booking_staff
customer_id          fk -> customers  nullable  null = a guest booking
guest_name           string   nullable  required for guest bookings
guest_email          string   nullable  required for guest bookings
guest_phone          string   nullable
start_datetime       datetime
end_datetime         datetime          start + products.duration_minutes
status               enum(pending_payment, confirmed, completed, cancelled, no_show)  default confirmed
order_id             fk -> orders  nullable  the order that bills this booking
notes                text     nullable
index(booking_staff_id, start_datetime)
```

- Recurring weekly hours come from `booking_availability`. One-off exceptions (leave, holidays) come from `booking_time_off`. An approved HR leave request does **not** create time off automatically in v1 ([Appendix C](#appendix-c-deferred-and-out-of-scope-items)).
- Times are in the tenant timezone.

### 66.2 Rules

- **Slots.** `getAvailableSlots()` generates candidate start times every `duration_minutes` from the start of each availability window, then removes those overlapping time off or an existing `pending_payment` or `confirmed` booking (Assumption A-57).
- **Validate before commit.** `createBooking()` and `rescheduleBooking()` lock the staff member's bookings for that day and re-check the slot inside the transaction, so two customers cannot book the same slot.
- **Guests.** Guest bookings follow the effective `guest_checkout_enabled` setting ([§38.6](#386-checkout-flow)).
- **Payment** (decides UD-21) is controlled by `tenant_settings.booking_requires_prepayment` (default false):
  - **false:** the booking is `confirmed` immediately. Staff bill it later through `createOrderForBooking()`, which creates an order through `OrderService::createOrder()` (`order_source = admin`, one service line for the product) and sets `bookings.order_id`. The customer pays through the normal order payment flow ([§40](#40-order-payments)).
  - **true:** a storefront booking is created as `pending_payment`, together with its order (`order_source = online`, so the unpaid-order expiry of §39.5 applies), in one transaction. A `pending_payment` booking holds its slot. When the order is confirmed, the `OrderService` hook calls `BookingService::confirmForOrder()`, and the booking becomes `confirmed`. When the order is cancelled or expires, `BookingService::cancelForOrder()` cancels the booking and frees the slot. Bookings made by staff are always `confirmed`.
- A customer may cancel their own `confirmed` booking before `start_datetime`.

### 66.3 Services and Routes

- `BookingStaffService`: `createStaff(User $user)`, `updateStaff()`, `deactivateStaff()`, `attachToProduct()`, `detachFromProduct()`, `listStaff()`
- `BookingAvailabilityService`: `setWeeklyAvailability(BookingStaff $staff, array $slots)` (replaces all rows), `addTimeOff(BookingStaff $staff, array $data)`, `removeTimeOff(BookingTimeOff $timeOff)`, `getAvailableSlots(Product $product, ?BookingStaff $staff, $date): array` (any eligible staff when `$staff` is null)
- `BookingService`: `createBooking(Product $product, BookingStaff $staff, $start, array $data)`, `rescheduleBooking(Booking $booking, $newStart)`, `cancelBooking()`, `markCompleted()`, `markNoShow()`, `createOrderForBooking(Booking $booking): Order`, `confirmForOrder(Order $order): void`, `cancelForOrder(Order $order): void`, `listBookings(array $filters)` (filters are staff, customer, date range and status), `listForCustomer(Customer $customer)`

| `tenant.public` | GET | `/api/products/{product}/available-slots` | `SlotController@index`: `?date=&booking_staff_id=` |

## 67. Repair

| | |

| **Context** | Tenant |

For tenants taking in customer items for repair (electronics, phones, appliances). A repair job is tracked from intake through diagnosis, parts used and completion. Parts are ordinary products, and payment reuses the order flow.

### 67.1 Tables

```
repair_jobs  [DB: tenant]  audited
id
customer_id          fk -> customers  nullable  null = a walk-in with no account

status               enum(received, diagnosing, awaiting_approval, in_repair, completed, picked_up, cancelled)
                                        default received
diagnosis_notes      text     nullable
estimated_cost       money    nullable
customer_approved_at datetime nullable
order_id             fk -> orders  nullable  set when the job is invoiced
received_at          datetime
completed_at         datetime nullable
picked_up_at         datetime nullable
```

```
repair_job_parts  [DB: tenant]
id
repair_job_id        fk -> repair_jobs
product_id           fk -> products
product_variant_id   fk -> product_variants  nullable
quantity             qty
unit_cost_snapshot   money    nullable
```

```
repair_job_labor  [DB: tenant]
id
repair_job_id        fk -> repair_jobs
description          string            e.g. "Screen replacement labour"
amount               money             in the base currency
```

### 67.2 Status Lifecycle

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `received` | `diagnosing` | Staff |
| `diagnosing` | `awaiting_approval` | `updateDiagnosis()` with notes and an estimate. Dispatches `repair_job.diagnosis_ready`. |
| `awaiting_approval` | `in_repair` | Requires `customer_approved_at`, set by the customer's approval route or by staff through `recordCustomerApproval()` |
| `diagnosing` | `in_repair` | Staff, when no estimate approval is needed (`estimated_cost` null) |
| `in_repair` | `completed` | Staff. Dispatches `repair_job.ready_for_pickup`. |
| `completed` | `picked_up` | `markPickedUp()` |
| any before `completed` | `cancelled` | Staff. Restocks every part (§67.3). |

### 67.3 Parts, Labour and Invoicing

- **Parts** can be added or removed only in `in_repair`, so parts are never consumed before the customer approves an estimate. `addPart()` deducts the part from the job's warehouse immediately (`adjustStock()`, reason `repair_part`) and snapshots its cost. `removePart()` restocks it. Both are all-or-nothing.
- **Labour** lines can be added in `diagnosing` or `in_repair`.
- **Invoicing.** `generateInvoice()` is allowed once, in `in_repair` or `completed`. It creates an order through `OrderService::createOrder()` with `order_source = admin`:
  - one product line per part, at the product's resolved price at the job's warehouse ([§38.4](#384-price-resolution)), with `warehouse_id` set and `stock_already_deducted = true` ([§39.2](#392-order-items-table)), so the order never reserves or deducts the part again
  - one non-product line per labour row (`product_id = null`)
  - tax is calculated on the product lines by the normal rules. Labour lines are not taxed (Assumption A-58).
- It sets `repair_jobs.order_id`. After invoicing, parts and labour are locked. Payment uses the normal order flow ([§40](#40-order-payments)).

### 67.4 Services and Routes

## 68. WooCommerce Integration

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Tenant |
| **Feature key** | `woocommerce` |
| **Code module** | `Integrations\WooCommerce` |
| **Depends on** | §27, §32, §35, §39, §40 |

Lets a tenant connect an existing WooCommerce store and keep it in sync with this platform's catalogue, tax and order data. It is for tenants migrating off WooCommerce gradually, or running both storefronts in parallel. It is a bounded integration module: a background sync engine plus a log. Core catalogue and order services have no knowledge of WooCommerce.

### 68.1 Settings

```

store_url             string   nullable
consumer_key          encrypted nullable
consumer_secret       encrypted nullable
is_active             bool     default false
sync_products         bool     default true
sync_categories       bool     default true
sync_orders           bool     default true
sync_tax_rates        bool     default true
order_sync_direction  enum(import, export)  default import
import_warehouse_id   fk -> warehouses  nullable  receives initial stock and fulfils imported orders
sync_interval_minutes int      default 15
last_synced_at        datetime nullable
```

`order_sync_direction` makes the direction that earlier drafts mentioned but never stored explicit (Assumption A-59). `import_warehouse_id` is required before product or order sync can be activated.

```

woocommerce_product_map  [DB: tenant]
id

woocommerce_product_id   int

last_synced_at           datetime nullable
stock_dirty_at           datetime nullable  set by an inventory movement; cleared by PushWooCommerceStock (§68.3)
unique(woocommerce_product_id, woocommerce_variation_id), index(stock_dirty_at)
```

```
woocommerce_tax_rate_map  [DB: tenant]
id
tax_rate_id              fk -> tax_rates
woocommerce_tax_rate_id  int

```

```
woocommerce_order_map  [DB: tenant]
id
order_id                 fk -> orders
woocommerce_order_id     int
direction                enum(imported, exported)
last_synced_at           datetime nullable
unique(woocommerce_order_id)
```

```
woocommerce_sync_logs  [DB: tenant]
id
sync_type            enum(product, category, tax_rate, order, stock)
direction            enum(pull, push)
trigger              enum(scheduled, manual)
status               enum(success, failed, partial)
items_processed      int      default 0
items_failed         int      default 0
error_details        json     nullable  per-item failure reasons
started_at           datetime
completed_at         datetime nullable
```

### 68.3 Sync Rules

- **Categories** (pull): WooCommerce categories create or update platform categories and map rows.
- **Tax rates** (pull): WooCommerce rates are mapped onto existing `tax_rates` ([§35](#35-tax)) or created, so rates are not entered twice.
- **Products** (pull): WooCommerce products create or update platform products (name, description, SKU, price, categories through the map, images). Variations become variants.
- **Stock.** Stock is imported **only** when a product is first mapped: its WooCommerce quantity is added at `import_warehouse_id` through `adjustStock()` (reason `woocommerce_import`). After that, the platform's `inventory` is the source of truth ([§32](#32-warehouses-and-inventory)). Ongoing stock is **pushed** to WooCommerce (decides UD-22). Every inventory movement on a mapped product sets `woocommerce_product_map.stock_dirty_at` through the `InventoryService` integration hook (a no-op without `woocommerce`), and a debounced `PushWooCommerceStock` job (unique per tenant, delayed 60 seconds) pushes the current available stock, summed across warehouses, for every dirty product in one batch call. WooCommerce stock is never read back after the first mapping, so the two stores cannot fight over the value. Orders placed in WooCommerce reach the platform through the order import and reduce stock here, and the next push corrects WooCommerce.
- **Orders, import:** new WooCommerce orders are created through `OrderService::createOrder()` with `order_source = woocommerce`, `idempotency_key = "woo:{id}"`, and lines fulfilled from `import_warehouse_id`. A WooCommerce order already paid in WooCommerce is recorded as one `order_payments` row with `payment_method = other` and `notes = "Paid via WooCommerce"`, and is then confirmed by the normal payment-status rules ([§39.4](#394-confirmation-payment-status-and-order-status)) (Assumption A-60). `max_orders_per_month` applies. An order that fails (for example no stock, or the limit is reached) is recorded in the log's `error_details` and retried on the next run.
- **Orders, export:** platform orders are pushed to WooCommerce and mapped with `direction = exported`.
- `pushProduct()` pushes a single platform product to WooCommerce on demand, for a product created here that should also exist there.

**Scheduling.** `RunWooCommerceSync` is self-scheduling. Enabling sync dispatches the first run. Each run, when it finishes and `is_active` is still true, dispatches the next run delayed by `sync_interval_minutes`. The job is unique per tenant and sync type, so a manual trigger and a scheduled run never overlap. The daily tenant maintenance job (§72.2) restarts a chain whose `last_synced_at` is older than twice the interval. There is no platform-wide polling task. Every run writes one `woocommerce_sync_logs` row.

### 68.4 Services and Routes

- `WooCommerceSettingsService`: `getSettings()`, `saveCredentials(array $data)`, `testConnection(): bool` (checks the credentials against the WooCommerce REST API before sync is enabled), `updateSyncToggles(array $data)`
- `WooCommerceSyncService`: `syncCategories(): WooCommerceSyncLog`, `syncProducts(): WooCommerceSyncLog`, `syncTaxRates(): WooCommerceSyncLog`, `syncOrders(): WooCommerceSyncLog`, `pushProduct(Product $product): void`, `getSyncLogs(array $filters): LengthAwarePaginator`, `getSyncMetrics(): array` (counts by type and status, and the last sync time per type)

| GET | `/api/admin/woocommerce/settings` | `SettingsController@show`: credentials are masked (§5.6) |
| PUT | `/api/admin/woocommerce/settings` | `SettingsController@update` |
| POST | `/api/admin/woocommerce/settings/test-connection` | `SettingsController@testConnection` |
| POST | `/api/admin/woocommerce/sync/categories` | `SyncController@categories` |

`products.social_commerce_excluded_channels` is defined in [§27](#27-catalogue-categories-brands-and-products). It holds back a product from the listed channels even when the account syncs products.

### 69.2 Channel Rules

| Channel | Products | Orders |
|---|---|---|
| `instagram` | Shoppable posts and tags. A tagged product links to the tenant's own storefront to complete the purchase. | Never. There is no native checkout. |
| `facebook_shop` | Yes | Yes (native checkout) |
| `tiktok_shop` | Yes | Yes (native checkout) |
| `whatsapp_catalog` | Yes, through the channel's catalogue API | Yes. Message-based confirmations use the notification system and the WhatsApp gateway ([§16](#16-message-delivery-email-sms-whatsapp-and-push)). |

- **Products (push):** the platform catalogue, minus excluded products, is pushed to the channel. Price and stock are always read from the platform's own tables ([§32](#32-warehouses-and-inventory), [§38.4](#384-price-resolution)). This module never becomes a second source of truth for price or stock. Simple and variable products are synced. Bundle, digital and service products are not (Assumption A-61).
- **Orders (pull):** orders placed through native checkout are created through `OrderService::createOrder()` with `order_source = social`, `idempotency_key = "social:{account_id}:{external_id}"`, lines fulfilled from `fulfilment_warehouse_id`, and payment recorded as for WooCommerce imports (Assumption A-60).
- **Credentials.** How a tenant obtains and refreshes each provider's access token (OAuth connection flows) is UD-23. Interim: the tenant supplies a token directly, and a failed sync caused by an expired token is logged.
- **Scheduling** is the same as WooCommerce: `RunSocialCommerceSync` is self-scheduling per active account, unique per account, and restarted by the daily maintenance watchdog. Manual triggers are per account.

- `SocialCommerceAccountService`: `connectAccount(string $channel, array $credentials)`, `testConnection(SocialCommerceAccount $account): bool`, `updateSyncToggles()`, `disconnectAccount()` (deactivates and removes the product maps), `listAccounts()`
- `SocialCommerceSyncService`: `syncProducts(SocialCommerceAccount $account): SocialCommerceSyncLog`, `syncOrders(SocialCommerceAccount $account): SocialCommerceSyncLog`, `pushProduct(SocialCommerceAccount $account, Product $product)`, `removeProduct(SocialCommerceAccount $account, Product $product)`, `getSyncLogs(array $filters)`, `getSyncMetrics()`

# Part 10: Implementation Reference

This part holds the conventions and indexes that apply across every module. The index sections (§70.3, §72, §79) list items and point to their owning sections. They never redefine them ([§1.3](#13-authority-rules)).

## 70. API Architecture and Conventions

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Both |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Depends on** | §5, §6, §10, §11, §12 |

Apply these conventions globally. Do not decide them afresh per controller.

### 70.1 Request and Response Format

- **JSON only.** Every endpoint accepts and returns `application/json`, except file uploads (`multipart/form-data`), file downloads (exports are delivered as temporary signed URLs, [§19.4](#194-asynchronous-exports)) and `/sitemap.xml` ([§30.2](#302-seo)).
- **Field naming.** Request and response fields are `snake_case`, matching column names.
- **One response envelope: `APIResponse`.** Every JSON response, success or error, in both contexts, is built by the single `App\Shared\Http\APIResponse` helper and has exactly these top-level keys:

  ```json
  {
    "success": true,
    "message": "Order created",
    "data": {},
    "meta": {},
    "errors": {}
  }
  ```

  | Key | Success | Error |
  |---|---|---|
  | `success` | `true` | `false` |
  | `message` | A short human-readable message | A short human-readable message |
  | `data` | The API Resource output: an object for a single record, an array for a collection | `null` |
  | `meta` | Pagination (§70.4) and other response metadata (for example `generated_at` on dashboards); `{}` when there is none | `{"error_code": "...", "details": {...}}`: the machine-readable code (§70.8) and its structured details |
  | `errors` | `{}` | Field errors keyed by field name (validation), otherwise `{}` |

  **Resources.** `data` is always produced by an API Resource. Controllers never return models, arrays or Laravel's default `{"data": ...}` resource wrapping; they return `APIResponse::success($resource, $message, $meta, $status)` or `APIResponse::error(...)`. Exception rendering (§70.8) uses the same helper, so there is no second response format anywhere, including 404, 429 and 503 responses produced by middleware.
- **Validation.** Every write action has a FormRequest. Controllers receive only validated data.
- **Money** is serialised as a decimal string with four decimal places (for example `"1250.5000"`), never as a JSON float. The currency code is returned next to it wherever the record carries one (Assumption A-62). Quantities (`qty`) are serialised the same way with three decimals.
- **Dates and times** follow [§5.10](#510-dates-times-and-display-formats): stored in UTC, returned as ISO 8601 with offset (`2026-09-22T20:09:00+00:00`) and `YYYY-MM-DD` for dates, whatever display format any setting or preference selects. Business-calendar logic ("this month", "due today", daily jobs) is evaluated in the context's business timezone.
- **Encrypted columns** are never returned ([§5.6](#56-encrypted-data)).
- **Soft-deleted records** are excluded from every list and show endpoint unless the owning section defines an explicit `?with_trashed=1` filter.
- **Successful status codes.** `200` for reads and updates, `201` with the created resource for creates, `202` for accepted asynchronous work (registration [§9.3](#93-registration-flow), exports, large coupon batches, manual sync triggers), and `204` for deletes.

### 70.2 Route Files and URI Prefixes

| Route file | Served on | Tenancy middleware | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routes/api.php` | Landlord domains (`central_domains`) | none | Landlord public, landlord admin, affiliate portal and billing webhook routes (`POST /api/webhooks/{provider}/{mode}`, [§15.6](#156-webhooks)) |
| `routes/tenant.php` | Tenant domains | `InitializeTenancyByDomain`, `PreventAccessFromCentralDomains` | Every tenant route except webhooks |
| `routes/tenant-webhooks.php` | Landlord domains | `InitializeTenancyByPath` | `POST /api/webhooks/{tenant}/{provider}/{mode}` ([§15.6](#156-webhooks)) |
| `routes/channels.php` | Both | per channel ([§72.4](#724-broadcasting-and-real-time)) | Broadcast channel authorisation |
| `routes/console.php` | n/a | n/a | Scheduler definitions ([§72.2](#722-scheduled-tasks)) |

`GET /sitemap.xml` is registered in `routes/tenant.php` outside the `/api` prefix ([§30.2](#302-seo)).

URI prefixes. These are the only prefixes in use:

| Prefix | Domain | Audience |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/*` (no audience segment) | Landlord | Public: registration, plan listing, public lookups, affiliate clicks, platform coupon validation |
| `/api/admin/*` | Landlord | Platform users |
| `/api/affiliate/*` | Landlord | Affiliates (authentication and portal, §21A) |
| `/api/*` (no audience segment) | Tenant | Storefront: public catalogue, cart, checkout, guest-accessible routes |
| `/api/auth/*` | Tenant | Customer authentication |
| `/api/account/*`, `/api/wishlist`, `/api/quotation-requests`, `/api/orders` | Tenant | Authenticated customer self-service. The owning section fixes the exact URI. |
| `/api/admin/*` | Tenant | Staff users (tenant admin API) |
| `/api/seller/*` | Tenant | Sellers |
| `/api/driver/*` | Tenant | Drivers |
| `/api/webhooks/*` | Landlord | Payment providers |

Prefixes used in earlier drafts are not used: `/api/central/*`, `/api/tenant/*`, `/api/customer/*` (replaced by `/api/account/*`), `/api/hr/*` and `/api/approvals/*` (both under `/api/admin/`).

The landlord and tenant route files both define `/api/admin/*`. They never collide, because the domain decides which file handles the request.

### 70.3 Route Group Map

Each route table in this document names its group. The group fixes the middleware stack. Middleware runs in the order listed. Per-route middleware (`feature:`, `module.notice:`, `usage.limit:`, `permission:`) is appended in the order defined in [§11.1](#111-concept-separation): feature, then module notice, then limit, then permission.

| Group | Route file | Middleware stack | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `landlord.public` | `api.php` | `request.context`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:public` | Registration, public plans, public lookups, platform-user auth (with `throttle:auth-sensitive`) |
| `landlord.admin` | `api.php` | `request.context`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:api`, `auth.as:platform`, `permission:{derived}`, then per route: `idempotency` | Platform admin API |
| `landlord.affiliate` | `api.php` | `request.context`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:api`, `auth.as:affiliate` | Affiliate portal (§21A.10) |
| `landlord.webhooks` | `api.php` | `request.context`, `verify.webhook:{provider}` | Billing webhooks |
| `landlord.internal` | `api.php` | `request.context`, `internal.edge` | Machine-to-machine endpoints for platform infrastructure. The only route is the edge TLS check ([§7.5](#75-custom-domains)). |
| `tenant.public` | `tenant.php` | `request.context`, tenancy, `platform.maintenance`, `tenant.active`, `throttle:tenant`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:public` | Unauthenticated storefront reads, auth routes (with `throttle:auth-sensitive`), public careers, CMS reads |
| `tenant.storefront` | `tenant.php` | `tenant.public` stack, `auth.as.optional:customer`, `guest.token` | Cart, checkout, guest-accessible orders and payments, support for guests |
| `tenant.customer` | `tenant.php` | `request.context`, tenancy, `platform.maintenance`, `tenant.active`, `throttle:tenant`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:api`, `auth.as:customer` | Customer account routes |
| `tenant.seller` | `tenant.php` | `request.context`, tenancy, `platform.maintenance`, `tenant.active`, `throttle:tenant`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:api`, `auth.as:seller`, `feature:marketplace` | Seller self-service |
| `tenant.driver` | `tenant.php` | `request.context`, tenancy, `platform.maintenance`, `tenant.active`, `throttle:tenant`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:api`, `auth.as:driver` | Driver app |
| `tenant.admin` | `tenant.php` | `request.context`, tenancy, `platform.maintenance`, `tenant.active`, `throttle:tenant`, `cors.dynamic`, `throttle:api`, `auth.as:staff`, then per route: `feature:{key}`, `module.notice:{key}`, `usage.limit:{key}`, `permission:{derived}`, `idempotency` | Tenant admin API |
| `tenant.webhooks` | `tenant-webhooks.php` | `request.context`, `InitializeTenancyByPath`, `verify.webhook:{provider}` | Storefront payment webhooks |

"Tenancy" means `InitializeTenancyByDomain` then `PreventAccessFromCentralDomains`. `request.context` runs again after tenancy is initialised, so the tenant ID is added to the log context (§77.7).

`idempotency` is appended to the routes that name it, always last, after authentication and authorisation, so a rejected request never occupies a key ([§70.11](#7011-idempotency)).

Rules:

1. A route table header of the form "Group `tenant.{group}` with `feature:x`", or a statement that every route carries `feature:x`, means each route in the table sits behind `feature:x` and `module.notice:x`. A row naming an additional feature (for example `feature:gift_cards` on a cart route) adds that feature and its module notice. Rows marked "always available" have neither.
2. `module.notice:{key}` uses the same key as the group's `feature:` middleware ([§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode)). Always-available groups have no module notice.
3. `usage.limit:{key}` is applied only to the create routes named in [§11.8](#118-limit-registry), plus any route where a row explicitly names it.
4. `permission:{derived}` is the spatie `permission:` middleware with the name derived by [§12.4](#124-permission-naming-and-derivation), guard `staff` (tenant) or `platform` (landlord). Rows marked "none" omit it. Auth routes that are public in their group (login, register, forgot, reset) have no `auth.as` and no permission.
5. `tenant.webhooks` deliberately omits `tenant.active`, `platform.maintenance` and every throttle, so payments are processed for `suspended` and `closed` tenants and during maintenance ([§6.5](#65-tenant-status-and-access), [§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode)). A `purged` tenant's webhooks return 410, because there is no database to record them in.
6. Route names follow `{context}.{audience}.{resource}.{action}`, for example `tenant.admin.products.index` and `landlord.admin.plans.store`. The audience is `public`, `storefront`, `customer`, `seller`, `driver`, `affiliate`, `admin` or `webhooks`.

### 70.4 Pagination

- Every list endpoint is paginated. No endpoint returns an unbounded collection.
- Default page size is 15, overridable with `?per_page=`, capped at 100. A larger value is clamped to 100, not rejected.
- **Length-aware pagination** (`?page=`) is the default.
- **Cursor pagination** (`?cursor=`) is used for lists that are scrolled rather than page-jumped and grow without bound: support and platform-support message threads, activity and audit logs, notification inboxes, POS session history, integration sync logs and AI assistant query logs.
- Response shape is the `APIResponse` envelope (§70.1): the page's items in `data` (an array), and in `meta.pagination` either `{current_page, per_page, total, last_page, from, to}` (length-aware) or `{per_page, next_cursor, prev_cursor}` (cursor), plus `meta.links` `{first, last, prev, next}`.
- Filters are plain query parameters named in each route table (for example `?status=&from=&to=`). Sorting uses `?sort=` with values listed by the owning section, where a leading `-` means descending.
- Lookup endpoints ([§45](#45-lookup-endpoints)) and small fixed registries (roles, permissions, feature lists) MAY return unpaginated collections because their size is bounded by configuration, not by tenant data.

### 70.5 Rate Limiting

Named limiters, defined in `AppServiceProvider`:

| Limiter | Key | Limit | Applied to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api` | token ID | 120 per minute | Authenticated routes |
| `public` | IP address | 60 per minute | Unauthenticated routes |
| `auth-sensitive` | IP address plus submitted email or phone | 5 per minute | Login, register, password forgot and reset, email resend, driver OTP, gift-card balance check, coupon validation (tenant and platform), job applications, tenant registration and verification (§9.8), affiliate application (§10.5), contact forms (§24.7) |
| `affiliate-clicks` | IP hash | 30 per minute | `POST /api/affiliate-clicks` (§21A.10), in addition to `public` |
| `tenant` | tenant ID | The tenant's `max_api_requests_per_minute` limit (§11.8): the plan value, or a limit override for a large tenant. Resolved through `PlanLimitService` and cached with the module states (§74). | Every tenant route except webhooks. It caps one tenant's total load, so a bot storm or runaway client on one store cannot degrade the shared servers for everyone else. |

The numbers are Assumption A-63. They are configuration values, not architecture. Limiter counters live in Redis with tenant-prefixed keys (§6.3).

Webhook routes are exempt from every throttle. They are protected by signature verification instead ([§15.6](#156-webhooks)), because a provider can legitimately burst traffic.

A throttled request returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

### 70.6 Route Parameters and Binding

- `{model}` parameters use implicit route-model binding against the current context's connection. Tenant models always resolve in the initialised tenant database.
- Numeric ID parameters are constrained to `[0-9]+` globally (`Route::pattern`). A static segment registered next to a parameter (for example `/purchase-orders/product-lookup` beside `/purchase-orders/{order}`) is registered first.
- Slug-bound storefront routes state the binding column in the owning section (for example `{product:slug}`).
- Non-model parameters (`{provider}`, `{mode}`, `{key}`, `{featureKey}`, `{limitKey}`, `{group}`, `{section}`, `{tenant}` on webhooks) are validated against their registry or enum. An unknown value returns 404.
- Static `metrics` segments (§22.4) are registered before the resource's `{model}` routes; this matters for `{tenant}`, which is a UUID and is not covered by the numeric pattern.
- Scoped bindings (for example `/products/{product}/variants/{variant}`) MUST use `scopeBindings()`, so a child that does not belong to the parent returns 404.

### 70.7 Versioning

All routes in this document are **v1** and unprefixed by version. A future breaking change introduces `/api/v2/...` alongside the existing routes rather than mutating them. Non-breaking additions (new optional fields, new endpoints) are made in v1.

### 70.8 Errors

Error responses use the `APIResponse` envelope (§70.1):

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "Human readable message",
  "data": null,
  "meta": {
    "error_code": "machine_readable_code",
    "details": {}
  },
  "errors": {}
}
```

- `meta.error_code` is the machine-readable code from the table below. Clients branch on it, never on `message`. Wherever this document says an error "carries X in `details`", X is in `meta.details`.
- Validation failures are 422 with `error_code = validation_failed` and the field messages in `errors` (`{"email": ["The email has already been taken."]}`), including nested keys such as `custom_fields.{key}` (§23.5).

| Status | `error_code` values | When |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing or invalid token, or an actor-type mismatch ([§10.2](#102-sanctum-configuration)). Invalid webhook signature. |
| 402 | `subscription_past_due`, `subscription_payment_required` | The tenant's subscription restriction applies, or the tenant is `awaiting_payment` ([§6.5](#65-tenant-status-and-access)) |
| 403 | `feature_unavailable`, `module_disabled`, `module_locked`, `module_suspended` ([§11.5](#115-module-lifecycle-and-disabled-behaviour), [§11.9](#119-access-resolution)), `limit_reached` ([§11.10](#1110-usage-tracking)), `forbidden` (permission or policy), `tenant_suspended` ([§6.5](#65-tenant-status-and-access)) | Module errors carry `details.module`, `details.state` and, for `locked` and `feature_unavailable`, `details.entitled_by_plans` |
| 404 | `not_found` | Unknown record, or a record outside the actor's scope. Scope failures return 404, not 403, so record existence is not disclosed. |
| 409 | `stock_conflict`, `price_changed`, `promotion_unavailable`, `totals_changed` | Checkout and POS commit re-checks under lock: stock, flash-sale quantity, promotion usage, or a quote that no longer matches `quote_hash` ([§38.6](#386-checkout-flow), [§51](#51-point-of-sale)). `details` carries what changed, and the client re-quotes. |
| 409 | `payment_in_progress`, `order_expired` | A payment attempt is already pending, or the unpaid order has expired ([§40.2](#402-online-gateway-payments)) |
| 409 | `idempotency_conflict`, `idempotency_in_progress` | A reused idempotency key with a different payload, or a request with the same key still running ([§70.11](#7011-idempotency)) |
| 409 | `state_conflict` | The record was changed by another request, or is in a state that forbids the action (for example deleting a redeemed coupon) |
| 410 | `tenant_closed` | The tenant is `closed` or `purged` ([§6.5](#65-tenant-status-and-access)) |
| 422 | `validation_failed`, `invalid_transition` ([§5.5](#55-enums-and-state-machines)), `refund_exceeds_payment` ([§40.4](#404-refunds)), `verified_purchase_required` (§42), `gift_card_currency_mismatch` (§46), other module-specific codes named in the owning section | |
| 422 | `module_requirements_not_enabled`, `module_has_dependents`, `module_disable_blocked` | Enabling or disabling a module ([§11.5](#115-module-lifecycle-and-disabled-behaviour)). `details` lists the modules or blocking reasons. |
| 422 | `plan_change_requires_confirmation` | A plan change with a non-empty impact preview, sent without `confirm_impact` ([§14.4](#144-plan-changes-and-proration)) |
| 422 | `legal_version_outdated`, `verification_code_invalid`, `verification_expired` | Registration ([§9.2](#92-legal-documents-and-acceptance), [§9.3](#93-registration-flow)) |
| 422 | `custom_field_has_values`, `section_type_not_allowed` | Deleting a custom field with values ([§23.2](#232-tables)); a CMS section outside its scope ([§24.2](#242-pages-and-page-sections)) |
| 422 | `payment_mode_mismatch`, `gateway_in_use`, `coupon_invalid` (with `details.reason`), `commission_on_hold` | Payment credentials saved in the wrong mode (§15.9); disabling a gateway in use (§15.10); a platform coupon rejected (§14.8); approving a commission before its hold ends (§21A.5) |
| 429 | `too_many_requests` | [§70.5](#705-rate-limiting) |
| 503 | `maintenance`, `tenant_provisioning`, `tenant_unavailable`, `registration_unavailable`, `affiliate_program_unavailable` | Platform maintenance, module notice hard block ([§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode)), a tenant that is `provisioning` or `provisioning_failed`, registration switched off or missing published legal documents ([§9.9](#99-onboarding-switches)), or the affiliate programme switched off ([§21A.1](#21a1-programme-switch-and-scope)) |

Exception rendering is centralised in the exception handler and always goes through `APIResponse`. Stack traces are never returned outside `local`.

### 70.9 CORS

- The `cors.dynamic` middleware ([§71](#71-middleware-reference)) replaces a static `config/cors.php` origin list.
- Allowed origins are every `domains.domain` (as `https://` origins, cached per [§74](#74-caching-strategy)) plus the platform admin frontend origins from the `PLATFORM_ADMIN_ORIGINS` environment variable.
- A wildcard origin is never used.
- `supports_credentials` is false, because every actor authenticates with bearer tokens ([§10.2](#102-sanctum-configuration)).
- Allowed headers include `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Accept`, `X-Guest-Token` and `Idempotency-Key`.

### 70.10 API Documentation

- `dedoc/scramble` generates OpenAPI documentation from routes, FormRequests and Resources. Controllers, FormRequests and Resources MUST be strongly typed so the output is complete.
- Two documents are generated: one for the landlord route files and one for the tenant route files.
- Documentation UIs are served only outside production, or in production behind `auth.as:platform`.

### 70.11 Idempotency

Every request that creates money movement, an order or a stock movement can be retried safely. The client sends an `Idempotency-Key` header, a UUID it generates once per logical action and reuses for every retry of that action.

```
idempotency_keys  [DB: landlord and tenant; identical shape]  [no timestamps]
id
scope              string    the caller: "staff:{id}", "customer:{id}", "seller:{id}", "guest:{sha256(guest token)}" (tenant);
                             "platform:{id}" (landlord)
route              string    route name, e.g. tenant.storefront.orders.store
key                string    8–128 characters, [A-Za-z0-9_-]
request_hash       char(64)  sha256 of the canonical JSON body plus the bound route parameters
status             enum(processing, completed)
response_status    smallint  nullable
response_body      encrypted nullable
locked_until       datetime  processing lease: created_at + 60 seconds
created_at         datetime
expires_at         datetime  created_at + 24 hours
unique(scope, route, key), index(expires_at)
```

**The `idempotency` middleware**, applied to the routes that name it:

1. A missing or malformed header returns 422 `validation_failed` on `Idempotency-Key`.
2. It inserts a `processing` row. The unique index decides the race between two concurrent retries.
3. If a row already exists:
   - a different `request_hash`: 409 `idempotency_conflict`. The key was reused for another request.
   - `processing` with an unexpired `locked_until`: 409 `idempotency_in_progress` with `Retry-After: 2`.
   - `completed`: the stored status and body are replayed, with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The controller does not run.
   - `processing` with an expired lease (the original process died): the request is executed again. See the second line of defence below.
4. After the controller returns, a 2xx or 4xx response is stored and the row becomes `completed`. A 5xx response or an exception deletes the row, so the client's retry executes normally. A 4xx is stored deliberately: a retry of a request that failed with `totals_changed` gets the same answer, and a changed request needs a new key.

**Second line of defence.** The middleware's row and the business transaction are separate, so a crash between them is possible. Every service reached through this middleware therefore also writes the key onto the record it creates, inside its own transaction, under a unique index: `orders.idempotency_key` (checkout and POS), and `order_payments.idempotency_key` (payment attempts, refunds and manual payments). A re-execution after a lost response hits that index, and the service returns the existing record instead of creating a second one. A duplicate charge, refund or order is therefore impossible even when the idempotency row is lost.

**Routes that require it** are the routes marked `idempotency` in their tables: checkout and payment initiation (§38.7, §40.7), direct and return refunds (§39.6, §41), manual payments (§40.7), gift-card purchase and issue (§46.5), installment payments and charges (§47), seller payout completion (§50), and in the landlord context platform payment refunds (§14.6) and affiliate payout completion (§21A.10). The landlord routes use the landlord table; their second line of defence is `payment_transactions.reference` and the payout's status transition under lock. A new route that moves money MUST carry it. POS sales carry the key in the body instead (`idempotency_key`, §51.6), because offline sync replays them in batches, and `orders.idempotency_key` gives the same guarantee.

Expired rows are deleted by the daily tenant and landlord maintenance jobs (§72.2). The key header is allowed by CORS (§70.9).

Webhooks do not use this mechanism. They are made idempotent by `webhook_logs.provider_event_id` and by the row transitions of the records they complete (§15.6, §40.1).

### 70.12 Bulk Operations

- A bulk endpoint accepts at most 100 items per request, and is named `POST /api/admin/{resource}/bulk` with body `{action, ids[] | items[]}`. The owning section lists its actions.
- Each item runs through the same service method, with the same validation, permissions and policies, as the single-item endpoint. Nothing bypasses the service layer.
- Items are processed independently, each in its own transaction. The response is 200 with a per-item result `{id, status: ok | error, error, message}`, so one bad item never rolls back the others.
- Changes to more than 100 records at once (a whole-catalogue price change, a CSV import) are imports, which are deferred (Appendix C).
- v1 defines bulk actions only where list screens need them: products (`activate`, `deactivate`) and coupons (`activate`, `deactivate`) (Assumption A-71). The route's own permission is derived as usual (`products.bulk`, `coupons.bulk`, §12.4), and each item is additionally authorised by the model policy.

## 71. Middleware Reference

This is the authoritative middleware list. No other middleware is used for access control.

| Alias | Class | Context | Behaviour | Owning section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `request.context` | `Shared\SetRequestContext` | Both | Accepts a valid inbound `X-Request-Id` or generates a UUID, returns it on the response, and adds `request_id`, `tenant_id` and the actor to the log context and to every job dispatched during the request. | [§77.7](#777-observability) |
| (stancl) | `InitializeTenancyByDomain` | Tenant | Resolves the tenant from the request host through `domains`, using the host cache ([§74](#74-caching-strategy)). Unknown or unverified host: 404. | [§6.2](#62-identification) |
| (stancl) | `InitializeTenancyByPath` | Tenant webhooks | Resolves the tenant from the `{tenant}` path segment. | [§6.2](#62-identification), [§15.6](#156-webhooks) |
| (stancl) | `PreventAccessFromCentralDomains` | Tenant | Rejects tenant routes on landlord domains. | [§6.2](#62-identification) |
| `platform.maintenance` | `Shared\EnsurePlatformNotInMaintenance` | Tenant | 503 `maintenance` when `platform_settings.maintenance_mode` is true. | [§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode) |
| `tenant.active` | `Tenant\EnsureTenantIsActive` | Tenant | Blocks by `tenants.status` (402 for `awaiting_payment`, 403, 410 or 503), then applies the subscription restriction (402). Both are read from the cached tenant record, so no extra query runs per request. | [§6.5](#65-tenant-status-and-access) |
| `cors.dynamic` | `Shared\HandleDynamicCors` | Both | CORS with dynamically resolved origins. | [§70.9](#709-cors) |
| `throttle:{limiter}` | Laravel | Both | Named limiters. | [§70.5](#705-rate-limiting) |
| `auth.as:{actor}` | `Shared\AuthenticateActor` | Both | Sanctum bearer authentication. 401 unless the token's ability and `tokenable_type` both match `{actor}`. Sets the default guard to `{actor}`. | [§10.2](#102-sanctum-configuration) |
| `auth.as.optional:customer` | `Tenant\AuthenticateCustomerOptionally` | Tenant | Resolves a customer when a valid customer token is present. Otherwise continues as a guest. An invalid token is treated as absent, not as 401. | [§10.2](#102-sanctum-configuration) |
| `guest.token` | `Tenant\ResolveGuestToken` | Tenant | Reads `X-Guest-Token` and makes it available to the request. It never issues tokens: `CartService` issues one when it creates a guest cart. | [§38.2](#382-guest-carts-and-merge) |
| `feature:{key}` and `feature:{key},wind-down` | `Tenant\EnsureFeatureEnabled` | Tenant | Resolves the module state (§11.9, cached). `enabled` passes. `disabled` and `locked` pass admin `GET`/`HEAD` requests when the registry marks the module "read when inactive", and pass routes declared with the `wind-down` parameter; otherwise 403 `module_disabled` or `module_locked`. `suspended`: 403 `module_suspended` on every route. `unavailable`: 403 `feature_unavailable`. `available`: 403 `module_disabled`. The key MUST exist in `config/modules.php`. | [§11.9](#119-access-resolution) |
| `module.notice:{key}` | `Tenant\CheckModuleNotice` | Tenant | Applies an active module notice: hard block (503), read-only (writes 503), or an informational header. | [§18](#18-module-notices-and-maintenance-mode) |
| `usage.limit:{key}` | `Tenant\EnsureWithinUsageLimit` | Tenant | 403 `limit_reached` when the live count is at the limit. | [§11.10](#1110-usage-tracking) |
| `permission.derived` | `Shared\AuthorizeDerivedPermission` | Both | Part of the `landlord.admin` and `tenant.admin` groups. Derives the route's permission name from its URI and action by the §12.4 rule at run time, and returns 403 `forbidden` (with `details.permission`) unless the actor holds it on the current guard. A route whose permission derives to nothing is refused (fail closed). Routes whose Permission column says "none" opt out with `->withoutMiddleware('permission.derived')`. Route files therefore carry no permission strings; `php artisan permissions:generate` writes the derived set to `config/permissions/generated/{landlord,tenant}.php`, which `PermissionSyncService` reads, and an architecture test fails the build when the generated files and the routes disagree. | [§12.4](#124-permission-naming-and-derivation) |
| `permission:{name}` | spatie `PermissionMiddleware` | Both | 403 `forbidden` unless the actor holds the named permission. Reserved for a route that needs a permission other than its derived one; none does in v1. | [§12.4](#124-permission-naming-and-derivation) |
| `verify.webhook` | `Shared\VerifyWebhookSignature` | Both | Resolves the webhook secret of the route's `{provider}` **and `{mode}`** (landlord gateway row, or the current tenant's row on the path-identified tenant route), verifies the signature over the raw body, 401 on failure. | [§15.6](#156-webhooks) |
| `signed` | Laravel `ValidateSignature` | Both | 403 unless the URL signature is valid and unexpired. Used for the emailed customer export link and the platform user's tenant export link (§6.7). | [§19.4](#194-asynchronous-exports) |
| `idempotency` | `Shared\EnforceIdempotency` | Both | Requires `Idempotency-Key`, and replays or rejects repeated requests, using the `idempotency_keys` table of the current context. | [§70.11](#7011-idempotency) |
| `internal.edge` | `Landlord\AuthenticateEdgeRequest` | Landlord | Allows only source IPs in `EDGE_ALLOWED_IPS` that also present `EDGE_SHARED_SECRET` in the `X-Edge-Secret` header, compared in constant time. Otherwise 404. | [§7.5](#75-custom-domains) |

Middleware classes live in `app/Shared/Http/Middleware/{Landlord|Tenant|Shared}` ([§73](#73-project-structure)).

Middleware from earlier drafts that is **not** used:

- `EnsureCentralAdmin`, replaced by `auth.as:platform` plus permissions.
- `EnsureTenantSubscriptionActive`. The subscription restriction is part of `tenant.active` (§6.5), so the tenant record is read once.
- Any header-based tenant identification (Assumption A-5).

**Permission middleware consistency.** Routes declare their permission explicitly, for example `->middleware('permission:products.view,staff')`. An architecture test ([§76.4](#764-architecture-tests)) asserts that every `landlord.admin` and `tenant.admin` route carries exactly the name derived by §12.4 or is on the "none" allow-list, and that the set of names equals `config/permissions/{landlord,tenant}.php`.

## 72. Jobs, Scheduling, Events and Broadcasting

| | |
|---|---|
| **Context** | Both |
| **Feature key** | none |
| **Depends on** | §6, §9 |

### 72.1 Queues and Job Standards

**Queues.** Four queues share one Redis connection and are supervised by Horizon ([§77.3](#773-queues)):

| Queue | Context | Carries | Why separate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `landlord-default` | Landlord | Provisioning, billing, platform coupons, affiliate commissions and payouts, landlord notifications, domain checks, daily metrics, fan-out dispatchers, purge | A burst of tenant work never starves provisioning or billing |
| `tenant-critical` | Tenant | Payment webhooks, payment and refund verification, `ExpireUnpaidOrder`, `PostAccountingEntry`, stock-affecting jobs | Money and stock work must never wait behind bulk work |
| `tenant-default` | Tenant | Notifications, daily maintenance, syncs, sitemaps, product views, broadcasts | Normal background work |
| `tenant-bulk` | Tenant | Exports, coupon generation, tenant migrations, backups | Long-running work, with its own worker pool and concurrency cap |

**Tenant context.** Tenant jobs are dispatched from within a tenant context. `QueueTenancyBootstrapper` serialises the tenant ID and re-initialises tenancy when the job runs ([§6.3](#63-tenancy-bootstrappers)). A job whose tenant is no longer `active`, `suspended` or `closed` (for example `purged`) is deleted without running. Jobs for `suspended` and `closed` tenants still run, so money already in flight is settled.

**Job standards.** Every job class declares the following. An architecture test enforces the declarations (§76.4).

| Property | Rule |
|---|---|
| `tries` and `backoff` | Declared explicitly. Default: 5 tries with exponential backoff (10 s, 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min). Provisioning uses 1 try (§9.4). |
| `timeout` | Declared explicitly, and always below the queue's `retry_after`. Default 120 s. `tenant-bulk` jobs up to 1 hour. |
| After commit | Every job dispatched inside a transaction is dispatched after commit (`afterCommit`), so a job never reads data that was rolled back. |
| Idempotency | Every job can run twice without a second effect. Money and stock jobs achieve this by locking the record and checking its state first (for example `PostAccountingEntry`, `ExpireUnpaidOrder`). |
| Uniqueness | Jobs that must not overlap implement `ShouldBeUnique` with a tenant-scoped key (for example one sync chain per tenant and sync type). |
| Payload | Jobs carry IDs, never models with loaded relations or secrets. A job that needs a secret reads it from its encrypted column when it runs (for example `ProvisionTenantDatabase` reads the registration's password hash, §9.4). |
| Failure | `failed()` records the tenant ID, the job and the error, and dispatches the owning section's failure notification where one exists. Failed jobs land in the landlord `failed_jobs` table. |
| Context | `request_id` (when dispatched from a request), `tenant_id` and the job UUID are added to the log context (§77.7). |

- A Laravel Notification implements `ShouldQueue` on the `tenant-default` or `landlord-default` queue of its context ([§17](#17-notification-system)).
- A job for a feature-gated module first checks `tenantCanAccess()` and exits without work unless the module is `enabled`. Wind-down jobs listed in §11.5 check `canRead()` instead, and never run for a `suspended` module.
- Job class names are imperative verb phrases (`ProvisionTenantDatabase`, not `TenantDatabaseProvisioningJob`).

### 72.2 Scheduled Tasks

The scheduler (`routes/console.php`) runs every minute on exactly one server ([§77.2](#772-processes)). There are only **landlord** schedule entries. Per-tenant work is reached through one daily job per tenant, never through one scheduled task per tenant per feature, so the number of scheduled jobs grows with the tenant count only once.

| Task | Frequency | Queue | Behaviour | Owning section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ProcessSubscriptionRenewal` | Daily, 01:00 UTC | `landlord-default` | Platform-charged renewals, the provider-renewal safety net, MRR churn movements for subscriptions past `ends_at` or past the grace period (§14.10), `subscription.renewing_soon` and `subscription.trial_ending_soon` | [§14.7](#147-service) |
| `RecordPlatformDailyMetrics` | Hourly at :30; records the previous day once, at the first run after midnight in `platform_settings.default_timezone` (00:30 local, D-41) | `landlord-default` | Upserts the previous day's `platform_daily_metrics` rows; sends `platform.billing_payment_failed_alert` when failed live charges occurred | [§22.6](#226-landlord-dashboard) |
| `RunLandlordDailyMaintenance` | Daily, 02:00 UTC | `landlord-default` | `TenantManagementService::schedulePurges()` (§6.7); registration expiry and closure of unpaid `awaiting_payment` tenants (`expireStaleRegistrations()`, `closeUnpaidTenants()`, §9.3); deletion of `tenant_features` and `tenant_limit_overrides` rows whose `expires_at` passed more than 90 days ago (their history stays in the landlord activity log, §11.7); landlord contact-submission retention (§24.7); landlord `webhook_logs` and `idempotency_keys` retention (§15.6, §70.11); landlord activity-log retention (§19.1); `failed` marking of custom domains past their verification window, and `RecheckCustomDomains` for active domains (§7.5); platform refunds with an unknown outcome (§14.9); expiry of affiliate referrals past their conversion window (§21A.4); affiliate click retention (§21A.3); `tenant_usage_snapshots` older than 400 days (§22.6) | §6.7, §7.5, §9.3, §14.9, §15.6, §21A |
| `ApproveEligibleAffiliateCommissions` | Daily, 03:30 UTC | `landlord-default` | With `affiliate_commission_approval = automatic`, approves pending commissions past `hold_until` without `requires_review`; otherwise sends `affiliate.commissions_awaiting_approval` when any are waiting | [§21A.5](#21a5-commissions) |
| `GenerateAffiliatePayouts` | Daily, 04:00 in `platform_settings.default_timezone`; acts only on `affiliate_payout_day` when the schedule is `monthly` | `landlord-default` | `AffiliatePayoutService::generate()` for the previous calendar month; idempotent per affiliate, currency and period | [§21A.6](#21a6-payouts) |
| `DispatchTenantDailyMaintenance` | Hourly | `landlord-default` | Dispatches `RunTenantDailyMaintenance` for every `active`, `suspended` or `closed` tenant whose local time (`tenants.timezone`) is now between 01:00 and 01:59. Each dispatch gets a random delay of up to 50 minutes, so the load of one timezone is spread across its hour. Tenants are read in chunks by ID. | this section |
| `BackupDatabases` | Daily, 03:00 UTC | `tenant-bulk` | Landlord backup, then one backup job per tenant database, rate-limited per database server | [§77.5](#775-backups) |

**`RunTenantDailyMaintenance`** (queue `tenant-default`) runs each task below in its own `try` block and its own transaction where it writes, so one failing task never blocks the others. Each failure is logged with the task name. Tasks for a disabled feature are skipped. Housekeeping tasks run inline. Tasks that call external providers or touch many rows are dispatched as their own jobs, shown in the Job column.

| Task | Job | Feature | Owning section |
|---|---|---|---|

| Safety nets for lost delayed jobs: unpaid orders past `payment_expires_at` get `ExpireUnpaidOrder`; `pending` gateway payments older than 15 minutes with no scheduled verification get `VerifyOrderPayment`; unknown-outcome refunds get `order.refund_needs_review` | inline dispatch | core | §39.5, §40.2, §40.4 |
| Accounting outbox recovery: `pending` requests older than 10 minutes are re-dispatched | inline dispatch | `accounting` | [§57.3](#573-journal-entries-and-automatic-postings) |
| Sitemap rebuild, when anything was published since the last build | `GenerateSitemapForTenant` | core | [§30.2](#302-seo) |
| Gift card expiry | `ExpireGiftCards` | `gift_cards` | [§46.3](#463-redemption-rules) |
| Installment charges, then overdue and default tracking | `ChargeDueInstallments`, `MarkOverdueInstallments` | `installments` | [§47.3](#473-flow) |
| Exchange-rate refresh (provider: UD-19) | `RefreshExchangeRates` | `multi_currency` | [§48.2](#482-rules) |
| Supplier quotation expiry | `ExpireSupplierQuotations` | `purchasing` | [§49.3](#493-supplier-quotations) |
| Sales quotation expiry | `ExpireSalesQuotations` | `sales_quotations` | [§53.2](#532-rules) |

| Product-subscription renewal orders | `ProcessProductSubscriptionRenewals` | `product_subscriptions` | [§55.2](#552-flow) |
| Integration sync watchdog: restarts sync chains older than twice their interval | inline dispatch | `woocommerce`, `social_commerce` | §68.3, §69.2 |

| Usage snapshot: computes the tenant's usage per limit key, the day's live orders and gross sales, failed webhooks and failed postings, and upserts `tenant_usage_snapshots` through `TenantUsageReporter` | inline | always | [§22.6](#226-landlord-dashboard) |

Daily tasks evaluate "today" in the tenant's timezone, which is also the moment they run (Assumption A-64).

**Removed scheduled tasks.** Earlier revisions of this document scheduled these per-tenant fan-outs. They are replaced by exact delayed jobs, which do no work when there is nothing to do and add no load per idle tenant:

| Removed | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| `ReconcilePendingOrderPayments` (every 15 minutes, every tenant) | `VerifyOrderPayment`, delayed per payment (§40.2), plus the daily safety net |
| `MarkReservedTables` (every 5 minutes, every restaurant tenant) | `MarkTableReserved`, delayed per reservation (§65.1) |
| `DispatchIntegrationSyncs` (every 5 minutes, every integrated tenant) | Self-scheduling `RunWooCommerceSync` and `RunSocialCommerceSync` chains (§68.3, §69.2), plus the daily watchdog |
| One daily fan-out per feature (ten landlord schedule entries) | `RunTenantDailyMaintenance`, one job per tenant per day |

At 100,000 tenants, the three removed high-frequency fan-outs alone would have dispatched more than 30 million jobs a day, almost all of them no-ops.

### 72.4 Broadcasting and Real-Time

- **Server.** One shared Laravel Reverb deployment serves the landlord and every tenant ([§77.4](#774-reverb)). Redis backs Reverb scaling.
- **Tenant channel prefixing.** Every tenant channel name is prefixed with `tenant.{tenant_id}.`. The prefix is added by a single helper used by every tenant broadcast event and by `routes/channels.php`, so channel names cannot collide across tenants.
- **Authorisation endpoints.** `POST /broadcasting/auth` is registered on landlord domains (guard `platform`) and on tenant domains (guards `staff` and `customer`, plus guest-token authorisation for guest support conversations: a guest is authorised only for a conversation whose guest token matches `X-Guest-Token`).

| Channel | Type | Authorised for | Events | Owning section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant.{tenant_id}.support-conversation.{id}` | private | The conversation's customer or guest, and staff with support permissions | `SupportMessageSent`, `SupportConversationStatusChanged` | [§59.2](#592-real-time) |
| `tenant.{tenant_id}.support-agents-online` | presence | Staff with support permissions | join and leave | [§59.2](#592-real-time) |
| `platform-support-conversation.{id}` | private | Platform users with support permissions (landlord domain), and staff of the conversation's tenant (tenant domain) | `PlatformSupportMessageSent`, `PlatformSupportConversationStatusChanged` | [§21](#21-platform-support-helpdesk) |

- Typing indicators are client whispers on the private channel. There are no server events for them (earlier drafts' `AgentTyping` and `CustomerTyping` are not used).
- Broadcast events implement `ShouldBroadcast` and are queued on the context's queue.

**Domain events.** Modules call each other through named service methods (integration hooks, [§2](#2-architecture-principles) Principle 7), not through events. The only domain event is `TenantProvisioned` ([§9.4](#94-provisioning-job)). Its listener dispatches `SendTenantWelcomeNotification`.

## 73. Project Structure

The folder split is an organisational convention inside one Laravel application ([§2](#2-architecture-principles) Principle 2).

### 73.1 Modular Monolith Layout

The application is a **modular monolith**: one deployable Laravel application whose code is organised by business module, not by technical layer. A module's controllers, models, services, jobs and policies sit together, so a module can be understood, tested, disabled and (if ever needed) extracted on its own. Microservices are deliberately not used: database-per-tenant isolation, one deployment and in-process transactions across core commerce matter more to this platform than independent deployability.

```
app/
  Modules/
    {Module}/                            the Code module from the owning section's header block (§1.5)
      Http/
        Controllers/Landlord/            landlord public controllers
        Controllers/Landlord/Admin/      platform-admin controllers
        Controllers/Tenant/              storefront and customer controllers
        Controllers/Tenant/Admin/        staff (tenant admin) controllers
        Controllers/Tenant/Seller/       seller controllers

        Requests/                        mirrors Controllers
        Resources/                       one Resource per returned model
```
